    singleton factors have finite poles: the omitted denominator
    has degree `(m-2)2^(m-1)+1`. Restoring integrality makes the
    normalized arc length grow as a positive power for `m>=3`.
    A separate effective polynomial example with three circle
    points does attain endpoint scale. Thus a viable transfer must
    control all places, and any polynomial exclusion must genuinely
    use sufficiently many rows. See Sections 10--11 of
    [the moving-field investigation](moving_residue_field_route.md).

38. **Changing anchors does not create an additional leading-height
    constraint.** For primitive anchored numerators,
    `h_ij=h_j bar(h_i)/N(gcd_G(h_i,h_j))` exactly. The retained
    pair distances and anchored angular estimates already make all
    pair residues small. Exact core divisibility under every anchor
    does require correction-order inequalities: an actual Gaussian
    constant-residue example violates them while satisfying the
    one-anchor equations. However, trimming total block log norm
    at most `2 sum_i log|K_i|` restores all those divisibilities.
    The loss and new coefficients remain negligible relative to
    every block for the growing extracted tuples. See
    [the transition and repair theorem](all_anchor_primitive_transition.md).

39. **Anchor norms and pair minors give the complete local coherent
    sign condition.** At a core prime, primitivity makes the relevant
    imaginary residues units. After this localization, the ideal
    generated by one anchor norm and its pair determinants is exactly
    the intersection of the two coherent isotropic-sign ideals.
    The statement holds for every ideal power. Row-norm coefficients
    and generically justified norm denominators also preserve the
    existing auxiliary exponent comparison. Individual cut norms
    and global cancellations between their actual values remain
    outside that comparison. See
    [the norm-coefficient audit](norm_coefficient_audit.md).

40. **The strengthened block equations have a converse producing
    actual endpoint clusters.** For primitive `h_i=K_i A_i`, let
    `P=product_(S nonempty)|H_S|`, `E=sum log|K_i|`,
    `T=max|Im h_i|`, and `sigma=min log|A_i|-(log P)/2`.
    The Gaussian lcm reconstructs a primitive circle at the exact
    least radius `P<=R<=P exp(E)`. Its normalized arc length is
    at most `8T exp(E/2-sigma)` under an explicit small-angle
    condition. Central truncation gives
    `sigma=w_empty/4+o(w_empty)` and `E+logT=o(w_empty)`, so the
    reconstruction has normalized length tending to zero. Thus
    suitable abstract families of these equations would really
    yield unbounded endpoint clusters; integrality is not an omitted
    condition in this converse. No such family or exclusion is
    proved. See [the reconstruction theorem](independent_block_reconstruction.md).

41. **A new arithmetic restriction excludes every norm-squareclass
    relation supported on at most six rows.** In the extracted
    profiles, balanced signed combinations of up to six phase
    ratios have primitive Gaussian numerator `g` with
    `log N(g)<=(15/16+o(1))W`. A nontrivial squareclass relation
    would make `N(g)` a square. Conjugate primitivity then forces
    `|Im g|/|g|>=|g|^(-1/2)`, contradicting the original angular
    precision with exponent margin `W/64+o(W)`. Full cut support
    excludes a unit numerator. The argument includes explicit
    finite conditions and all Gaussian units. If the anchor norm
    squareclasses span dimension `d`, it follows that
    `2^d>=sum_(j=0..3)binom(k-1,j)`. For square cores,
    `d<=omega(D)`, so the correcting factors must have growing
    arithmetic complexity. This does not yet force positive
    height proportional to a block or improve the general growth
    rate. See [the squareclass theorem](norm_squareclass_separation.md).

42. **The elementary squareclass baseline is now separated from
    the six-wise improvement.** For an arbitrary arc with `C<1`,
    augment the norm squareclass labels by Gaussian-unit parity.
    If their binary rank is `d`, then
    `1+binom(M,2)<=2^d`, without any uniform-profile extraction.
    The proof excludes all relations on at most four labels and
    repairs the case where an averaged balanced word is exactly
    a unit. Omitting the unit bit has explicit Pell counterexamples.
    Thus bounded rank already gives a uniform bound; the six-wise
    result adds a stronger restriction on extracted profiles.
    See [the baseline and group audit](squareclass_baseline_and_power_groups.md).

43. **Exact higher powers give stronger phase separation, in the
    signed Gaussian group.** A cyclotomic integer-value argument
    bounds the phase of an exact `ell`th power using
    `delta_ell=phi(lcm(ell,4))/2`. Applied to the full cut profile,
    it excludes coefficient patterns with absolute Bernoulli load
    less than `ell/(2delta_ell)`. In particular, balanced signed
    relations modulo four on at most 24 rows are excluded, and
    `|G_4|>=binom(k-1,12)`. Ordinary fourth-power norm relations
    do not suffice; an unrecorded Gaussian unit can also change
    the separation exponent. Both failures have explicit examples.
    The resulting correction-conductor bound still grows only
    logarithmically in `k`. See [the higher-power theorem](higher_power_phase_separation.md).

44. **Negligible corrections can saturate all power-class tests
    simultaneously.** Independent correction cut blocks with
    private exponent-one primes realize exactly the universal
    relations among all primitive pair norms, for every power
    order at once. They also saturate the signed phase classes,
    admit equal-norm integral correction factors, and can meet
    prescribed finite congruence depths at every chosen core
    prime. Their heights become negligible when the core powers
    subsequently grow. This does not make the actual imaginary
    parts small. It rules out obtaining the required height gain
    from those tests alone. See [the construction and its scope](power_class_saturation.md).

45. **The conductor-depth distinction has an exact threshold.**
    For primitive `A` and `L|A`, the incident branch congruence
    is equivalent to `N(L)|Im(KA)-t`. Therefore
    `N(L)>|K||A|+|t|` forces the actual small-value equation.
    With negligible coefficients and targets, every fixed depth
    fraction greater than one half suffices; an exact primitive
    example fails at one half. The same congruence uniquely
    determines a small ratio `K/t` when `2UT<|L|`. Individual
    lattice indices and direct cross-row elimination do not yet
    give a simultaneous height bound. See [the CRT theorem](full_depth_crt_route.md).

46. **The direct global-GCD application has a quantified boundary
    loss, even after fixing all target shifts.** Every fixed prime
    set carries at most `4|S|W/M=o(W)` conductor mass. Normalize
    `y_i=h_i/(2it_i)`, so `y_i-1=bar(h_i)/(2it_i)` and the shifts
    are exactly one. For fixed `n` extracted rows, the point height,
    outside-prime boundary, and global common-divisor height are
    respectively `W/4`, `nW/4`, and `W/2^(n+1)`, each up to
    `o(W)`. Thus the available all-points GCD inequality with
    boundary coefficient `1/(n-1)` remains compatible even if
    its other height coefficient is replaced by zero. This is
    a failure of that application, not of every possible global
    GCD transformation. See [the calculation and primary sources](global_gcd_applicability.md).

47. **A growing multiquadratic field does not amplify the naive
    near-square norm or trace calculation.** For
    `delta_i=sqrt(x_i^2+t_i^2)-x_i`, replacing radical monomials
    by products of the `delta_i` in a downward-closed family
    leaves their integral lattice unchanged. Its trace determinant
    is computed exactly, with every shared norm factor retained.
    The maximal order can have a much smaller discriminant, but
    dividing tiny defect products by shared conductor primes is
    nonintegral: the defects are local units at those primes.
    Thus maximal-order combinations remain a precise possible
    route, with a real denominator issue to overcome. See
    [the field and integrality audit](multiquadratic_nearsquare_audit.md).

48. **The small Gaussian completion has an exact continued-fraction
    parametrization.** For fixed primitive `P`, put `Q=N(P)` and
    let `r mod Q` represent its Gaussian ideal by `x=r t mod Q`.
    If `2UT<|P|`, the entire window `|h/P|<=U`,
    `0<|Im h|<=T` has at most one primitive `h` up to sign.
    It is obtained from the last convergent of `r/Q` whose
    denominator is at most `T`; integer coprimality, parity, and
    one norm inequality decide whether that candidate works.
    Its next partial quotient must exceed `|P|/(UT)-2`.
    This makes the remaining search explicit, but does not bound
    the possible shared products `P`. See
    [the sparse convergent theorem](sparse_convergent_parametrization.md).

49. **A finite design freezes enough factor data to determine an
    eight-point configuration.** Each anchor pair uses 64 of the
    128 cut blocks. An explicit family of 49 frozen blocks gives
    each anchor pair 33 or 34 of those factors, and hence a strict
    majority of its logarithmic size in a sufficiently uniform
    profile. The sparse Gaussian uniqueness lemma then fixes all
    seven anchor phases across the entire small coefficient and
    residue window. The labelled primitive configuration is unique
    up to a common Gaussian unit. The Fano-plane construction is
    optimal for this particular strict anchor-majority criterion;
    it does not determine a unique block/correction factorization.
    Different frozen collections remain unbounded, so this is an
    injectivity result rather than a uniform count. For growing
    tuples, a related construction freezes `2^(k-2)+k-2` blocks;
    controlling targeted second and fourth moments retains the
    full extraction range `k=floor(c log_2 M)`, `c<1/2`.
    See [the reconstruction theorem and candidate procedure](sparse_phase_lattice_reconstruction.md)
    and [the 49-block design audit](fano_freezing_audit.md).

50. **Shared continued-fraction candidates have an exact compatibility
    test.** Pairwise root agreement is equivalent to the existing
    primitive determinant divisibility and is sufficient for the
    generalized CRT; literal root compatibility supplies no extra
    higher-row condition. Removing the small convergent prefix saves
    only negligible logarithmic height. Crossing the following large
    quotient incurs a coefficient of conductor-scale height. A common
    residue can also be obtained with negligible row scalars, provided
    their coordinate contents are retained. See
    [the exact CRT and Euclidean identities](shared_convergent_compatibility.md).

51. **A mixed near-square expression admits a valid integral shared-factor
    division.** Writing `G_ij=N(gcd_G(h_i,h_j))`, the expression
    `(delta_i delta_j+x_i delta_j+x_j delta_i-t_i t_j)/G_ij`
    is exactly the algebraic integer `sqrt(q_ij)-x_ij`. Its trace
    lattice is larger by index `product G_ij`, while the displayed
    small basis values lose the same leading factor. Triple-word
    differences recover the residue cocycle. Rank-three distance
    minors and their integral normalizations retain exact conductor
    factors but do not yet force a small nonzero integer. See
    [the integral pair-defect calculation](maximal_order_pair_defects.md).

52. **The sparse frozen design restricts the available symmetries.**
    Reanchoring permutes and conjugates the core blocks and preserves
    their weights and the least radius. Flipping whole prime
    allocations only in nonconstant unfrozen blocks makes at least
    one normalized residue exponentially large; the effect survives
    primitive normalization. A nonisometric projective map preserving
    all 49 frozen oriented factors must have logarithmic coefficient
    height at least `(49/4-o(1))w`. These restrictions concern precisely
    the stated frozen-data operations. See
    [the symmetry and normalization proof](reanchoring_and_frozen_symmetry_obstruction.md).

53. **Small projective maps inflate the least radius even when all
    factors may change.** For a nonisometric matrix of logarithmic
    height `J`, transformed primitive anchor numerators have pair
    gcds bounded by the old small residues and `exp(O(J))`. With
    `m` nonanchor rows, negligible errors give
    `log R_new=mW/4+o(W)` and
    `log C_new=(m-2)W/8+o(W)`. The finite bound implies that any
    nonisometric endpoint-preserving map must instead satisfy
    `J>=(1-o(1))W/(12m)` in the growing extracted regime.
    Rotations and reflections are the exact exceptions. See
    [the projective gcd theorem and height threshold](projective_radius_inflation.md).

54. **The projective orbit determines the radius to relative logarithmic
    error `O(1/M)`, with no matrix-height restriction.** On a same-unit
    cohort of `L` endpoint points, the average logarithmic height of
    the rational cross-ratios is `W/8+O(W/L)`. An exact conductor
    factor survives all residue cancellation. Averaging its cut
    weights and using pairwise obtuseness supplies explicit finite
    constants. Two projectively equivalent `M`-point endpoint
    clusters consequently satisfy
    `log R_new/log R_old=1+O(1/M)` after primitive normalization.
    This rules out a fixed-power descent within such an orbit;
    smaller reductions remain possible under this theorem. See
    [the invariant average and finite bounds](projective_orbit_radius_rigidity.md).

55. **Fixed-degree rational maps also have a quantitative obstruction
    to descent.** For a non-pure degree-`D` map, one algebraic root
    distinct from `i,-i` gives integral linear factors whose common
    ideals divide a fixed coefficient times the primitive pair
    residues. Field norms, a binary resultant, and exact primitive
    reduction yield
    `log C_new >= (m-2D)W/8-O_D(m^2(E+J+1))`.
    Thus a fixed-degree map of negligible coefficient height cannot
    preserve endpoint scale when `m>2D`. Pure higher powers separately
    raise the intrinsic radius to that power and also inflate the
    normalized arc. Degree-one rotations and reflections remain.
    See [the ideal-norm proof and explicit finite inequality](fixed_degree_rational_map_inflation.md).

56. **Graph traces and higher sign differences retain exact arithmetic
    budgets.** Every normalized trace of a product of primitive pair
    defects is an integer. Its largest Galois cuts have the same sign
    and dominate all other terms, giving a positive leading growth
    exponent for every nonempty graph in the extracted regime.
    Three rows give a further integral three-radical spin defect
    and an exact Heron equation. The full fixed-character sign cube
    admits an exact highest-order difference equal to a residue
    product. For restricted symmetric sign families, the actual lcm
    denominator and the order of symbolic cancellation obey a sharp
    budget inequality. These computations leave additional arithmetic
    cancellation or further integral divisions open. See
    [the graph, spin, and sign-word identities](graph_trace_and_spin_defects.md).

57. **Angular order and joint inert-prime compatibility alone do not
    increase the leading sieve cost.** A family of actual ordered
    Gaussian circle points realizes the congruence pattern
    `z_i=z_j mod p^a` exactly when `i=j mod p^a`, simultaneously
    at every inert prime and depth. Its total cost lies between
    the universal `F(M)` and `F(M)+2M^2`. Nonnegative pair
    reweighting cannot improve the conductor coefficient of the
    complete-graph cut bound. An angular Vandermonde estimate adds
    a useful `O(M^2)` term, without changing the established growth
    rate. The example has singleton conductor mass, so coupling
    these congruences to the extracted balanced conductor remains
    a possible route. See [the exact compatibility test](ordered_inert_sieve_route.md).

58. **The balanced profile determines a simultaneous height norm for
    all projective units.** For every integer zero-row-degree edge
    vector `c`, the product of chord differences `Lambda_c` has
    `h(Lambda_c)=(1+O(delta))w ell(c)`, where
    `ell(c)=(1/2)sum_S |sum_(i<j in S)c_ij|` is a genuine norm
    and `delta` tends to zero in the central extraction. The error
    is uniform even for unbounded coefficients. Thus the evaluated
    cross-ratios have their full possible multiplicative rank
    `k(k-3)/2`. Universal additive exchanges respect the same cut
    valuations; further arithmetic control of their remaining unit
    values is still required. See
    [the exact norm and correction budget](coupled_crossratio_height_norm.md).

59. **A height gap selects the correct Heron branch and reconstructs
    all pairs.** The normalized integral Heron equation for two
    primitive anchors and a primitive pair candidate has exactly
    a sum-angle and a difference-angle branch. The oriented core
    bounds their cross-conjugate gcd by the small corrections.
    Hence the sum branch has logarithmic modulus `W/2-o(W)`, too
    large for the required `W/4+o(W)` pair height. The surviving
    branch determines the entire primitive Gaussian numerator
    and its exact gcd. Solving all anchor triples in this range
    therefore reconstructs an integral circle and makes all
    remaining four-index identities automatic. A coherent
    unoriented four-point norm model shows why the branch gap
    cannot simply be omitted. See
    [the reconstruction theorem](heron_height_gap_reconstruction.md).

60. **Minimal reconstruction charts cannot be glued by their strict
    whole-block overlap alone.** The 49-cut minimum holds for
    reconstruction along any connected graph on eight vertices:
    cuts map bijectively to edge bits of each spanning tree, and
    48 cuts supply at most 230 incidences rather than the required
    231. Distinct minimal charts therefore have no connected
    overlap with that strict margin. Moreover one can construct
    an actual Gaussian integer of imaginary part one with any
    fixed number of independent, asymptotically balanced blocks
    and negligible correction height. Every majority window on
    that row is simultaneously feasible. The missing restriction
    must involve shared factors across different rows. See
    [the overlap theorem and cyclotomic construction](freezing_chart_overlap.md).

61. **The quadratic polynomial division model has an exact pencil
    classification.** For real quadratics with
    `deg(F_i-F_j)=2` and `F_i-F_j | F_i F_j+1`, every family of
    at least three lies in one affine pencil. Their complex
    numerators share a common linear factor. Such families can
    have arbitrarily many rows and constant primitive residues,
    but their least-radius degree grows with the row count and
    their conductor has a common factor and private factors.
    They do not realize the required full balanced profile.
    Higher degree is not settled by this classification. See
    [the polynomial model test](polynomial_heron_pencil_test.md).

62. **Full projective-unit rank now holds on a power-sized subset.**
    Without extracting every cut pattern, an `M`-point endpoint
    cluster supplies `k` same-unit rows whenever
    `K=binom(k,2)<=sqrt(M)/64`. For every integer zero-row-degree
    edge vector, one common choice of rows satisfies
    `h(Lambda_c)>=W ||c||_2/(32 sqrt(K))`.
    The proof selects a positive Gram matrix of quadratic sign
    functions and charges nearest-endpoint rounding by each
    row's own interior allocation. It also retains the residue
    errors in an `L^2` estimate. Thus the full rank `k(k-3)/2`
    is available for `k` of order `M^(1/4)`, beyond the logarithmic
    range of the full-block normal form. This is not an extraction
    of exponentially many balanced blocks at that size, and it
    does not yet improve the count bound. See
    [the finite theorem and audits](power_size_projective_unit_rank.md).

63. **Rank and universal exchanges miss the first six-point cancellation.**
    For every fixed number of rows, the actual rational family
    `x_i(T)=i+(k+1)^i/T` has full projective-unit rank and the
    coefficient-uniform estimate
    `h(Lambda_c)=(||c||_1/2)log T+O_k(||c||_1)`.
    It satisfies all additive Plucker exchanges and even matches
    the entire leading balanced-cut height norm on four and five
    rows. At six rows a specified product of two cross-ratios has
    balanced height `7W/32`, whereas this family has `W/4+O(1)`.
    The missing `W/32` cancellation belongs to one particular
    three-versus-three block. Thus a count argument must retain
    more than rank, individual heights, and universal identities.
    The family is not an endpoint lattice cluster. See
    [the exact comparison](projective_rank_exchange_countermodel.md).

64. **The faithful polynomial model has a linear degree bound.**
    Suppose the real polynomials `F_i` and all pair differences
    have degree `D`, every difference divides `F_i F_j+1`, and
    the Gaussian polynomial lcm of `F_i+i` has degree at most
    `2D`. Then `D` is even and the number of nonanchor rows is
    at most `3D/2`. Exact root-layer incidences give a positive
    Gram matrix; Newton identities place the imaginary root
    moments in its kernel; conjugate-paired Vandermonde
    independence gives kernel dimension at least `D/2`.
    Multiplicities are included, and no global conjugate-
    coprimality assumption is needed. In particular quartics
    admit at most six rows in this model. The bound depends on
    degree and does not transfer to arbitrary integer sequences.
    See [the proofs and audits](polynomial_divisor_incidence_bound.md).

65. **Three nonanchor rows realize the full seven-cut arithmetic system.**
    Seven explicit Gaussian linear factors give four actual
    points with primitive radius comparable to `n^7` and arc
    length `O(n^3)=O(R^(3/7))`. Every nonempty cut occurs with
    weight `2 log n+O(1)`, and all six canonical primitive
    residues stay bounded. Exact polynomial identities and
    bounded resultant losses justify the arithmetic claims;
    `n=2 mod 4` handles the ramified factor without rotating a
    small imaginary coordinate. The empty cut is absent from
    the intrinsic profile. This fixed four-point family does
    not disprove uniformity, but excludes a proposed obstruction
    based on only three-row compatibility. See
    [the construction](three_row_quartic_construction.md).

66. **That exact polynomial triple admits no fourth polynomial anchor.**
    A prospective real polynomial `F` must have each difference
    `F-F_i` dividing the degree-eight polynomial `F_i^2+1`.
    Its degree is therefore at most eight, and it lies on one
    of sixteen explicitly known real divisor directions through
    each anchor. Noncollinearity makes a finite intersection
    calculation exhaustive even for irrational coefficients.
    All 768 line-pair checks produce six candidates; only the
    original three satisfy all anchor conditions. Independent
    audits and a standard-library rational-arithmetic
    certificate verify this maximality in every polynomial
    degree. It is specific to this triple and does not exclude
    isolated integer extensions or other families. See
    [the theorem and certificate](quartic_extension_maximality.md).

67. **The polynomial extension obstruction holds throughout its conic family.**
    Both real branches of the three-row rational-conic construction
    are maximal whenever all seven factors remain distinct and
    conjugate-disjoint. Exact gcds of coefficient minors cover
    all 1,536 parameter-dependent direction pairs, including
    exceptional parameters omitted by a finite sample. Every
    possible exceptional real root is a repeated-row, pole, or
    conjugate-factor degeneration. The three remaining companion
    intersections fail an exact leading-coefficient test.
    The standard-library certificate was run independently by
    the root orchestrator, and its exhaustion argument was
    audited. This is a theorem about the whole specified family,
    not all polynomial triples. See
    [the proof and certificate](quartic_conic_family_maximality.md).

68. **A different symmetry gives four real quartic rows, with a rationality obstruction.**
    Eight explicit roots realize the four singleton supports
    and the four triple supports. Each row has degree four,
    every pair gcd has degree two, all pair imaginary residues
    are nonzero constants, and the least-radius degree is eight.
    Every three-row subtuple has all seven nonempty cuts, so a
    universal version of the preceding maximality claim is
    false over the reals. In this displayed symmetric family,
    rational coefficients would require rational `u,a,b` with
    `u>1/2`, `a^2=u(u+1)`, and `b^2=u^2-1/4`. An elliptic
    curve argument excludes those rational parameters.
    This supplies a precise distinction between real algebraic
    compatibility and arithmetic realizability. It does not
    classify every realization of the eight-support pattern.
    See [the formulas and arithmetic obstruction](four_row_quartic_eight_block_family.md).

69. **A common-circle constraint leads to a nonsymmetric rational four-row realization.**
    For the eight simple blocks with singleton and triple supports,
    telescoping pair differences forces the four triple roots
    onto a circle centered on the real axis; a cubic root count
    excludes a vertical line. Their remaining coefficient
    constraint is an explicit second conic. On the unit circle,
    rational half-angle parameters must have product one and
    second elementary symmetric sum minus six. A rational
    osculating-quadratic calculation supplies a nondegenerate
    solution, and exact verification gives four rational
    quartic rows and all six primitive pair polynomials.
    Eight integer factors with odd norms at every even parameter
    yield five actual lattice points at radius `asymp n^8`
    and arc length `O(n^4)`. This lies outside the rank-zero
    symmetric slice in item 68. All six two-row cuts and the
    full four-row cut are absent, so it does not realize the
    required full fifteen-block profile. Its endpoint constant
    is fixed, not tending to zero. See
    [the rational construction and certificate](four_row_rational_quartic_construction.md).

70. **The full fifteen-block polynomial model has an exact finite reduction.**
    For four degree-eight rows, normalize the common root to `-i`.
    Four oriented triple roots determine one real interpolation
    polynomial of degree at most seven. Four additional real scalars
    determine all six pair norm quadratics as two-by-two determinants.
    Six quadratic divisibility tests, together with explicit degree,
    coprimality, and root-separation conditions, are necessary and
    sufficient for the full fifteen simple supports. Rational input
    passing these tests gives Gaussian-rational edge and private roots.
    A reflection slice retains every support and reduces to six real
    equations in six parameters. The exact identity certificate passes;
    no nondegenerate solution, impossibility theorem, or transfer from
    arbitrary integer sequences is asserted. See
    [the full-profile reduction](full_fifteen_block_quadratic_reduction.md).

71. **Every order-eight Hadamard cut system is excluded by actual integer phases.**
    Eight distinct lattice points formed from independent,
    conjugate-coprime Gaussian blocks with an anchored order-eight
    Hadamard incidence matrix and one common unit class cannot lie on
    an arc of length `sqrt(R)/2`. The proof permits arbitrary block
    sizes, exponents, unit blocks, and a common Gaussian multiplier.
    Exact row combinations isolate fourth powers at balanced columns
    and squared ratios or products at columns with equal absolute sums.
    Gaussian integrality forces sufficiently large block norms.
    Column sums are congruent modulo four, and Parseval leaves only
    three possible absolute spectra; each gives a contradiction.
    In the cases using balanced columns the upper bound is `R<29`,
    while eight-point spacing forces `R>=392`. Independent audits and
    exact projection checks pass. A primitive Pell example shows why
    even a fixed independent row twist invalidates the pure-power
    separation step. This theorem excludes a critical sparse mixed
    profile but does not cover the extracted full cut distribution.
    See [the integer Hadamard obstruction](semibent_eight_point_phase_obstruction.md).

72. **Very small invariant zero relations must vanish on all two-direction configurations.**
    For even `m`, an integer `SL_2` invariant of degree two in every
    row vector has a scalar specialization on each balanced cut.
    An exact zero at the integer data forces the corresponding block
    to divide that scalar times explicit small residues and correction
    factors. Below the recorded height threshold the scalar is zero.
    Invariance then gives vanishing on every configuration with at
    most two projective directions. This is an arithmetic restriction
    on exact zero relations, beyond generic nonzero-value estimates.
    Its kernel is nontrivial, and the note retains a quantitative
    pigeonhole argument showing why the restriction alone need not
    prevent very small numerical relations. For primitive rows the
    inside imaginary residues cancel completely, and the scalar's
    realness gives a divisor with the full block norm. The first
    smaller cuts leave squarefree, translation-invariant quadratics;
    actual pair residues exclude a single matching restriction but
    do not yet exclude sums. See
    [the invariant relation lemma and its scope](small_invariant_relations_at_balanced_cuts.md).

73. **The first smaller-cut modulus is explicit, and outside arithmetic alone permits new cancellation.**
    With six nonanchor rows, four outside coordinates give a real
    congruence between two matching products. After removing the
    recorded correction and common contents, its modulus is at
    least `N(H_S) exp(-12s) T^(-2)`. This excludes a nonzero
    single matching at sufficiently small coefficient height.
    A general restriction can instead have rank three. An exact
    fixed invariant has all twenty balanced specializations zero
    and all fifteen smaller specializations of rank three, so the
    finite exclusions do not exhaust the invariant kernel. For a
    genuine two-term restriction the associated cross-ratio has
    height `8w+o(w)`, while the new modulus has log size only
    `w-o(w)`; the direct comparison gives no positive saving.
    A separate exact four-row construction, reanchored from the
    rational five-point family, has bounded primitive residues
    and a fixed matching combination divisible by `n^2+1`.
    That growing divisor has only bounded overlap with every
    individual row and bracket. It is not realized as a new cut
    of an enlarged full-profile cluster. Both certificates and
    independent audits pass. See
    [the real congruences and cancellation example](near_balanced_invariant_congruences.md).

74. **The six-row invariant kernel has exact polar coordinates and a controlled height cycle.**
    Five integral matching coordinates satisfy the Segre cubic
    `Phi=BCE-AD(A+B+C+D+E)`. Its five gradients and the ten
    complementary triangle products span the same integer lattice,
    and this is precisely the balanced kernel in the quadratic
    matching-monomial lattice. Primewise upper and lower gcd bounds
    retain every central correction and pair residue. The primitive
    matching and gradient heights are `18w+o(w)` and `16w+o(w)`.
    The dual quartic has an exact inverse identity
    `grad J(grad Phi)=-4(product Delta_ij)(A,B,C,D,E)`.
    The forward common factor is supported on the twenty size-three
    cuts; the inverse common factor is supported on the thirty
    size-two and size-four cuts. The resulting height cycle is
    `18w -> 16w -> 18w`, returning the original projective point.
    All polynomial identities, integer-lattice indices, finite height
    constants, and cut minima were independently audited and checked.
    This identifies a joint arithmetic map, but the change of
    embedding alone gives no circle-radius descent. See
    [the exact Segre gradient arithmetic](segre_gradient_arithmetic.md).

75. **The standard duality loop preserves moduli, and Richelot need not preserve rational configurations.**
    The dual coordinates represent the same six projective-line
    points embedded on a conic. Standard duality, its inverse, and
    the outer-permutation dictionary supply no new six-point moduli.
    A Richelot operation does change moduli, but an exact example
    starting from `0,1,2,3,4,5` defeats every choice of pairing:
    one of the fifteen is degenerate, and each of the other fourteen
    has a Galois automorphism fixing four output points and swapping
    two. Its output therefore has an irrational projective cross-ratio
    and cannot be transformed into a rational six-tuple. This is a
    failure of automatic closure for the proposed operation, not an
    assertion about every special endpoint input or every joint map.
    The finite determinant, resultant, squareclass, and Galois checks
    pass. See [the symmetry and rationality audit](segre_igusa_symmetry_scope.md).

76. **A new joint rational involution preserves an ordered arc but necessarily loses endpoint scale.**
    A quadratic deck operation on the Igusa quartic induces the exact
    quartic Segre map
    `(-AFUG,-BUGV,CUGV,-DFGV,-EF^3)`. It is an involution on its
    stated open domain and changes six-point moduli: an exact example
    excludes all 120 possible normalizations of the original set.
    The five auxiliary linear forms have ten signed pair identities.
    Their complete local-content audit includes six actual exceptions
    to the generic gcd, and proves the output matching-height bounds
    `42w-o(w) <= h_out <= 48w+o(w)`, compared with the original `18w`.
    Five multiplicatively independent projective characters preserve
    their rational heights. These facts exclude preservation of the
    full nearuniform profile with negligible corrections and residues.
    See [the exact involution](joint_segre_involution.md) and
    [the actual height and unit audit](joint_involution_unit_arithmetic.md).

    One of the two opposite arc orderings always gives `F<0`, for which
    the new points lie inside the original first-to-fourth subarc.
    Thus an arc-preserving version exists without a spacing condition.
    This is proved by exact signs and order, with the excluded equality
    ruled out by the full-profile unit height. The Gaussian lifts have
    explicit degree-seven formulas and raw moduli `exp(64w+o(w))`.
    Their actual angular width and matching height first imply
    `log R_out>=30w-o(w)`. An additional matching-content audit
    now rules out the apparent remaining descent range. Five cuts
    give an actual common Gaussian chord factor of size
    `exp(6.5w-o(w))` when the old anchor is retained. More strongly,
    eight directly analyzed cuts and their eight complements give
    size `exp(8w-o(w))` for the six transformed points alone.
    The complementary-cut symmetry is an exact Gaussian reflection;
    the local proofs retain arbitrary cancellation depths, prime
    powers, and both orientation correction errors.

    Combining this actual common content with the matching height
    proves `R_out>=R_in^(49/48-o(1))` for the arc-preserving choice,
    even after dropping the old anchor and allowing common rotation.
    Every labeling of the specified pullback fixing three old rows
    has normalized output arc length at least `exp(w/3-o(w))`.
    Thus this joint-map candidate cannot supply an endpoint descent.
    Subsequent arbitrary projective changes and other maps are not
    covered. No general point-count growth improvement follows.
    The certificates and independent proof audits pass. See
    [the exact arc containment](joint_involution_real_arc_control.md),
    [the Gaussian conductor calculation](joint_circle_conductor_lift.md),
    [the actual versus generic matching content](joint_circle_matching_content.md),
    and [the complete standalone inflation theorem](joint_involution_standalone_inflation.md).

77. **Complementary cuts double the small-relation threshold, but the full relation lattice remains compatible with it.**
    In the actual degree-two invariant system, the two coprime norm
    moduli attached to a balanced cut and its complement divide the
    same integer coefficient. An exact relation outside the balanced
    kernel therefore has coefficient height at least `2w-o(w)`.
    The balanced evaluation map has exact rank
    `s=binomial(m,m/2)/2`, proved by a positive-definite matching
    incidence Gram matrix. The full and restricted primitive
    evaluation heights are `A_m w+o(w)` and `(A_m-2s)w+o(w)`, where
    `A_m=m 2^(m-2)-(m/2)binomial(m,m/2)`.
    The unconditional successive-minima estimate only guarantees an
    outside relation at coefficient exponent `A_m/s>2` for `m>=6`;
    the separate four-row case is exactly critical.

    An explicit CRT construction using the actual balanced matrix
    realizes both heights, all complementary congruences, and a first
    outside relation of size `exp(2w+O_m(1))`. This is a model of
    the linear arithmetic constraints, not a circle configuration.
    It shows why quotient covolumes and many short relations alone
    do not supply the missing contradiction. Fixed-depth higher-jet
    kernels are also quantified, without asserting that actual small
    relations satisfy the stronger jet conditions. See
    [the exact coefficient, rank, and lattice audit](invariant_relation_lattice_threshold.md).
    [The row-degree comparison](invariant_degree_variation.md) also
    proves that degree two gives the smallest of these guaranteed
    exponents among equal positive row degrees for `m>=6`. The
    specified unequal four-row families remain exactly critical;
    arbitrary unequal degrees are not excluded.

78. **A Pfaffian identity gives exact all-prime real-part content, including a positive occupancy formula.**
    For the twenty-eight primitive pair numerators `x_ij+i t_ij`, put
    `X=product |x_ij|`, `T=product |t_ij|`, and let `L_X` be the
    least common multiple of the 105 perfect-matching products of
    real parts. Schur's identity proves `B_X=X/L_X | T`.
    At every odd prime, the exact difference
    `v_p(T)-v_p(B_X)` is a sum of
    `binomial(|n_c-n_(-c)|,2)` over opposite residue classes and
    depths, within each conductor allocation group. The same formula
    holds at two using residues modulo `2^(l+1)` at depth `l`.
    Nested maximum matchings retain arbitrary prime powers.

    A lower bound `2log B_X>=W_4-B` on endpoint clusters would suffice
    for the intrinsic eight-point target, but is unproved. An actual
    integer-circle family with fixed within-group angular span has
    growing balanced mass and globally bounded `B_X`; it excludes
    an inference from circle arithmetic alone and is not an endpoint
    counterexample. Nearly equal products of pair sums have exact
    common factor `Gamma_0 delta`, with `delta|B_X|T`. Their small
    differences give an upper bound on `delta`, not the needed lower
    bound. Higher fixed linear cancellation in that degree-four
    space still leaves the original matching-height exponent. See
    [the Pfaffian content and short-arc audit](eight_point_pfaffian_content.md).

79. **Reciprocal chords produce a positive integer detecting a balanced cut, with its denominator cost retained.**
    For two ordered groups of four points, clear the 24 cross-matching
    denominators primitively. The resulting positive permanent
    numerator `N` and nonzero determinant numerator `K` are integers.
    If `X_sep` is the conductor factor whose layers separate these
    groups, then `gcd(N,X_sep)=1`, `N>=X_sep+24`, and the reduced
    denominator of `N/K` is divisible by `X_sep^6`.
    The exact determinant identity retains a quotient of the actual
    primitive chord residues; it is not legitimate to discard that
    quotient and assert divisibility by its entire conductor factor.

    In a full fair inherited profile, `log N=log K=(29/64)W+o(W)`,
    while `log X_sep=W/128+o(W)`. The new positive lower bound is
    therefore compatible with the available height. Averaging the
    Cauchy conductor calculation gives only the old quadratic defect;
    Borchardt's identity introduces `N` without identifying it as an
    old residue product. All statements were checked on actual
    Gaussian integer circles with arbitrary-depth proofs. See
    [the exact reciprocal-chord identities](reciprocal_chord_content.md).

80. **The near-constant sum kernel has an exact large denominator, even at the prime two.**
    Normalize the symmetric kernel to
    `S_ij=sec((theta_i-theta_j)/2)`, with diagonal entries one.
    Every permutation product is positive rational. Its common
    denominator over all permutations is exactly `L_X^2`, proved
    by the opposite-residue bipartite graphs and permutations that
    transpose positive-weight matching edges while fixing the other
    vertices. This avoids cancellation from unwanted norm factors.
    The real deviation `per(S)-8!` is strictly positive and `O(Theta^2)`,
    but its termwise denominator has logarithm `14W+o(W)` in a fair
    inherited profile.

    More generally, subtract the positive Taylor polynomial through
    any fixed total degree `d`. The resulting remainder has logarithm
    `-(d+1)W/2+o(W)`. Clearing every permutation product and every
    Taylor monomial separately costs at least
    `max(14,127d/128)W+o(W)`. The factor `127/128` uses the actual
    primitive radius after removing the two constant inherited cuts.
    The resulting positive integer has logarithm at least
    `(13/2)W+o(W)` for every integer `d>=0`.
    Thus these Taylor orders do not force an integer below one.
    The reduced denominator of the final summed remainder may be
    smaller; that possible arithmetic cancellation is not excluded.
    All 40,320 permutation products were checked on each of three
    actual Gaussian examples. See
    [the exact sum-kernel denominator budget](sum_kernel_denominator_budget.md).

81. **Simultaneous smaller-cut congruences exclude two independent small six-row relations.**
    For two actual numerical zero invariants in the five-dimensional
    balanced kernel, their two restriction equations at an inside
    pair have the same primitive cross-ratio values and the same
    modulus. Eliminating those values makes the determinant of their
    two coefficient rows divisible by a real modulus of size at least
    `exp((1-eta)w-12sigma) T_max^(-2)`, where `T_max` bounds each
    primitive pair residue. The fifteen restriction determinants
    determine the exterior product: an explicit ten-by-ten minor
    has determinant `-2`.

    Consequently independent relations satisfy
    `log C_Q+log C_R >= (1-eta)w-12sigma-2log T_max`.
    At coefficient height below `w/2-o(w)`, the space of exact
    relations has dimension at most one. The complementary-divisor
    bound automatically puts such relations in the balanced kernel.
    This rules out the earlier CRT model, which had three independent
    constant-coefficient relations there. It is an additional actual
    compatibility constraint, not a conclusion from its two heights.
    The remaining six-row Minkowski estimate only guarantees a second
    kernel relation at exponent `16/3`, so no count improvement follows
    yet. The proof, finite losses, and coefficient matrix were
    independently audited. See
    [the two-small-relations theorem](two_small_invariant_relations.md).

    An exact complement reflection strengthens this further. The
    integral rows `Z/P_i`, with `Z=(product K_i)(product H_S)`,
    become primitive after division by positive integer content.
    A common trim `H_S/gcd(H_S,bar(product K_i))` retains the
    complementary core with explicit correction losses. Every
    invariant zero keeps its original coefficients, and each
    primitive pair numerator is conjugated. Applying the smaller-cut
    argument again gives a second, coprime divisor of the same
    restriction determinant. For six rows the stronger bound is
    `log C_Q+log C_R >= 2(1-eta)w-156sigma-4log T_max`.
    Hence all exact relations below coefficient height `w-o(w)`
    span a space of dimension at most one. The proof covers reflected
    rows with zero imaginary coordinate and charges every removed
    core factor. See
    [the complement-reflection theorem](complement_reflection_invariant_relations.md).

    For general even row count, an integer adjugate gives the same
    modulus divisibility for all maximal minors of the first-smaller
    restriction matrix. At thirty rows, Minkowski supplies 104
    independent short numerical relations whose images are proper at
    every such cut. The common restriction kernel and possible common
    factors prevent converting this into a contradiction. See
    [the general rank comparison](smaller_cut_relation_rank.md).

82. **Final sum-kernel denominators can cancel at primes absent from every old residue.**
    Actual primitive, common-unit eight-point circles have
    `v_17(D_sum)=4e` and `v_17(T)=0` for arbitrarily large `e`,
    while their reduced permanent and every fixed Taylor remainder
    are integral at seventeen. The construction lifts a simple zero
    of a complementary six-row permanent. Conversely, an isolated
    pole has an exact valuation formula until that complementary
    coefficient reaches the next pole order, and four disjoint pole
    pairs give a unique leading permanent term with no cancellation.
    The examples have fixed positive angular span and growing
    primitive radius. They exclude primewise residue-only control,
    not a global height estimate or an endpoint bound. See
    [the exact local cancellation construction](reduced_sum_kernel_cancellation.md).

    The Pfaffian--Hafnian identity yields another exact rational
    normalization. After removing the quadratic factor `sqrt(O)`,
    the matching terms have exact common denominator `L_X`, and
    their positive numerator `K` satisfies
    `L_X^2 Pf((t/x)S)/sqrt(O)=(T_signed/B_X)K`.
    Its fair-profile height is `27W/4+o(W)`, leaving no small-integer
    contradiction. A separate actual family at nineteen has
    `v_19(L_X)=e`, `19` dividing no old residue, and a reduced
    Hafnian square with no nineteen in its denominator. Three or
    more pole pairs instead give a proved no-cancellation case when
    the prime divides no residue. All prime-power constructions and
    normalizations were checked. See
    [the Pfaffian--Hafnian arithmetic](pfaffian_hafnian_arithmetic.md).

83. **A shrinking-arc family retains bounded pair residues while reduced Taylor denominators grow.**
    An explicit Pell sequence gives Gaussian pencils
    `B_j=G+j(1-i)bar(G)` with
    `Im(B_j bar(B_l))=l-j`. Every primitive pair residue is therefore
    bounded by `l-j`. The least-common-multiple construction gives
    actual primitive circles with `R asymp_m d^(m/2)` and angular
    width `Theta asymp_m d^(-1)`, where `d=N(G)` tends to infinity.
    Selecting every second row keeps one fixed primary unit class
    without changing these exponents.

    The reduced denominator of each fixed positive Taylor remainder
    grows at least as `d^(2(h+1))`, despite a pair-residue product
    bounded in terms of the cardinality alone. The three-point case
    lies in endpoint arcs of arbitrarily small fixed constant; the
    four-point normalized constant stays bounded; for every `m>4`
    it grows as `d^(m/4-1)`. Thus no general residue-only denominator
    bound can be inferred even from shrinking angles. This does not
    refute an eight-point endpoint estimate or the uniform bound.
    The complete radius and integer identities were independently
    audited and checked on 54 primitive circles. See
    [the shrinking bounded-residue construction](shrinking_arcs_with_bounded_pair_residues.md).

84. **The restriction hierarchy extends to all depths and has a sharp finite endpoint.**
    Let `K_k` impose zero restrictions when at least `m/2-k+1`
    rows collapse. The next restrictions are squarefree translation-
    invariant polynomials of degree `2k` on `n=m/2+k` variables.
    Their dimension is `t=binomial(n,2k)-binomial(n,2k-1)` when
    `3k<=m/2`, and zero otherwise. The squarefree derivative/raising
    commutator proves `K_(floor(m/6)+1)=0`. Products of disjoint
    triangle invariants and squared brackets show that the index
    is sharp for every even row count.

    An integral ballot-matching basis extends the actual maximal-
    minor modulus to every level. Complement reflection gives
    logarithmic modulus at least
    `2(1-eta)w-2m(2m+1)sigma-4k log T_max`.
    Basis conversion costs a constant depending only on `m,k`.
    Thus sufficiently short numerical relations already in `K_k`
    have proper next restriction images. This does not put them
    in `K_(k+1)`; that induction step remains unproved. The complete
    algebra and prime-power losses were independently audited.
    See [the all-cut hierarchy](all_cut_invariant_relation_hierarchy.md).

85. **Common isometries cannot amplify a fixed restriction beyond its two complementary blocks.**
    Signed Gaussian valuations remove arbitrary rational row content
    and any common rotation height. For the same labelled directions,
    a new block at a fixed nonempty proper set `S` satisfies
    `log N(H_S') <= log N(H_S)+log N(H_(S^c))+2m(sigma+sigma')`.
    The corresponding least-common-multiple bound retains the two
    old block weights only once and sums the new correction costs.
    Repeated reanchoring and reflection therefore cannot increase
    the leading modulus past `2w` while their total corrections
    remain `o(w)`.

    Permuting the full configuration and replacing the active pivot
    by the old anchor changes a numerical invariant relation. An
    exact four-row example changes its value from zero to sixteen.
    Ordinary relabeling instead moves the restriction determinant
    and its prime support together. High-height nonisometric maps
    remain outside this exclusion. See
    [the fixed-relation symmetry audit](reanchoring_relation_moduli.md).

86. **Actual short numerical-zero subspaces can have deficient first-smaller images.**
    Multiplying every relation on `m-3` remaining rows by a fixed
    nonzero triangle gives an actual zero subspace of dimension
    `r_(m-3)-1`; every first-smaller restriction image has dimension
    at most `m/2-2`. The projected block weight is `8w`, and an
    odd-row Hamilton-cycle calculation gives primitive evaluation
    height `8 A_(m-3)w+o(w)`.

    At forty rows, successive minima already force 189 independent
    relations inside this subspace below the doubled coefficient
    threshold `2w/189`, although every restriction image has rank
    at most eighteen. This is conditional on the actual full profile,
    not an endpoint construction. An exact eight-row example verifies
    the same algebraic phenomenon. Therefore the actual evaluation
    hyperplane and shortness alone do not repair a first-layer global
    rank argument. See
    [the height-sensitive relation-space obstruction](actual_relation_subspace_obstruction.md).

87. **Irreducible factor descent preserves shortness and amplifies inherited block weights.**
    Every numerical zero invariant of row degrees at most two has
    an irreducible multihomogeneous invariant zero factor, with
    coefficient sum at most `2^(3^m-1)` times the original sum.
    Passing to its `s` supported rows preserves the numerators,
    corrections, and primitive pair residues; each nonempty cut
    weight becomes `2^(m-s)w`. The common full-support block is
    retained explicitly.

    Irreducible zero factors on four rows reduce to degree one in
    each row, giving coefficient-height lower bound
    `2^(m-3)(1-eta)w-8sigma`. Smaller supports are impossible at
    distinct directions. An explicit absolutely irreducible five-
    cycle combination nevertheless has a fixed actual rational zero;
    its ten-row multiples have proper first-smaller images. Thus
    factorization provides a valid descent step and excludes small
    supports, but needs a further arithmetic theorem from five rows
    onward. See [minimal-support descent](minimal_support_invariant_descent.md).

88. **Five-row boundary heights have an exact arithmetic interpretation, with no degree-ratio gap.**
    The twenty-two degree-two bracket graphs span the six-dimensional
    anticanonical system on the split degree-five del Pezzo surface.
    For each pair boundary, the gcd of graph values containing that
    edge, divided by the global gcd, has logarithm
    `log n_S+log n_(S^c)+O(beta)`. The basepoint-free residual linear
    system accounts for the archimedean term as well. Consequently
    the actual primitive invariant height is `10w+o(w)` and each
    boundary divisor height is `2w+o(w)`, with explicit finite losses.

    A smooth anticanonical section is an elliptic curve; its embedding
    divisor has degree five and each boundary has degree one. Those
    degree ratios exactly match the arithmetic weights. The earlier
    binomial five-cycle relation is a special smooth pencil with five
    paired boundary points forming a five-torsion orbit. Its ratio of
    two graph monomials already has height `10w+o(w)`, excluding fixed
    or negligible-height coefficients in that special pencil. The
    displayed interior example is two-torsion and supplies no rank
    assertion. See [the five-row arithmetic dictionary](five_row_del_pezzo_arithmetic.md).

89. **A fixed rational elliptic section realizes disjoint boundary contacts at the critical heights.**
    On `E:y^2=x^3-2`, the point `P=(3,5)` has infinite order. Blowing
    up `O,P,3P,7P` gives a smooth anticanonical section with ten distinct
    boundary points indexed by
    `{0,1,3,7,-1,-3,-7,-4,-8,-10}` times `P`. At `NP`, its height is
    `(5N^2+22N+121) hhat(P)+O(1)`, while each boundary height is
    `(N-k)^2 hhat(P)+O(1)`.

    An arithmetic progression controls all fixed bad-prime contacts;
    a real compactness subsequence controls the archimedean terms.
    The remaining ten intersection ideals are pairwise coprime and
    have logarithmic norms `H/5+O(sqrt(H))`, including prime powers.
    Thus these proportions are realized by actual rational moduli
    points on a fixed irreducible zero curve, with bounded coefficient
    height. The ideals may contain inert primes and do not supply the
    two separate Gaussian orientations or a small-correction chart.
    See [the elliptic height compatibility theorem](five_row_elliptic_height_compatibility.md).

90. **CM symmetry supplies independent split-prime elliptic denominator blocks, with an explicit rationality gap.**
    On `E:y^2=x^3-2x`, `P=(2,2)`, the points `[n+i]P` over `Q(i)`
    have no denominator at an odd inert prime: Frobenius and its
    conjugate would force `2P=O` modulo that prime, which is impossible.
    The ramified denominator depth is at most two. An explicit bound
    on the complex x-coordinate gives denominator norm height
    `2(n^2+1) hhat(P)+O(1)` without an elliptic-logarithm estimate.

    Same-orientation and conjugate gcds for finitely many shifted
    indices divide fixed denominator ideals. Bounded trimming gives
    independent Gaussian integers, supported only on odd split primes,
    of equal leading norm height. These are genuine elliptic arithmetic
    factors, but their moving point is nonrational. Taking the rational
    trace introduces inert denominators; an exact example introduces
    both three and seven. Translating the descent datum changes which
    boundary points are rational and restores the ordinary rational
    denominator problem.

    For the fixed rational test in item 89, a positive lower limit of
    total inert denominator weight divided by `N^2` remains unproved.
    Ordinary primitive-divisor existence does not supply its splitting
    type or required mass. See [the CM norm construction and rational gap](elliptic_split_inert_norm_route.md).

91. **Odd-support restrictions give a five-row pair-rigidity theorem.**
    On `m=2q+1` rows, the successive restrictions have degree `2k+1`
    in `q+k+1` squarefree outside variables. Their hierarchy terminates
    sharply at `K_(floor((m-3)/6)+1)=0`. On five rows the first
    restriction is linear on three outside rows. Complementary
    Gaussian moduli force small pairs of numerical-zero sections to
    have proportional restrictions on all ten boundary lines.

    Proper zero factors are excluded with an explicit coefficient
    cost `F_5=242 log 2`. Two remaining independent irreducible
    anticanonical curves would share at least five boundary points
    and their given interior point, contradicting intersection number
    five. Consequently
    `log C_Q+log C_R >=2(1-eta)w-110sigma-2log T-F_5`.
    There can be at most one sufficiently small five-row relation;
    this does not exclude that one relation. The finite rank and
    incidence checker and the arithmetic/geometric proof have been
    audited separately. See [odd-support rigidity](odd_support_relation_rigidity.md).

92. **Rational CM contacts can have negligible inert mass and no dominant prime power.**
    On `y^2=x^3-2x`, `P=(2,2)`, every fixed finite shift set admits
    `N_j->infinity` for which all ordinary denominators of
    `(N_j-k)P` have full quadratic logarithmic height, while their
    total inert-prime weight is `o(N_j^2)`. The proof decomposes
    denominator ideals by Boolean inversion over the Gaussian prime
    divisors of a product of rational split primes. Inert primes
    occupy only conjugation-stable cells, whose total proportion is
    at most `product_(q|m)(1-2/q+2/q^2)`, tending to zero.
    Disjoint auxiliary moduli, CRT, and a real compact subsequence
    handle all fixed shifts simultaneously.

    The largest cell and the largest individual prime-power weight
    can also be made `o(N_j^2)`. Whole conjugate cell pairs therefore
    give balanced independent Gaussian allocations for both
    complementary cuts of each rational boundary contact. This
    removes a universal positive-inert-mass obstruction even while
    preserving rationality. The particular non-CM-for-`Q(i)` test in
    item 89 remains a separate question. Recovering the same rational
    moduli point and small primitive residues from these allocations
    is not proved. See [the rational CM theorem](rational_cm_inert_mass.md).

93. **A common median rotation isolates a small three-row integer frame.**
    For any three selected odd conjugate-primitive rows, the Gaussian
    gcd `g=gcd_G(D_23 P_1,D_13 P_2)` realizes the median of their
    signed valuations at every split prime. Rotation by `1/g` and
    ordinary primitive normalization makes those three rows pairwise
    Gaussian-coprime and preserves every primitive pair residue.
    They can then be written `Q_i=U v_i`, `U in SL_2(Z)`, with the
    first three `||v_i||_infinity<=2T`.

    In a full `m`-row profile, put `A_m=2^(m-3)`. The matrix `U`
    and all outside frame vectors have logarithmic height
    `A_m w+o(w)`; two outside vectors have determinant of
    logarithmic size `2A_m w+o(w)`. Explicit finite error bounds
    and 2,500 exact six-row checks support the normal form.
    Applying its large unimodular matrix changes the circle metric,
    so this is not a radius-decreasing operation. See
    [the median rotation theorem](median_rotation_integer_frame.md).

94. **The CM denominator phase has an exact elliptic-function law.**
    For `Q_n=(n+i)P`, Gaussian denominator generators satisfy
    `gamma_(N-l)/gamma_N=epsilon gamma_(-l) f_l(NP)`, where
    `gamma_n=beta_n/bar(beta_n)`, `epsilon` is a Gaussian unit,
    and `f_l` is a fixed ratio of conjugate chord lines. The odd
    local intersection calculation includes its base-section
    correction. Norm one eliminates any residual valuation at the
    unique ramified prime, so no uncontrolled bad-prime factor
    remains. Fixed-target elliptic logarithm bounds exclude bounded
    corrections to this family. Their direct moving-target
    dependence does not suffice for arbitrary `o(N^2)` correction
    heights. See [the phase law](cm_denominator_phase_lift.md) and
    [its independent audit](cm_denominator_phase_lift_audit.md).

95. **Combined phase equations force positive residue growth in every fixed CM shift family.**
    Assign distinct fixed integer shifts `k_b` to the Boolean blocks.
    The common function field of the row phase ratios is birational
    to the elliptic curve unless every nontrivial complementary pair
    has the same sum `k_b+k_(bar b)`. This follows from their primitive
    divisor valuation vectors: a common map has degree at most two;
    a genus-one double cover is impossible, and a genus-zero double
    cover is exactly the constant-sum reflection case.

    Both cases contain a rational function `u` defined over `Q` of
    degree two: `x` in the birational case, or the secant slope
    through `-CP` in the constant-sum case. Thus
    `h(u(NP))=2 hhat(P)N^2+O(N)`. Exponentially close correction
    targets of height `o(N^2)` satisfy the fixed image equations
    exactly by the product formula. Applying the rational expression
    for `u` yields a Gaussian rational target of height `o(N^2)`.
    Its distance from the rational `u(NP)` is at least
    `exp(-2 hhat(P)N^2-o(N^2))`, by the nonzero Gaussian numerator.
    Finitely many exceptional image values are handled by the
    fixed-target elliptic-logarithm theorem.

    Comparing with the exact pair-numerator exponent proves, for
    fixed `m>=3` and arbitrary distinct fixed shifts,
    `liminf log max_(i<j)|t_ij|/N^2 >=(2^(m-1)-2) hhat(P)>0`,
    even for moving corrections of height `o(N^2)`. The symmetric
    binary ordering is included. This closes the moving-correction
    gap for the whole specified family. Its least lattice radius is
    exactly `|lcm_G(P_i)|/|gcd_G(P_i)|`, and the normalized angular
    span grows at least as
    `exp(((2^m-6)/2) hhat(P)N^2-o(N^2))`. Thus the original
    `m` points themselves cannot form fixed-`C` endpoint arcs.
    The radius proof retains the full prime powers and arbitrary
    common Gaussian rotation. This does not cover arbitrary
    extracted profiles, varying phase maps, or the independent
    rational-contact allocations in item 92. See
    [the collective phase theorem](cm_denominator_phase_lift_audit.md).

96. **The common five-point lift is an oriented congruence and norm system.**
    In the median frame write the complex columns of `U` as `z,w`.
    Then `bar(z)w=B+i`, `A=N(z)`, `C=N(w)`, and `AC-B^2=1`.
    Each row satisfies the actual oriented equation
    `bar(z)Q_i=X_i+i s_i=A r_i+(B+i)s_i`, hence
    `X_i^2+s_i^2=A N(Q_i)` and `X_i=B s_i mod A`.
    Two Gaussian barycentric identities retain the prescribed
    rational cross-ratios and the integral row scales.

    The ten median-oriented contact divisors impose homogeneous
    congruences on `(z,w)` in a rank-two Gaussian lattice of
    logarithmic index `20w+o(w)`. The required vector has coordinate
    height `4w+o(w)` and satisfies `Im(bar(z)w)=1`, together with
    the barycentric and exact block equations. Its small box volume
    alone is insufficient: abstract contact lattices of arbitrarily
    large index can contain a fixed vector representing one. The
    remaining condition must use the shared five-row moduli and
    full factorization. Median core trimming and the Hermitian
    discriminant are explicitly accounted for. See
    [the exact common-lift system](five_point_cm_norm_lift.md).

97. **Whole rational CM cells have a birational collective phase field.**
    For fixed auxiliary products, Boolean inversion of the CM
    kernel divisors gives effective primitive-torsion divisors.
    The difference of a nonstable divisor and its conjugate is
    principal. Its normalized function describes the cell-generator
    phase, with a fixed-prime correction of height `O(log N)`.
    This retains all prime-power intersection depths.

    Assign all nonstable cells at each of at least two distinct
    rational contacts to distinct complementary cut pairs. The
    collective row-phase functions generate the full elliptic
    function field. A rational image is excluded by incompatible
    Abel sums of fibers in different torsion cosets. A genus-one
    kernel is trivial because the nonstable torsion supports have
    no nonzero translation stabilizer and the contact multipliers
    have gcd one. This yields a simultaneous approximation
    obstruction at precision better than the rational x-coordinate
    height, for those specified functions.

    All cells must be used as whole cells, the auxiliary products
    are fixed, and every additional phase contribution must be
    described or have negligible height. In particular the ten
    peripheral five-row blocks cannot be absorbed as small
    corrections. The theorem supplies no uniform constants along
    the growing-auxiliary construction in item 92. See
    [the cell-phase theorem and its scope](rational_cm_cell_phase_field.md).

98. **The CM exclusion survives slowly varying shift parameters.**
    For fixed `m>=3`, the residue exponent in item 95 remains valid
    for arbitrary distinct integer shifts satisfying
    `max_b |k_b(N)|<=N^(1/2-epsilon)`, with fixed `epsilon>0`.
    Corrections may still have any logarithmic height `o(N^2)`.
    Function degrees remain bounded and coefficient, trimming, and
    phase-constant heights are `O_m(1+max|k_b|^2)`.

    Elimination is performed anew after specialization, with bounded
    matrices and nonzero pivots chosen at the actual ranks; affine
    and homogenizing-variable saturation remove extraneous
    components. This controls the image equations and rational
    coordinate expression uniformly. A fixed secant function on
    `E x E` gives the required height upper bound even when the
    reflection center moves. Generic targets are excluded by the
    Gaussian numerator argument. Moving denominator-zero exceptions
    have bounded degree and height `O_m(1+max|k_b|^2)`, and the
    audited elliptic-logarithm cost is `o(N^2)` in the stated range.

    The positive normalized-arc growth exponents persist as well.
    The argument does not cover arbitrary shifts of size `o(N)`,
    growing function degrees, varying curves, or arbitrary
    extracted Gaussian profiles. See
    [the slowly varying shift theorem](cm_slow_shift_phase_exclusion.md).

99. **The five-point lifting equations retain five equally sized residual factors.**
    The ten median contact clusters give row products `J_i` with
    three factors in each anchor row and seven in each outside row.
    Writing `Q_i=J_i R_i` leaves `log|R_i|=w+o(w)` for all five
    rows. The anchor equation is
    `Delta J_1R_1-dJ_2R_2+bJ_3R_3=0`; two further barycentric
    equations retain the outside rows, orientations, and integral
    scales. Full-depth congruences and the common norm equations
    are recorded with their actual coefficient coprimalities.
    All displayed norm comparisons remain height-balanced.

    For the CM section with centers `O,P,3P,7P`, the normalized
    pencil coordinates and all ten stable-boundary labels now have
    an exact rational certificate. This is a coordinate calculation,
    not a point-count estimate. See [the grouped lift](five_point_cm_norm_lift.md)
    and [the explicit moduli chart](m0_5_cm_coordinates.md).

100. **Every admissible contact lattice admits an integral frame, but a short frame is rigid.**
    For primitive real contact vectors and pairwise conjugate-coprime
    odd Gaussian contact moduli `G_e`, local `SL_2` matrices, CRT,
    and integral elementary matrices produce a common frame with
    `q(z,w)=Im(bar(z)w)=1`. This preserves the shared rational
    moduli and their barycentric relations. Under a stated outside
    distinctness hypothesis, all ten clean contact depths can also
    be made exact. Neither construction bounds the lift height or
    the unassigned prime factors.

    Put `Delta=product G_e`, `D=N(Delta)`, and normalize
    `Delta=1 mod 2`. Any vector `x` with `q(x)=1` gives the
    integral lattice basis `x,(x+Delta bar(x))/2`; the matrix of
    `2q` in this basis is `[[2,1],[1,(1-D)/2]]`. Thus the abstract
    integral Hermitian class supplies no further obstruction.
    However, `Delta` divides the determinant of every pair of
    lattice vectors. At five-row height `4w+o(w)`, there is at
    most one frame up to a Gaussian unit; every other frame has
    height at least `6w-o(w)`. Two short allocations on the same
    rational contacts must differ on at least `4w-o(w)` of full
    oriented prime-power norm weight. The corresponding formulas
    for any fixed number of rows, including optional private
    factors, are recorded. This proves uniqueness, not nonexistence.
    See [the contact-lattice theorem](oriented_contact_lattice_rigidity.md).

101. **The remaining five-row shear is one exceptionally small CRT representative.**
    Once a coordinate-primitive first column `z=J_1R_1` is fixed,
    every determinant-one partner is `w_0+t z`, `t in Z`.
    The grouped contacts give one class `t=tau mod M`, with
    `log M=14w+o(w)`. The exact fourth-contact overlap is
    `C_4=gcd_G(G_45,s_4z)=gcd_G(G_45,z^2)`; its norm costs only
    `o(w)` for a full-profile first column. No whole prime is
    discarded. With `A=N(z)`, reduced `e=Re(bar(z)w_0)`, and
    `rho=min_k |tau+kM+e/A|`, the shortest partner satisfies
    `min|w|^2=A rho^2+1/A`. The required frame therefore needs
    `rho<=exp(o(w))`. No lower bound excluding that event is proved.

    Changing the median anchor triple changes the primitive source
    model by a rational projective matrix of height at least
    `exp(4w-o(w))`; it does not supply a second short frame in the
    same lattice. The relative determinant and the correction
    overlap are retained in [the shortest-lift reduction](contact_lattice_shortest_lift.md).

102. **There are at most two sufficiently short frames across all orientations of fixed rational data.**
    Fix primitive rational contact vectors and disjoint odd split
    contact norms of product `D`. For two determinant-one frames,
    put `u=det_C(x,x')`, `v=det_C(x,bar(x'))`. Then
    `N(v)=N(u)+4`, and the full agreeing and flipped prime powers
    imply `D | a(a+4)`, `a=N(u)`. The quotient is a Gaussian norm,
    not necessarily a square or a fixed Pell parameter.

    The stronger constant theorem is: if `D>H^6`, there are at
    most two Gaussian-unit classes of frames of Euclidean norm
    at most `H`, allowing every Gaussian orientation. Every frame
    gives a positive integral Gram form `F=U^tU` with determinant
    one. Every three coefficient rows have determinant divisible
    by `D` and bounded by `H^6`; hence all forms lie in one
    two-dimensional linear space. Diagonalization confines them
    to one parameter interval of length at most
    `2 arcosh(H^2/2)`. The coupled determinant separates distinct
    parameters by more than `arcosh(H^2/2)`, excluding three.

    For fixed `m`, the full-profile heights satisfy the hypothesis
    for `m>=4` when private paired norms are fixed too, and for
    `m>=6` using shared contacts alone. An exact two-frame example
    shows sharpness for general fixed contact systems. Rational
    source vectors and norms must remain fixed within the counted
    set; this is not a count of original circle points. See
    [the constant frame-multiplicity theorem](coupled_orientation_frame_packing.md).

103. **The first Gram lift has an exact Gaussian quotient and an explicit obstruction target.**
    Let `Gamma` be the lattice of integral symmetric binary forms
    satisfying all rational contact congruences. Given a first
    frame `U=(z w)` and `F=U^tU`, the map
    `Psi_F(G)=a w^2-2bzw+c z^2` has kernel `Z F` and image
    `Z+2iZ`. Contact membership is exactly `Delta | Psi_F(G)`,
    where `N(Delta)=D`. With `T=tr(F^(-1)G)`,
    `T^2-N(Psi_F(G))=4det(G)`; parity and integral reconstruction
    are explicit. Every positive integral determinant-one Gram
    solution corresponds to an actual admissible frame.

    An independent `G in Gamma` must satisfy
    `||G||_F >= sqrt(D)/||U||_F^2`. Thus a nonzero indefinite or
    rank-one form below `sqrt(D)/H^2` would exclude the first
    frame of height `H`. The natural products of source linear
    forms, multiplied by the full missing contact factors, exceed
    this threshold. Their private and shared-only costs, including
    every prime-power exponent, are audited separately. See
    [the exact primal-dual Gram audit](primal_dual_gram_contact_audit.md).

104. **Balanced fixed elliptic six-curves require singular five-point projections.**
    Suppose a smooth genus-one curve maps birationally into
    `bar(M)_(0,6)` and every one of its twenty-five boundary
    pullbacks has the same positive degree `d`. Each forgetful
    image is a curve `Gamma_j ~ delta_j(-K)` on the degree-five
    del Pezzo surface, with covering degree `r_j` satisfying
    `r_j delta_j=2d`. Its arithmetic genus is
    `1+5delta_j(delta_j-1)/2`, and its normalization genus is
    `g_j in {0,1}`. The singularity delta-invariants therefore
    sum to `1+5delta_j(delta_j-1)/2-g_j`.

    At most two of the six images are smooth: three smooth
    projections would be even-degree elliptic isogenies whose
    kernel sums contain a common nonzero two-torsion translation
    fixing every moduli coordinate. For `d=1`, even singular
    anticanonical images number at most three. Degree-two deck
    involutions first give a four-element cap in `F_2^3` as the
    only possible larger case. That reflection cap forces four
    fixed points to specialize to the same stable boundary,
    contradicting boundary degree one. Consequently at least
    three projections must be birational `|2(-K)|` images with
    genus-one normalization and singularity delta-invariant five.

    A further common-branch argument excludes three singular
    anticanonical images. Their three reflection involutions would
    give degree-two rational maps with distinct double poles and
    the same values at `0,1,infinity`. Interpolation makes each
    triple-collision equation quadratic in the pole parameter;
    three distinct poles cannot solve it. The derivative version
    also excludes a nested triple collision at an anchor. Thus
    if three anticanonical projections occur, exactly one is
    smooth elliptic and two are singular rational. The proof
    includes ramification and coincident boundary-support points.

    This rules out further extensions of the smooth five-row
    elliptic construction. No theorem places arbitrary extracted
    profiles on such a fixed curve, or excludes the remaining
    singular projections. See [the elliptic forgetful obstruction](six_row_elliptic_forgetful_obstruction.md).

105. **The remaining degree-one elliptic six-curve question is an exact septic incidence problem.**
    In the Kapranov model, boundary degree one forces a degree-seven
    map to `P^3`. The five point-center ideals have pullback length
    one; the ten connecting-line ideals have pullback length
    exactly three. The additional line contact may be tangency at
    an endpoint. These conditions, together with avoidance of the
    boundary planes, are also sufficient for all twenty-five
    boundary degrees to equal one. No containing quadric is
    possible, since its restriction to each connecting line would
    have three zeros and the six lines among four frame points
    already kill every quadratic coefficient.

    Equivalently, on a smooth elliptic curve choose a degree-seven
    line bundle and four generating sections. Every pencil
    vanishing at two frame points must have fixed divisor of
    degree exactly three. An explicit four-section interpolation
    enforces the six lines among four centers and leaves four
    common-zero conditions for the fifth center. Expected
    dimension does not establish a solution in the required open
    set. An independent exact cubic-surface calculation produces
    embedded genus-one septics, but does not impose these ten
    contacts. See [the Kapranov criterion](six_row_elliptic_kapranov_septic.md)
    and [the cubic-surface class audit](cubic_surface_septic_class_audit.md).

106. **Higher-degree contact jets have an exact quotient and an optimized product barrier.**
    For an actual unimodular frame `U`, let `Q_U` be its positive
    integral Gram polynomial. Evaluation of a degree-`d` form at
    `(w_0,-z)` has integral kernel `Q_U S_(d-2)` and image `Z[i]`.
    For the lattice `Gamma_(d,h)` defined by membership in every
    contact ideal `(d_e,L_e)^h`, with `d>=h>=1`, the exact quotient is
    `Gamma_(d,h)/(Q_U Gamma_(d-2,h-1)) = (Delta^h)`.
    This includes full prime-power contact depths. A form outside
    the Gram kernel therefore has coefficient norm at least
    `D^(h/2)/||U||_F^d`.
    The full lattice's determinant-volume guarantee remains above
    this threshold for every `d>=h`; it does not itself force a
    smaller vector outside the Gram kernel.

    For a canonical source product with row multiplicities `n_i`,
    supplying each missing contact by its rational norm, the exact
    logarithmic excess above that threshold is
    `sum_C |sum_(i in C)n_i-h| * w + o(w)`. Convex symmetrization
    reduces its minimum to two real weights, giving a computable
    positive constant `h c_m`; in particular `c_m>=1`, and
    `c_4,...,c_9 = 1,3,7,15,31,61`. Coherently oriented products
    also retain this gap under nonnegative integer combinations.
    Arbitrary signed cancellation and reductions of the specified
    norm multipliers remain outside the theorem.

    As the row count grows, `c_m` has order
    `2^(m-3)/sqrt(m-3)`. This shrinking relative gap does not supply
    a form below the threshold, and all profile errors here fix
    row count, degree and contact order first. Exact checks cover
    twenty-one contact-jet lattices, including prime-power depth
    two, and 450 weighted source profiles. See [the higher-degree
    jet audit](higher_degree_gram_jet_barrier.md).

107. **Signed source products recover the full contact-jet lattice up to small anchor factors.**
    Let `Lambda_(d,h)` be the integer span of all canonical weighted
    degree-`d` source products, and let `delta` be the least common
    multiple of the three nonzero anchor determinants. Then
    `delta^d Gamma_(d,h) subset Lambda_(d,h) subset Gamma_(d,h)`.
    The proof works at full prime-power depth, including additional
    shallow collisions among outside rows. Since `delta<=T^3`, the
    index is subpower for every fixed degree. Away from the contact
    norms its exact local exponent is
    `d(d+1)v_p(g)/2`, where `g` is the gcd of all source determinants.

    In particular, signed products represent
    `delta^(2h) Q_U^h`, so substantial cancellation into the Gram
