    kernel really occurs. Saturation does not bound representation
    heights or produce a small form outside that kernel. The exact
    covolume after orthogonal projection off the kernel is
    `D^h/J_d`, with
    `J_d=sqrt(H^(4d)-(H^4-4)^d)/2` and `H=||U||_F`.
    Its geometric-mean scale still exceeds the required threshold
    by a factor of order `H`. See [the saturation theorem](signed_source_product_saturation.md)
    and [the exact Smith defect](prime_to_D_smith_saturation_audit.md).

108. **The mixed elliptic case exists, but repeated boundary support gives an arithmetic obstruction.**
    The three rational maps
    `f_lambda(x)=(1+2lambda)x(x-1)/(1+lambda x)`, at
    `lambda=3,-57/121,-9/25`, have branch pairs
    `{u,v},{u,s},{v,t}` for four distinct rational values. Their
    connected degree-eight fiber product is an elliptic curve,
    birational onto a six-point moduli curve with all twenty-five
    boundary degrees one. Exactly one forgetful image is smooth
    anticanonical, two are singular rational anticanonical, and
    three are birational images in `|2(-K)|`. Its quotient by the
    rational translation group of order four is isomorphic to
    `y^2=x(x+405)(x-35)`. The point `(45,450)` has infinite order:
    reduction counts 20 and 24 at 13 and 17 force all rational
    torsion to be the four rational two-torsion points.

    This first example has twenty-five boundary incidences at only
    nineteen source points. Six pairs of distinct boundary divisors
    pull back to the same effective point. Equal fixed Cartier
    pullbacks force their exact finite contact contents to have
    gcd comparable to either content, including at bad primes.
    On the smooth five-point quotient, the previously proved
    arithmetic dictionary instead bounds that gcd by the square
    of the primitive-residue product. Thus this fixed example
    cannot carry a full independent profile with subpower residues.
    The conclusion needs no elliptic approximation theorem. See
    [the explicit curve](mixed_elliptic_six_curve_example.md),
    [its independent audit](mixed_elliptic_six_curve_independent_audit.md),
    and [the contact-overlap obstruction](mixed_elliptic_six_curve_contact_overlap.md).

109. **A second elliptic six-curve realizes all shared integer contacts with bounded determinant remainders.**
    The pencil
    `f_lambda=(x^2+lambda(-60-73x))/(x-1+lambda(x^2-11x-38))`,
    at `lambda=0,-240/5329,8/257`, has four distinct common
    arguments with four distinct target values. After one common
    projective normalization, its connected genus-one fiber
    product maps birationally to six-point moduli, meeting each
    of the twenty-five boundaries transversely at a different
    rational point. This avoids the obstruction in item 108.
    Independent checks verify the complete boundary support,
    ramification, complementary inverse roots and contact orders.

    The source has positive rational rank. Its translation quotient
    has the exact quartic
    `Y^2=T(67144321T-212248804)(T-4)(46513T-208624)`.
    Retaining its nonsquare leading coefficient, good reductions
    have 28 and 40 points at 23 and 37, forcing rational torsion
    to be the four two-torsion points. With a branch point as
    origin, `(-1/2,45299439/4)` is an explicit non-torsion point.

    For a fixed non-torsion point `P` on the source, simultaneous
    recurrence at the real place and finitely many bad primes
    supplies infinitely many positive `N` for which actual contact
    integers `d_C(N)` are pairwise coprime and have
    `log d_C(N)=N^2 hat h(P)+O(N)`. Primitive integer rows for
    `infinity,0,1,a,b,c` then satisfy the exact factorization
    `|det(v_i,v_j)|=b_ij product_(C containing {i,j})d_C`,
    with bounded positive integers `b_ij`. The logarithmic moving
    row and moving-pair sizes are respectively `4N^2 hat h(P)`
    and `8N^2 hat h(P)`, up to `O(N)`. Thus the shared rational
    source pattern and its expected heights really occur.

    These integer contacts may contain inert primes. Gaussian
    orientations, the six private factors, the original Gaussian
    primitive residues and a first short determinant-one frame
    are still missing. This is neither a lattice-arc construction
    nor a uniform point-count theorem. See [the disjoint curve](disjoint_mixed_elliptic_six_curve.md),
    [its independent audit](disjoint_mixed_elliptic_six_curve_independent_audit.md),
    and [the integer contact-profile theorem](disjoint_mixed_elliptic_integer_contact_profile.md).

110. **Gaussian CM denominator splitting extends to arbitrary finite rational contacts.**
    The earlier finite-shift construction no longer requires every
    contact to belong to one cyclic subgroup. For pairwise coprime
    auxiliary integers `m_e`, CRT coefficients give a rational
    `Q_0` with `Q_0-B_e=[m_e]S_e` simultaneously in `E(Q)`.
    Along `Q(n)=[Mn]P+Q_0`, compact recurrence bounds every omitted
    local term of the finitely many translated CM isogenies.
    Boolean denominator cells and diagonalization then give
    `log b(Q_j-B_e)=H_j+o(H_j)`, with inert-prime mass and the
    largest prime-power mass both `o(H_j)`. Whole conjugate cell
    pairs supply any fixed balanced Gaussian allocations.
    An independent audit verifies all height factors and the
    stage-dependent errors. This applies to any fixed finite set
    of reduced rational contacts on a positive-rank Gaussian CM
    elliptic curve. It does not identify the six-curve of item 109
    as such a curve or supply a compatible Gaussian frame.
    See [the arbitrary-contact theorem](cm_arbitrary_rational_contact_splitting.md)
    and [its audit](cm_arbitrary_rational_contact_splitting_audit.md).

111. **The disjoint elliptic first-frame problem has four fixed norm directions.**
    Grouping its twenty-five contacts gives pairwise coprime
    `D_inf,D_0,D_1,D_rho` of logarithmic weights `7,7,7,4` times
    `h=N^2 hat h(P)`. Across all Gaussian orientations, shared
    congruences for a determinant-one frame `(z,w)` are exactly
    divisibility of `N(z),N(w),N(z+w),N(-3z+2w)` by those groups.
    Writing those norms as `A,C,K,L`, one has
    `L=15A+10C-6K` and `4AC-(K-A-C)^2=4`.
    At the required frame height `exp(4h+o(h))`, the four residual
    norm factors have logarithmic upper budgets `1,1,1,4` times
    `h`. Conversely, positive solutions with the parity condition
    give an integral determinant-one Gram form and hence a frame.
    This is an exact remaining Diophantine system, not an exclusion.

    A separate application of Siegel's theorem shows that any
    hypothetical infinite family of these integral frames escapes
    every fixed algebraic curve in `E times SL_2`. Thus the existing
    pointwise bound of two candidates does not justify extraction
    onto a fixed finite algebraic cover. Exact rational source
    configurations from two odd multiples are also available.
    See [the four-norm reduction](disjoint_elliptic_first_frame_barrier.md)
    and [the explicit configurations](disjoint_mixed_elliptic_explicit_configs.md).

    Completing each group to its full elliptic target fiber supplies
    the four linear forms `3X-16Y,2X+Y,2X-9Y,4X-25Y`, up to fixed
    rational factors on a suitable subsequence. The missing contents
    have degrees `1,1,1,4`. Dividing the norm residuals by these
    contents gives rational coefficients of heights at most
    `h,h,h,4h`, respectively, in an exact Pell-type system.
    A Gaussian norm section has even order at every rational point,
    so a norm section of degree eight cannot contain any of the
    degree-seven anchor contact divisors. This rules out that
    specific section construction; higher-degree norms and moving
    arithmetic frames remain possible. See [the complete-fiber identities](disjoint_elliptic_boolean_fiber_identities.md).

112. **Seven-row balance imposes new genus and symmetry restrictions.**
    For `m` geometrically independent rational quadratic covers
    of a common projective line, the branch-pair graph is a forest.
    If it has `c` components, Riemann--Hurwitz gives
    `g=1+2^(m-2)(m+c-4)`. Four covers therefore have genus at least
    five. On a balanced degree-one curve in `Mbar_(0,m+3)`, each
    normalized coordinate has degree `2^(m-1)`, so a common
    quadratic quotient automatically forces that independence.
    Consequently the six-row common-quotient construction cannot
    extend to a balanced degree-one elliptic seven-curve.

    Without assuming a common quotient, a balanced degree-one
    genus-one curve in `Mbar_(0,n)`, `n>=7`, has at most three
    single-label forgetful maps of degree two. Pairwise deck
    involutions commute because double-forgetful degree divides
    four; four of them would be independent after normalizing
    three other anchors, contradicting the rank-three bound for
    elementary two-subgroups of elliptic automorphisms. At least
    `n-3` forgetful maps are therefore birational. At seven rows,
    three involutions yield `(2,2)` correspondences, not the
    common quadratic maps needed for the genus obstruction.
    The proof passed an independent audit. It leaves general
    elliptic seven-curves, varying higher-genus families, and the
    global uniform bound unresolved. See [the seven-row theorems](seven_row_quadratic_quotient_obstruction.md).

113. **A fixed rational frame has a quantitative height obstruction even with small denominator and divisibility errors.**
    Let `z=a+ib,w=c+id` be fixed rational functions on the disjoint
    elliptic source, with `ad-bc=1`. Allow a common integer
    denominator `q_N` and contact-divisibility errors `e_B(N)`
    with logarithms `o(h_N)`, where `h_N=N^2 hat h(P)`.
    A bounded resultant argument at all primes shows that a full
    contact cannot divide the cleared norm of its prescribed
    combination unless that rational norm vanishes at the contact
    point. Rational leading coefficients then force both real
    components to vanish. Determinant one forces a pole in a
    complementary combination at each of the twenty-five contacts.

    Thus the common pole divisor of `a,b,c,d` has degree at least
    twenty-five. The projective frame map `[1:a:b:c:d]` has height
    at least `25h_N+O(N)`, contradicting the short-frame upper bound
    `4h_N+o(h_N)` after denominator clearing. Independent review
    checked the all-prime bound, norm orders, degree and height
    normalization. This excludes fixed rational formulas even
    with the stated varying errors; the underlying rational map
    itself must be fixed. It does not exclude arbitrary moving
    frames or prove uniformity. See [the fixed-frame theorem](fixed_rational_frame_contact_height.md).

114. **Bounded-degree frame formulas may move if their coefficients remain subpower.**
    The previous obstruction extends to rational matrix maps whose
    presentation degrees are bounded by one fixed `D` and whose
    coefficient heights `H_N` are `o(h_N)`. Coefficient height must
    be measured jointly for numerator and denominator, retaining
    their relative scale. Local jets at the fixed rational contacts
    give resultant errors `O_D(H_N+1)`, without assuming unique
    factorization in the elliptic coordinate ring. They again force
    a common pole divisor of degree at least twenty-five.

    An independent constructive height lemma supplies the missing
    uniform comparison. If `Phi=[1:f_1:...:f_4]` has pole-divisor
    degree `d`, bounded presentation degree and coefficient height
    `H`, then
    `|h(Phi(Q))-d hat h(Q)|`
    is at most
    `C_(E,D)(sqrt(hat h(Q)(H+1))+H+1)`.
    The proof bounds the pole points, translates their divisor into
    `|d[O]|`, constructs the principalizing section by bounded jet
    linear algebra, and controls projection constants by a fixed
    embedded-curve Nullstellensatz. Thus the frame height is at
    least `25h_N-o(h_N)`, contradicting `4h_N+o(h_N)` even when
    the bounded-degree rational formulas vary.

    The same proof permits varying degrees `D_N` when a combined
    degree-dependent constant satisfies
    `C(D_N)^2(H_N+1)=o(h_N)`. This states the required complexity
    control; it supplies no bound for arbitrary growing degrees.

    This is not an extraction theorem for arbitrary frames. No
    argument shows that their presentation degrees and coefficient
    heights satisfy the hypotheses. See [the moving-frame exclusion](moving_bounded_degree_frame_contact_height.md)
    and [the independent uniform height lemma](moving_frame_uniform_height_lemma.md).

115. **Contact anisotropy gives a degree obstruction without rational contacts.**
    On any smooth projective geometrically integral curve over a
    characteristic-zero field where `-1` is nonsquare, let `Delta`
    be a determinant-one frame's common pole divisor, of degree
    `delta`. For each fixed ground-field direction, the two
    conjugate isotropic sections have zero-divisor sum
    `2Delta+div(norm)`, interpreted after constant base change.
    A prescribed norm-zero contact of multiplicity `m` costs at
    least `m` section-zero degrees if its residue field contains
    `i`, and at least `4ceil(m/2)` otherwise. In the latter case,
    determinant one also forces a pole of order `ceil(m/2)`.
    Such anisotropic contacts for distinct directions cannot
    overlap. For reduced contacts of total degree `D` and
    anisotropic degree `A`, this gives `D+3A<=2r delta` and
    `A<=delta`, where `r` is the number of directions.

    In particular effective contact divisors of degrees
    `7,7,7,4` in the four fixed norm directions force `delta>=5`.
    Each odd-degree divisor contributes at least three extra
    units, giving `34<=8delta`; reduction and disjointness are
    unnecessary. This repairs the degree-four obstruction even
    for nonrational source contacts, but converting degree into
    evaluated height still needs the fixed-map or controlled
    coefficient hypotheses above. The proof passed independent
    review. See [the contact-divisor theorem](conjugate_isotropic_contact_divisor_accounting.md).

116. **The doubled four-norm profile has an exact rational realization.**
    Put `f=-2+(t^4-t^3)/(t^7+1)` and
    `U=[[f,f-1],[1,1]]` on `P^1/Q`. This determinant-one frame has
    common pole degree seven. The first three norm zero divisors
    have degree fourteen; the fourth contains the degree-eight
    divisor `Z(t^8+1)`, by
    `(t^4-t^3)^2+(t^7+1)^2=(t^8+1)(t^6+1)`.
    All selected divisors are reduced, disjoint, defined over
    `Q`, and supported at closed points whose residue fields
    contain `i`. Seven is optimal since one norm's fourteen
    zeros already require `2delta>=14`.

    Thus the four norm-contact conditions alone allow the
    doubled profile `14,14,14,8` below the threshold `delta<=8`.
    This is an explicit limit on extending item 115, not a
    construction of the full source and cut profile or an
    integer lattice-arc counterexample. Independent exact
    polynomial, residue-field, and infinity checks passed.
    More precisely, the first three norm numerators are
    irreducible over `Q`, certified modulo `43,127,59`.
    Their degree-fourteen closed points cannot be divided
    into seven `Q`-defined degree-two cut contacts. This
    identifies an explicit missing refinement in the example.
    See [the construction and verifier](scaled_split_contact_profile_q2.md).

117. **Keeping both isotropic marks gives an exact toric-height formula.**
    For an integral frame with columns `z,w`, the primitive
    Gaussian rows `(-w,z)` and `(-bar(w),bar(z))` have determinant
    `-2i`. Their marked coordinate on a source row is
    `t_j=P_j/bar(P_j)`. In the independent block model, for any
    fixed exponent set `A` with coordinate sums zero,
    `h([t^a]_(a in A))`
    equals `1/2 sum_S log Norm(H_S) width_A(1_S)`.
    Integral corrections change this by at most a constant
    times the sum of their logarithmic sizes. Complementary
    cuts have equal widths; empty and full cuts disappear only
    when they really are common scaling of every retained mark.

    The finite and archimedean contact heights of the two marks
    also obey an exact balance. Conjugate tropical vectors
    cancel automatically, so these monomial heights provide
    the existing cut-weight information with no additional
    positive margin. Source-collision determinants remain
    available for non-toric arguments. See [the lifted contact
    and height dictionary](lifted_isotropic_mark_toric_heights.md).

118. **Individual doubled contacts force completely split fibers.**
    In the frame `U_f=[[f,f-1],[1,1]]`, seven separate reduced
    degree-two split contacts are seven distinct `Q(i)`-points
    in the corresponding oriented fiber. For `deg f<=8`, its
    remaining fiber degree is at most one, so the first three
    required fibers must split completely over `Q(i)`; degree
    eight cannot hide a nonsplit residual point. A monic integral
    polynomial has at most two `Q(i)`-points over `i`, by Gaussian
    integrality and two divided-difference identities. The bound
    is sharp and also excludes its fixed rational source Mobius
    reparametrizations. Rational-coefficient polynomials are not
    excluded: `(t^3+7t)/6` already has three such points.
    See [the individual-contact refinement](individual_split_contact_refinement_q2.md).

119. **The aggregate rational frame has a sharp denominator obstruction.**
    At every rational parameter `[a:b]` of primitive height `H`,
    excluding its pole, the frame in item 116 has reduced
    denominator at least `H^6/4`. Cancellation divides two, and
    its six nonreal poles supply six full powers of height.
    The sequence `[1-N:N]` attains order `7H^6`; the only integral
    specializations occur at `0,1,infinity`, all giving the same
    constant frame. No fiber has at most two support points.

    More generally, a fixed rational function admitting rational
    parameters of growing height with subheight denominators
    must have either one rational pole or two real quadratic
    conjugate poles of equal multiplicity. This follows from
    resultant cancellation bounds and Roth's theorem. Thus even
    a fixed rational target Mobius change cannot repair the
    degree-seven example. These are fixed-map exclusions, not
    a general arc bound. See [the exact specialization bound](scaled_frame_specialization_denominator.md)
    and [the pole classification](rational_parameter_quasi_integral_poles.md).
    Independent audits and exact gcd and ramification checks passed.

120. **Classical quasi-integrality simplifies the fixed elliptic-frame obstruction.**
    For any fixed nonconstant `f in Q(E)` and arbitrary rational
    points with canonical height `h_n` tending to infinity,
    `log den(f(Q_n))=(deg f)h_n+o(h_n)`. Lang's fixed-place
    approximation theorem gives `log+|f(Q_n)|=o(h_n)`; the exact
    rational denominator identity and elliptic height comparison
    give the conclusion. Hence subheight common denominators
    already exclude every fixed frame with a nonconstant entry,
    without contact or determinant assumptions. All-constant
    frames still require the unbounded contact moduli. This is
    an application of a classical theorem, not a new general
    approximation or endpoint theorem. See [the fixed-frame simplification](fixed_elliptic_frame_quasi_integrality.md).

121. **Moving elliptic frames also have a quantitative denominator obstruction.**
    Fix `E/Q`, presentation-degree bound `D`, and joint numerator
    and denominator coefficient height `H_n`. Along `nP`, with
    `P` nontorsion, the condition
    `(H_n+1)log(n+2)^6=o(n^2)` implies
    `log den(f_n(nP))=(deg f_n)n^2 hat h(P)+o(n^2)`.
    David's elliptic-logarithm theorem, including its moving-height
    parameter modification, controls all bounded-degree moving
    poles; a uniform section estimate controls the evaluations.
    For arbitrary `Q_n in E(Q)`, with `h_n=hat h(Q_n)` and fixed
    Mordell--Weil rank `r>=1`, the sufficient margin becomes
    `(H_n+1)log(h_n+2)^(r+5)=o(h_n)`.

    If all denominator-section zeros lie in one fixed number
    field, the weaker condition `H_n=o(h_n)` suffices: translation
    sends each moving pole to the fixed origin, where Lang's
    theorem applies over the same field. This latter consequence
    is non-effective. In either case a common clearing denominator
    for a fixed finite tuple is at least `exp(2h_n+o(h_n))` on
    indices with any nonconstant entry, even if that entry varies.
    No bounded-degree, controlled-height extraction from arbitrary
    circle arcs has been proved. See [the moving-map theorem and fixed-field corollary](moving_map_archimedean_denominator_exclusion.md).
    The proof and both extensions passed independent reviews;
    the primary David and Lang statements were inspected directly.

122. **Deleting points and clearing midpoint reflections do not supply a fixed-power descent.**
    If `m` points are retained from a primitive endpoint cluster,
    its newly exposed common-factor weight is exactly
    `gamma_S=2log(R/R_S)`. An obtuse sign-vector cohort of size
    `L>=ceil(m/(4ceil(C/2)))` gives `gamma_S<=2log R/L`.
    Combining this with item 54 shows that deletion of `O(1)`
    points followed by one rational projective change preserving
    fixed endpoint constants still satisfies
    `log R'>=(1-O(1/m))log R`. Iterated small losses are not excluded.
    See [the deletion-stability corollary](projective_orbit_radius_rigidity.md).

    Independently, adjoining the reflection of an actual primitive
    reconstructed cluster about any pair midpoint requires a
    Gaussian denominator that primitive normalization cannot remove.
    With core product modulus `P`, separating-block modulus `s_ij`,
    and corrections `K_i,K_j`, its resulting normalized arc constant
    is at least `2P/(s_ij |K_i K_j|)^(3/2)`. In the growing fair
    core this is `R^(1/4-o(1))`, uniformly over every pair.
    Thus this particular symmetrization cannot preserve the
    endpoint scale. It is not an exclusion of the original cluster.
    See [the reflection scaling obstruction](midpoint_reflection_scaling_obstruction.md).

123. **Primitive affine triangle data obey an exact radius divisibility.**
    For `m>=5` Gaussian-primitive circle points of norm `N=R^2`,
    let `D_I` be their integer triangle determinants,
    `g=gcd_I |D_I|`, and `p_I=D_I/g`. With
    `K=binom(m,3)` and
    `b_m=binom(floor(m/2),3)+binom(ceil(m/2),3)`, one has
    `N^b_m | product_I |p_I|`. The local proof retains common
    triangle content: with two valuation levels its exact
    contribution is the minimum repeated-level pair excess;
    with three levels some triangle has valuation zero.
    Thus `R<=H^(K/(2b_m))`, where `H=max_I |p_I|`.
    Five or six points give exponent five; the general exponent
    tends to two from above. The arc bound gives
    `g<=(C^3/8)R^gamma_m`, with `gamma_m=3/(2(m-1))`
    for even `m` and `3/(2m)` for odd `m`. This also bounds
    the index of the lattice generated by point differences.

    For a full independent set of affine relations of index `q`,
    complementary exterior minors are exactly `+/-q p_I`.
    Their Euclidean norm product is at least
    `q sqrt(K)R^(2b_m/K)`. The corresponding basis upper bound
    remains of order `sqrt(R)/g` with explicit rank-dependent
    factors. The existing quartic five-point family attains
    relation-lattice covolume `Theta(sqrt R)`, verified by its
    ten degree-four determinant polynomials and polynomial gcd
    one. These results constrain multiple relations but do not
    improve the general endpoint growth rate. See [the radius divisibility](affine_shape_radius_divisibility.md)
    and [the joint affine-relation audit](joint_affine_relation_lattice.md).

124. **Even fixed endpoint arcs can have radius cubic in affine-shape height.**
    For `T=600k`, five explicit Gaussian-primitive integer points
    have radius `sqrt(product_(a=1)^6(T^2+a^2))/720`, triangle
    content `g=T/15`, and primitive joint triangle height
    `H=25T^2/4+100`. Hence `R/H^3` tends to `4/703125` and
    `R/H^2` diverges. All five lie on arcs shorter than
    `5 sqrt(R)`; their normalized span tends to `2sqrt(5)`.
    The construction reverses a polynomial family with common
    third-order contact and checks every Gaussian denominator,
    triangle gcd, and coefficient identity exactly.
    Thus a universal quadratic affine-shape reconstruction
    bound is false even on a fixed endpoint arc. The example
    does not address sufficiently small arc constants, a
    growing number of points, or full-cut profiles. See [the family and explicit affine conic](five_point_affine_shape_cubic_family.md).
    Both new proofs and their exact checks passed independent reviews.

125. **The complete conic feature content has an exact affine formula.**
    After normalizing three points, all quadratic-feature minors are
    the base primitive triangle determinant times explicit cubic
    expressions in primitive triangle data. Their full common content
    and the left relation-lattice covolume can therefore be computed
    exactly, retaining the common integer factor and avoiding an
    erroneous extra metric factor. The resulting upper bound is
    `3 sqrt(binom(m-3,2)) C^9 R^(3/2)/(512g^3)`; no opposing lower
    bound gives a radius saving. Six-point conic compatibility becomes
    an identity in the actual half-angle brackets. These identities
    still matter for abstract triangle relaxations, but add no
    condition to a system already using those half-angle coordinates.
    The exact checker passed 105 integer circle configurations.
    See [the conic feature audit](affine_conic_feature_content_audit.md).

    A separate symmetric-coefficient audit retains the exact reflection
    `e_m conjugate(e_k)=R^(2k)e_(m-k)`. At each Gaussian prime, the
    excess valuation beyond the termwise minimum is paired exactly
    with the complementary coefficient's excess at the conjugate
    prime. The reflected coefficient magnitudes likewise repeat the
    lower coefficient data with explicit radius powers. These identities
    and the elementary short-arc error estimate yield no new saving;
    further simultaneous-cancellation input is not excluded. This is
    consistent with the existing angular-moment product-rigidity theorem,
    which first needs a separate cancellation argument. See [the coefficient audit](self_inversive_coefficient_audit.md).

126. **Five polynomial circle points cannot have primitive triangle degree one.**
    Over `Q(i)[t]`, every Gaussian-polynomial-primitive family of at
    least five distinct equal-norm points with nonconstant norm has
    some primitive triangle determinant of degree at least two.
    The radius divisibility from item 123 extends to polynomial UFDs.
    Primitivity makes the common norm have no real root, so it cannot
    divide a product of real polynomials of degree at most one.
    If the radius grows with polynomial degree `d` and every difference
    has degree at most `ell`, the exact circumradius identity gives
    `d<=3ell-2`. In particular degree five with quadratic differences
    is impossible; an independent Gram-content argument reaches the
    same conclusion. This restriction does not cover arbitrary integer
    sequences or exclude all higher-degree polynomial constructions.
    See [the polynomial affine-line obstruction](polynomial_affine_line_obstruction.md).

127. **Signed deformations of the six-factor family have an exact span obstruction.**
    All six coefficient choices with the same five subset sums have
    the form `(u,2u,v,u+v,2u+v,3u+v)`. Put `P=product a_r` and
    use the five products `w_j` from item 124. Two exact chord
    factorizations give, for the integral clearing `z_j=w_j/P`,
    `|z_1-z_4| |z_2-z_4|/R =
    8 sqrt((T^2+u^2)/(T^2+4u^2)) >=4`.
    This handles signs and all relative parameter degenerations
    without an asymptotic expansion. Before primitive normalization
    its normalized span is therefore at least two. Exact boundary
    shapes with `P=0` have at most three distinct rows.

    When `u,v,T` are integers, all six `a_r` are nonzero, and
    each `a_r` divides `T`, the literal factors `1+/-iT/a_r`
    have common Gaussian point content of norm at most 1600.
    A complete signed-support audit excludes all primes except
    the bounded contributions at two and five, including the
    rank-deficient covers. The primitive normalized span is
    consequently at least `1/sqrt(10)` throughout this family.
    Both the exact chord identity and common-content argument
    passed independent audits and the exact checker. General
    rational clearings outside these hypotheses remain open;
    this is not a five-point theorem for arbitrary circles.
    See [the signed-family and primitive-normalization proof](five_point_affine_shape_cubic_family.md).

128. **The six-factor obstruction now survives every rational common clearing.**
    The normalization gap left in item 127 is closed. For arbitrary
    integers `u,v,T` with `gcd(u,v,T)=1` and
    `P=2u^2 v(u+v)(2u+v)(3u+v)!=0`, let `G` be the Gaussian
    gcd of the five degree-six products `w_j`. Then
    `N(G)<=1600P^2`, without assuming any `a_r` divides `T`.
    Inert prime contributions charge directly to `P`; the ramified
    prime costs at most six extra Gaussian valuations. At split
    primes, the full signed-support classification reduces every
    boundary case to `u`, `u+v`, or `2u+v`; only the bounded
    mod-five exception remains away from those boundaries.
    Thus `|G|<=40|P|`, and the exact two-chord identity proves
    primitive normalized span at least `1/sqrt(10)`.

    Degree-six homogeneity and Gaussian Bezout uniqueness extend
    the result to every rational projective parameter triple and
    every common Gaussian rational clearing of this specific family.
    Exact boundary parameters have at most three distinct nonzero
    rows. The local proof and exhaustive finite cover certificate
    passed independent audits. This is a restriction on the full
    six-factor construction, not on arbitrary five-point circles.
    See [the complete primitive-content proof](six_factor_primitive_content_bound.md).

129. **Intrinsic chord stars and small-residue elimination retain the missing arithmetic.**
    For an actual same-unit triple with common Gaussian factor `G`
    and three isolating factors `A_0,A_1,A_2`, its two-chord star
    satisfies `d_01 d_02/R=4 |s_01 s_02| |G|/|A_0|`.
    In an actual eight-row full-cut construction with 127 independent
    blocks of log norm `w+O(1)`, every star's `G` contains 31 blocks
    and its center factor contains 32. All 168 content quotients
    therefore equal `exp(-w/2+O(1))`; multiplying stars preserves
    the deficit. This construction does not have verified small
    residues or an endpoint arc, so it is not a counterexample.

    Fixing all 28 signed residues and eliminating the shared
    contents gives quadrics
    `x_ij(x_i t_j-x_j t_i)=t_ij(x_i x_j+t_i t_j)`
    with small coefficient height. Their open compatibility variety
    is birational to affine seven-space, rather than a curve;
    the seven anchor real parts remain free. Integer quotients,
    positivity, conjugate-primitivity, and exact Gaussian gcds must
    still be imposed. These are the unproved height restrictions.
    See [the intrinsic star and elimination audit](intrinsic_star_content_audit.md).

    An ordered Ptolemy audit also retains the exact nonnegative
    `2log cosh(rho/2)` surplus. Four actual integer-circle points
    from `H_j=2(n+j)+i` have this surplus constant while their
    logarithmic radius grows. Their normalized span tends to 12;
    they do not test the small-constant eight-point target. No
    conductor-scale surplus follows from that example or from the
    pointwise gap identity alone. See [the consecutive Ptolemy audit](ordered_consecutive_ptolemy_nonlinear_audit.md).

130. **Fixed-family primitive content has an exact integral-closure criterion.**
    For nonzero fixed homogeneous Gaussian product rows `W_j` and a
    nonzero same-degree polynomial `P`, dehomogenize on every projective
    parameter chart. Then `P` belongs to the integral closure of the row
    ideal on every chart if and only if there is one fixed Gaussian
    integer `C!=0` such that `gcd_G(W_j(x))` divides `C P(x)` for
    every nondegenerate primitive ordinary integer parameter vector.
    Sufficiency follows from finitely many monic integral-dependence
    equations, with their coefficient denominators cleared once.
    Necessity uses a failed Rees divisor, a closed smooth point over a
    finite number field, and ordinary integer approximations to
    transverse p-adic points at one fixed completely split prime.
    The resulting local valuation defect is unbounded.

    This is a criterion for exact divisibility; a local defect alone
    does not prove that the Archimedean quotient `|G|/|P|` is unbounded.
    Coupled with an appropriate homogeneous chord-product lower bound,
    the sufficient direction proves a positive primitive arc constant
    for that fixed family. Item 128 is an instance, since its local proof
    gives `G | (1+i)^6 5 P`. No finite-family extraction from arbitrary
    endpoint clusters is asserted. See
    [the criterion and its specialization proof](fixed_factor_primitive_content_criterion.md).

131. **The integer cotangent system retains exact Gaussian gcds automatically.**
    Clear all anchor and pair residues using
    `L=lcm(|t_i|,|t_ij|)` and `X_i=L x_i/t_i`. The exact integer
    equations become `(X_i X_j+L^2)/(X_i-X_j) in Z`. For any such
    pair, with `delta=X-Y`, the actual Gaussian content is
    `N(gcd_G(X+iL,Y+iL))=|delta|d`, where
    `d=gcd((X^2+L^2)/delta,X,L,delta)` divides `L`. The reduced
    pair quotient has imaginary part of absolute value `L/d`.
    Thus restoring this particular gcd condition introduces no
    additional large-height restriction in the normalized system.

    A valuation-stratum argument gives at most `(p+1)p^e-1` finite
    coordinates for an inert odd prime with `e=v_p(L)`, and at most
    `4*2^e-1` at two. Odd `L` therefore permits at most three finite
    coordinates. The seven-clique `{-18,-6,-3,0,2,6,12}` at `L=6`
    attains the dyadic bound with `e=1`. These are bounds depending
    on `L`, not uniform endpoint bounds. Complementing all divisors
    relative to the smallest positive coordinate is an exact anchor
    reflection; it preserves the primitive radius and normalized arc.
    See [the gcd reduction](integer_cotangent_gcd_reduction.md) and
    [the local bounds](integer_cotangent_local_bounds.md).

132. **An all-pair ordinary lcm gives an equivalent integer height target.**
    Include anchor edge cotangents `Q_0i=X_i` and every pair quotient
    `Q_ij`. Reduce `Q_e/L=a_e/b_e`, and let `epsilon_e` be two when
    both coprime entries are odd, and one otherwise. Then the exact
    primitive squared radius is
    `N=lcm_e((a_e^2+b_e^2)/epsilon_e)`. At each split prime,
    primitivity makes the point allocation exponents attain both
    extremes, so the maximum pair denominator exponent recovers the
    complete radius exponent. Using only anchor edges can lose a
    conjugate orientation; an explicit example gives lcm 5 instead of 25.

    For positive finite coordinates with `A=min X_i`, the exact
    normalized span is `2 N^(1/4) arctan(L/A)`. The original uniform
    problem is equivalent to proving that there exist fixed `k,c>0`
    for which every `k`-coordinate integer clique with `X_i>=L` obeys
    `N>=c(A/L)^4`. This inequality remains unproved. The known
    four-point Pell family gives a fixed-`L=24` triple with
    `N` of order `V^6` and `(A/L)^4` of order `V^8`, so three
    finite coordinates cannot suffice. The specific six-factor
    five-point family satisfies the inequality with `c=1/1600`.
    Exact Gaussian arithmetic checked 13,599 pair quotients and
    1,863 cliques, including all reanchorings and three Pell instances.
    See [the lcm formula and equivalent target](integer_cotangent_lcm_height_target.md).

133. **The cotangent spectrum is fixed, and primitive eigenbasis determinants
    discard every conductor profile outside `2L`.**
    On all `n` labels, orient the integer cotangents consistently,
    put `s_i=sum_(j!=i)Q_ij`, and form the Gaussian integer matrix
    `B_ii=s_i`, `B_ij=Q_ij+iL`. Lagrange interpolation identifies it
    with a conjugate of `2iL z d/dz-iL(n-1)` on degree-below-`n`
    polynomials. Its eigenvalues are exactly `iL(2r-(n-1))`.
    All spectral projector denominators divide
    `(2iL)^(n-1)(n-1)!`. Primitive integral right and left
    eigenvectors have pairings dividing their spectral gap products,
    so their basis determinants are bounded in terms of `n,L`.

    This bound carries no good-prime conductor contribution. For
    `pi` not dividing `2L`, integer cotangents force
    `v_pi(r_i-r_j)=min(v_pi(r_i),v_pi(r_j))` for the rational nodes.
    Sorting these valuations as `e_1<=...<=e_n`, the raw eigenbasis
    determinant has valuation `-sum_i(n-i)e_i`, exactly the sum of
    its column contents. The determinant after primitive column
    normalization is therefore a unit at `pi`. This calculation
    includes arbitrary repeated, negative, and mixed valuation levels;
    it is not limited to fair two-level cuts.
    Local invertibility also shows that the left eigenbasis determinant,
    all primitive left/right pairings, and every spectral projector
    denominator have prime support contained in `2L`.

    Fixed eigenvalues and projector denominators do not control
    archimedean heights: the matrix satisfies
    `||B||_F^2-sum_r|lambda_r|^2=2sum_i s_i^2`, and even the
    two-label projectors have unbounded norm at fixed `L`. Arbitrarily
    many fixed labels also admit fixed-`L` unbounded-entry families,
    whose primitive radii grow too fast to be endpoint counterexamples.
    Exact arithmetic checked 12 actual circle cliques, their primitive
    left/right eigenvectors and determinant supports, and 1,281 ordered
    valuation profiles. See [the spectral identity and content audit](integer_cotangent_spectral_audit.md).

134. **Primitive spectral columns retain an exact allocation-height invariant.**
    For column `r` of the `n`-label cotangent eigenbasis, put `m=n-r-1`.
    Let `K_m` be the product, over split conductor primes, of the prime
    to the sum of the largest `m` allocation exponents minus the sum of
    the smallest `m`. Equivalently it is the modulus of the Gaussian
    lcm/gcd ratio of all `m`-coordinate products. If `S` is the Euclidean
    norm of the raw barycentric column, its primitive integral version
    satisfies exactly `||u_r||^2=S^2 d_r/K_m`, where
    `d_r` is a positive integer dividing `(2L)^(2(n-1))`.
    The two-sided local difference bound proves this at bad primes too.

    For `n=2h`, the central column is ordinary integral up to a Gaussian
    unit and satisfies `sum_i u_i z_i^j=0` for `0<=j<h`. Its good-prime
    coefficient valuation is half the excess absolute deviation of the
    point's allocation exponent above the median minimum. Balanced cuts
    disappear from these coefficients. On eight fair labels the minimum
    column log height is `38w+o(w)`, larger than the pair-cotangent height
    `32w+o(w)`; on six labels it is `7w+o(w)` versus `8w+o(w)`.
    Fixing the central coefficients gives a smooth one-dimensional
    moment locus on distinct nonzero nodes, but their actual coefficient
    height cannot be discarded. The expanded exact checker passes all
    12 cliques, and an independent audit recovers the four-point Pell
    coefficients `(15,1,-12,-4)`. See
    [the primitive column heights](integer_cotangent_eigenvector_heights.md).

135. **Universal circle coordinates have an exact polynomial-certificate obstruction.**
    Every fixed `k+1` rational circle tuple is represented, up to common
    Gaussian scaling, by `W_0=product(X_i-iL)` and
    `W_i=(X_i+iL)product_(j!=i)(X_j-iL)`. Common rational scaling makes
    every pair cotangent integral, so these coordinates have no
    fixed-family extraction gap. In variables `L,Y_i=X_i-iL`, the row
    ideal is the squarefree degree-`k` ideal omitting one variable.
    Every power is integrally closed. Its chartwise degree-`qk` sections
    have every monomial exponent at most `q`, hence `L`-order at most `q`.
    A balanced `G^q` chord certificate would require `L`-order at least
    `2q`; it therefore cannot exist, even as a finite menu. The ordinary
    integer positive-cone quantifiers and common denominator clearings
    are retained. Global proper birational changes with compatible line
    bundles and a common multiplier descend to the same obstruction.

    Absolute-value control remains different from exact divisibility.
    With the positive cotangents ordered `X_1<X_2<...<X_k`, the target
    `|G|<=C L^2 product_(i>=3)X_i` is equivalent to uniformity after
    allowing one extra finite cotangent. This norm bound implies (H)
    directly. Conversely, apply (H) to the subtuple deleting `X_1`,
    compare its all-edge lcm with the full lcm, and use
    `rho<=2^(k/2)product X_i`. The norm target fails for three finite
    cotangents by Pell and remains unproved for a larger fixed number.
    See [the universal obstruction and norm target](universal_circle_content_certificate_obstruction.md)
    and [the elementary normal-ideal proof](universal_cotangent_monomial_ideal.md).

136. **Mixed conjugate content certificates also fall short of the endpoint order.**
    Put `n=a+b>0`. A degree-`kn` polynomial chartwise integral over
    `I^a conjugate(I)^b` has coalescence order at most
    `floor(2n-n/2^(k-1))`, strictly below the required `2n`.
    In coordinates `t=2iL,y_i=X_i-iL`, the two ideals on `t=1` are
    generated by products omitting one of the factors `y_i` and `y_i+1`,
    respectively. At a Boolean vertex with `s` zero coordinates,
    integral closure requires multiplicity at least
    `a max(s-1,0)+b max(k-s-1,0)`. Summing over all `2^k` vertices and
    applying multiplicity Schwartz--Zippel proves the strict deficit.
    For `a=b=1,k>=2`, the exact maximum is three, attained by a Hermitian
    triangle area, so conjugation increases contact without reaching four.
    Arbitrarily many selected chords and finite menus give the same
    obstruction. This excludes the stated mixed exact-divisibility
    method, not the absolute norm target. See
    [the mixed content proof](mixed_cotangent_content_ideal.md).

137. **Fixed six-point central moments allow angular coalescence.**
    The elliptic curve `Y^2=X(X-3)(X-99)` has the nontorsion point
    `(1,14)`. Every positive multiple has square first coordinate, and
    odd multiples approach `(0,0)` along the bounded real oval. Writing
    `X=q^2,p=Y/(99-X)` yields six rational equal-radius points with
    primitive central vector `(5,-5,5,-5,-1,1)` and angular span tending
    to zero. This disproves an angular-height obstruction based solely
    on the size or alternating signs of the central integer vector.

    It is not an endpoint counterexample: the three conjugate pairs
    have equal products, so rectangle separation forces
    `Delta sqrt(R)>=2sqrt(2)` after the least primitive normalization.
    The unbalanced conductor mass satisfies
    `W_unbal<=2log(5)+15log(2L)`, including primes dividing `2L`.
    Thus this family cannot have the six-label full fair profile with
    `log L=o(w)`, whose unbalanced mass would be `21w+o(w)`.
    Exact arithmetic verifies 15 elliptic multiples, their central
    vectors, moments, contents, and independent all-edge least radii.
    See [the six-point family and conductor audit](six_point_fixed_moment_elliptic_obstruction.md).

138. **Six-point Witt conditions permit comparable pair squareclasses.**
    The rational vectors `1,Re(q),Im(q)` form a maximal totally isotropic
    space for `diag(u_i)`, so the central moment form must be hyperbolic
    over `Q`. Removing squared singleton factors leaves the pair-squareclass
    form `diag(epsilon_i product_(j!=i) B_ij)`. At a pair prime `B_ij`
    congruent to one modulo eight, its local condition is that the product
    of the eight adjacent edge labels be a quadratic residue modulo `B_ij`.
    Fifteen comparable prime labels can satisfy all these conditions:
    quadratic reciprocity gives an undirected residue-coloring, finite
    Ramsey gives a monochromatic clique, and the eight signs cancel.
    The two-adic and real forms are also hyperbolic; Hasse--Minkowski
    gives the rational conclusion. Fixed-modulus prime asymptotics put
    all labels in `[H,2H]` for every sufficiently large `H`.

    This is a squareclass compatibility result, not a full fair central
    vector: small singleton factors, `sum u_i=0`, the isotropic-basis
    height, and circle realization are still missing. An exact witness
    checks 15 comparable primes, all 105 mutual symbols, every local
    invariant, and 600 sign-sensitive edge formulas. See
    [the Witt and pair-squareclass audit](six_point_witt_pair_squareclass_obstruction.md).

    A separate local audit also prevents a false Vandermonde contradiction.
    At a good two-level cut with minority size `s<h`, precisely `n-s-1`
    consecutive moments survive on `n-s` majority unit nodes. Their
    rectangular matrix has a one-dimensional kernel with every cofactor
    a unit. The lower moments give the analogous minority kernel, and
    one boundary moment couples the two. Full local rank is compatible
    with the prescribed central valuations and gives no extra growth.
    See [the local central-moment reduction](local_central_moment_cut_reduction.md).

139. **Primitive triangle content has an explicit denominator bound.**
    For an integer cotangent clique with common denominator `L`, primitive
    Gaussian circle rows of squared radius `N`, and ordinary gcd `g` of
    their triangle determinants, the all-prime calculation proves
    `g | 4L^3` and `gcd(g,N) | L`. Raw anchored areas are exactly
    `4L^3 |X_i-X_j| product_(ell != i,j)(X_ell^2+L^2)`, whose gcd equals
    the Gaussian row-content norm times `g`. The exact universal-row
    content also yields a selected-pair divisor and proves the desired
    common-factor norm estimate when `|X_2-X_1| d_12=O(L^2)`, where
    `d_12|L`. Without that additional condition it recovers the cubic
    radius lower bound; the affine-shape exponents remain below four.
    The checker passes 790 cliques, including four Pell instances.
    See [the affine-content calculation](integer_cotangent_affine_content.md).

140. **The six-point pencil retains an exact degree-twenty primitive radius.**
    For a fixed rational central vector and a cleared hyperbolic frame,
    both complete isotropic rulings admit explicit Gaussian circle lifts
    on `d^2=Delta(s,t)`, with `Delta` homogeneous of degree twelve. The
    raw conic expression `K` is minus the product of ten quadratic
    triangle minors, one for each balanced `3|3` partition, hence has
    degree twenty. If `h=gcd(A,B,C)`, the Gaussian metric ideal has norm
    exactly `4|A|h`, including at two. Two further explicitly specified
    contents `e,f` give the least squared radius
    `N=|K|/[h Norm(e) Norm(f)]`; `Norm(e)|Delta` and `f|g_V` for the
    integer maximal-minor gcd `g_V`.

    With no vanishing proper central subsum, actual homogeneous Bezout
    constants bound every content valuation. For this FIXED frame,
    `N asymp H^20`, where `H=max(|s|,|t|)`. Near angular coalescence,
    `theta N^(1/4) asymp |d|/H`. Bounded endpoint scale therefore requires
    `d^2=Delta(s,t)` with `|d|=O(H)`. The constants still depend on the
    moving weights and frame. Two exact witnesses check the polynomial
    identities, least-radius formulas, and degree-twelve squarefreeness;
    another 1,770 cases check the metric and coefficient contents.
    See [the circle cover](six_point_isotropic_circle_cover.md) and
    [the exact radius formula](six_point_circle_cover_radius_content.md).

141. **Full fair central vectors avoid resonance, and their six-point covers have genus five.**
    A dominant prime cut supported on `T`, with `|T|<h` among `2h` labels,
    makes the central coefficients on `T` have larger valuations than
    every coefficient outside it. Thus no sum over `T` and one further
    label can vanish. The proof retains the errors
    `(2h-1)v_p(2L)+4h epsilon_p` from normalization and approximate cut
    allocations. Independent fair blocks with subpower private factors
    and `log L=o(w)` provide the needed dominating primes by summing
    valuation mass. This excludes every vanishing proper central subsum.

    At a nonsingular parabolic parameter, affine coordinates put the
    six columns at `(t_i,t_i^2)`. Their weighted moments `S_0,...,S_4`
    vanish, while `S_5!=0`. Differentiating conic incidence along the
    isotropic ruling gives `Delta'=-12/S_5`, after the specified local
    normalization. Every branch is therefore simple. Consequently both
    degree-twelve covers have genus exactly five whenever the central
    vector has no vanishing proper subsum, including an eventual full
    fair six-core. This controls the type of curve, not its moving
    arithmetic heights. Exact checks cover 2,016 central valuation
    cases, 1,303 subsum witnesses, 4,000 allocation perturbations, and
    102 parabolic branch derivatives. See
    [the prime-cut separation](central_subsum_cut_separation.md) and
    [the simple-branch proof](six_point_simple_branch_genus.md).

142. **Repeated opposite coefficients force an actual reflection symmetry.**
    For six distinct unit-circle nodes with weights
    `(a,-a,a,-a,b,-b)`, nonzero real `a,b`, and moments of orders zero,
    one and two vanishing, all six nodes form three reflection pairs.
    Rotate the last pair to conjugate points. The real parts of the
    first and second moments force equal sums and squared sums of the
    real coordinates in the two remaining pairs. Equal real parts of
    distinct unit-circle points force conjugacy. Thus three pair
    products coincide, with no restriction on `b/a` or on the original
    angular width. The integer-circle rectangle theorem gives
    `theta sqrt(R)>=2 sqrt(2)` on a minor arc. A single opposite
    coefficient pair does not suffice: the exact cotangent example
    `(2,3,5,12,17)` has central vector
    `(126,-7,50,-169,841,-841)` and all 21 unordered pair products,
    including squares, distinct. Thirty rational reflection cases
    and this scope counterexample pass. See
    [the reflection theorem](six_point_repeated_weight_reflection.md).

143. **The moment curves have an exact fixed-residue interpretation.**
    For `2h` nonzero normalized nodes the positive and negative central
    moments are equivalent to
    `sum_i u_i dz/(z-q_i)=kappa z^(h-1) dz/product_i(z-q_i)`.
    This is a fixed-residue curve with two ordered zeros of order
    `h-1` and `2h` labeled simple poles. A primary-source check of
    Chen--Gendron--Prado--Tahar's 2026 revision independently agrees
    with the two genus-five components at six labels. The paper's
    period-residue convention differs by `2pi i` from coefficient
    residues and is retained explicitly. For integral central weights,
    `F=product q_i^u_i` is a rational function and its logarithmic
    derivative is the relative-period differential up to sign and
    the stated scaling. Integer residue periods do not make arbitrary
    points' relative positions integral. See
    [the exact dictionary and source](central_moments_isoresidual_dictionary.md).

144. **The radius divisor yields an explicit Belyi period map.**
    The same nonresonance condition makes `K` squarefree: at a two-line
    degeneration the tangent of its vanishing triangle minor pairs
    nontrivially with `(u_i x_i)` on the collinear triple. Different
    balanced partitions have disjoint roots. Thus `K` has twenty simple
    zeros, disjoint from the twelve simple roots of `Delta`.

    For integral central weights, `F=product q_i^u_i` has the exact
    differential `d log F=i kappa d^3(s dt-t ds)/K`, where the nonzero
    constant `kappa` comes directly from `beta(x,dy)`. This identity
    follows from quadratic isotropy, without a period-integrality
    assumption. Each of the twelve branch points maps to `F=1` with
    ramification index five. The forty lifts of the `K` roots have zero
    or pole orders equal to absolute balanced central subsums. Therefore
    `F` is Belyi, with exact degree
    `2 sum_(10 unordered balanced partitions I|Ic)|sum_(i in I)u_i|`.
    That degree grows with the weights. The conic tangency checker
    passes 120 exact cases. Separate exact factorization and Sturm
    counts show that the two displayed first-ruling branch polynomials
    are irreducible of degree twelve and have only two real roots each;
    they do not support an all-real-branch shortcut. See
    [the period-map proof](six_point_belyi_period_map.md).

    Its symmetric trace descends further: `G=(F+F^(-1))/2` and
    `J=(F-F^(-1))/(2i d)` belong to the rational base field `Q(r)` and
    satisfy `G^2+Delta J^2=1`. The rational map `G` has degree `D=deg F`.
    Its fiber over `1` has twelve points of index five and `(D-60)/2`
    points of index two; over `-1` there are `D/2` points of index two;
    its twenty poles have the balanced-subsum orders above. The full
    ramification count is `2D-2`. This is an exact rational Pell-type
    reformulation, not a uniform height bound or an identification of
    the underlying dessin with a particular graph.

145. **A controlled rational hyperbolic frame exists, with polynomial coefficient cost.**
    If `U=max|u_i|`, Cassels' small-zero theorem in dimensions four and
    two constructs two independent rational isotropic directions in the
    quotient orthogonal to `1`. Explicit lifts, Cramer duals, and the
    quadratic correction give a rational hyperbolic frame containing
    `1`, with cleared height at most `C_0 U^C`. The final denominators
    divide `2 delta^2`, for an actual nonzero three-by-three minor
    `delta`. The construction needs Cassels' theorem; inverting linear
    pivots alone does not produce these isotropic directions. The bound
    is polynomial in the moving coefficient height, not subpower in the
    fair-core scale. See
    [the frame-height proof](rational_hyperbolic_frame_polynomial_height.md).

    The homogeneous resultant constants are then bounded by fixed powers
    of `U`. Squarefreeness of `Delta K`, its nonzero integer discriminant,
    and Cauchy's root bound also give a polynomial lower bound for `|K|`
    on the allowed real parameter locus. Thus the actual controlled
    frame satisfies `U^(-C) H^20 <= N <= U^C H^20` for an absolute `C`.
    This radius comparison alone supplies no angular or rational-point
    height bound; item 146 adds the angular comparison. For the
    fair scales `log U=7w+o(w)` and `log(A/L)=8w+o(w)`, an additional
    endpoint-restricted estimate `A/L<=U^(c+o(1))` with `c<8/7` would
    suffice; it remains missing. See
    [the moving-radius corollary](six_point_moving_frame_radius_height.md).

    Two elementary candidate families also retain their denominator
    obstruction. For fixed-offset translates or fixed-ratio homotheties
    of five cotangents, indexed by a reduced rational `A=s/t` tending
    to infinity, homogeneous quartic lifts have uniformly bounded
    common content. The primitive central height is `asymp s^4`, and
    its ratio to the least cotangent is `asymp s^3 t=A^3 t^4`.
    This excludes those families only. See
    [the rational shift-and-scale audit](six_central_ratio_shift_scale_audit.md).

146. **The angular comparison is polynomial in the moving weights, and the trace has an exact polynomial Pell identity.**
    For `P_ij=A(dx)^2+B dx dy+C(dy)^2`, the normalized circle nodes obey
    the exact identity `|q_i-q_j|^2=Delta P_ij/K`. The raw and primitive
    integer edge versions retain the complete Gaussian contents.
    The integer form `sum P_ij^2` has no real zero where `Delta>=0`.
    Root separation for its squarefree part together with `Delta`
    bounds its minimum below by a fixed negative power of `U`.
    Consequently the controlled frame satisfies
    `U^(-a)|d|/H <= theta N^(1/4) <= U^a |d|/H` in the small-arc
    regime. Bounded endpoint scale therefore imposes the integer
    window `d^2=Delta_u(s,t)>0`, `|d|<=C_end U^a H` with
    `gcd(s,t)=1`; no frame-dependent compactness constant is hidden.
    See section 3 of
    [the moving-frame proof](six_point_moving_frame_radius_height.md).
    The exact checker passes both nonresonant witnesses and 1,770
    metric/content cases, now also checking all fifteen chord identities
    at each witness.

    Separately, retain the actual product
    `B=product M_I^(|sum_I u_i|)` as the denominator of the trace `P/B`.
    Its passport gives `P+B=a A^2`, `P-B=b Delta^5 C^2` with rational
    constants and `-ab` a rational square. After an explicit rational
    rescaling, `2B=a(A^2+Delta^5 C^2)`. The logarithmic arithmetic
    heights of all forms and constants are bounded by
    `O(U^2 log(2U))`, not by `O(log U)`. Specializing at `d^2=Delta`
    yields a Gaussian norm automatically; forgetting its prescribed
    second coordinate `d^5 C` loses information. Thus this identity
    adds no independent height restriction. See
    [the constant-preserving Pell derivation](six_point_trace_polynomial_pell.md).

147. **Every triangle quadratic has an explicit quadratic splitting field.**
    For a triple `I` with nonzero subsum `S_I`, on either isotropic
    ruling one has
    `disc(M_I) in (-S_I product_(i in I)u_i) Q^(times 2)`.
    Indeed `1^perp/<1>` is the orthogonal sum of the two weighted
    zero-sum binary spaces supported on `I` and its complement.
    Each has this discriminant squareclass. Their four pairs of
    isotropic lines give exactly two roots on each ruling, including
    the rational split case and a possible root at infinity.
    A good prime dividing a primitive value of `M_I` must split in
    this field; the prime exceptions explicitly include frame
    denominators, weights, subset sums, and two. Good split roots
    are simple and can lift to arbitrary valuations, so no height
    bound follows from splitting alone. See
    [the splitting-field proof](six_point_triangle_splitting_fields.md).
    Its exact checker passes 120 quadratics on both rulings, including
    36 rationally split cases, and 4,372 good-prime tests.

148. **Endpoint parameters for a fixed central vector have an effective gap.**
    Above a polynomial threshold in `U`, the integer window in item 146
    places the normalized rational parameter within
    `C(C_end) U^b H^(-10)` of one real branch root. Reduced rational
    separation then gives the ninth-power gap
    `H_next >= H_previous^9/[2 C(C_end) U^b]` for parameters near
    the same root in the same bounded chart. Thus the number of
    parameters of height at most `B` is effectively
    `U^O(1)+O(log log B)` for fixed endpoint constant. This counts
    parameters in a fixed-weight pencil, not lattice points on one
    circle. If the nearby root lies on a rational irreducible branch
    factor of degree `m<=9`, nonzero integer evaluation further gives
    `H^(10-m)<=C(C_end) U^O(1)`. The existing irreducible degree-twelve
    witnesses lie outside that case. Neither statement controls a
    first isolated solution for arbitrary moving weights. See
    [the independently audited parameter-gap proof](six_point_endpoint_parameter_gap.md).

149. **Triangle splitting conditions are compatible locally, including the exact unbalanced-cut correlations.**
    At a clean minority-pair cut of height `a`, the two minority
    central weights have valuation `a` and the other four are units.
    Barycentric residues make the four noncrossing triangle
    discriminants squares over `Q_p`. For a crossing triple their
    valuation is `a+v_p(S_I)`; the subsum can cancel and its residual
    class is variable. Singleton cuts likewise leave each individual
    split, nonsplit, or ramified class variable. Exact checks at the
    Gaussian-split prime thirteen realize these alternatives, including
    pair heights one and two and the crossed-unit formula. See
    [the clean-cut squareclass calculation](triangle_discriminant_unbalanced_cut_reduction.md).
    These statements concern exact clean cuts. The all-prime additive
    valuation-error estimates do not preserve squareclass, and one
    cannot discard a perturbed prime's whole cut mass at a cost bounded
    by the private-factor valuation.

    For fixed admissible weights, primes completely split in the
    finite compositum of the ten triangle fields and `Q(i)` satisfy
    every reciprocity relation simultaneously. Distinct comparable
    such primes exist sufficiently far out with the weights fixed.
    Simple-root lifting and CRT impose any prescribed positive
    balanced-minor valuations at all ten new primes while putting the
    rational base parameter in a real circle interval. Near each
    degeneration `Delta` is a negative nonzero square modulo its
    prime, so these primes also admit local circle lifts. If an actual
    rational seed is available, finitely many existing local profiles
    can be preserved by sufficiently close approximation. There is
    still no common rational square root of `Delta`, no assertion
    about all other primes, and no control at the required relative
    fair scales. See section 4 of
    [the joint local construction](six_point_triangle_splitting_fields.md).

150. **Every fixed rational Mobius orbit obeys a quadratic central-height bound.**
    For six fixed rational cotangents `s_i`, a rational matrix
    `M=(a,b;c,d)` transforms the primitive central vector projectively
    to `[((a s_i+b)^2+(c s_i+d)^2)^2 / product_(j!=i)(s_i-s_j)]`.
    All matrix dependence compresses to the primitive integral Gram
    matrix `Q_0` proportional to `M^T M`. Fixed weighted quartic
    evaluation, including a bounded coefficient content, gives
    `U asymp_s H(Q_0)^2`. If all image cotangents are positive with
    minimum `X`, exact squared chords give
    `X^2<=16H(Q_0)^2/[det(Q_0)c_ij]` for any fixed base squared chord
    `c_ij>0`. Thus `U>=c_s X^2`, unconditionally on a fixed orbit.
    Rational matrix contents and output rotations are fully retained;
    an unbounded common factor cannot rescue that orbit.
    See [the Gram-compression proof](mobius_fixed_six_obstruction.md).

    Normalizing three nodes to `0,1,infinity` writes a sufficient
    constant explicitly in the remaining three cross-ratios, their
    denominator clearing, and the inverse weighted evaluation matrix.
    This is not an optimal constant or a bound uniform over moving
    cross-ratios. The exact checker verifies 1,276 matrix images,
    540 positive-image chord/height inequalities, and two rational
    normalization constants with the infinity-row sign. The larger
    finite scan also reproduces its three reported minima. No general
    arc-count growth improvement follows from the fixed-orbit result.

151. **A split prime has an exact denominator-dependent cotangent capacity.**
    For a clique with `k` finite integer cotangents in denominator `L`,
    anchor included, and exact all-edge norm lcm `N`, every prime
    `p=1 mod 4` satisfies
    `k+1 <= (v_p(N)+1)(p-1)p^(v_p(L))`.
    The Cayley coordinates in `Q_p` occupy an integer valuation interval
    of length exactly `v_p(N)`. At one valuation level, integrality of
    every pair cotangent forces distinct unit residues modulo
    `p^(v_p(L)+1)`, giving the displayed capacity. It is sharp even
    for positive cliques: translating the eight-node norm-five clique
    by suitable integer multiples preserves `L=6` and `v_5(N)=1` while
    making every finite cotangent positive and arbitrarily large.
    See [the capacity proof](split_prime_cotangent_capacity.md).
    The independent checker verifies three exact norm lcms and seven
    positive translations. This imposes small-prime divisibility but
    contains no lower bound in the archimedean ratio `X_1/L`.

152. **Endpoint factors have an exact vertical-line gcd formula.**
    Writing an endpoint chord as `Q_j-P=d_j v_j` with ordinary
    primitive `v_j` gives `2P=v_j(-d_j+i t_j)` with integer `t_j`.
    For two factors having the same real part `-d`, the Gaussian gcd
    norm is exactly
    `gcd(delta^2,delta d,delta t_i,d^2+t_i^2)`, where
    `delta=t_j-t_i`. This is the index of the corresponding rank-two
    integer ideal lattice, and is at most `d|delta|`. Substitution
    in the lcm product estimate shows that three same-content
    endpoint factors on an arc of length `C sqrt(R)` have integer
    cotangent spread at least `2^(-2/3) C^(-2) d R^(1/3)` in the
    stated small-arc regime. For the full primitive anchored tuple,
    the lcm of its endpoint factors reconstructs the radius between
    `R` and `2R`, including the ramified content. See
    [the vertical-line proof](endpoint_vertical_line_gcd.md).
    The exact checker passes 54,900 gcd cases and 680 primitive
    reconstruction cases. The upper spread bound `2R` is still
    compatible with the lower bound, pairwise gcd costs grow
    quadratically, and the chord contents can vary. Uniformity does
    not follow.

153. **The moving-base Gram content can be written without an unspecified normalization.**
    With anchor infinity and chosen finite coordinates `A/L<B/L`,
    put `delta=B-A` and `d=gcd(delta,A,(A^2+L^2)/delta)`.
    The clique divisibility implies `d|L`, including at two, and the
    primitive Gram matrix of the inverse three-node normalization is
    exactly
    `(delta/d,A/d; A/d,(A^2+L^2)/(delta d))`, with determinant `(L/d)^2`.
    At the remaining normalized cross-ratios, the actual six-entry
    weighted quartic evaluation has primitive height
    `U=||Nhat f||_infinity/C_eval`, where `C_eval` is its ordinary
    gcd and the infinity row is minus the leading coefficient.
    See [the moving-base content audit](moving_base_gram_content_audit.md).
    Under the explicit assumptions `log A=log B=log delta=8w+o(w)`,
    `log L=o(w)`, and `log U=7w+o(w)`, the identity gives
    `log(C_eval/R_eval)=9w+o(w)` with the defined actual evaluation
    scale `R_eval=||Nhat f||/H(Q_0)^2`. No subpower bound on
    `R_eval` is inferred from these assumptions. The checker passes
    19,821 pair Gram reductions and three exact weighted-content
    regressions. This locates the moving-orbit loss and does not
    remove it.

154. **The four-point Pell family is closed under the tested fifth-point symmetries.**
    On its required Pell progression, the leading rays of its three
    moving whole Gaussian blocks agree. A whole-block conjugation has
    limiting ratio `omega^(m-2b)`, with `omega=(1-2i)/sqrt(5)`.
    No nonzero power is a Gaussian unit, so exactly the original four
    switches can cluster on their ray. The complete rational
    pair-reflection orbit has no additional integral point either:
    its affine orientation equations have just those four binary
    solutions. The exact checker enumerates all sixteen whole-block
    switches and the full integral binary orientation system. See
    [the fifth-point symmetry proof](four_point_pell_fifth_symmetry_obstruction.md).

    A fifth whole-block row cannot preserve a vanishing endpoint
    constant by adjoining one new binary Gaussian factor `H`, coprime
    to its conjugate and the old conductor, at any size. A retained
    same-orientation pair has angular separation at least `cV^(-2)`.
    The active fifth row also forces `conjugate(H)/H` near one of
    finitely many targets `epsilon omega^j`; Gaussian separation or
    its quadratic field norm gives a second lower bound
    `theta>=c|H|^(-2)-C V^(-2)`. Equality is excluded by coprimality
    over five, apart from units already covered by the finite-ray
    argument. Splitting at `|H|=epsilon_0 V` gives
    `theta sqrt(R|H|)>=c_0>0` uniformly in the size of `H`.
    This was independently audited after removing the earlier fixed
    relative-rate restriction. It does not cover partial switches
    inside the moving prime factorizations, shared conductor factors,
    or constructions changing the original four points. The fixed
    `L=24` simultaneous-divisor problem is only a subproblem, since
    an arbitrary fifth rational point can enlarge that normalizer.
    Item 235 now closes the partial-factor gap on the same circle within
    `sqrt(R)/4` of the designated anchor. Its proof uses an integral frame
    and covers every integer point, independently of its factorization or
    cotangent normalizer. Changing the circle by a growing common factor
    remains outside that fixed-neighborhood conclusion.

155. **Three equal-content endpoint factors attain the three-halves lcm exponent.**
    The integral hyperbolic matrix `[[17,4],[4,1]]` preserves
    `Re((1+2i)xy)`. Applied to the three seeds `i,1+3i,4-3i`, it
    gives actual anchored cofactors `2(1+2i)(ab,ac,bc)` with common
    real part `-10`, ordinary-primitive complements, and exact lcm

    Every proposed exponent above `3/2` therefore fails for these

    tuple by its exact Gaussian gcd `5(1+i)` retains the obstruction
    with fixed primitive contents `(1,2,1)`. Adjoining the fourth

    size on an explicit progression; that family attains, but does

    See [the exact Pell families](vertical_lcm_pell_counterfamily.md).
    The root reran forty exact indices, including full normalization,
    primitive complements, equal norms, and lcm reconstruction.
    Neither fixed-cardinality example is an unbounded endpoint cluster.

156. **Moving weighted evaluation content has an exact fair-cut table.**
    For a clean good cut `S` among the five finite labels, of height
    `e` and size `s`, set `h=1` when both canonical selected labels
    lie in `S`. The raw weight valuations are
    `[2h+(3-s)1_(j in S)]e`, with infinity valuation `2he`.
    The weighted-matrix denominator clearer has valuation `(s-1)e`
    for `h=0` and zero for `h=1`. The resulting `C_eval/e`
    valuation table is `(0,1,2,2,--)` for `h=0` and
    `(--,2,2,1,0)` for `h=1`, as `s` runs from one to five.
    A full fair core consequently contributes `29w` to `log ell`
    and `38w` to `log C_eval`. These are core contributions unless
    the remaining valuation mass is controlled. Exact finite minima
    and maxima give stability under the stated private-factor errors.
    An unconditional positive cotangent-clique family has fixed
    `Q_0=[[1,1],[1,2]]`, determinant one, and
    `v_13(ell)=v_13(C_eval)=2e`. This refutes a content bound based
    solely on the Gram form; its least cotangent is one, so it has

    [the content table and construction](moving_base_fair_content_table.md).
    The root reran the exact table and eight Hensel-lift examples.

157. **Gauss reduction preserves the central vector when the markings move.**
    A primitive positive integral Gram form of determinant `m^2`
    reduces by `SL_2(Z)` to height at most `2m^2`; determinant one
    reduces to the identity. The homogeneous central weights are
    `q(v_i)^2/product_(j!=i)det(v_i,v_j)`. Simultaneously replacing
    `Q` by `S^T Q S` and every marking by `S^(-1)v_i` preserves each
    weight exactly. Independent projective rescalings multiply all
    six weights by one common scalar, including a moving infinity
    mark. Thus primitive `U` is unchanged. Large canonical form
    entries at small `m` instead force large transformed integer
    marking vectors. The note explicitly retracts the false
    determinant-one grid inference and two false coefficient-gcd
    divisibilities, each with an actual counterexample. See
    [the marked-node reduction audit](gauss_reduction_marked_nodes_audit.md).
    The root checker passes 180 covariance/reduction cases and 129
    reduced forms; a separate Astra audit found no mathematical defect.

158. **A simultaneous lcm inequality gives exponent five-thirds for four factors.**
    For sorted same-content factors `w_j=-d+i t_j`, primewise
    divisibility gives `(product w_j)^2 | L^3 product gcd(w_i,w_j)`.
    Hence `|L|>=d^(-1)t_1^(2/3)t_2^(1/2)t_3^(1/3)t_4^(1/6)`,
    without a comparability assumption. An exact higher-gcd identity
    retains the triple-sharing loss rather than discarding it.
    Ten formal pair/triple blocks satisfy all those identities at
    lcm exponent `5/3`, so additive realization is still necessary
    for an improvement. The blocks are not an actual circle family.

    The root extended the result to varying contents using
    `N(gcd(w_i,w_j))<=|det(w_i,w_j)|`. If
    `w_j=-d_j+i t_j`, `x_j=t_j/d_j` are positive and increasing,
    and `r=floor(k/2)`, then
    `|L| >= (product d_j)^((2r-k+1)/(r(r+1)))`
    `product x_j^((2r-j+1)/(r(r+1))) >= (min x_j)^(2-1/(r+1))`.
    Thus equal contents are unnecessary for this subquadratic bound.
    With `k=2r` actual endpoint factors, it also bounds their content
    product by a constant depending on `C,r` times `R^(r/2)`.
    Every fixed-cardinality exponent remains strictly below two,
    so no uniform count or general growth improvement follows.
    See [the simultaneous inequality and its scope](four_vertical_lcm_five_thirds.md).
    Root checks passed 4,096 valuation tuples, 10,920 vertical tuples,
    493 multiplicity tests, and 1,080 varying-content tuples.
    A separate [bounded exact search](four_vertical_lcm_search.md)
    checks primitive complements and the possible `1+i` lift needed
    for an integral center. The root reran the `t<=40` boxes for
    four contents, the bounded progression/random searches, and
    nineteen positive Pell indices. The targeted examples give no
    shrinking four-factor quadratic ratio; this is finite evidence,
    not an asymptotic lower bound.

159. **Radius and central content have an exact common homogeneous description.**
    For six primitive markings `v_i`, positive primitive Gram form
    `Q` with determinant `r^2`, write `q_i=v_i^T Q v_i` and
    `Delta_ij=det(v_i,v_j)`. The central weights are
    `w_i=q_i^2/product_(j!=i)Delta_ij`; their exact primitive
    multiplier has valuation minus the minimum of
    `2v_p(q_i)-sum_(j!=i)v_p(Delta_ij)`. The minimal clearer of
    the six specialized weights must be distinguished from the
    clearer of the entire evaluation matrix. Only their respective
    content quotients agree for fixed representatives. The multiplier
    itself is covariant; the primitive vector is invariant.

    The root audit removed the apparent independent polar-gcd data:
    `gcd(B_ij,r Delta_ij)^2=gcd(q_i q_j,r^2 Delta_ij^2)`.
    Thus the edge denominator norm is exactly
    `odd(q_i q_j/gcd(q_i q_j,r^2 Delta_ij^2))`, also the reduced
    denominator of the squared unit-circle chord. Their integer lcm
    is the intrinsic least squared radius `N`. Put
    `lambda_ij=v_p(q_i)+v_p(q_j)-2v_p(r)-2v_p(Delta_ij)` and
    `s_i=sum_(j!=i)lambda_ij`. At every prime,
    `v_p(u_i)=(s_i-min s)/2`; for odd primes
    `v_p(N)=max_(i<j)max(0,lambda_ij)`, and `v_2(N)=0`.
    The archimedean identity is also exact:
    `|w_i| product_(j!=i)delta_ij=(2r)^5/sqrt(product q_i)`.
    See [the common-data radius/content formulas](homogeneous_central_content_radius.md).

    Under the specified full good-cut profile and cotangent height
    assumptions, the sixteen incident norm blocks exhaust the norm
    heights. The eight blocks for each pair divide its nonzero
    difference; this lower bound and the cotangent-size upper bound
    force difference logarithm `8w+o(w)`. Thus the remaining norm
    and difference valuation mass is `o(w)`. Item 156 then
    gives global `log ell_E=29w`, `log C_E=38w`, and
    `log R_eval=29w`, each up to `o(w)`; raw evaluated height has
    logarithm `45w` and primitive `log U=7w`. The evaluation scale
    is not subexponential. These formulas expose the same global
    compatibility problem, without proving an endpoint bound.
    Root and independent Astra checks passed 45 edge identities,
    both ramified parity cases, exact Gaussian reconstruction, and
    the balanced-cut regression distinguishing the two clearers.

160. **Every fixed first-order monomial test passes the relaxed four-factor profile.**
    For an integer vector `r`, reduce `product w_j^(r_j)` to `N/D`
    and apply Gaussian integrality to the off-axis component of
    `i^(-sum r_j)N conjugate(D)`. When that component is nonzero,
    its modulus cost is at least `T/(d ||r||_1)` for fixed common
    content `d` and all heights at least `T`. In the ten-block
    pair/triple incidence profile from item 158, the exact cost
    exponent is
    `[sum_pairs |r_i+r_j|+sum_triples |r_i+r_j+r_k|]/6 >=1`
    for every nonzero integer vector. A parity argument proves this
    for zero total sum; triangle inequalities prove the other case.
    See [the monomial phase scope audit](vertical_monomial_phase_barrier.md).
    Thus this entire specified first-order inequality family does
    not exclude the relaxed `5/3` profile. The profile has not been
    realized as actual vertical Gaussian factors. Higher-order
    reciprocal cancellations and additive sums remain outside the
    statement. Root checks passed 6,560 incidence vectors and 5,616
    exact Gaussian quotient cases, retaining twelve zero-projection
    exceptions. No general growth improvement follows.

161. **The good-prime signed edge data form an exact local collision tree.**
    At split primes away from twice the Gram determinant, the two
    isotropic directions give local coordinates with
    `lambda_ij=n_i+n_j-2v_p(z_i-z_j)` on one branch. Unequal
    depths give the positive value `|n_i-n_j|`; equal depths
    give a nonpositive even collision depth. Opposite isotropic
    branches give `n_i+n_j`. At inert good primes every norm is
    a unit and `lambda_ij=-2v_p(Delta_ij)<=0`. Thus positivity
    is not restricted to pairs on opposite isotropic branches.
    Every negative edge forces its half-depth into the actual
    all-edge cotangent denominator. Summed over the fifteen
    six-point edges, this costs at most `15 log L`, so a
    subpower denominator permits only subpower negative mass.
    Explicit split-prime families have fixed positive maximum
    and unbounded negative depth, but their `log L` is linear
    in their own `log N`; they are not subpower-denominator
    counterexamples. See [the local tree audit](local_signed_chord_tree.md).
    The root reran exact split/inert, general-form, central-content,
    and denominator checks, including the prime 13 variant.

162. **The positive squared-distance tree sum can retain its full denominator.**
    The tree sum `tau` obeys
    `0<tau<=k^(k-2) delta^(2(k-1))`. Its denominator divides
    `N^(k-1)`, and primitive Gaussian families with pairwise
    coprime norms attain exactly that full power: at each norm
    prime the unique most singular term is the star tree.
    In particular four translated parameters `2(T+j)`,
    `0<=j<=3`, with `T` a multiple of five, have pairwise
    coprime norms, `den(tau)=N^3`, and angular endpoint
    constant tending to 12. This refutes the proposed
    `den(tau)<=B N^((k-1)/2)` estimate even on bounded
    four-point endpoint arcs. It does not address arbitrarily
    large cardinality or sufficiently small arc constants.
