    `log d_ab=(1/2+1/(2(M-1)))log N+O_M(1)`; consequently all
    pairs lie in `[sqrt(N),N^(1/2+1/M)]`. Every coordinate
    attains both extrema, so primitive normalization does not
    remove the claimed baseline. Gaussian arguments remain
    uncontrolled: this is an allocation construction, not an
    actual endpoint counterexample. Luna constructed it and
    root checked M=4 and M=8 using exact integer powers. See
    [the construction](pair_norm_squareclass_code_audit.md) and
    [the checker](check_pair_norm_squareclass_code.py).
    A separate [binary graph audit](good_pair_graph_compatibility_audit.md)
    makes the analogous valuation-only limitation precise.

    The full angular hypotheses do exclude repeated pair labels.
    Root's three-half-sum argument and independent Astra/Luna
    audits establish this directly for a fixed-unit C<=2 cluster:
    a hypothetical four-label parity relation produces three
    nonreal Gaussian integers of norms each greater than sqrt(N),
    while their product of norms is at most N^(3/2). B2 rigidity
    excludes zero words; Gaussian units choose the required roots.
    This extends the direct constant range of the existing
    C<1 four-wise theorem in [the earlier baseline](squareclass_baseline_and_power_groups.md).
    It is not a new qualitative packing bound for arbitrary C,
    nor a growth-rate improvement. See [the checked refinement](angular_pair_squareclass_independent_audit.md).

216. **Joint accounting recovers a determinant gain, including at two.**
    At p|det(M), p not dividing K, write ell=v_p(det(M)),
    c_i for ordinary image contents, t_i for normalized Gaussian
    phase valuations, and beta_ij=v_p(b_ij). For odd split p,
    `beta_ij >= min(c_i,c_j) + 1_(t_i t_j>0) min(|t_i|,|t_j|)`.
    A nonzero t_i forces c_i=ell. Consequently

    `2 sum c_i + sum |t_i| - width(t) <= 3ell + sum beta_ij`.

    The corresponding inert-prime statement has all t_i=0.
    The coefficient three is sharp even with a unit source
    anchor. At two, K odd and det(M) even force exactly one
    odd matrix entry. If r outputs are odd-odd, the analogous
    inequality is `2 sum c_i+r <= 3ell+sum beta_ij+1`, so the
    existing factor two remains sufficient.

    Let D_delta be the entire part of |det(M)| coprime to K.
    The right side of the compressed endpoint bound in item 212
    can be multiplied by
    `max(1,D_delta^(2m-3)/T^2)`. Thus determinant primes can
    contribute a gain after ordinary contents are accounted for
    jointly with phase overlaps. For M=diag(n+1,n), one has
    D_delta=n(n+1), T=2n^2+2n+1, and K=(2n+1)^2; the matrix
    loss collapses to `O_m(n^6)`, independently of m. Hence
    `N' >>_(m,C) N^[(3m-4)/8]/n^6` and a radius-nonincreasing
    image requires `n >>_(m,C) N^[(m-4)/16]`.
    Astra proved the odd-prime joint bound; root supplied the
    ramified extension and Astra independently checked it.
    Root's persistent checker verifies both global gain bounds
    in all 7,808 nonconformal test cases, including the actual
    Pell endpoint source. See [the complete joint proof](mobius_joint_content_conductor.md).
    The output-conformal minimum from item 213 also optimizes
    these gain bounds: every other integral representative is
    L_lambda M_*, scaling T,K,det by s,s^2,s for s=Norm(lambda),
    while its good determinant part divides that of M_*.
    This gives a stronger descent obstruction, not a general
    point-count bound.

217. **Forward and backward angular distortion requires separate anchor normalization.**
    For a unit real column u, the exact phase derivative is
    `|det(M)|/(u^t M^t M u)`. The exact chord multiplier for
    source columns H_i,H_j is
    `|det(M)| sqrt(f_i f_j)/sqrt(Norm(MH_i) Norm(MH_j))`.
    Thus actual source/target arc constants obey the expected
    condition-number comparison, but their allowed upper bounds
    cannot be substituted as equalities.

    Under the full hypotheses on both normalized configurations,
    the symmetric content inequality uses the geometric mean
    of two arithmetic losses, D_f and D_rev. Reanchoring the
    target changes the inverse matrix to M^{-1}S^{-1}; it does
    not generally preserve T and K of the original M. A same-loss
    formula needs compatible unit anchors or independently
    verified equal invariants. Retaining the anchor norm also
    improves the one-sided denominator from T^m to
    `Norm(B_0) T^(m-1)`. A local unimodular estimate ties the
    anchor derivative to its raw stretch, but leaves K uncontrolled.
    Sol derived the distortion formulas; root caught and corrected
    the inverse-anchor gap with Sol. The diagonal family in item
    216 has distortion tending to one with unbounded intrinsic
    arithmetic height, even after its improved determinant gain.
    See [the exact formulas and qualified conclusions](mobius_endpoint_distortion_audit.md).
    No stronger general point-count estimate follows.

218. **Actual-source reanchoring has an exact primewise normal form.**
    For reduced complex coefficient ratio w=v/u, changing to actual anchor
    H_j gives w_j=w conjugate(H_j)/H_j and Gaussian cancellation
    gcd(u H_j,v conjugate(H_j))=gcd(u,conjugate(H_j))gcd(v,H_j), up to a unit.
    If Norm(v)/Norm(u)=a/b in lowest terms, the normalized invariants are
    `T_j=epsilon(a+b)k_j/2`, `K_j=epsilon^2 ab k_j^2`, and
    `det_j=epsilon(b-a)k_j/4`; epsilon is unchanged at every actual anchor.
    At a split prime, put d=v_pi(w), e=v_barpi(w), t_j=v_pi(H_j)-v_barpi(H_j).
    Then `v_p(k_j)=dist(t_j,[min(d,-e),max(d,-e)])`.
    Source and full target least radii are unchanged by this reanchoring.
    A fixed norm-ratio family has unbounded external anchor factors, but
    is not asserted to have radius-nonincreasing targets.
    See [the exact formula](mobius_actual_anchor_normalization.md),
    [the independent all-anchor audit](mobius_all_anchor_descent_audit.md),
    and [7,488 exact anchor checks](check_mobius_actual_anchor.py).

219. **External and same-side anchor factors are charged to target residues.**
    Let I_p be the coefficient interval in item 218, S_p the full source
    interval, and `G=product p^dist(I_p,S_p)`. Every primitive target pair
    residue b'_ij is divisible by G, while gcd(G,N')=1. Moreover
    `G|k_j|GN` and `product_j(k_j/G)|N^(m-1)`.
    Pair residues are exactly invariant under common rational output
    rotations, including the ramified case. For the full target, with r
    odd-odd primitive columns and E=binom(m,2),
    `B'<= (C'/2)^E 2^[r(m-r)/2] (N')^(m/8)`.
    Consequently `G<=(C'/2)2^[r(m-r)/(2E)](N')^[1/(4(m-1))]`,
    without target extraction. Same-side distances also prove
    `(product k_j)^(m-1) product C_ij | (B')^2 product f_ij`,
    where C_ij is the pair norm obtained by clipping source valuations to I_p.
    See [external factors](mobius_external_anchor_conductor.md) and
    [the exact overlap identity](mobius_internal_overlap_residues.md).

220. **The discriminant charge is capped by the source and determinant.**
    The stronger pair transfer is
    `e'_ij | gcd(K,abs(det) e_ij) b_ij`.
    With source anchor one, every e_ij divides N, so set
    `J=gcd(K,abs(det)N)`. The compressed radius theorem, including its
    good-determinant gain, now uses `T^m J^(m-2)` instead of `T^m K^(m-2)`.
    The parity proof also covers v_2(J)=1. For unimodular maps, a separate
    expansion argument gives
    `N'>=c_(m,C) T^(m-3)/(J^(m-2) N^(5m/8))`.
    Thus radius descent imposes both lower and upper height restrictions;
    their ranges still overlap. The strengthened bounds passed 7,808
    nonconformal configurations in the persistent conductor checker.
    See [the source cap and expansion proof](mobius_source_capped_content.md).

221. **Both endpoint residue products control the entire determinant core.**
    Put `c=epsilon abs(b-a)/4` and `F_m=floor((m-1)^2/4)`.
    At every odd core prime, including inert primes, local normalization
    gives a good-determinant matrix. If rho_i are its row-content valuations,
    the exact determinant identity and joint pair transfer give
    `beta_ij+beta'_ij >= v_p(c)-abs(rho_i-rho_j)`.
    Summing and applying the cut bound proves `c_odd^F_m | B B'`.
    The ramified calculation adds at most binom(r,2) powers of two, giving
    the full divisibility `c^F_m | 2^binom(r,2) B B'`.
    Hence for C,C'<=2 and N'<=N,
    `c <= 2^[m(m-1)/(2F_m)] N^[m/(4F_m)]`.
    This bounds the complete reduced norm difference at exponent O(1/m),
    but does not bound the norm sum a+b.
    See [the joint core proof](joint_source_target_residue_core.md).

222. **Every clipped source conductor survives in the target.**
    The local fractional-linear valuation map is affine with slope plus
    or minus one inside I_p, constant outside, with endpoint cancellation
    moving outward. Therefore every clipped pair norm C_ij divides the
    odd part of f'_ij. In particular
    `Nclip=product p^length(I_p intersect S_p) | gcd(N,N')`, where a
    disjoint intersection contributes zero. Coverage at all source primes
    forces N|N', excluding strict descent in that regime.
    Output-conformal padding by norm s changes the source cap to
    `s gcd(sK,abs(det)N)`, a multiple of sJ, so the same output minimum
    still optimizes the capped bounds. At actual anchors,
    `J_j=k_j gcd(K_c k_j,abs(c)N)`.
    Combining all-anchor capped bounds with item 219 cancels the complete
    product of k_j; the coefficient sum remains.
    See [the clipping and cancellation proof](mobius_capped_anchor_clipping.md).

223. **Actual four-point endpoint sets permit arbitrarily high coefficient cores.**
    Every four distinct rational circle phases admit the rational involution
    swapping opposite cyclic labels. On a short arc it is nonconformal and
    preserves the entire finite set. Its reduced norm-ratio denominator
    is at least C^(-2)sqrt(N). Applying it to the actual shrinking Pell
    four-point family gives unbounded core height with N'=N exactly.
    The pole lies between samples, so a short finite image does not imply
    a short image of the full intervening interval. This rules out the
    proposed high-core rigidity argument using only four correspondences;
    it leaves a many-point theorem open.
    See [the obstruction](mobius_four_point_selfmap_obstruction.md) and
    [exact Pell checks at indices 1, 11, 21](check_mobius_four_point_selfmap.py).

224. **Removed conductor is bounded by source imbalance and target residues.**
    With W=log(N), P=product f_ij, the exact source cut deficit is
    `D=m^2 W/4-log(P)<=mW/4`. An erased cut with n rows on its outside
    contributes binom(n,2) to target residues. For k=floor(m/4),
    `A=k/(m-2k-1)` and `c_m=binom(k,2)+A(k-m/2)^2`, this gives
    `c_m log(N/Nclip)<=log(B')+A D`.
    Together with item 222 it proves, for m>=5 and C,C'<=2,
    `N'>=N^(1-4/m)/8`, with no target unit extraction or matrix-height bound.
    The exact optimized exponent is
    `rho_m=2k(m-2k-2)/(m+2k(m-2k-2))`.
    The earlier projective-orbit theorem already gave a near-unit radius
    exponent; this result supplies an explicit primewise conductor charge.
    It permits N'=N and does not improve general point-count growth.
    See [the cut proof](mobius_erased_conductor_budget.md) and
    [the persistent joint checker](check_mobius_joint_anchor_residues.py),
    which also checks items 219--222 on 1,752 configurations and the cut
    constants through m=100. The full source-unit extension retains
    `P_odd=P_full/2^[s(m-s)]` in the source deficit and gives
    `N'>=N^(1-4/m)/16` for the full source and full target.
    The corresponding full-core divisibility has the parity charge
    `2^[binom(s,2)+binom(r,2)]`; no source extraction is needed.
    The least primitive circle norm remains odd even when half-angle
    parities mix. See [the arbitrary-unit audit](mobius_arbitrary_unit_retention_addendum.md).
    With the mixed-source fixtures, the persistent checker now passes
    2,187 configurations, including 492 nontrivial odd cores.

225. **A nonconformal endpoint map with controlled radius approaches rank one.**
    The clipped conductor divides ab, while the full determinant-core
    estimate controls abs(a-b). Combining these with item 224 gives an
    intrinsic condition-number restriction for moving sources of arbitrary
    units. If both endpoint constants are at most two, N'<=N, and m>=8,
    `kappa(M)>=N^z_m/512`, where
    `z_m=(1-q_m)/2-m/(4F_m)`,
    `q_m=m(1+2A_m)/(8c_m)`, and the cut constants are those of item 224.
    The exponents satisfy `z_m>=1/66` and
    `z_m=1/2-3/m+O(1/m^2)`; z_8=1/66 exactly.
    This follows from the rotation-invariant identity
    `T/abs(det)=2(a+b)/abs(a-b)=kappa+1/kappa`.
    Fixed-unit sources admit the smaller constant 64. The general result
    keeps all source and target points and imposes no matrix-height bound.
    A two-radius form also covers images of somewhat larger norm.
    It leaves nearly singular maps admissible and does not construct a
    descent or bound the source cardinality. See
    [the invariant geometric restriction](mobius_endpoint_condition_number.md).

226. **A reflection union has a cardinality-dependent endpoint cost.**
    A primitive Gaussian tuple invariant under a rational circle reflection
    has reflection coefficient among the four Gaussian units. Counting its
    distinct radial levels gives
    `C_U^2>=8(ceil(|U|/2)-1)` for a symmetric arc of width below pi.
    For an actual m-point source with C<=2, reflection in any pair midpoint
    and union with the source produces exactly 2m-2 points, after primitive
    realization. Thus `C_U>=sqrt(8(m-2))`. If Q is the exact squared-radius
    multiplier, the general pair has `Q>=4(m-2)^2/C^4`, improved to
    `Q>=64(m-2)^2/C^4` for the two extreme source points. This rules out
    unbounded point amplification at a bounded endpoint constant by full
    reflection unions, without a fairness hypothesis. It does not bound
    the original nonsymmetric cluster. See
    [the radial-count proof](reflection_union_radial_count_obstruction.md)
    and [18 exact Pell union checks](check_reflection_union_radial_count.py).

227. **Finite samples force a critical triangular form for an admissible map.**
    Write `h_q=floor(q^2/4)/(q(q-1))`. For every n,r>=2 with n+r=m+1,
    a rational map between source and target tuples of least norms N,N'
    satisfies `kappa<=4(2N)^h_n(2N')^h_r`. Together with item 225,
    N'<=N confines an admissible map to
    `kappa=N^[1/2+O(1/m)]`. This argument uses finite samples and allows
    poles between them. An exact angular-product identity then chooses
    one actual anchor with both controlled common coefficient content
    and controlled stretch. After an integral output rotation the map is
    represented by `[[a,b],[0,d]]`, with nonzero integer diagonals
    `a,abs(d)<=D_m N^[g_m+b_m]`, where
    `g_m+b_m=13/(4m)+O(1/m^2)` and D_m is explicitly bounded as m grows.
    The shear has `abs(b)<=N^[1/4+O(1/m)]` with displayed constants, and
    an almost-full source conductor divides
    `(a^2+b^2+d^2)^2-4a^2d^2`. The critical regime remains compatible with
    finite geometry; no existence or exclusion of an admissible map is
    proved. See [the normal-form proof](mobius_finite_sample_critical_form.md)
    and [the independent finite-geometry checks](check_mobius_finite_geometry.py).

228. **The critical form lifts every point to one explicit near-square circle.**
    For the integral matrix `[[A,B],[0,D]]`, put
    `Gamma=B^2-A^2+D^2+2iAB`, `T=A^2+B^2+D^2`, and
    `K=T^2-4A^2D^2=Norm(Gamma)`. The least positive integer h clearing
    all anchored phases Gamma*q_i satisfies `h | N/Nclip`. Hence
    `Z_i=h Gamma q_i` are distinct Gaussian integers with common norm
    `Nlift=h^2 K=(hT)^2-4(hAD)^2`, and `N | Nlift`. Their common Gaussian
    gcd has norm exactly Nlift/N. The orientation and full-tuple denominator
    costs are proved, including nested layers and arbitrary phase units.
    The normalized near-axis strip is at most
    `sqrt(h)(2abs(AB)/K^(1/4)+K^(1/4)Delta)`.
    Current critical bounds make this `N^O(1/m)`, which is too wide to
    apply Temur's near-square strip theorem at a smaller growth scale.
    His defect and strip hypotheses are separate. The lift also remains
    conditional on the unknown admissible-map existence. See
    [the lift and primary-source comparison](critical_shear_near_square_lift.md)
    and [1,720 exact full-tuple checks](check_critical_shear_near_square_lift.py).

229. **Global row-product minimization need not decrease the circle radius.**
    On an actual primitive four-point Pell cluster of least norm
    N=358853785 and endpoint constant below two, the exact global
    GL(2,Z) minimizer of the transformed row-norm product is, modulo
    integral output rotations and reflections, `[[1,155],[0,1]]`.
    Its product decreases by more than 75,000, but its least target norm
    is N'=84815456245>236N, and its image violates C'<=2. A two-variable
    exact formula excludes every first-column norm at least two; a finite
    integer enumeration then certifies the global minimum. This invalidates
    the product objective as a standalone descent construction, including
    at the critical shear scale. It does not refute a further theorem
    specific to eight or more rows. See
    [the proof](mobius_product_reduction_obstruction.md) and
    [the exact global-minimum certificate](check_mobius_product_reduction_obstruction.py).

230. **Bounded-radius images are discrete near the conformal locus.**
    For any source of at least three distinct rational circle phases,
    without an endpoint hypothesis, the normalized operator distance is
    `epsilon(M)=(kappa-1)/(kappa+1)`. A nonconformal rational map satisfies
    `N'>=(1-epsilon)^2/(64 epsilon^2 N)`. Hence N'<=N forces
    `epsilon>=1/(8N+1)`. A rational shear p/q with 0<abs(p)<q has
    `N'>=(q-abs(p))^2/(64p^2 N)`. This prevents an infinitesimal
    departure from the conformal locus with nonincreasing radius.
    Modulo output conformal transformations, the full search with N'<=N
    is finite, but it need not contain a nonconformal candidate. For m>=8
    and both endpoint constants at most two, item 225 already supplies
    a much stronger distance bound tending to one; this endpoint-free
    result does not improve that critical regime or the point-count bound.
    See [the discreteness proof](mobius_local_descent_gap.md) and
    [the exact phase, shear, and distance checks](check_mobius_local_descent_gap.py).

231. **All anchor versions of the critical lift share one canonical tuple.**
    Put e=N/Nclip, k=K/Nclip, and g=Norm(L), where L is the common
    Gaussian multiplier in item 228. Then `g e=h^2 k`, `h | e`, and
    the ordinary content d of L is coprime to h and divides both coordinates
    of Gamma. The complementary factors
    `K±=B^2+(A±D)^2` give positive integers n±,u± with
    `N=e n+ n-`, `u+u-=k`, `u+n+-u-n-=4AD`, and
    `gcd(n+,n-) | 4AD`. In the critical regime the n± have near-square-root
    size and all cofactors remain N^O(1/m).
    For every actual source reanchor, `Gamma_j(q_i/q_j)=s_j Gamma q_i`
    and `T_j=s_j T` with the same positive rational s_j. Removing ordinary
    content therefore gives the same ordered integer tuple, rational
    near-square center, and radial coordinates at every anchor. Those
    coordinates are exactly the normalized row stretches.
    For an ordinary-primitive triangular matrix, the maximum integer
    content that can be divided out while retaining the displayed integer
    center is `d0=gcd(d,T) | 2abs(A)`. Within this aligned family, the
    resulting normalized imaginary strip is at least
    `sqrt(2h abs(A)) abs(B)/K^(1/4)` at its anchor. Additional rational
    rotations are not covered by this optimization. These identities do
    not remove the polynomial strip cost or the map-existence premise.
    See [the content and covariance proof](critical_lift_shared_content_audit.md),
    [1,720 factor/content checks](check_critical_shear_near_square_lift.py),
    and [2,205 covariance plus 3,840 primitive-matrix checks](check_mobius_canonical_discriminant_lift.py).

232. **A direct primitive axis lift can require a power of the source radius.**
    For a Gaussian-primitive tuple and an integral proposed phase multiplier
    Gamma, let A=z0/gcd(z0,Gamma). Its exact least positive integer clearing
    denominator is `Norm(A)/gcd(Re(A),Im(A))`. Any rational Gaussian common
    multiplier taking the entire primitive source to integral points is
    already Gaussian integral. On the actual four-point Pell family,
    R is comparable to V^3, and every such multiplier of length Q has
    horizontal coordinate diameter
    `w>=16V/(5Q)-4Q/V`. A bounded diameter therefore requires
    Q at least a fixed positive multiple of R^(1/3). This exponent is
    attained by conjugate(B), with exact horizontal diameter 16.
    Even the pair factor Gamma=PAC=X+i needs clearing denominator
    h=Norm(B), comparable to R^(2/3); its displayed near-square defect
    becomes h^2. The same scale holds for all six pair factors.
    This is an obstruction for four-point sources and unnormalized
    horizontal width. It neither excludes a useful normalized vertical
    strip nor a many-point improvement. See
    [the direct-lift proof](direct_primitive_axis_lift_obstruction.md) and
    [the independently reconstructed exact checks](check_direct_primitive_axis_lift.py).

233. **Large cardinality alone cannot guarantee a nonconformal radius descent.**
    The rational half-angle projective stabilizer of an entire integer
    circle is exactly its eight conformal and anticonformal square
    symmetries. Its positive subgroup is cyclic, contains a quarter-turn,
    and cannot have larger order because rational projective finite orders
    are only 1,2,3,4,6. At every strict record norm for r2(N), a projective
    image with N'<=N must realize the entire same circle. It is therefore
    conformal or anticonformal. Record cardinalities are unbounded, so
    there are arbitrarily large primitive configurations with no
    nonconformal radius-nonincreasing map. These full circles have
    endpoint constant at least `(3pi/2)N^(1/4)`, and thus do not satisfy
    a fixed short-arc hypothesis. The result identifies a necessary role
    for that hypothesis in an existence theorem; it does not refute such
    a theorem or bound endpoint cardinalities.
    See [the symmetry and record-norm proof](full_circle_record_descent_obstruction.md)
    and [the exact full-circle stabilizer checks](check_full_circle_record_symmetry.py).

234. **Actual integer cotangent cliques can saturate derivative concentration.**
    For `F(t)=product_i(t-X_i)`, the pair divisibilities imply
    `F'(X_i) | (X_i^2+L^2)^(k-1)`. The exponent cannot be reduced
    unconditionally, even for positive actual cliques of every fixed size.
    Choose a split prime `p>k`, `P=p^e`, `L=lcm(1,...,k-1)`, and a lift
    `a` of a root of minus one for which every `(a+jP)^2+1` has exact
    valuation e. The coordinates `X_j=L(a+jP)` satisfy every pair
    condition, while derivative valuation is `(k-1)e`, resultant valuation
    is ke, and all-edge conductor valuation is e. Their actual conductor
    satisfies `N asymp_(k,p) P^(k+1)` when `a asymp_p P`; for k>=4 these
    examples lie outside the low-conductor endpoint regime. Thus they do
    not obstruct an endpoint-restricted refinement. See
    [the concentration and height audit](integer_cotangent_derivative_concentration.md)
    and [36 exact clique checks](check_integer_cotangent_derivative_concentration.py).
    Separate [four-offset divisibility](integer_cotangent_four_offset_vandermonde.md),
    [inert-radical aggregation](integer_cotangent_inert_radical_obstruction.md),
    and [translation checks](integer_cotangent_translation_obstruction.md)
    supply no new general growth rate. The four-offset radius inequality
    is already a consequence of three pair identities; its extra integer
    invariant is unchanged by divisor complementation.

235. **The Pell four-point family has a complete isolated endpoint neighborhood.**
    For `U^2-5V^2=1`, `V>=16`, the exact unimodular matrix
    `T=[[2V,V-U],[-U-V,2V]]` sends its anchored differences to the fixed
    nodes `(0,0),(16,0),(0,2),(4,-6)`. Every integer point on the same
    circle has integral coordinates `(s,t)` satisfying
    `a s(s-2t-16)+b t(2s+t-2)=0`, with coprime a,b of order V^2.
    A chord of length at most `sqrt(R)/4` pulls back to coordinates
    smaller than V; divisibility then forces both fixed quadratics to
    vanish. Their four common zeros are precisely the original points.
    This excludes arbitrary partial Gaussian factor switches and arbitrary
    cotangent denominators in the specified neighborhood. It does not
    assume coprime Pell blocks. See
    [the complete proof](pell_four_point_complete_neighborhood.md) and
    [the independent audit](pell_four_point_local_ball_independent_audit.md).
    Exact checks verify the identities and constants on 30 Pell instances
    and all 2,624 integer points on the first four complete circles.
    Growing nonunit common multipliers and arbitrary source configurations
    remain outside this family theorem.

236. **Every fixed unimodular quadrilateral type is isolated at endpoint scale.**
    Fix integer nodes `u_0=0,u_1,u_2,u_3` with no three collinear.
    If `z_i=z_0+T u_i`, `T in GL_2(Z)`, lie on a common origin-centered
    circle, then for sufficiently large R a neighborhood
    `|w-z_0|<=c(u)sqrt(R)` contains only these four integer points.
    Their fixed conic pencil has an injective quadratic-part map. Rational
    rank-one boundaries give bounded radii; irrational boundaries force
    `R^2 asymp_u h^3`, where `h=trace(T^T T)`. The primitive pencil
    coefficients have size at least a fixed multiple of h and bounded
    content. Pulling back a short chord and using coprime divisibility
    isolates the pencil's four base points. The proof also handles
    bounded nonzero determinants after explicitly clearing preimage
    denominators. See [the fixed-type theorem](fixed_quadrilateral_unimodular_isolation.md).
    This does not extract a bounded type from an arbitrary large cluster.
    [Exact unimodular normalization checks](check_unimodular_quadrilateral_normalization.py)
    pass on 533 randomly transformed bounded-determinant quadrilaterals.

237. **The moving quadrilateral has an exact fifth-point distance product.**
    For cyclically ordered base points, put
    `A=D012,B=D013,C=D023,E=D123, Pi=ABCE`. The integer side-line
    products F and G have unique primitive positive coefficients
    `-aF+bG=sQ`, with a>b and integer s>=1. The pencil discriminant is
    `16Pi`, and `4s^3R^2=Pi ab(a-b)`. Every fifth integer point gives
    `F=kb,G=ka`, up to the common sign, and exactly
    `product_(i=0)^3|W-P_i|=4|k|sR^2/sqrt(Pi)`.
    Therefore four points in span `S<=K R^(1/3)` force every fifth
    anchor distance to satisfy `d>=4K^(-3/2)sqrt(R)-K R^(1/3)`.
    In particular `R>K^15/64` gives isolation within
    `2K^(-3/2)sqrt(R)`, uniformly over all such four-point shapes.
    See [the exact pencil and Gaussian-gcd proof](moving_quadrilateral_fifth_point_product.md)
    and [the local four-cluster corollary](bounded_jarnik_scale_four_cluster_isolation.md).
    The exact checker passes 438,240 ordered configurations and samples
    the direct five-by-five evaluation determinant.

    This is a spatial use of the classical five-point determinant:
    `|det[1,x,y,x^2,xy]|=|k|s`. With Gaussian pairing gcd gamma,
    `Pi=s^2 Norm(gamma)`; the exact nested valuation is
    `v_p(s/sqrt(Pi))=(sum t_i)/2-e-min(delta01+delta23,delta02+delta13)`.
    For two-level cuts it gives the familiar 2+2, 3+1, and 4+0 budgets.
    Setting S equal to the whole five-point span recovers only exponent
    2/5. No new general endpoint exponent or point-count rate is claimed.

238. **All classical odd-subset product bounds still admit growing real configurations.**
    Equally spaced real points in an arc `C sqrt(R)` with
    `m=floor(c log R/log log R)`, any fixed `0<c<1/2`, satisfy every
    odd-subset inequality
    `product chords >= 2^(k^2) R^(k^2)` for subsets of size 2k+1,
    once R is sufficiently large. The sine lower bound proves these
    inequalities simultaneously; an integer real-column determinant
    derives the exact classical constant. The shape-dependent
    four-cluster inequalities in item 237 follow from the five-point
    product bound itself, so the construction satisfies them as well,
    including moving shapes. See
    [the all-subset feasibility proof](real_equispaced_points_pass_all_odd_vandermonde_bounds.md).
    These are real points, not lattice points, and are not counterexamples
    to the target. They show why the retained geometric inequalities alone
    cannot remove radius growth. Similarly, [short-window frame extraction](density_threshold_unimodular_frame_extraction.md)
    only reaches a density of order R^(1/6), much weaker than the known
    logarithmic estimate. Additional arithmetic remains necessary.

239. **Common quartet gcds and individual quartet sizes obey different bounds.**
    The Gaussian gcd G of all pairing contents is exactly the gcd of all
    products of two disjoint differences. At a Gaussian prime, put
    `r=min v(z_i-z_j)` and partition the normalized differences modulo
    that prime. Then `v(G)=2r`, except that a residue class containing
    m-1 points gives `v(G)=r+r_B`, with r_B the minimum within that class.
    Conjugation on a common circle gives the further exact equality
    `Norm(G)=gcd_Q Norm(gamma_Q)`: a quartet using extreme valuation
    levels attains both conjugate minima simultaneously. The witnessing
    quartet can vary with the prime, so this does not bound the smallest
    individual quartet content. See [the matching-content theorem](quartet_matching_gcd_cut_budget.md)
    and [the independent circle-conjugation audit](quartet_matching_gcd_cut_budget_independent_audit.md).

    With `Gamma_Q=Norm(gamma_Q)` and
    `J_m=min_s{2[C(s,4)+C(m-s,4)]+(m-s)C(s,3)+sC(m-s,3)}`,
    arbitrary nested levels give `N^J_m | product_Q Gamma_Q`.
    Its weight is an exact redistribution of the triangle product and
    the pencil factors s_Q. For m=2n>=6, equally weighted balanced cuts
    force every quartet to have
    `Gamma_Q>=N^(beta_m-o(1))`, where
    `beta_m=3(n-1)(n-2)/[(2n-1)(2n-3)] -> 3/4`, while the global gcd
    is coprime to N. Actual primitive Gaussian rows realize these cuts
    using pairwise coprime blocks `2jMq+i`. Their angular span is of
    order 1/q, but R is of order q^K and their endpoint constant grows
    as q^(K/2-1). They therefore obstruct selection from the cut data
    and primitivity alone, without refuting endpoint-sensitive selection.
    Exact checks cover 1,000 global-gcd cases, cut identities through
    m=16, 1,000 nested profiles, and two primitive six-row realizations.
    The [circle-conjugation scan](check_moving_quadrilateral_gamma_content.py)
    also verifies the norm-gcd equality on 24,384 whole-cluster primitive
    normalizations containing 762,000 quartet occurrences. The quartets
    retain their source coordinates; separately normalizing each quartet
    would erase the conductor content under study. Explicit primitive
    five-point examples have unbounded common quartet content, and actual
    clusters distinguish the common gcd from the individual minimum.
    No new general counting rate follows.

240. **Global matching content is controlled jointly by triangle content and singleton factors.**
    For primitive equal-norm Gaussian rows, let g be the integer gcd of
    triangle determinants, D the Gaussian gcd of all differences, G the
    global pairing gcd from item 239, and
    `E=Norm(product_i gcd_{j!=i}(z_j))`. Exact primewise formulas prove
    `E|N`, `Norm(D)|g`, `Norm(G) Norm(D)|4Eg^2`, and `Norm(G)|2Eg^2`.
    The factors defining E are pairwise coprime and measure exactly the
    source prime layers whose cut has one point on one side. They cannot
    be omitted from the comparison with g.

    With `K=C(m,3)`, `b=C(floor(m/2),3)+C(ceil(m/2),3)`, and
    `d=C(m-1,3)-b`, retaining those layers strengthens the triangle product
    to `N^b E^d | product_I |D_I/g|`. On an arc of length C sqrt(R),
    `g^K E^d <= (C^3/8)^K R^(K gamma_m)`, where
    `gamma_m=3/[2(m-1)]` for even m and `3/(2m)` for odd m.
    Since `2d>=K` for m>=9, this gives
    `Norm(G)<=C^6 R^(2 gamma_m)/32`. The corresponding stronger joint
    bound is `Norm(G) Norm(D)<=C^6 R^(2 gamma_m)/16`.
    See [the complete local proof and center normalization](global_matching_triangle_content_normalization.md).
    Root checked the proof and reran the 1,200-tuple exact checker.
    An independent [whole-cluster check](check_cluster_global_gaussian_content.py)
    verifies the four divisibilities on 24,384 primitive clusters with
    762,000 quartet occurrences. These finite checks supplement the proof.

    Dividing translated differences by D gives an integral configuration
    with radius R/|D| but center -z_0/D. Primitivity makes that fraction
    reduced, and any similarity preserving the normalized lattice points
    has a Gaussian-integer multiplier. Clearing the center denominator
    therefore restores radius at least R. Neither this normalization nor
    the small global gcd selects a bounded quartet or improves the count's
    growth rate.

    The [adjacent-minor audit](adjacent_circle_minors_dodgson_obstruction.md)
    also identifies the two even real evaluation minors as a Gaussian
    Vandermonde expression. Their quotient with its conjugate is the
    monomial product phase of the rows. Dodgson condensation yields exactly
    the product of two existing odd determinant inequalities; no sign
    regularity of the even minors is assumed. Exact checks cover degrees
    one through four. The [polynomial value-sharing audit](polynomial_value_sharing_abc_applicability_gap.md)
    similarly retains all hypotheses of the direct Mason identities;
    those estimates still depend on polynomial degree and give no uniform
    lattice bound.

241. **The global matching factor has an exact deletion-factor decomposition.**
    Normalize `u_i=(z_i-z_0)/D` and define
    `A_i=gcd_{j<k, j,k!=i}(u_k-u_j)`, `A=product_i A_i`.
    These factors are pairwise Gaussian-coprime and `G~D^2 A`.
    At each prime, a nonunit A_i means that every row except i lies
    in one residue class; its valuation is exactly the residual matching
    content. This proof works for arbitrary distinct Gaussian rows,
    without the circle condition.

    The numbers `e_ij=A_i A_j (u_j-u_i)/A` are integral with common
    gcd one. Choosing `sum_i c_i A_i=1` and `b_j=sum_i c_i e_ij` gives
    `e_ij=A_i b_j-A_j b_i`. Each column `(A_i,b_i)` is individually
    primitive, by the exceptional-residue calculation. The precise inverse
    map is `u_j=U+A b_j/A_j`, where `U=sum_i c_i A_i u_i`.
    Thus all denominator factors and the transformed circle center remain
    visible; the construction supplies no integral radius descent.
    See [the saturated Plucker normalization](saturated_quartet_plucker_normalization.md).

    Full sign cubes of pairwise coprime blocks `x_j+i`, with even x_j,
    give 2^k distinct primitive circle rows with exactly `D~2i`, `G~4`,
    and all A_i units. Choosing `x_j=2jMq` gives angular width of order
    1/q but radius of order q^k. For k>=3 their endpoint constant diverges
    as q^(k/2-1). These actual examples show that small global content,
    saturated integral Plucker identities, and small unscaled angles do
    not replace the endpoint condition. The exact checker passes 600
    arbitrary tuples, 100 forced deletion-factor tuples, and four primitive
    circle cubes; root reran it and audited the proof.

    The four-row even-minor vector is also exactly `E=i s_Q gamma_Q`
    in the fixed cyclic convention, so `Norm(E)=Pi_Q`. Its factorization
    recovers precisely the pencil data of item 237 and supplies no extra
    arithmetic condition. No new general counting rate follows.

242. **Preserving the full quartet gcd can require an unbounded number of rows.**
    Actual primitive circle tuples with m distinct singleton source cuts
    can require every one of their m rows to preserve G. Take pairwise
    coprime blocks `kappa_j=2jMq+i` and rows
    `z_j=conjugate(kappa_j) product_{l!=j} kappa_l`. At a Gaussian prime
    of kappa_j to exponent e, the full G has exponent e, whereas deleting
    its unique exceptional row leaves exponent at least 2e in every
    matching. The block-norm coprimality and exact majority residues are
    proved in [the subset-extraction obstruction](global_content_subset_extraction_obstruction.md).
    An exact checker verifies the minimum preserving subsets for m=4..8,
    including a compact five-row fixture, and root reran it.

    The complete balanced source profile independently requires at least
    `ceil(m/2)+2` retained rows to preserve its zero source valuations in G:
    every cut must retain at least two rows on each side. This abstract
    threshold is exact for the source cuts, and is a lower bound for the
    actual full Gaussian gcd in the primitive realizations of item 239.
    Their global G is coprime to N, so the obstruction is not confined to
    the singleton factors E. Accidental primes may require more rows.
    Both construction families have diverging endpoint constants; neither
    disproves extraction under the actual C sqrt(R) hypothesis or improves
    the general count.

243. **Individual pair rotations and reflections have uniformly bounded integral domains on endpoint arcs.**
    For a pair rotation `rho=b/a=A/B` in reduced Gaussian integers,
    `H=Norm(B)|N` and its integral source domain is exactly `Z intersect B Z[i]`.
    Dividing that domain by B preserves an integral center. Equal-norm
    separation gives `sqrt(H)>=sqrt(2) R/|b-a|`, so on length L=C sqrt(R),
    `|S_(a->b)|<=1+L/sqrt(2H)<=1+L|b-a|/(2R)<1+C^2/2`.
    Thus `|S_(a->b)|<=ceil(C^2/2)`, and for C<=sqrt(2) its only
    source point is the starting anchor. No source primitivity or
    quarter-circle restriction is needed. See [the rotation-domain proof](pair_rotation_domain_capacity.md).
    Root checked the proof and reran the 21,664-domain audit: its Gaussian
    arithmetic and full-circle counts are exact; arc inequalities are
    numerical sanity checks with an explicit tolerance.

    For a pair-bisector reflection `sigma(z)=eta d/conjugate(d) conjugate(z)`,
    the integral domain is `Z intersect d Z[i]`, with D=Norm(d) dividing N.
    Divide that domain by d and adjoin its lattice-reflected image. For
    source angular width below pi/2, radial projection then gives
    `ceil(|S_ab|/2)-1<=C^2/(2sqrt(D))`, and for the internally paired
    subset A_ab gives `ceil(|A_ab|/2)-1<=C^2/(8sqrt(D))`.
    In particular `|S_ab|<=2+C^2/sqrt(D)` and
    `|A_ab|<=2+C^2/(4sqrt(D))`. Three domain rows require
    `D<=C^4/4`; three internally paired rows require `D<=C^4/64`.
    The diagonal-axis projection uses the exact parity
    `x+y == x-y == N/D mod 2`. See [the reflection-domain proof](pair_reflection_domain_capacity.md).
    Its checker verifies stronger sagitta inequalities using only integer
    arithmetic on 2,584 actual arcs and 7,064 anchor pairs; root reran it
    including the ceiling refinement.

    These results exclude positive-fraction descent by one or a bounded
    number of the specified symmetries: each acts integrally on only O_C(1)
    source rows. They do not bound the number of different domains.
    Balanced binary cut profiles of arbitrary size can already have every
    rotation domain equal to its starting anchor and every reflection
    domain equal to its two anchors. Hadamard profiles satisfy the analogous
    three-row exclusion with only linearly many coordinates. Their actual
    endpoint phase condition still has to be imposed. No new bound on the
    full cluster's growth rate follows.

244. **Fixed profiles with five separately determined block phases have bounded endpoint radius.**
    Let S be a fixed sign matrix in a Gaussian block representation,
    allowing independent row units, a common Gaussian multiplier, and
    shared prime support. Every block is required to be conjugate-coprime,
    and its norm contributes to `product_v n_v<=R^2`. A coordinate v is
    isolable when its standard vector belongs to the rational span of
    the row differences `S_i-S_0`. Equivalently, a fixed rational row
    lambda_v satisfies `lambda_v 1=0` and `lambda_v S=e_v`.

    Apply these rows to the lifted phase equations, retaining the integer
    lifts and independent row-unit terms. Every isolable block phase is
    within O_(S,C)(R^(-1/2)) of a member of a fixed finite set of rational
    multiples of pi. Roth's theorem, applied in a tangent or cotangent
    chart, gives `dist(arg(kappa),T)>=c |kappa|^(-2-epsilon)` for every
    conjugate-coprime nonunit block. Rational targets give a stronger
    bound; an exact target would force a unit or a factor 1+i and is
    excluded. Thus each such block has
    `n_v>=a R^(1/(2+epsilon))`. Five of them contradict the radius
    product for unbounded R when epsilon<1/2. The resulting threshold
    is finite but ineffective and depends on S,C.

    For a normalized Hadamard matrix H with constant column removed,
    `H^T H=mI` and `H^T1=0` provide the isolating rows directly. This
    excludes full fixed Hadamard profiles with at least five nonunit
    blocks even with independent row units. Existing common-unit
    elementary exclusions are stronger in their own scope and are
    acknowledged in [the proof and Roth reference](fixed_hadamard_roth_phase_obstruction.md).
    The extension also applies to any fixed sign matrix with five
    isolable nonunit coordinates. It does not require disjoint support,
    provided the displayed factorization and norm budget are valid.

    General balanced profiles can have many more columns than row
    differences and no isolable coordinates. The theorem therefore
    excludes a specified family of actual phase realizations, not all
    endpoint clusters. Root and an independent Sol audit checked the proof,
    including the unit terms, exact-target exclusion, shared-support case,
    and norm exponents. Exact rational checks verify the Walsh inverses
    through order 64. It proves no improvement in the general counting
    growth rate and has not been formalized in Lean.

245. **Coupled block products extend the fixed-target argument, with an exact packing limit.**
    For a fixed sign matrix S, let `V=span_Q{S_i-S_0}`. Each fixed
    integer vector v in V gives a Gaussian product of blocks or their
    conjugates whose phase is within O(R^(-1/2)) of a fixed finite
    root-of-unity direction set. Write e_jp for the signed valuation of
    block j at the two primes over p. Removing conjugate content is an
    ordinary positive integer cancellation, up to a recorded unit, and
    the reduced product has exact logarithmic norm
    `h(v)=sum_p |sum_j v_j e_jp| log p`.
    Its loss from `sum_j |v_j| log Norm(kappa_j)` is exactly
    `2 sum_p min(sum_j(v_j e_jp)_+,sum_j(-v_j e_jp)_+) log p`.
    These formulas allow shared primes and arbitrary nested layers.

    Only nonunit reduced products count toward a lower bound. For them
    Roth gives `h(v)>=log R/(2+epsilon)-O(1)`. Fixed nonnegative weights
    with `sum_t w_t |v_tj|<=1` in every column therefore exclude unbounded
    endpoint radius if `sum_t w_t>4`. A proved cancellation saving of
    delta times the total block log norm lowers the threshold to
    `4(1-delta)`. If a reduced product is an exact fixed ell_t-th Gaussian
    power, its root phase strengthens the weighted criterion to
    `sum_t w_t ell_t>4`. Units and root orders are retained explicitly.
    See [the coupled-product theorem](coupled_block_roth_packing.md).

    For all complete balanced cuts on M rows, the exact optimum over
    every integral vector in V is `2(M-1)/(M-2)<4`. The lower bound on
    each vector's mean absolute coefficient is `(M-2)/(2(M-1))`, and
    uniformly weighted pair-sum vectors attain the dual bound. This is
    the existing height classification applied to the new criterion,
    independently checked in [the phase-lattice audit](coupled_balanced_phase_l1_minimum.md).
    Root reran its exact checks for M=6,8,10. Repairing this optimum by
    cancellation would require a saving greater than
    `(M-3)/(2(M-2))`, approaching one half; disjoint support has none.
    The square-block subclass also admits the older elementary global
    square-root argument. No general saving or counting improvement is
    inferred from these conditional refinements.

246. **A primitive rank-one phase pattern is excluded, with an effective eleven-core growth bound.**
    Suppose the fixed sign matrix S has row-difference kernel `Q r`,
    with every coordinate of r equal to +1 or -1. Conjugating blocks
    where r is negative reduces the kernel to the constant vector.
    All block phases then share one moving parameter; pair differences
    remove it and have fixed finite rational-angle targets. The reduced
    pair product is a unit exactly when the two blocks are associates.

    Assume all k blocks are conjugate-primitive nonunits and the whole
    set of normalized row products has Gaussian gcd one. Every associate
    class has size at most `floor(k/2)`: prime-free and conjugate-prime-free
    rows must put the entire class on opposite sides of their common
    plus-count. A cyclic matching between classes gives pair weights
    of total k/2 with every block used to weight one. Thus k>=9 gives
    the strict Roth packing gain and bounds R for each fixed S,C.
    Shared primes and repeated block directions are allowed. If a unit
    block is present, five nonunit coordinates suffice by the earlier
    isolation theorem, without the whole-set primitivity hypothesis.

    For the 11-by-11 core of a normalized order-twelve Hadamard matrix,
    pair phases lie within half the arc's angular span Delta of
    `(pi/12)Z`. Integer linear and quadratic forms give the effective
    separation `dist(arg g,(pi/12)Z)>=1/(4 Norm(g))` for every
    conjugate-primitive nonunit g. Whole-set primitivity bounds each
    associate class by five, so an eleven-cycle of nonassociate pairs
    gives `R^2>=prod_j Norm(kappa_j)>=(1/(2 Delta))^(11/2)`. Therefore
    every such realization has

    ```text
    L >= (1/2) R^(7/11),
    R <= (2C)^(22/3)  if L <= C sqrt(R).
    ```

    These conclusions permit arbitrary row units and a common Gaussian
    multiplier; primitivity applies to the normalized row products,
    not individually to each point. See [the rank-one theorem and effective
    core proof](rank_one_kernel_relative_roth_obstruction.md). Root and
    an independent Astra audit checked the phase targets, prime-content
    argument, matching, and constants. Exact checks cover 55 Paley pair
    isolators, four quadratic derivative bounds, and 6101 class partitions.
    The coupled-product checker also passes 1491 exact cancellations,
    including 74 unit reductions, and nine power-root cases.

    This theorem requires the whole phase pattern: omitted columns of a
    submatrix can introduce uncontrolled moving row phases. It does not
    cover higher-dimensional phase kernels or prove extraction of a
    qualifying pattern from an arbitrary large endpoint cluster. It
    improves the arc growth exponent within the stated family, while the
    best general counting growth rate remains unchanged.

247. **Several moving phase groups admit a shared norm budget, including an effective varying family.**
    Let V be the full row-difference span and K its orthogonal kernel.
    A signed coordinate group I is usable when its signed indicator
    belongs to K and all signed coordinate differences within I belong
    to V. These conditions retain every source column. The first fixes
    the signed plus-count within the group; the second removes its moving
    phase from pair products. Whole-set Gaussian primitivity then bounds
    each associate class by half the group size, exactly as in item 246.
    Disjoint usable groups can be matched separately and their norm
    costs summed. Individually isolable nonunits and nonunits in a group
    containing a unit have weight one; coordinates in all-nonunit groups
    have weight one half. If their total weight P exceeds four, the
    fixed profile has bounded endpoint radius. More precisely, for each
    eta>0, `L>=c(S,eta) R^(1-(2+eta)/P)`.

    There is also an effective family whose constants do not depend on
    the number of moving parameters. Take b copies of the order-twelve
    Hadamard core, and interleave their ten successive row increments.
    This gives `10b+1` rows, `11b` columns, and kernel dimension b.
    The within-group pair certificates have denominator six and l1 norm
    at most twenty, uniformly in b. The elementary fifteen-degree
    separation and the common norm budget give

    ```text
    L >= (1/40) R^(1-4/(11b)),
    R <= (40C)^(22b/(11b-8))  if L <= C sqrt(R),
    C >= (1/40) 5^((11b-8)/4).
    ```

    All blocks in this explicit family are assumed conjugate-primitive
    nonunits, and the whole normalized row set has Gaussian gcd one.
    Repeated directions, shared primes, row units, and a common Gaussian
    multiplier are allowed. The last inequality uses the minimum block
    norm five and bounds b itself at fixed C. For two groups the arc
    growth exponent is 9/11. See [the group theorem and interleaved
    construction](partition_kernel_phase_groups.md).

    Root's exact checker verifies 550 full-space pair certificates,
    kernel dimensions for b=1,2,3,4, and all exponent identities. An
    independent Astra proof audit checked the general signed-group
    condition, mixed-unit deletion, phase targets, content, and constants.
    The theorem handles particular higher-dimensional kernels but does
    not extract them from arbitrary large clusters. Consequently the
    general counting growth rate is still unchanged.

248. **Unequal rank-one kernel weights have an exact power-class packing criterion.**
    For a fixed row-difference kernel `Q r` with every r_j nonzero,
    orient the columns so `a_j=|r_j|>0`. Two blocks are in the same
    power-direction class precisely when their signed prime valuations
    divided by a_j agree at every prime. If `d_C=gcd_{j in C}a_j`,
    unique factorization gives exact class roots
    `kappa_j=unit*rho_C^(a_j/d_C)`. Units remain outside the powers.
    Whole-set primitivity bounds each class's total a-weight by half
    the total weight. An antipodal transportation between classes can
    therefore give every vertex demand a_j.

    Write y_jh for that transportation. The primitive pair certificate
    uses coefficients `a_h/gcd(a_j,a_h)` and `-a_j/gcd(a_j,a_h)`.
    Its conjugate-primitive product is a forced power of order
    `lcm(a_j,a_h)/lcm(d_C,d_D)`. With certificate weight
    `y_jh/lcm(a_j,a_h)`, every coordinate has load one, and the exact
    amplified Roth weight is
    `P=sum_{j<h} y_jh/lcm(d_C(j),d_C(h))`. The condition P>4 excludes
    unbounded endpoint radius. The finite number of collision partitions
    makes the resulting constant uniform for fixed S,C.

    If all primitive kernel weights are at most B, then
    `P>=k/H_B`, where `H_1=2` and `H_B=2B-1` for B>=2. Thus nine
    blocks suffice for B=1, and `k>=8B-3` suffices for B>=2. If every
    class gcd is one, the stronger threshold `sum a_j>8` applies.
    These conclusions retain arbitrary row units, shared primes, and a
    common multiplier. They are fixed-profile statements; no bound on
    B is extracted from an arbitrary large cluster.

    With exactly two power classes, the row exponents lie on an integer
    line. Whole-set primitivity identifies the normalized products with
    a single primitive Gaussian rotation orbit and retains the exact
    radius `R=|d| |Gamma|^s`. For four distinct points in an angular
    interval shorter than pi/2, three successive orbit gaps give
    `L>=sqrt(2)R^(2/3)`. An arc at least pi/2 wide satisfies the same
    inequality directly for R>=1. Thus `R<=C^6/8` on an endpoint arc,
    independently of S and its kernel weights. This uses the existing
    elementary pair
    separation after a new exact classification of this degeneration;
    it is not a new general bounded-rank principle.

    See [the weighted power-class theorem](weighted_rank_one_power_class_packing.md).
    Root and an independent Astra audit checked the roots, units,
    fractional loads, strict gap, and two-class modulus. The exact checker
    passes 16144 transports, 71 power-divisibility cases, 132
    two-class integer-line cohorts, and 448 unit-inclusive orbit brackets.
    The general uniform bound remains
    unproved.

249. **The direct simultaneous monomial Subspace test has an exact height obstruction.**
    For Gaussian direction characters `chi_v` and any projective tuple
    `[chi_v0:...:chi_vq]`, the absolute logarithmic projective height is
    exactly
    `log H=(1/2)sum_p (max_t E_p(v_t)-min_t E_p(v_t))log p`.
    Denominator clearing is primitive at both primes above p; this formula
    retains shared primes, nested powers, unit cancellations, and common
    translations of the exponent tuple. It is a range cost, not the
    maximum of separately computed character heights.

    For complete balanced cuts and disjoint blocks of asymptotically
    equal logarithmic size, put `a_M=(M-2)/(2(M-1))`. Two distinct
    characters have mean range at least a_M; any three distinct
    characters have mean range at least `3a_M/2>=1/2`, by
    `range(0,a,b)=(|a|+|b|+|a-b|)/2`. Adding characters cannot reduce
    this range. These costs exceed `q/(2(q+1))`, the height ratio
    needed to trigger the standard monomial-vector Subspace inequality
    from only q first-order endpoint errors. The obstruction covers
    every finite tuple of distinct integral phase characters in an
    affine translate of the full phase lattice.

    See [the exact vector-height audit](monomial_vector_subspace_height_barrier.md).
    The theorem's normalization was checked against primary sources,
    including by real and imaginary parts when targets lie outside
    Q(i). Root checked the proof and reran 201 exact Gaussian projective
    heights, 1681 range identities, and 46 balanced configurations.
    This does not exclude smaller actual error products, extra finite
    place estimates, additive identities, higher jets, or nonmonomial
    constructions. Even a successful Subspace inequality would still
    leave exceptional subspaces to control. No endpoint realization of
    the balanced benchmark is claimed.

250. **Complete balanced cuts obstruct natural exact extraction even after regrouping.**
    For selected rows and retained columns, the omitted product can be
    absorbed into a common Gaussian multiplier and row units exactly
    when its prime valuation difference vanishes on every selected row:
    `(1/2)sum_omitted (S_ij-S_0j)e_jp=0` for every split prime p.
    With disjoint nonunit prime supports, every omitted column must
    therefore be constant on the selected rows.

    Allowing identical or complementary restricted columns to be
    regrouped does not produce a qualifying rank-one profile from the
    complete M=2k balanced-cut matrix. For t selected rows, the exact
    number of remaining nonconstant blocks is
    `b_red(M,t)=(1/2)sum_{h=max(1,t-k)}^{min(t-1,k)}binom(t,h)`.
    It is 0,1,3 for t=1,2,3, and exceeds t for every t>=4 when M>=6.
    Each regrouped block stays a conjugate-primitive nonunit under the
    disjoint-support hypothesis. The row-difference rank is at most
    t-1, so the larger profiles cannot have a one-dimensional kernel;
    the smaller ones cannot supply nine blocks.

    The full row-difference space also has no nonzero vector supported
    on at most two columns. A slice-exchange argument gives the same
    conclusion after restriction and regrouping whenever t>=4, so the
    signed groups of item 247 cannot be obtained that way either.
    See [the omitted-column and regrouping audit](complete_balanced_omitted_column_obstruction.md).
    Root corrected the valuation factor and required the regrouping
    step, then checked the all-size counting and slice arguments.
    An independent Astra audit checked the proof. The revised exact
    checker tests arbitrary two-support coefficients through kernel
    projection rank: 2695 original support tests and all reduced
    patterns for M=6,8 pass, accounting for 152 reduced classes.
    This is an obstruction to the specified operations, not to more
    general arithmetic transformations. Shared primes can change the
    cancellation criterion, and no endpoint realization of the disjoint
    balanced model is asserted. The general uniform bound is still
    unproved.

251. **The scalar/covolume obstruction holds in every positive multidegree.**
    For an even-total degree vector d on m>=4 supported rows, write
    `D=sum d_i=2E`, let r be the invariant-space dimension, let s be
    half the number of subsets of degree E, and put
    `A=D 2^(m-3)-sum_S max(0,d(S)-E)`. Whenever `max d_i<=E`,
    `A>=2 min(s,r-1)`. The inequality is strict for m>=5 and
    `max d_i<E`; the saturated case has r=1 and A=0.

    The proof removes every forced bracket power associated with a pair
    of degrees summing to more than E. Each removal preserves A and r
    and increases s by one. The residual degree cone has four explicit
    types of rays. Superadditivity of A and the balanced-subset antichain
    bound settle every m>=10. For m=5 through 9, exact ray minima reduce
    the entire remaining question to 32 positive integer vectors. Four
    rows reduce to equal degrees and satisfy `A=2(r-1)`. The exceptional
    odd-total five-row all-ones ray is treated separately: on that cone
    A=D, so a positive even integer total gives A>=6.

    In the actual full-cut model with negligible corrections and pair
    residues, the primitive evaluation height is `Aw+o(w)` and the
    complementary scalar threshold is `2w-o(w)`. The correct
    successive-minima denominator for a guaranteed outside-kernel
    relation is at most `min(s,r-1)`, including when numerical
    evaluation vanishes on the scalar kernel. Thus no choice of positive
    multidegree can give a strict height contradiction by this precise
    scalar/covolume argument. This does not bound individual irreducible
    numerical zeros lying in every scalar kernel, and near-uniform
    extraction alone does not guarantee the negligible corrections.

    See [the arbitrary-degree theorem](arbitrary_degree_scalar_height_obstruction.md),
    which supersedes the preliminary degree-one/two restriction.
    Root independently checked the forced-factor and cone proofs and
    enumerated all 32 residual vectors by direct subset masks and
    polynomial multiplication. The companion exact checker also passes
    all cone ratios, finite ray formulas, four-row identities, and 21
    forced-factor examples. This is a limitation of a method, not an
    improved general growth bound.

252. **Exact pair compatibility permits a bipartite near-critical graph.**
    For every M divisible by four with M>=12, split the rows into equal
    halves A,B. Assign distinct split primes to all cuts choosing half
    the rows in each half, with weights `T+O(1)`, and add a fixed-weight
    A|B cut. Actual primitive common-unit Gaussian tuples then satisfy
    the full endpoint-derived lower pair-norm bound, while the pairs
    satisfying the near-critical upper norm bound are exactly
    `K_(M/2,M/2)`. There are no good triangles, although every layer is
    balanced and the total pair log norm attains the Plotkin maximum.

    Good four-cycles have exact identities `F_1=q_1 G`, `F_2=q_2 G`,
    with coprime positive integers q_1,q_2 and one conjugate-primitive G.
    Each cancellation integer has logarithmic size `beta W+O(1)`,
    where `beta=M^2/(8(M-2)^2)<=0.18`. This is below the W/4 leading
    height available for the imaginary part of a product of two good
    factors even if each factor's imaginary part is bounded. The direct
    divisibility test therefore gives no growing residue lower bound.
    Odd source exponents prevent a square; rounding exponents to
    `1 mod 2ell` prevents any prescribed fixed ell-th power from being
    forced by these cycle identities.

    See [the bipartite compatibility construction](bipartite_pair_factor_compatibility_obstruction.md).
    Root and an independent Astra audit checked the norm/modulus
    exponents, primitive valuations, signature injectivity, and cycle
    reductions. The exact checker passes 400 source cuts, 36 good pairs,
    220 triangles, and 225 four-cycles on twelve rows; decimal logarithms
    additionally check one finite norm-window instance. The construction
    does not control angles or the small imaginary-coordinate conditions
    of an endpoint cluster. It is not a counterexample to the target;
    those simultaneous phase conditions remain available to a proof.

253. **One irreducible five-row relation has a height bound at every boundary node.**
    Let Q be an integer numerical-zero invariant of degree two in each
    of five rows in the actual full-cut Gaussian model. If Q is
    irreducible and its anticanonical curve passes through any of the
    fifteen boundary nodes, then
    `log C_Q>=2(1-eta)w-110sigma-2log T`.
    This is an individual-relation bound; it does not require two
    independent numerical zeros.

    At either incident pair boundary, irreducibility makes the
    restriction nonzero, and passage through the node makes it one
    integer coefficient times one outside difference. The actual
    specialization congruence therefore supplies an ordinary modulus
    for that coefficient, with loss `10sigma+log T`. Complement
    reflection supplies a coprime second modulus, with loss
    `100sigma+log T`. Their product gives the stated bound. All source
    prime powers and row corrections are retained.

    Consequently, below this coefficient threshold, the irreducible
    curve meets the ten boundary lines at ten distinct non-nodal
    rational points. In outside coordinates its restriction coefficients
    satisfy `alpha_S beta_S (alpha_S+beta_S)!=0` at all ten cuts.
    The two slope functionals at a node have joint rank two; there is
    no justification for multiplying both incident bounds into one
    coefficient. Support projection from M rows retains the amplification
    `w_5=2^(M-5)w_ambient`.

    See [the individual boundary-node bound](five_row_boundary_node_height.md).
    Root checked the specialization, coefficient modulus, reflection
    losses, irreducibility step, and inherited scale against the earlier
    odd-support and reflection proofs. The exact checker verifies all
    fifteen nodes and the six-dimensional invariant space using all
    twenty-two graph coordinates. The remaining non-nodal individual
    height bound is unproved; aggregate boundary heights alone cannot
    establish it, as the existing elliptic compatibility example shows.

254. **A product-of-halves symmetry gives a phase bound with moving prime supports.**
    Partition 2k common-unit rows into equal halves A,B. Suppose each
    nonconstant threshold layer either has equal counts in the two
    halves or is exactly A or B. The latter layers form one
    conjugate-primitive Gaussian factor Gamma of log norm V. Nested
    layers at a star prime cannot also be regular nonconstant layers.
    Multiplying the actual rows in each half isolates
    `(product_A z_i)/(product_B z_i)=(Gamma/bar Gamma)^k`.

    Put `W=log R^2`, let D be the complete common-factor log norm, and
    let `lambda=log(4/C^2)>=0`. Cross-pair and within-half averages of
    the strict endpoint pair-norm lower bound give
    `V>D+2lambda` and
    `V+D<W/k-2(k-1)lambda/k`.
    Thus Gamma is a nonunit, while its argument is within half the
    source angular width of the fixed grid `pi Z/k`. The fixed-target
    Roth bound forces `V>=W/(4+2epsilon)-O_(k,C,epsilon)(1)`.
    For every fixed k>=5 this contradicts the upper budget at large
    radius. Prime supports, weights, and powers may all vary.

    Twelve rows give an effective elementary specialization. The grid
    `pi Z/6` has only axis and quadratic slopes. Integer linear and
    quadratic forms give angular distance at least `1/(4 Norm Gamma)`.
    Combining this with the pair budget yields
    `L>(1/2)R^(2/3)` under the endpoint hypotheses, and more precisely
    `R<exp(-6D) C^26/2^14`. Hence this exact profile cannot occur at
    C<=1 on any nonzero integer circle. No good-pair graph assumption
    is required, so this excludes the endpoint realization of item 252
    even with unequal weights and moving supports.

    The exact low-row cases are stronger: four and eight rows in this
    profile are impossible for C<=2, and six rows are impossible for
    C<=sqrt(2). These follow from axis, diagonal, and quadratic-ray
    integer bounds, with the sharp within-half fraction 2/3 for six
    rows. They exclude every radius, not just sufficiently large ones.

    See [the half-symmetric phase-height theorem](half_symmetric_star_phase_height_gap.md).
    Root derived and checked the within-half budget, isolation branch,
    nested-prime separation, and effective constants. An independent
    Astra audit checked the final proof and every low-row constant;
    Luna also checked the corrected low-row cases. The exact checker
    passes 1262 cut incidences and 45 actual ten-row pair identities
    with a common unit and multiplier. The result needs
    exact equal-count symmetry in the remaining layers. An exceptional
    factor of small logarithmic height can still move the isolated
    target angle; a perturbative extension is not proved. No extraction
    of such a partition from an arbitrary large endpoint cluster is
    known, so the general growth bound is unchanged.

255. **Arbitrary short endpoint arcs have affine allocation rigidity of every order.**
    If C<=sqrt(2), the split-prime allocation vectors of all points on
    an arc of length `C sqrt(R)` are affinely independent over the
    reals, with arbitrary Gaussian units. For one literal common unit
    the assertion holds for C<=2. If r counts only primes at which
    the allocation varies, this gives the conditional count `M<=r+1`.

    The exact arbitrary-unit chord numerator is at least sqrt(2), so
    every distinct pair has `log P_ij>W/2` at the stated constants.
    Trim each allocation coordinate to width e_p and use the linear
    vector `f_i(p)=sqrt(e_p log p)(2b_i(p)/e_p-1)`. The elementary
    inequality `|a-b|<=a+b-2ab/e` gives
    `<f_i,f_j><=W_0-2log P_ij<0`. Unlike the threshold-layer embedding,
    this has only one coordinate per varying prime. Any real affine
    relation would equate positive sums on disjoint index sets, whose
    cross inner product is strictly negative, a contradiction.

    For R>1, taking norms and prime valuations converts every proposed
    multiplicative relation with Gaussian-unit value into such an
    affine relation. Thus the points are multiplicatively independent
    modulo units. Products of every common length are consequently
    distinct unless their multisets agree, with repetitions allowed.
    At R=1 the arc contains at most one point; equal-length rigidity
    still holds, while a single unit is torsion. This strengthens the
    earlier B_32 conclusion at C=1/2 without requiring a special cut
    profile. For general C, subdivision gives
    `M<=ceil(C/sqrt(2))(r+1)`.

    See [the general linear-allocation theorem](linear_allocation_affine_rigidity.md).
    Root derived the embedding and arbitrary-unit extension; Astra
    independently checked and wrote the proof, and Sol independently
    audited its final form. Root reran 45302 exact pair tests on 761
    actual circles and 7844 arcs in each unit regime, and checked a
    separate three-point example at squared radius 1786690 with
    normalized span below sqrt(2) and affine rank three.
    This is a linear improvement in the conditional prime-rank bound,
    not an improved asymptotic growth rate in R: r can still grow, and
    complete balanced and fair patterns already have full affine rank.
    The requested uniform bound remains unproved.

256. **Full prime rank bounds every moving allocation width.**
    Fix r,C and suppose the allocation rows have affine rank r across
    all r varying split primes. Their widths e_j are bounded by an
    effective constant depending only on r,C. This hypothesis is
    automatic at minimal support r=M-1 in the small-arc unit regimes
    of item 255, but not for arbitrary C or a general fair profile.

    Choose an invertible allocation-difference matrix B and write
    H=max e_j, Delta=det B, J=adj B. Exact phase inversion, retaining
    arbitrary row units and the complete common divisor, gives
    `|4Delta phi_j-pi m_j|<=2r! C H^(r-1) exp(-W/4)` with
    `max(2|Delta|,|m_j|)<=(2+2C)r! H^r`. The coefficient bound does not
    involve the unbounded phase lifts or prime heights. Matveev's
    two-logarithm estimate in degree two, applied to a prime of maximum
    width, gives `H<A(r,C) log(2H)`, hence `H<4A(r,C)^2`.

    Once widths are bounded, all prime phases approach one fixed finite
    rational-pi grid. Roth with epsilon=1/4 gives `p_j>=a R^(4/9)`.
    Multiplying with the actual exponents yields bounded R whenever
    `sum e_j>=5`. This radius bound is generally ineffective. At
    minimal support the primitive positive central weights also have
    bounded total denominator, relative to the moving common divisor.
    Actual Gaussian norm-only examples have central denominator e+3
    unbounded, confirming that the phase input is essential.

    See [the full-prime-rank width theorem](minimal_prime_rank_width_bound.md).
    Astra derived the proof; root and Sol independently checked the
    original Matveev Corollary 2.3 specialization, including
    `2^32*32*log(2e)<2^40`. Luna checked the finite-grid and central-weight
    algebra. The checker passes 1105 exact matrices, 249 literal phase
    inversions and seven norm-only examples. There is no full-column-rank
    assertion for the many-prime general case.

257. **One exactly isolable whole sign pattern suffices for fixed M>=9.**
    For C<=sqrt(2) with arbitrary units, or C<=2 with one literal common
    unit, group all threshold layers of the same unoriented cut into
    one conjugate-primitive Gaussian block Gamma_S. Its norm weight
    satisfies `V_S<=2W_var/M` by the obtuse Bessel inequality. This
    includes arbitrary nested prime powers: a chain cannot contain both
    orientations of the same nonconstant cut.

    If the standard coordinate for this whole pattern lies in the
    rational row-difference span, an exact signed product of source
    rows isolates `(Gamma_S/bar Gamma_S)^(h/2)`, up to a recorded unit.
    All other layers cancel primewise, including layers sharing a prime
    with the target. The target phase lies within a fixed multiple of
    the source angular width of a finite rational-pi grid. Roth gives
    `V_S>=W/(4+2epsilon)-O(1)`. For M>=9 this contradicts the Bessel
    upper bound at unbounded radius. Finite sign matrices at fixed M
    make the bound uniform over all supports and certificates.

    A centered positive-definite Gram matrix gives a sufficient
    criterion for several exceptional columns; neither balance nor
    mutual orthogonality of those columns is required. Their inverse
    pairing affects the error constant, not the radius exponent.
    The row-difference rank is M-1 by item 255. Consequently an unbounded
    fixed-M sequence in these regimes must have at least M distinct
    sign classes. This is a pattern-count restriction separate from
    the prime-count restriction, since one prime can have several layers.

    See [the isolable-pattern theorem](isolable_pattern_bessel_phase_gap.md).
    Root supplied the Bessel refinement, Sol wrote and extended the
    theorem, and Astra independently audited the exact cancellation,
    units, centered pairing and finite-profile quantifiers. The checker
    passes a 28-column literal source with nested regular layers,
    nonorthogonal pairings of ranks two through four, a centered
    unbalanced example, and a singular pairing witness. Full fair
    patterns can have no isolable coordinate and are not excluded.

258. **Full-cut affine products cannot extract a nontrivial half symmetry.**
    Take complete nonunit source cut blocks with disjoint rational-prime
    supports, and integer output coefficient rows of degree one. For
    fixed output halves A,B of size k>=2, a valuation vector has only
    equal-count or star threshold layers exactly when its half-value
    multisets agree, or it is constant on each half. All source subset
    sums must obey this condition if the outputs have exact half symmetry.

    If one subset sum is a nonconstant star, adding an outside source
    coefficient column or subtracting an inside column forces that
    column to be constant on each half. Otherwise two equal finite
    multisets receive different translations, which cannot produce
    either equal multisets or a star. Thus every coefficient column is
    half-constant, and the formal products repeat within each half.
    Distinct outputs therefore have no star layers. Their cross-pair
    average is at most W_var/2, contradicting the endpoint pair lower
    bound for C<=sqrt(2) arbitrary units or C<=2 common unit.

    The [four-output argument](affine_full_fair_to_half_symmetric_obstruction.md)
    uses singleton and pair cuts to exclude distinct half-symmetric
    products even without the endpoint hypothesis. The
    [all-size extension](full_cut_affine_star_extraction_obstruction.md)
    requires the no-star alternative: six distinct degree-one outputs
    can have every subset sum regular, as the explicit Gaussian example
    demonstrates. It is the endpoint pair inequality that excludes
    those regular-only outputs.

    Luna proved the four-output case, root proved the all-size extension,
    and both Luna and Astra independently audited that extension. The checkers pass
    1200 cross-partition pairs, 7371 threshold profiles, 4428 shifted
    multisets, all sixteen subset sums of the six-output example, and
    its exact primitive Gaussian norm budget. Shared-prime source
    layers and uncontrolled correction factors are explicitly outside
    this extraction obstruction. No source endpoint counterexample
    or general counting theorem follows.

259. **Five rows of total primitive width at most four have an endpoint gap.**
    In the weighted four-cube, every five vertices contain a pair at
    distance at most half the total coordinate weight. Under the
    contrary assumption there are no Hamming-one or complementary
    pairs. Elementary classification then leaves only XOR translates
    of zero together with the four weight-three vertices. Their six
    leaf-pair distances sum to three times the total weight, giving
    the contradiction.

    Apply this to the actual prime-threshold encoding when
    `E=sum e_p<=4`, padding with zero weights. Some pair has
    `P_ij<=sqrt(N_0)=R/|d|`, where d is the complete common Gaussian gcd.
    The exact chord bound gives
    `L>sqrt(2|d|) sqrt(R)` with arbitrary units and
    `L>2sqrt(|d|) sqrt(R)` in one literal common unit class.
    No affine-rank or limiting hypothesis is needed.

    Together with item 256 this gives bounded radius for every fixed
    minimal-support M>=5 in the stated small-arc regimes: E>=5 is
    covered by the width/Roth theorem, and the remaining M5,E4 case
    is excluded by the cube lemma. The alternative determinant proof
    has `|det B|<=3` and only quadratic phase targets, but gives a
    weaker constant and needs full affine rank.

    See [the five-point primitive-width gap](four_width_five_point_endpoint_gap.md).
    Astra proved the classification and radius bookkeeping; root
    independently checked both and the auxiliary quadratic argument.
    The checker exhausts all 4368 five-vertex subsets, the 16 exceptional
    translates, and the determinant distribution, with 682 literal
    Gaussian pair certificates and 600 quadratic-grid checks. The
    general problem has no bound on total width or minimal prime support.

260. **A full fair core forces a large reduced half-product correction.**
    In an exact disjoint full-cut core, remove the genuine A/B star
    contribution from the quotient of the k rows in A by the k rows
    in B. Let H be the conjugate-primitive numerator of the remaining
    norm-one quotient, and let K_i be the actual correcting row factors.
    Exact oriented valuations, including cancellation by those factors,
    give
    `log Norm(H)>=sum_(S nonstar) |q(S)|w_S-sum_i log Norm(K_i)`,
    where `q(S)=|S intersect A|-|S intersect B|`.

    The complete-cut imbalance coefficient is
    `B_k=(k/2)(binom(2k,k)-2)`, equal to 4,27,136,2766 for
    k=2,3,4,6. For fixed k with w_S=w+o(w) and small row corrections,
    this is a positive radius-scale lower bound. Retaining the complete
    common Gaussian divisor gives `W=D+Bw+o(w)`,
    `B=2^(2k-1)-1`. The actual endpoint pair inequalities imply
    `D<=w+o(w)`, so
    `log Norm(H)/W>=B_k/(B+1)-o(1)`.
    For eight rows the coefficient is 17/16; it improves to 136/127
    only when D=o(w). The displayed divisor in a core factorization
    need not be complete; its discrepancy is bounded by the total
    correcting norm and has been included in the proof.

    See [the forced correction-height theorem](full_fair_half_product_correction_height.md).
    Astra proved the valuation and counting formulas; root independently
    checked cancellation, norm conventions, all common-content terms,
    and the passage from relative row corrections to the original radius.
    Exact checks cover seven- and 31-cut Gaussian examples with arbitrary
    units and deliberate cancellation at a singleton core prime. The
    eight-row full-core extraction cannot supply a correction of height
    o(W) for a moving-target version of the half-symmetric argument.
    This does not rule out a different arithmetic use of that correction.

261. **Every short integral pattern relation is excluded at large endpoint radius.**
    Let L_S be the intersection of Z^T with the rational row-difference
    space of the exact whole-pattern sign matrix. For fixed M,C in the
    unit regimes of item 255, every sufficiently large endpoint cluster
    satisfies `8||v||_1>=M` for each nonzero v in L_S. This strengthens
    item 257 from a standard coordinate to every short integer vector,
    in arbitrary corank and with shared nested primes permitted.

    Clear a row certificate `lambda^t S=2t v`, with sum lambda=0.
    Its exact signed row product equals
    `u(Beta_v/bar Beta_v)^t`, where Beta_v is the conjugate-primitive
    reduction of the actual block product. Item 255 makes this reduction
    nonunit whenever v is nonzero: otherwise a nontrivial signed product
    of the source points would be a unit, contradicting affine allocation
    independence. This uses only the earlier elementary chord argument,
