    so there is no circular use of Roth.

    Bessel gives `log Norm(Beta_v)<=2W||v||_1/M`; its isolated fixed-grid
    phase gives `log Norm(Beta_v)>=W/(4+2epsilon)-O(1)` by Roth.
    A vector with `8||v||_1<M` supplies a strict power gap. For fixed M
    there are finitely many matrices and short integral vectors, so the
    radius bound is uniform over all prime supports and allocation widths.

    In corank one, with positive primitive kernel weights a_j, every pair
    must consequently have `8(a_j+a_h)/gcd(a_j,a_h)>=M` at large radius.
    For M>=17 the weights are pairwise distinct. Affine rigidity gives
    T=M, so their maximum is at least M and their sum at least M(M+1)/2.
    The preliminary incomparable-cut qualifier is unnecessary on actual
    endpoint arcs: all-order independence excludes the unit collision
    even for nested cuts.

    See [the integer pattern-lattice minimum](corank_one_local_bessel_pair_filter.md).
    Sol derived the pair test; root integrated all-order independence
    to obtain the general lattice statement and remove the extra
    comparability hypothesis. Astra independently checked that step
    and its noncircularity. A 64-row Walsh construction has primitive
    kernel weights 3,5,32 and a length-two certificate, so it is excluded.
    The checker verifies its exact signed Gaussian product and all 2016
    pair norm inequalities with arbitrary units and common content.
    Its arguments are uncontrolled; the example demonstrates a gap in
    norm-only tests, not an endpoint construction. Root also proved that
    the complete full-fair matrix has exact lattice minimum `2^(M-2)`:
    its characters are integer zero-sum subset sums, and pairing subsets
    with and without one nonzero coordinate gives the lower bound;
    a two-label difference attains it. The checker verifies 216 short
    coefficient vectors and the sharp pair examples. Thus the full-fair
    profile passes this test, and no general growth improvement follows.

262. **A single five-row section has exact boundary-scale compatibilities.**
    The [boundary slope table](five_row_boundary_slope_relations.md)
    gives all ten pairs `(alpha_S,beta_S)` in six fixed graph coordinates,
    with the explicit convention `Delta_ij=Y_i X_j-X_i Y_j`. All fifteen
    pairs of incident boundary lines satisfy one signed shared-node
    identity. For each such pair, the four coefficient functionals have
    exact rank three, so that identity is their only linear relation.
    The resulting map to the two projective slope ratios is dominant:
    two generic slope pairs can be scaled to obey the common-node
    hyperplane and then lifted to a section. Thus the node alone imposes
    no algebraic equation on those two ratios. Its compatibility retains
    the relative scales, and supplies no new scalar coefficient modulus.
    Luna derived the table and exact rank checks. Root corrected the
    initial mixed-sign identities and required explicit verification of
    the displayed list and exact rational elimination; the repaired
    checker passes all fifteen identities and rank-three tests.

263. **The generic boundary numerator retains an exact small-area frame.**
    The [shared-triplet factorization](five_row_shared_triplet_residue_obstruction.md)
    writes each nonnodal numerator as `C_abc(alpha U+beta V)`, with
    integral Gaussian `U,V`. Removing its forced core leaves eight
    oriented blocks in each term, of modulus `exp(4w+o(w))`. Exactly
    `Norm C_abc=G_ab G_ac G_bc`, so
    `Im(U bar V)=-r_ab r_ac r_bc t_ab t_ac t_bc` is a nonzero integer
    of absolute value at most `exp(12sigma)T^3`. The binary norm form
    has discriminant minus four times this integer's square. Therefore
    the numerator cannot vanish for nonzero real coefficients, but a
    short nonzero combination is not excluded. Complement reflection
    gives an exact high-height renormalization of its conjugate; the
    complementary core divisibility of the original numerator was
    already trivial. All twenty residual core monomials are distinct.
    These facts explain why literal stacking or conjugation alone does
    not yield a coefficient-height gain. Sol derived the factorization
    and reflection identity; Astra independently derived the area
    cancellation, and root checked the correction charges and scope.
    The exact checker retains all thirty-two cuts, integer primitive
    residues, and the Gram, discriminant, reflection and shear identities.
    This recovers the existing short-frame obstruction and is not a
    positive result on the general growth rate.

264. **Singular and ramified actual points force an individual coefficient gap.**
    For an irreducible five-row numerical-zero invariant, the
    [singular-point argument](five_row_singular_point_height.md) proves
    `8log C_Q+80sigma+20log T >= (10-70eta)w-log32`
    whenever the actual moduli point is singular. In the normalized
    chart `F(a,b)`, its coefficient sum is at most `C_Q` and its

    singular coordinates by `2log C_Q`, and the twenty-two graph

    Comparing with the audited full-cut height gives the stated gap.
    A rationally irreducible but geometrically reducible section has

    the same gap applies without a geometric irreducibility assumption.

    More generally, ramification of any one of the five forgetful maps

    The discriminant bounds the retained coordinate, and
    `a=-B(b)/(2A(b))` bounds the other, with `A(b)!=0` forced by

    bound applies if even one `lambda_i` is zero. Below it, the
    actual point is smooth and all five forgetful maps are unramified.
    Root and Astra independently derived the singular bound; Astra
    audited the ramification extension and constants. Exact checks
    cover 242 discriminant identities in both variables, rational
    singular fixtures, twenty chart-height examples, and a smooth

    Luna also constructed a geometrically integral anticanonical

    This excludes additional strata of an individual relation. It

265. **Every gradient multiplier has an exact 24w ordinary core divisor.**
    The [gradient discriminant dictionary](five_row_gradient_discriminant_core_count.md)

266. **All five reduced multipliers can satisfy the stress constraints at exponent six.**
    The [cofactor stress construction](five_row_gradient_cofactor_stress_obstruction.md)

    minor is the corresponding product of three G_i and three actual

    Two four-support cofactor circuits, divided by that common

    It also gives an ordinary affine stress on the actual five unit
    circle points `P_i/bar(P_i)`, so circular sign constraints alone

267. **Five-row boundary restrictions are exactly integer Petersen circulations.**
    The [circulation dictionary](five_row_petersen_circulation.md)
    identifies the ten boundary lines with the Petersen vertices and
    the fifteen shared-node coefficients with signed edge flows.
    Opposite endpoint coefficients agree with opposite signs; each
    vertex has coefficients `(alpha,beta,-alpha-beta)`, so the flow
    is conserved. The incidence rank is nine and the cycle rank six.
    The full twenty-two-graph map has a maximal minor of determinant
    minus one, identifying the entire integer invariant lattice with
    the saturated cycle lattice. Each pentagon graph gives a primitive
    five-cycle flow; each triangle times squared edge gives a primitive
    six-cycle flow. The first six displayed graph coordinates generate
    only the index-two, even-parity sublattice; that restriction does
    not apply to general integer Q. The fifteen gluing equations have
    rank fourteen, and `sum_S F_S(z)=0` in common variables exactly.

    The [slope-cycle equations](five_row_petersen_slope_cycles.md)
    then eliminate the vertex scales. On the nonnodal open set,
    propagate nonzero scales along a spanning tree. Five of its six
    chord gluings are necessary and sufficient: vertex conservation
    makes the sum of all edge mismatches zero, so the last mismatch
    vanishes automatically. Omitting the longest fundamental cycle
    gives five equations of degree at most six. For example,
    `r13 r45 (r23+1)(r25+1)=r23(r14+1)` follows from the five-cycle
    `23-14-25-13-45-23`. The resulting circulation determines a
    section uniquely up to scale; rational slopes give a rational

    Luna computed the circulation and cycle identities, root proved

    Exact checks cover the integral minors, all primitive graph cycles,

268. **An exact Vieta replacement transfers the core but leaves a residue-growth cost.**
    The [root-swap audit](five_row_vieta_swap_content_and_residue_audit.md)
    fixes four rows of one invariant and replaces the fifth by the
    second rational root. In a determinant-one integer frame `(P_i,u)`,
    the resulting nonzero binary quadratic is `s(lambda_i t+C_i s)`.
    Its ordinary content is `g_i=gcd(lambda_i,C_i)`, and its primitive
    second root is `(C_i P_i-lambda_i u)/g_i`. This is independent
    of the chosen frame and has bracket `-lambda_i/g_i` with the old
    root. For each retained row,
    `q_i(P_j)=g_i Delta_ij Delta'_ij` exactly. The ramification gap
    ensures distinct roots for sufficiently small irreducible Q.

    The actual zero increases the quadratic's forced content from
    weight fourteen to nineteen. Precisely,
    `F_i|g_i Norm(K_i)`, with inside cut exponent
    `max(0,2|U\{i}|-5)` and outside exponent
    `max(0,2|U\{i}|-4)`. Put `E_i=g_i Norm(K_i)/F_i`.
    Sixteen inherited oriented blocks divide `E_i P_i'`, and eleven
    of them are shared with each retained row. The norm of the lost
    core divides the ordinary integer E_i, allowing its full loss to
    cancel in the new primitive residue estimate:
    `|t'_ij|<=2 C_Q exp((2+78eta)w+5beta+2sigma)`.
    This permits exponent-two residue growth, while the extracted
    regime requires a subexponential residue budget. The new row's
    modulus allowance has exponent thirteen, compared with
    exponent eight for the original row. For irreducible Q, a collision
    with a retained row forces
    `log C_Q >= (4-28eta)w-6beta-log8`, by its nonzero boundary
    restriction and the retained four-point matching height. Below
    that threshold the new residues are nonzero, but their upper
    exponent remains two.

    Radius changes are charged through the original Gaussian anchor
    `z_0`, with `z_j/z_0=P_j/bar(P_j)` and
    `R=sqrt(Norm z_0)`. If the reduced new phase denominator is B,
    the exact required anchor multiplier is
    `B/gcd_G(B,z_0)`, up to a unit. Its modulus is at most
    `4sqrt(6) C_Q exp((5+75eta)w+3beta+4sigma)/sqrt(E_i)`;
    this allows a positive radius-growth exponent. Replacing it with an ordinary
    lcm of row norms would lose the source radius normalization.
    Neither integrality on the original circle nor preservation of
    its short arc follows from the rational root swap. Root proposed
    the replacement; Luna independently checked the primitive-root
    algebra, and Sol and Astra derived and cross-audited the content,
    core transfer and residue bounds. Two independent exact checkers
    each cover ten literal full-cut replacements, including shared
    corrections. Their vanishing invariants have unrestricted height,
    so these fixtures verify identities and do not produce endpoint
    examples. A low-height algebraic fixture also shows that a swap
    can change the row norm or collide with another row outside the
    sufficiently small full-cut regime. No descent or general
    improvement in the point-count growth rate is claimed.

269. **The five simultaneous other roots have one complete projective compatibility equation.**
    For five distinct old directions at an unramified zero of one
    degree-two-each invariant, the
    [common-section root identity](five_row_simultaneous_vieta_identity.md)
    proves
    `sum_(i<j) det(v_i,v_j)det(v_i',v_j') /
    (det(v_i,v_i')det(v_j,v_j'))=6`.
    All five replacements hold the other four old rows fixed.
    In an affine chart, write `lambda_i=partial_i Q`,
    `a_i=partial_i^2 Q/2`, `d_i=product_(j!=i)(x_i-x_j)`.
    A complete polynomial certificate gives
    `6d_i lambda_i-sum_j d_j(2x_i+3x_j-S)a_j=K_i Q`,
    with an explicit symmetric cubic K_i. Combining this with the
    three infinitesimal invariance equations proves the sum-six
    identity, including infinite new roots.

    The value-plus-five-diagonal-Hessian matrix of the six graph
    sections has exact determinant
    `6 product_(i<j)(x_j-x_i)^2`. Hence the sum-six equation is also
    sufficient on its unramified open locus: its rank-one two-by-two
    moment matrix reconstructs `(A,B)`, then the gradients
    `(Ax_i+B)/d_i`, and then one unique Q up to scalar. Rational
    directions give rational coefficients, with no small-height
    conclusion. Root proved the thirty polynomial identities and
    determinant; Luna, Sol and root independently checked signs,
    root extraction and projective normalization. Exact fixtures
    cover reconstruction and infinite roots. This exhausts algebraic
    compatibility of the five projective swaps on the stated open
    locus, while leaving their primitive integer contents uncontrolled.

270. **Simultaneous swaps force one nearby direction but no arithmetic growth saving.**
    The [joint cut table](five_row_simultaneous_vieta_cut_patterns.md)
    has selected incidences `0,3,2,5,5` at old cut sizes one through
    five. Each row selects sixteen blocks and shares eleven with a
    retained row. The six size-four-or-five blocks are common only
    at the level of `E_i P_i'`; they need not divide the primitive
    swapped rows. The exact product of inherited contents has cut
    exponents `0,0,4,8,15`. A single old anchor cancels the lcm of
    inherited denominator blocks, but cannot be counted five times
    against a product of new denominators.

    The [real and valuation consequences](five_row_vieta_crossratio_near_swap_obstruction.md)
    of item 269 give one affine shift smaller than four times the
    old diameter, hence one new phase within a fixed multiple of the
    original short-arc width. They also give one pair cross-ratio
    term with absolute value at least `3/5`. A rational family has
    four shifts equal to T and the remaining shift tending to `-5/3`.
    The converse in item 269 reconstructs its common Q; an exact
    modulo-eleven discriminant certificate and nonzero boundary
    restrictions show that arbitrarily large T retain geometric
    irreducibility and boundary nonnodality. Thus even on that
    stratum the projective identity cannot force two nearby swaps.
    These fixtures have no small-coefficient full-cut hypothesis.
    Every cross-ratio term also cancels the rescaling
    `P_i' -> E_i P_i'` exactly, so the identity alone cannot select
    a row with large exceptional integer content. Charging the actual
    source radius and transferred gcd still permits primitive
    residue exponent `9/4`, which is weaker than the existing
    exponent-two bound; the radius-multiplier allowance is unchanged.
    At every core cut, at least six cross-ratio terms have no
    formally forced core factor. This is a degree count, not an
    assertion that those actual terms are prime-adic units.

    The original anchor coordinates give an additional upper bound.
    If `S=max_j|Y_j|`, the X-squared coefficient of the row quadratic
    is exactly `g_i Y_i Y_i'` and is at most
    `2C_Q S^2 exp(24(1+eta)w+3beta)` in absolute value.
    Unless the new point collides with the original anchor, this
    gives
    `E_i <= 2C_Q S^2 exp((5+43eta)w+3beta+2sigma)/|Y_iY_i'|`.
    Thus negligible original imaginary numerators limit E_i to
    exponent five; this supplies no lower bound on E_i or descent.
    Luna derived the joint cut table, Sol proved and checked the
    near-root, anchor-coordinate and formal valuation consequences,
    and root derived and audited
    the distinction between projective direction and primitive

271. **Every core-divisible gradient stress lifts to one integer section with only correction-scale index.**
    The [first-jet lifting theorem](five_row_first_jet_integral_lifting.md)
    takes the integral kernel of the six graph evaluations to the
    saturated lattice `K=ker_Z[G_i(X_i^2,X_iY_i,Y_i^2)^t]` by
    `Q -> (lambda_i/G_i)_i`. Its exact image index is
    `I=epsilon delta rho`, where `epsilon in {1,3}`,
    `delta|B^2`, `rho|B`, and `B=product_(i<j)b_ij`.
    Thus `I|3B^3` and `I<=3exp(30beta)`, with no w term.

    Every three-column minor of the value/first-jet map factors as
    the signed complementary triangle times one of twenty
    degree-four-each sections. These twenty sections form an
    index-three sublattice of the sixteen-dimensional integral
    quadratic-product lattice. If g is the evaluation gcd, their
    evaluation gcd is `epsilon g^2`. The exact image index is
    `s a_0/(g product_i G_i)`, where a_0 is the Veronese-cofactor
    gcd. The forced factors cancel through
    `product_i G_i=D_0 L`, with respective equal-weight logs
    `120w=30w+90w`. The residual factors delta and rho are bounded
    prime by prime using graphs and triples attaining each cut's
    minimum order; pair corrections may overlap arbitrarily.

    Multiplication by I therefore realizes any integral stress as
    gradients of a single integer numerical-zero Q. The earlier
    full-support cofactor stress lifts with normalized gradient
    bound `15exp(6(1+eta)w+33beta)`. This controls its gradient,
    not its coefficient height. Astra proved and checked the
    integral factorization and index; root independently audited
    the homogeneous argument, lattice-index formula and divisibility
    estimates. Verification includes all two hundred complete
    chart-polynomial identities, six hundred additional literal
    minors and three explicit integral lifts. The remaining issue
    is the position of the coefficient preimage lattice, not an
    unaccounted growing index at the clean core primes.

272. **A clean split-prime frame can create excess content missed by normalized resultants.**
    The [literal content obstruction](five_row_vieta_clean_prime_content_obstruction.md)
    uses one fixed geometrically irreducible section with graph
    coefficients `(35,50,-4,-4,-4,-4)` and `C_Q=1884`.
    Its normalized chart is
    `(81-27b)a^2+(19b^2-84b-39)a+15b^2+35b`.
    At `(a,b)=(2,3)` all five row multipliers are nonzero; the
    other a-root is infinity. All fifteen boundary-node values,
    all five normalized multipliers and the coefficient gcd 120
    are units modulo 29. Its discriminant is squarefree there.

    For `n=29^m`, the exact Gaussian frame uses `H=(5+2i)^m`
    and primitive rows `-1,-r+i,-r-2n+i,-r-4n+i,-r-6n+i`,
    with even r chosen so the four nonconstant rows have exactly
    H as their 29-primary oriented core. All ten old primitive
    pair residues have absolute value at most six and their pair
    correction product is 768, independently of m. The moving
    row's quadratic is `480n^2 Y(X+(r+4n)Y)`, giving
    `g_i=480n^2`, `F_i=n`, and `v_29(E_i)=m`.
    The extra factor is a frame effect and an other-root collision,
    despite good normalized coefficients and boundary data.

    This is not a full-fair profile: only one block grows and
    `sigma=(log n)/2+O(1)`, `log E_i=2log n+O(1)`.
    It therefore does not refute a global estimate charging the
    correction height. Root identified the possible frame loss;
    Astra constructed the fixed section and six exact prime-power
    fixtures. Root audited the algebra and requested the prime-29
    strengthening to remove bad boundary reduction as an explanation.
    The checker derives the discriminant from the actual polynomial
    and verifies all unit, content, Gaussian-gcd and residue claims.
    A coefficient resultant alone does not control these contents.

273. **The normalized Vieta height is controlled, but the actual moving-frame content is not.**
    The [normalized-height and frame calculation](five_row_elliptic_vieta_frame_obstruction.md)
    gives the elementary inequality
    `h(a')<=2h(b)-h(a)+log C_Q+(log6)/2`
    for the two rational roots of a nonzero row quadratic in the
    normalized bidegree-(2,2) chart. It includes infinite roots and
    requires no elliptic smoothness or height comparison. In the
    asymptotic full profile this already gives `h(a')<=4w+o(w)`.
    Root proposed the binary-factor bound; Astra proved its exact
    coefficient-norm certificate and audited the normalization.

    The primitive matrix restoring three actual retained rows is
    `M=(Delta_bc P_a,Delta_ca P_b)/d`, where
    `d=gcd_Z(Delta_bc,Delta_ca)`. Its height is `12w+o(w)` and
    its determinant has log `16w+o(w)`. The old normalized vector
    has height `4w+o(w)` and acquires ordinary content
    `exp(8w+o(w))` under M. For any new primitive vector v', the
    exact height correction is
    `log(||Mv'||/||v'||)-log gcd_Z(Mv')`.
    The normalized bound alone therefore allows row height
    `16w+o(w)` before this content, weaker than the existing
    `13w-log E_i+o(w)` estimate. A fixed-Q unimodular frame family
    proves that a Q-only error cannot replace this moving-frame term.

    On a fixed smooth elliptic section the forgetful involutions
    are `iota_i(P)=T_i-P`. For their degree-two canonical heights,
    the exact difference is
    `F_j(iota_i P)-F_j(P)=-4<P-T_i/2,T_i-T_j>`.
    The note retains all coordinate-comparison constants when Q
    moves; this identity does not control the integer frame content.
    Root audited the signs, exact frame formulas and scope. The
    checker proves the polynomial norm identity, checks 9,216
    primitive factor pairs, 3,840 labelled cut cases and 360 exact
    frame/content cases. No radius or residue exponent improves.

274. **Actual prime-weight obtuse boxes have linear support and radius cost `O(M log M)`.**
    The [prime-weight countermodels](strict_obtuse_prime_box_countermodels.md)
    show that strict weighted obtuseness, prime integrality, width one,
    and all lower chord-packing inequalities cannot alone force
    superlinear prime support or `log R/(M log M)` to diverge.
    For Walsh order M, distinct split primes in one relative-width
    `1/(M-1)` interval give `r=M-1`, affine rank `M-1`, and
    `log R=(2+o(1))M log M`. The nonzero Gram eigenvalues are
    exactly `M log p_j`. Existence of the nearby primes follows by
    pigeonholing a dyadic interval using the fixed-modulus prime
    number theorem, without a short-interval theorem.

    Five copies of each Walsh column, with one injectively assigned
    bit flip per row, have `r=5(M-1)` and
    `log R=(10+o(1))M log M`. All unordered pair difference supports,
    hence pair norms, are distinct. In both constructions
    `P_ij^2/N>256(M-1)^4/C^4`, so every common-unit integer chord
    lower bound fits below the corresponding chord of an abstract
    equally spaced endpoint arc. The literal Gaussian realizations
    have common row unit and complete common gcd one, but their
    actual arguments are uncontrolled. These are countermodels to
    norm-only deductions, not endpoint counterexamples.
    Astra constructed the families; root audited the proof and ran
    308 exact pair tests, including Gaussian norms and gcds.

275. **Hadamard augmentations have short integer characters with a small explicit denominator.**
    The [Hadamard character construction](hadamard_augmentation_short_character.md)
    treats `S=[H_0,F]`, where `H_0` is an order-M Hadamard core and
    F has k extra columns. Parseval bounds the integer Fourier
    vectors `w_j=(H_0^t F)_j`. A collision of two q-subset sums
    gives nonzero `v in {0,+1,-1}^{M-1}`, `ell=||v||_1<=2q`, and
    the literal certificate
    `lambda=H_0 v`, `sum lambda=0`, `lambda^t S=M(v,0)`,
    `||lambda||_1<=M sqrt(ell)`.
    The sufficient finite condition is
    `binom(M/2,q)>(2q floor(sqrt(2kM^2/(M-1)))+1)^k`.
    For fixed k, `q=floor(k/2)+1` works for all sufficiently large M.
    Explicitly, with `a=ceil(log_2(2k))`, `M>=64ka` gives
    `ell<=8ka`; with one extra column, `ell<=2` already for M>=8.

    The certificate denominator is M, with no allocation determinant
    or prime-width factor. A truncated-Hadamard example disproves a
    same-row-count complete-core extraction even at redundancy two:
    deleting two rows gives M=2 modulo four and strictly negative
    off-diagonal Gram entries, but no order-M Hadamard matrix.
    Astra proved the character bounds; Sol and root audited them.
    The checker covers 120 exhaustive one-extra order-eight cases,
    16 Walsh/Paley fixtures, 256 integer pigeonhole inequalities,
    and four truncated-core examples.

276. **Short Hadamard characters give an effective uniform row bound in that family.**
    The [effective phase theorem](effective_hadamard_short_character_phase_gap.md)
    replaces the fixed-matrix Roth cutoff by a degree-two Matveev
    estimate, retaining the complete common Gaussian factor, nested
    prime layers and arbitrary row units in the stated small-arc
    ranges. Affine rigidity makes the reduced composite direction
    Beta nonunit, and Bessel gives `V=log Norm(Beta)<=2ell W/M`.
    Doubling the exact signed product isolates
    `Lambda=M log(Beta/bar(Beta))-m log(-1)`, with
    `0<|Lambda|<=M sqrt(ell) C exp(-W/4)` and
    `max(M,|m|)<=2M sqrt(ell)` for C<=2.
    Its height is `h(Beta/bar(Beta))=V/2`; Matveev gives
    `log|Lambda|>-2^40 V log(eB)`.

    Thus `M>=16*2^40*ell*log(2eM sqrt(ell))` forces
    `W<8log(2M sqrt(ell))`, contradicting
    `W>=(M-1)log5` once M is large. Bounded augmentation therefore
    has an effective point bound independent of R. More generally,
    an actual order-M core profile with M>=128 and k>=1 must have
    `k>M/[2048*2^40*(log M)^2]`.
    The unit regimes are C<=sqrt(2) with arbitrary units or C<=2
    with one literal unit class. The result does not extract a
    Hadamard core from general endpoint points.

    A separate cyclotomic relative-norm calculation gives the
    effective fixed-target bound
    `dist(arg pi,beta)>=2^(-d_beta) Norm(pi)^(-d_beta/2)`.
    Applied to the moving allocation grid, it gives a strict
    radius-power gap when `sum e_j/d_j>2`; uncontrolled grid degree
    prevents a general growth improvement. Sol proved these bounds;
    Astra and root independently audited them, including the original
    Matveev constant. The exact checker includes a Gaussian signed
    product with independent units and common inert content, the
    primitive composite polynomial, and a quadratic-target norm-one
    fixture.

277. **The effective uniform family theorem survives bounded row deletion.**
    The [deleted-row extension](deleted_hadamard_uniform_family_bound.md)
    begins with ambient Hadamard order N and retains M=N-d rows,
    with k additional exact cut classes. Subset-collision records
    include the d deleted-row signs as well as the k extra-column
    Fourier sums. This makes `lambda_full=H_0 v` vanish on every
    deleted row, so the retained certificate still has
    `sum lambda=0`, `lambda^t S=N(v,0)` and
    `||lambda||_1^2<=MN ell`.
    The integer box condition acquires only a factor `(2q+1)^d`;
    fixed k,d still allow `q=floor(k/2)+1` at large N. For k=0,
    `N-1>2^d` gives `ell=2` directly.

    The Matveev coefficient is the ambient N, while the Bessel
    height denominator is the actual retained M. This yields an
    explicit effective cutoff `U(k,d)` independent of R, given in
    the note, in the same small-arc unit regimes. It includes the
    deleted-two-row obstruction to a square Hadamard extraction.
    Root proved the extension and its integer cutoff; both Astra
    instances and Sol audited the proof. Luna's checker constructs
    32 exact certificates, verifies every deleted coordinate and

    It also checks 16 eventual counting thresholds, seven
    zero-extra thresholds, 30 exact integer cutoffs U(k,d), and
    their conservative analytic inequalities. No general profile
    extraction follows.

278. **Positive-density Walsh profiles have an effective uniform bound for every fixed arc constant.**
    The [dense Walsh restriction theorem](walsh_dense_restriction_uniform_bound.md)
    labels the actual rows by `A subset F_2^t`, with fixed density
    `|A|/2^t>=delta>0`. Its exact cut support contains every distinct
    nonconstant restriction of an ambient Walsh character and at most
    k other cut classes. Repeated ambient characters are grouped as
    one actual cut class. For every fixed C,k,delta, the ambient
    dimension t and hence the point count are effectively bounded
    independently of R, with arbitrary row units.

    The arc is partitioned into `J=ceil(C/sqrt(2))` pieces. One label
    color has density at least `delta/J`. An elementary translate-
    intersection argument constructs an affine s-flat in any density-
    rho subset once `2^t>=2^(s-1)(2/rho)^(2^(s-1))`.
    Its exact recurrence is `alpha_(i+1)>=alpha_i^2/2`, obtained
    by summing intersections over translations outside the current
    i-dimensional stabilizing subspace. No external Ramsey theorem
    or asymptotic equidistribution is required.

    Restriction to this flat preserves a complete `2^s`-row Walsh
    core with nonunit blocks and at most k extras. At each split
    prime, actual threshold sets remain nested after restriction,
    so two nonconstant layers cannot become complementary cuts.
    Merging surviving blocks therefore causes no rational prime
    cancellation. Constant layers become additional common Gaussian
    content, with the source rows, radius and units unchanged.
    Choose `2^s>=max_(0<=r<=k)U(r,0)` from item 277. The resulting
    small-arc flat is excluded, giving the explicit ambient bound
    `2^t<2^(s-1)(2J/delta)^(2^(s-1))`.

    This includes Walsh profiles with bounded row deletion and
    bounded augmentation for every fixed C. It does not cover the
    full-fair profile: its Walsh labels may be the sparse affine
    simplex `{0,e_1,...,e_(M-1)}`, of density `M/2^(M-1)`, which
    contains no affine two-flat. Root proposed the affine restriction
    route; Astra proved the density and exact normalization lemmas,
    and Sol independently audited both. Root checked the full proof
    and ran 2,533 exact affine-flat constructions, all 14 affine-plane
    restrictions of a nested-prime Gaussian fixture, and six sparse
    full-fair examples. The Gaussian fixtures test identities, not
    endpoint existence. The general uniform theorem remains unproved.

279. **Literal Walsh-core extraction from full-fair cuts removes a fixed or near-total fraction of the mass.**
    The [exact extraction cost](full_fair_walsh_extraction_mass_cost.md)
    restricts M full-cut source rows to m selected rows. Each
    nonconstant target cut has exactly `2^(M-m)` source preimages;
    the constant class has `2^(M-m)-1`. With one log-norm weight w
    per source class, a complete m-row Walsh core and all constant
    restrictions retain `[m 2^(M-m)-1]w`, while the nonconstant
    extras have weight `[2^(m-1)-m]2^(M-m)w`.
    The removed fractions are `1/2+o(1)` at m=4 and `15/16+o(1)`
    at m=8. For `m>=delta M`, the removed fraction tends to one.
    Keeping k additional target classes replaces m by m+k in the
    retained count. Near-fair weight errors and correction mass
    `o(W)` do not change these limiting fractions.

    Row relabeling, choice of target core and complement pairing
    cannot improve this literal mass calculation. Removing
    nonconstant blocks also changes relative phases by their signed
    arguments; the new radius permits only precision
    `exp(-W_keep/4)`, not an order-one error. The note records a
    formal phase diagnostic and literal primitive blocks
    `n+i(n+1)` with growing height and order-one individual argument.
    Neither is asserted to be a full endpoint example, or to rule
    out cancellation between different blocks. A separate phase
    estimate is still required for a valid extraction.
    Luna derived the counts; root audited the scope, added bounded
    extras and near-fair errors, and checked 4,410 four-row class-set
    cases, 495 eight-row cases, 16 larger closed-form counts and
    105 relabeling cases. Arbitrary tested class sets are not
    mislabeled as valid Walsh cores.

280. **Walsh completion has an exact orthogonal Gaussian Fourier lattice.**
    For the stripped full-cut completion
    `Z_x=d product_v(a_v+i chi_v(x)b_v)` on `F_2^t`, the
    [Fourier lattice dictionary](walsh_completion_fourier_ideal_lattice.md)
    proves that `C=H Z/2^t` is Gaussian-integral by an explicit
    XOR subset expansion. Its coefficient energy is exactly the
    squared core radius and its nonzero-shift autocorrelations vanish.
    Writing `T_v=a_v I+i b_v P_v`, with P_v a translation, gives
    `T_v^* T_v=Norm(Gamma_v) I` and
    `C=d (product T_v) delta_0`. This supplies an explicit
    orthogonal Gaussian integer lattice, not a covolume inference.

    For each odd block, its image is exactly the congruence system
    `Gamma_v | C_y+C_(y+v)` and
    `bar(Gamma_v) | C_y-C_(y+v)`. With pairwise coprime block norms,
    intersecting those images gives the full product lattice.
    For overlapping odd blocks, the exact alternative criterion
    retains every physical-row divisibility
    `A_x | (H C)_x`. The inverse has both a power-of-two denominator
    and an odd denominator, so their coprimality proves saturation.
    A nested-prime source example shows that the shorter single-block
    tests can otherwise admit a false minimum vector.

    The full product lattice has precisely the unit translates of
    its canonical coefficient vector on the minimum shell. Its
    physical rows are `epsilon chi_h(x)Z_x`, already distinguished
    by the sparse labels `0,e_1,...,e_t`. A row-unit function
    preserves the lattice exactly when it is a common unit times
    a Walsh character. Actual correcting factors instead leave
    explicit moving phase centers in the source-chord equations.
    Thus this is fixed-core uniqueness, with no proved moving-core
    height loss or propagation of small phases to missing rows.
    Astra derived the Fourier identities; root supplied the
    orthogonal-lattice route and audited the full proof. Sol
    independently checked saturation and corrections. The persistent
    checker covers orders 4,8,16, 72 full memberships, 2,401 local
    congruence cases and all 256 order-four unit functions.

281. **A radius-nonincreasing endpoint Möbius map must bring its expansion line close to the source arc.**
    The [compression and singular-line theorem](mobius_source_aligned_compression_radius_gap.md)
    uses the same physical half-angle matrix and condition number
    kappa as the established endpoint map theorem. Let N,N' be the
    least primitive squared radii and let d be the projective angle
    from the contracting right singular line to the entire source
    half-angle arc. Integrating the projective derivative and summing
    the M-1 consecutive target lattice chords gives
    `kappa sin^2(d)<=Theta sqrt(N')/(M-1)`.
    This uses the traversed monotone image lift, even across an
    angular seam, rather than replacing it by the shortest target arc.

    When both complete tuples satisfy endpoint constants at most two
    and `N'<=N`, the existing lower condition bound implies
    `sin^2(d)<=[512 C/(M-1)]N^(1/4-z_M)`.
    Here `z_14=139/552=1/4+1/552` and `z_M>=z_14` for M>=14.
    Hence the line of maximal angular derivative must approach the
    source arc by a power of N. If the expanding right singular
    axis is an actual source row, the entire source arc lies in its
    smooth compression region. The image endpoint condition is then
    automatic under `N'<=N`, and exact chord separation gives
    `N'>=kappa^2 cos^2(Theta/2)/Theta^2`. Combining the bounds yields
    `N<=(512 sqrt(2) C)^552` for that aligned class, uniformly in
    M>=14. Conformal maps are explicitly excluded from the lower
    condition bound. Maps with their high-derivative line in or near
    the source arc remain outside this exclusion.

    The conductor proof retains all new target primes and uses the
    ordinary integer lcm of pair denominator norms. Root corrected
    an initial Gaussian-lcm wording that would double-charge opposite
    orientations. An exact four-row full-cut fixture erases all seven
    old cut-prime widths, but has coprime new squared radius
    `N'=2393873733075157`, exceeding `N=2576450045`; it is not an
    endpoint example. Sol proved the aligned inequality, root supplied
    the general singular-line extension, and Astra independently
    audited both. The checker verifies the conductor example and
    36 determinant/radius comparisons on an actual four-point Pell
    endpoint source. No general point-count improvement follows.

282. **An equal-diagonal critical shear must pay with actual anchor content.**
    For the primitive half-angle map `((a,b),(0,a))` at actual source
    anchor `z_j`, put `g_j=gcd(Re z_j,Im z_j)`. The exact refined
    clipping divisor is `Nclip | |b|(b^2+4a^2)g_j`. At an odd prime
    dividing `b`, the coefficient interval is `[-v_p(b),v_p(b)]`;
    clipping the source range `[-e_j,e-e_j]` costs at most
    `v_p(b)+min(e_j,e-e_j)`. This keeps the interior-anchor factor
    that a binary-only argument would omit. A literal three-row
    prime-power tuple shows that factor is necessary.

    Under both endpoint constants at most two, `N'<=N`, and the same
    actual anchor's diagonal bound `a<=D_m N^(g_m+b_m)`, the result is
    `g_j>=K_m^(-1)N^eta_m`, with
    `eta_m=1-q_m-3u_m/2-3(g_m+b_m)=1/4-61/(4m)+O(m^-2)`.
    Elementary uniform estimates give `g_j>=2^-57 N^(1/8)` for
    `m>=256`. For source constant at most `sqrt(2)`, the existing
    total interior-allocation bound then leaves at most `8sqrt(m)`
    eligible anchors when `N>=2^912`. On literal binary sources,
    `g_j=1` gives `N<=2^456` in this map class. For integer shears
    `a=1`, the diagonal bound is automatic at their stated anchor.

    General critical representatives need not have equal diagonals,
    and no descent existence is inferred. Root proved the refinement
    and Sol independently audited the valuation and uniform constants.
    Luna separately audited the full proof, normalization and anchor count.
    The checker passes 7,776 local intervals, 3,780 actual Gaussian
    source/image tests, eight sharpness fixtures, seven exact exponent
    cases, and 500 rational condition certificates. See the
    [anchor-content proof](parabolic_shear_anchor_content_obstruction.md).

283. **A reproducible all-edge search supplies exact four- and five-cotangent fixtures.**
    At `L=6` and positive `X<=10000`, a divisor graph exhaustively
    checks 193,836 four-cliques and 85,642 five-cliques. The least
    four-finite objective in this box is attained at
    `(1146,1257,1842,4104)`, with
    `N=2163838625=5^3*13*17*29*37*73` and
    `N/(A/L)^4=2163838625/1330863361`. Its offset triangle invariant
    is `164250`; complement reanchoring gives
    `(1146,1590,3033,12978)` with the same objective. The five-finite
    record is `(9,12,18,22,48)`, `N=325`, objective `5200/81`.
    Independent Gaussian denominator calculations agree with the
    all-edge lcms of both fixtures. No asymptotic family, Pell
    classification, global minimum, or endpoint counterexample is
    inferred from this finite search. See the
    [bounded-search record](integer_cotangent_lcm_objective_search.md).

284. **A positive even/odd Bezoutian can be blind to an arbitrarily deep balanced cut.**
    For positive roots, write `P(z)=product(z+X_i)=E(z^2)+zO(z^2)`.
    The coefficient matrix of
    `(E(s)O(t)-E(t)O(s))/(s-t)` is positive definite and has determinant
    `product_(i<j)(X_i+X_j)` in both degree parities. The proof uses
    the strictly increasing phase of `P(iy)` and a fully normalized
    resultant identity. Thus the matrix detects opposite-root sums;
    repeated roots in one isotropic orientation need not affect any
    local Smith invariant.

    Actual positive integer cotangent cliques realize this at every
    even total row count `2s>=6`. Choose fixed split `p>s^2+1`,
    `P=p^e`, and slopes
    `(a,a+P,...,a+(s-1)P,P+1,...,P+s-1)`, with all inside quadratic
    norms of exact p-valuation e. Clearing all pair denominators gives
    `p`-unit L, an exact depth-e balanced `s|s` cut, and p-unit
    Bezoutian determinant. The independent outside denominators force
    `N>=P^(2s-1)/C_s`, so these examples are rigorously outside the
    endpoint regime. No low-conductor refinement is disproved.

    At six rows and p=17 the normalized matrix is `((14,10),(10,4))`
    modulo 17, with determinant 7; all five leading Hurwitz determinants
    are units too. The checker passes 52 matrices of degrees 2--14,
    including repeated roots, and 20 literal cliques of 6--14 total rows
    and depths 1--4. It compares complete all-edge lcms with Gaussian
    denominator lcms and checks every balanced layer and radius bound.
    Astra proved the result and root independently audited the general
    proof and ran the checker. See the
    [positive-matrix obstruction](integer_cotangent_positive_bezoutian_obstruction.md).

285. **Both rational isometric anchors can preserve the radius and retain the entire missing content factor.**
    For a general positive-determinant triangular map, put
    `delta=ad`, `D=b^2+(a-d)^2`. Isometric source lines are rational
    exactly when `delta D=s^2`; conformal source and image anchoring
    then gives `((delta,+/-s),(0,delta))` after a common scalar.
    For a virtual rational half-angle H of signed coordinates r_p,
    adjoining it changes the exact least norm by
    `E_H=product p^dist(r_p,J_p)`, while its physical ordinary content
    is `G_H=product p^max(0,min(r_p-L_p,U_p-r_p))`.
    These factors are coprime. The sharpened parabolic divisor contains
    `G_H`, which can be large even when `E_H=1` and every old row has
    content one. At good primes dividing s, both isometric roots are
    the same midpoint of the original oriented coefficient interval.

    The exact negative-Pell family `b^2-2c^2=-1`, `M=((1,b),(0,2))`,
    has source points `-(c^2+1)+/-ib` and target points
    `(c^2-2)+/-2ib`, with equal least norm `N=c^2(c^2+4)`.
    The correct rational phase gauges use the negative-imaginary
    source and target points as references. Its two virtual physical
    points are `-c^2+/-2ic` and their images `c^2+/-2ic`; all lie on
    the existing circles and have content c. Primitive normalization
    gives shears `((1,+/-c),(0,1))`, and their clipped divisor is exactly
    `N=c(c^2+4)G_H`. Thus neither a second isometric anchor nor complete
    conductor sharing removes this cost automatically.

    Both augmented four-point tuples have endpoint constants at most
    eight for c>=5. The original source and target constants tend to
    `2sqrt(2)` and `4sqrt(2)`, so this is expressly outside the
    `C,C'<=2` hypotheses and does not refute a many-point refinement.
    Irrational isometric roots require a quadratic extension; their
    exact formal field norm is recorded without claiming a rational
    clipping theorem. A fresh Astra instance proved the result; root
    and a fresh Sol instance audited the half-angle/physical gauge,
    both Gaussian orientations, least radii and scope. The checker
    passes 136 normalizations, six Pell tuples, 36 oriented prime
    profiles and 612 interval profiles. See the
    [virtual-anchor cost audit](isometric_virtual_anchor_content_barrier.md).

286. **Reciprocal stretch projections lie in one finite divisor set.**
    Let a nonconformal map at actual source and target anchors have an
    integral triangular representative of positive determinant delta.
    If N,N' are the least squared radii and Q is the clipped conductor,
    then `H=4delta^2 NN'/Q^2` is a positive integer and
    `m<=2tau(H)`. The proof writes normalized squared stretch as the
    physical projection `T/(2delta)+Re(conj(W z_0)z_i)/(2delta N)`.
    Both the forward and inverse projection coordinate gcds contain Q.
    The inverse clipped conductor equals the forward one at every
    split prime: the clipped valuation map is an affine isometry,
    and endpoint cancellation moves outward before inverse clipping.
    Thus `2delta(N/Q)x_i` and `2delta(N'/Q)/x_i` are positive integers
    with fixed product H. Each first integer occurs at most twice by
    circle-line intersection. The proof retains the factor two and
    the determinant of the actual triangular representative; it does
    not apply a raw adjugate in the wrong target phase gauge.
    Full clipping and N'<=N force N'=N, giving `m<=2tau(4delta^2)`.
    The exact checker passes 760 actual-frame cases, 3344 projection,
    reciprocal and integer-product identities, and 441 prime profiles.
    Astra, root and two Sol audits agree. See the
    [reciprocal divisor theorem](mobius_reciprocal_stretch_grid.md).

287. **The divisor theorem improves growth for admissible critical maps.**
    The selected-anchor critical reduction gives
    `H<=4 D_m^4 2^(2m q_m) N^(4h_m+2q_m)`, with exponent
    `(21+o(1))/m` and uniformly bounded prefactor. The coarse certified
    version is `H<=2^74 N^(44/m)` for m>=256. An elementary prime split
    proves `log tau(n)<=(log2+o(1))log n/loglog n`; no prime-counting
    theorem is needed. Combining it with item 286 gives
    `m=O(log N/(loglog N logloglog N))` for nonconformal maps between
    tuples with both endpoint constants at most two and N'<=N.
    This is a growth-rate improvement for that map class. An arbitrary
    endpoint tuple is not known to admit such a map, so the audited
    general bound remains `(1+epsilon)log R/loglog R`. The source
    hypotheses, inverse integrality, constants and asymptotic inversion
    were independently checked by Sol and root. See the
    [conditional growth audit](reciprocal_divisor_conditional_growth_audit.md).

288. **Six explicit Pell points attain the full-clipping divisor bound.**
    For positive odd `k^2-2b^2=-1`, the six physical points
    `{+/-2b+i b^2, +/-k+i(b^2+1), +/-2k+i(b^2-2)}` have primitive
    common norm `N=b^2(b^2+4)`. In the actual anchor gauges specified
    in the note, the shear `((1,b),(0,1))` permutes this set, has
    N'=Q=N, and has squared stretches `(1,1,1/2,1/2,2,2)`.
    Thus all three divisors of H=4 occur twice, proving that the
    multiplicity-two divisor bound can be sharp. The normalized arc
    constant tends to `4sqrt(2)`, outside the at-most-two critical
    hypotheses. Root constructed the family, Sol verified every
    physical row, both prime orientations, tuple primitivity and
    clipping, and Luna independently audited the proof. Returning to
    one fixed projective chart gives a trace-zero involution; the
    shear itself acts between different actual anchor gauges.
    The checker passes b=1,5,29,169 and ten split-prime
    profiles. See the [sharpness family](full_clipping_six_point_pell_sharpness.md).

289. **Large binary endpoint tuples need not supply a map by self-permutation.**
    If m>=128, gcd(m,6)=1, N>2^176, the endpoint constant is at most
    two, and every point has ordinary coordinate gcd one, then the
    rational projective automorphism group is trivial. The finite
    orientation-preserving group is cyclic of order dividing m and
    belonging to {1,2,3,4,6}; hence a possible nonidentity map is one
    orientation-reversing involution fixing an actual sampled point.
    Its nonconformal fixed-anchor shear has exact determinant core a^2
    and forces that point's gcd to be at least `2^-22 N^(1/8)`.
    A conformal reflection instead forces its gcd to be sqrt(N).
    Both contradict the binary assumption. The theorem does not
    construct large tuples or classify distinct representatives in
    their projective orbit. In particular a minimum over such
    representatives supplies no automatic second minimizer.
    Astra proved the result; root and Luna independently audited the
    group, anchor, core/parity and constant steps. The checker passes 144 finite-order
    matrices, 2212 core normalizations, 132 exponent certificates and
    26 conformal content cases. See the
    [self-map obstruction](binary_endpoint_projective_selfmap_obstruction.md).

290. **Closed translations permit independent prime flips but can admit no descent.**
    At a clean collision prime, CRT can independently prescribe the
    local translation zero or minus twice the shared isotropic root,
    preserving every integer pair cotangent. Literal four-point
    cliques verify independent flips of two cut orientations. One
    source has L=1, X=(157,182,447), exact N=212298125 and
    normalized arc constant in (1.53,1.54). Its closed translations
    are precisely eight classes modulo 76850. Every nonzero closed
    translation has absolute value at least 4664, forcing one target
    pair cotangent to have absolute value at least 808015. That
    single reduced edge norm already exceeds N. Thus every nonzero
    closed integer translation increases the least radius, even for
    this endpoint-sized source and determinant-one matrices.
    This rules out a universal one-step translation descent; it does
    not settle a construction confined to sufficiently many points.
    Sol proved both results, and root checked the CRT, all-edge
    radius and rational arc certificate. See the [prime-orientation
    audit](integer_cotangent_closed_translation_prime_orientation_flip.md)
    and [no-descent example](integer_cotangent_closed_translation_descent_obstruction.md).

291. **The positive Cauchy difference has exactly the derivative kernel.**
    For positive distinct cotangents, let C_ij=1/(X_i+X_j), let B be
    the positive even/odd Bezoutian, and use its diagonal weights
    w_i=P'(-X_i)/P(X_i). The exact identity
    `C-diag(w)=diag(O)^(-1) V B V^t diag(O)^(-1)` has rank floor(k/2).
    Its kernel basis simplifies to `X_i^(2q)/F'(X_i)`; the apparently
    new opposite-root denominators cancel. The Cauchy inverse also
    gives `diag(w) C^(-1) diag(w)=C` and complementary positive ranks.
    The principal-minor inequalities on positive weights reduce to
    products of `(X_i+X_j)/|X_i-X_j|`, already greater than one.
    These exact identities expose why this particular positivity and
    kernel extraction gives no new arithmetic height gain. They do
    not exclude a different global inequality combining the matrices
    with the endpoint assumptions. Sol and root independently derived
    the identities, a second Sol audited the proof, and the exact
    checker passes 35 cases of both degree parities and the literal
    Pell and L=6 fixtures. See the
    [Cauchy derivative audit](cauchy_bezoutian_derivative_kernel_audit.md).

292. **Complementary offsets have an exact scale-invariant divisor kernel.**
    For m finite cotangents with minimum A, put S=A^2+L^2,
    d_i=X_i-A, c_i=S/d_i, h_d=gcd d_i and h_c=gcd c_i. Then
    `H=S/(h_dh_c)=lcm(d_i)/gcd(d_i)` is integral and invariant under
    common scaling; its distinct divisors d_i/h_d give `m-1<=tau(H)`.
    Relative to the actual anchor edge conductor n_A, the exact formula
    is `H=epsilon_A n_A gcd(A,L)^2/(h_dh_c)`. That content ratio
    cannot simply be dropped: the literal positive clique L=70,
    X=(85,182,210) has H=12125=25N, though its normalized arc
    constant is larger than two. The short translation fixture instead
    has H=290 and N=212298125. The direct divisor count therefore
    still needs a new endpoint estimate for its parameter; it does
    not reproduce item 287 unconditionally. Sol proved the formulas,
    root checked the normalization, and Luna independently audited
    and checked the lcm identity. See the
    [complementary-divisor audit](integer_cotangent_complementary_divisor_kernel.md).

293. **A four-point secant construction has an exact conductor and denominator cost.**
    A rational secant center P=A/s with K=Norm(A)-Ns^2 nonzero
    gives the involution `w=(A bar(z)-Ns)/(s bar(z)-bar(A))` on
    the rational circle of norm N. Intersecting two seed chords
    guarantees four integral partners. For `sz_i-A=g_i v_i`, with
    v_i integer primitive and S_i=Norm(v_i), the other partners are
    integral exactly when `g_i S_i|K` and the stated coordinate
    congruence modulo s holds. At a source prime, the coefficient
    interval in absolute allocations is `[r-j,e+j-r']`, reordered
    if necessary. Thus `N/Q|gcd(N,Norm(A/gcd_G(A,s)))`: source
    primes outside the center numerator survive completely.
    If L is the Gaussian lcm of the reduced partner denominators
    and G is their common Gaussian content after clearing, then
    `N_union=N Norm(L)` and `N_target=N Norm(L)/Norm(G)` exactly.
    A guaranteed integral partner implies Norm(G)|N and hence
    Norm(L)|N_target. New split-prime costs use the sum of two
    orientation maxima, which an ordinary norm lcm can miss.
    The actual paired-anchor determinant is `|K|D_0/c^2`; the
    chord-intersection area estimate alone leaves an N^2 upper scale.
    Astra proved these formulas and root audited both gauges,
    integrality, primitive target reduction and area exponents.
    See the [secant bridge](fixed_secant_conductor_bridge.md).

294. **Mixing one binary valuation class erases the prime completely.**
    The reciprocal clipping isometry has a strong fiber consequence:
    if one source valuation fiber maps to both binary target extremes,
    the inverse clipped width is zero, so the forward width is zero.
    A self-permutation can therefore retain a binary cut only by
    preserving or complementing it. Luna proved and checked literal
    3|1 and 2|2 four-point fixtures at p=5 of depth two; root audited
    the signed-target endpoints and squared-radius normalization.

    For a physical secant involution the forward and inverse intervals
    are the same in absolute coordinates. Consequently every 3|1
    binary split among four paired seeds is erased by all three
    pairings, even if the other partners are neither integral nor
    binary. If B_seed is the product of these source prime powers,
    then B_seed|N/Q. An admissible critical map would require
    `B_seed<=2^(m q_m)N^q_m`. In a formal equal-weight profile of
    all nonconstant binary patterns, every four-seed choice has
    3|1 weight fraction `2^(m-1)/(2^m-2)`, approaching one half.
    This blocks that particular four-seed construction in the hard
    profile; it neither realizes the formal profile in a short arc
    nor excludes other maps. See the [fiber lemma](binary_four_involution_cut_compatibility.md)
    and Section 6 of the [secant note](fixed_secant_conductor_bridge.md).

295. **Large binary endpoint symmetry groups have order at most four and act freely.**
    For every cardinality m>=32, N>2^36 and endpoint constant at
    most two, a primitive binary tuple has rational projective
    automorphism group {1}, C2, or C2 x C2, acting freely. In
    particular every odd-cardinality tuple in this range has trivial
    group, without the earlier coprimality-to-six restriction.
    Indeed a nonconformal permutation sigma preserves or complements
    each retained cut, so sigma^2 preserves every retained cut.
    Any moved edge of sigma^2 then has full odd edge conductor
    dividing E=N/Q. But `E<=2^8 N^(1/4)<sqrt(N)/2`, whereas
    endpoint separation gives odd edge conductor greater than
    sqrt(N)/2. The factor two is retained for arbitrary unit classes.
    A fixed sampled point would forbid every complemented cut and
    give the same contradiction for sigma itself. Conformal symmetries
    are excluded separately by Gaussian Bezout and the existing
    unit-axis radial count. Finite real projective group structure
    then gives the stated free groups. This extends item 289 to all
    cardinalities and classifies remaining symmetries; it is not a
    general point-count theorem. Root derived the cut argument and
    Astra audited and persisted the proof, and Luna independently
    verified its parity, cutoff, cut logic and group argument. See the
    [group classification](binary_endpoint_projective_group_classification.md).

296. **The mirror denominator equals a primitive-chord factor, with exact edge content.**
    For physical extreme points z_0,z_a, ordinary contents g_0,g_a,
    odd edge conductor n_0a and reduced midpoint-reflection
    denominator norm D, the exact identity is
    `D n_0a gcd(g_0,g_a)^2=N`. If the primitive chord direction
    is u+iv, then `D=(u^2+v^2)/epsilon`, where epsilon is two
    exactly when u,v are both odd. These formulas connect the
    complementary-divisor anchor content to the already established
    reflection-union cost and primitive-chord strip transform.
    The union formula N_union=ND, its radial obstruction, and the
    six-point Pell unions were established earlier; they are not
    new count improvements here. In particular fixed-L failure of
    cross-pair integrality does not prohibit adjoining a reflected
    tuple after clearing denominators; the exact resulting radius
    must be charged. Root proved the dictionary and Luna audited it;
    the checker passes 357 tuple/pair cases and three Pell instances.
    See the [mirror/edge content dictionary](mirror_union_least_radius_cost.md).

297. **A large endpoint tuple has at most one nonconformal image class.**
    For `m>=512,N>2^744`, all admissible nonconformal maps from the
    same primitive endpoint source to endpoint targets of norm at most
    `N` have the same oriented primitive physical projection normal.
    The exact actual-anchor covariance is
    `W_new z_k=Norm(H)W z_j`, so changing charts adds no sign or
    denominator. Its height is `N^(23/(2m)+O(1/m^2))` and its angle
    from the opposite source arc is `N^(-1/4+O(1/m))`. Integer
    determinants of two such normals are therefore zero at the stated
    absolute threshold. Their common ordered Gram axes imply that the
    composite has condition number only `N^O(1/m)`; applying the
    existing lower condition bound to the two actual target circles
    forces that composite to be conformal. Primitive conformal tuples
    differ by Gaussian units, so their least radii agree exactly.
    Thus the full projective self-group has order at most two without
    a binary hypothesis. An endpoint orbit containing one realization
    above the threshold has at most two conformal classes in total.
    These are uniqueness statements, not map-existence results. Root,
    Astra, Sol and Luna audited the coordinates and composition;
    the checker passes 8064 covariance identities, 600 inverse-axis
    cases, 12544 finite-order products, 1350 composite identities and
    133 exponent certificates. See
    [normal rigidity and orbit uniqueness](critical_projection_normal_rigidity.md).

298. **The direct offset kernel usually retains half the source height.**
    For finite cotangents `A=X_1<...<X_m` and the circle anchor `0`,
    the offset kernel `H=lcm(X_i-A)/gcd(X_i-A)` has the exact local
    formula
    `v_p H=range_i(T_p(i)+v_p r_(1i)-v_p r_(0i)+delta_i)`.
    Here `T_p(i)` is the allocation-segment overlap between rows
    `0,1,i`, `r_e=L/gcd(Q_e,L)` is the exact cotangent-chart
    imaginary residue, and `delta_i` is the ramified correction.
    Thus its logarithmic height differs from the cut overlap by at
    most `2log L+log 2`, including inert primes. Removing the two
    anchors loses at most `W/ell` of that overlap, where
    `ell=ceil((m-1)/(4ceil(C/2)))`. The correct odd-edge parity factor
    yields the actual lower bound
    `log H>=(1/2-1/ell)W-2log L-2log C`.
    In particular a small `L` does not turn this kernel into
    `N^O(1/m)`. The formal full-fair calculation gives half-height
    for every anchor pair, but is not an asserted endpoint family.
    Root and Sol audited the formula and parity; the checker passes
    698 actual cliques and 498 formal cuts. See the
    [cut and residue dictionary](integer_cotangent_offset_height_cut_residue_dictionary.md).

299. **Even squareclass relations give a uniform polynomial height bound.**
    For distinct positive integer roots `c_j<=D`, an integer square
    value of `P(Z)=product_(j=1)^(2k)(Z-c_j)` with `Z>D` satisfies
    `Z<=(8kD)^(2k+1)`. The square-root polynomial truncated at its
    constant term has common denominator `2^(2k-1)`. Its remainder
    is small enough to force exact rounding at large `Z`, while the
    resulting nonzero integer polynomial has degree at most `k-1`
    and controlled coefficient height. The exponent is linear in `k`;
    no ineffective or fixed-curve constant is used. Repeated roots
    must be removed because their product can be a polynomial square.
    The initial two-label elimination likewise shows that, for
    `A>(H+B)^6`, divisors satisfying `Y_n^2=2An-n^2-B^2` have at
    most two members in a squareclass, and two must satisfy `nn'=B^2`.
    Root corrected the intermediate squareclass scaling; the safe
    polynomial threshold is unchanged. Root, Astra and Luna derived
    the even-product argument independently. The checker includes
    125 cases at each of degrees 2,4,6,8 and a repeated-root control.
    See the [elementary height lemma](runge_even_product_square_bound.md)
    and [two-label elimination](luna_divisor_squareclass_elimination.md).

300. **The conditional map class now has square-root logarithmic growth.**
    Actual source projections give integers
    `Y_i=Im(conj(C)z_i)/Q` and positive divisors `n_i|H` satisfying
    `Y_i^2=2TE n_i-n_i^2-(2delta E)^2`, where
    `H=4delta^2 EE'`. Set `Z=2EE'T` and
    `c_n=E'n+E(H/n)`. Then `E'Y_i^2=n_i(Z-c_n)`, and equal roots
    correspond exactly to complementary labels `nn'=(2delta E)^2`.
    At least `m/4` distinct roots remain after selecting labels.
    Prime-exponent parities with an extra parity coordinate lie in
    dimension `r+1`, `r=omega(H)`. Unless `m<=4(r+1)`, a dependence
    of even size at most `r+2` gives the monic integer square value
    of item 299. Since every root is at most `H^2`, this proves
    `log Z<=5(r+3)log H`. Combining the finite alternative with
    `log H<=74log 2+44(log N)/m` and
    `log Z>=(log N)/4-8log 2` forces `r` to be a positive multiple
    of `m` as `m` grows. Finally `H>=(r+1)!` gives
    `m^2 log m=O(log N)` and hence
    **`m=O(sqrt(log R/loglog R))` in the admissible map class.**
    This improves the growth rate in item 287 without using a prime
    number theorem. The six-point Pell family remains compatible:
    its labels 1,2,4 give roots 5,4,5, leaving no eligible dependence
    after the repeated root is removed. Root, Astra and Sol audited
    every denominator, parity and asymptotic step; the physical
    checker passes 280 actual maps, 1232 square projections and 13
    actual even-squareclass relations, plus explicit degeneracy controls.
    The general map-existence gap remains. See the
    [conditional growth proof](reciprocal_squareclass_runge_growth.md).

301. **The original source has a monic model, but its roots remain large.**
    At an actual source anchor, primitive half-angle rows `a_i+ib_i`
    have norms `f_i|2N`. Put `d_i=2N/f_i` and
    `c_i=d_i b_i^2=N-Re(conj(z_0)z_i)`. Then
    `2N-c_i=d_i a_i^2`, so even squareclass relations among the
    divisors `d_i|2N` already give monic integer square equations
    without an auxiliary map. Their roots are radial deficits with
    `c_i<=C^2 sqrt(N)/2`, not `N^O(1/m)`. If `g_0` is the anchor's
    ordinary content, the exact common normalization is
    `gcd(2N,c_1,...,c_(m-1))` equal to `g_0` or `2g_0`.
    Thus a pointwise primitive anchor permits removal of at most two.
    For `C<=2,N>=4`, each squareclass contains at most two nonanchor
    points by the spacing of integer squares; the number of classes
    is still uncontrolled, as in the earlier squareclass baseline.
    More strongly, for `C<=sqrt(2)` and every actual anchor, all but
    fewer than `1/(4epsilon^2)` roots satisfy
    `c_i>=N^(1/2-epsilon)`. The threshold Gram is positive
    semidefinite with diagonal one and nonpositive off-diagonal
    entries, so its norm is at most two and each off-diagonal row
    has squared sum at most one. This bounds the number of oversized
    anchor-pair norms and proves the root-height floor, with no
    unit-class loss. Thus selecting many original rows does not
    provide small roots in this particular monic construction.
    This identifies the missing height savings
    in a direct application of item 300. The checker passes 12452
    pair dictionaries, 6210 exact anchor gcds including 774 nontrivial
    contents, 698 even-product squares and all radial-cap counts.
    See the [direct monic bridge](direct_projection_monic_height_bridge.md).

302. **The conditional growth theorem needs no radius ordering.**
    Apply the arbitrary-unit retention inequality to a nonconformal
    endpoint map and its inverse. For `m>=8`, both
    `N'>=N^(1-4/m)/16` and `N>=(N')^(1-4/m)/16` hold, so the
    logarithms of the two least squared radii are comparable. Item 300
    can therefore be applied in either direction. For arbitrary fixed
    positive arc constants `C,C'`, partition the two arcs into
    `ceil(C/2)` and `ceil(C'/2)` pieces and retain a largest common
    label class. Dividing each selected tuple's full Gaussian gcd
    decreases its normalized arc constant. The inherited map stays
    nonconformal, and the estimate transfers back to the parent radius.
    Thus `M=O_(C,C')(sqrt(log R/loglog R))` holds whenever such a map
    exists, with no ordering assumption. Root and Luna audited the
    normalization; dividing by gcd modulus `g` changes the endpoint
    constant by the factor `1/sqrt(g)`. See
    [the extended conditional theorem](reciprocal_squareclass_runge_growth.md).

303. **Affine recentering preserves the direct model's large root scale.**
    For selected distinct deficits `c_i=d_i b_i^2`, choose a reference
    `c_r` and put `G_aff=gcd_i(c_i-c_r)` and
    `G_eff=gcd(G_aff,2N-c_r)`. An exact primewise identity gives
    `G_eff=(gcd_i d_i)(gcd_i |a_i|)^2`, including two. A larger
    rational-affine divisor introduces a denominator; clearing it
    restores exactly the roots `(c_i-c_r)/G_eff`.
    On an actual arc with `C<=sqrt(2)`, the obtuse allocation Gram
    and primitive relative residues prove, for `q` selected rows,
    `G_eff<=2g_0 N^(1/(q+1)+1/(2(q-1)))`. At every anchor, when
    `q>3/(4epsilon^2)+4`, the same Gram and an exact sine identity
    force `diam(c_i)>=N^(1/2-epsilon)`. Choosing a small-content
    actual anchor with `g_0<=N^(1/(2sqrt(m)))` therefore leaves a
    fixed positive power of `N` in the normalized diameter for
    `q` proportional to large `m`. This rules out the small-root
    premise for this particular affine monic construction at such
    an anchor. It does not exclude different constructions or
    normalization at a high-content anchor. Also the selected
    divisor labels retain `lcm_i d_i>=N^(1-1/q)/g_0`; this controls
    their ordinary lcm height, not their squareclass rank. See the
    [affine normalization proof](direct_projection_affine_normalization_height_tradeoff.md).

304. **Even cut occupancy does not divide the moving-degree remainder.**
    Let `P(X)=product_(i=1)^(2k)(X-c_i)`, let `S` be the degree-`k`
    polynomial part of its square root, and put
    `R=2^(4k-2)(P-S^2)`. If `p^e|2N`, at least one root is
    divisible by `p^e`, and all remaining roots `U` are `p`-units,
    then `R(2N)=-[2^(2k-1)F_k(U)]^2 mod p^e`, where
    `F_k(U)=[t^k]product_(u in U)(1-ut)^(1/2)`.
    Every mixed even occupancy admits a unit value of `F_k` at
    every split prime `p>8k`, including compatible local norm-square
    equations and a square product of labels. Thus occupancy parity
    alone gives no factor of `p` in this remainder, at arbitrary
    degree. The literal primitive binary tuple of norm `1105`
    supplies a four-factor example with remainder `4 mod 5`; it
    is not claimed to have endpoint constant two. A large endpoint
    tuple could impose additional residue congruences, which remain
    unproved. The checker verifies 252 prime-power congruences,
    36 scaling identities, 135 local models and the global fixture.
    See the [exact local remainder obstruction](direct_monic_remainder_local_obstruction.md).

305. **A direct high-content-anchor slice has improved growth.**
    For any actual anchor `z_0=g v`, put `Q=Norm(v)=N/g^2` and
    `rho=sqrt(Q)=R/g`. The normalized deficits and tangential
    coordinates are integers satisfying
    `y_i^2=s_i(Z-s_i)`, where `Z=2N/g` and
    `0<s_i<=D=floor(C^2 rho/2)`. Each deficit accounts for at most
    two nonanchor points. Write `r=pi(D)`. If `M>2r+3`, a
    parity-augmented relation among at most `r+2` distinct deficits
    gives an even monic square product, and hence
    `Z<=(8(r+2)D)^(r+3)`. Elementary dyadic binomial estimates give
    `pi(D)<=8D/log D`; for `D>=16`, the logarithm of this threshold
    is at most `44D`. Since `log Z>=log N/2`, the explicit radial
    range `rho<=log N/(50C^2)` forces `M<=2pi(D)+3`; bounded
    `D` is handled by direct counting.
    Consequently `M=O_C(1+rho/log(2+rho))` in this range. In
    particular an arc containing an anchor with
    `rho<=log R/loglog R` has
    `M=O_C(log R/(loglog R)^2)`. This improves growth in a
    directly specified family without requiring an auxiliary map.
    No Gaussian-primitivity or odd-norm hypothesis is needed.
    The earlier two-Pell theorem is stronger on its smaller radial
    range, where it gives a uniform count. Arbitrary arcs need not
    contain a high-content anchor, so the general bound is unchanged.
    See the [direct radial squareclass growth proof](anchor_radial_deficit_squareclass_growth.md).

306. **The short-radial-anchor hypothesis cannot hold at two nearby points.**
    If `z_i=g_i v_i`, with `v_i` primitive and `rho_i=|v_i|`,
    the nonzero integer determinant of two nonantipodal directions gives
    `rho_i rho_j>=R/L`. On an arc of length `L<=C sqrt(R)<pi R`,
    at most one actual point can have `rho_i<R^(1/4)/sqrt(C)`.
    Thus two polylogarithmic actual radial directions cannot jointly
    supply the small-deficit model at large radius. A separate angular
    example also disproves choosing an `O(R^(1/4))` integer normal
    inside every endpoint angular interval. Its nearby exterior normal
    still gives bounded projection width: the exact general estimate is
    `m<=2(floor(rho(L|sin delta|+L^2/(4R)))+1)`.
    These are restrictions on candidate selections, not a dichotomy
    covering all many-point arcs. See the
    [actual and virtual normal audit](radial_virtual_normal_constraint.md).

307. **The chord-normal endpoint square has no independent first residue test.**
    For the primitive extreme chord `Q-P=g w`, put `s=Norm(w)`,
    `B=det(w,P)` and `T=gs/2`. Actual endpoint integrality forces
    `s|2B`, so `t=2B/s` is integral and `4N=s(g^2+t^2)`.
    The index-`s` frame congruence and its circle conic reduce to
    `2Bq_i=0 mod s`, which is automatic. The reciprocal identity
    `p_i(gs-p_i)=q_i(2B+q_i)` is that same conic rearranged;
    the projection equation retains its nonzero square constant `T^2`.
    The two endpoints have content `(s/2)gcd(g,t)`, while the full
    projected tuple has content `gcd(B,T,{p_i,q_i})`. An interior
    row bounds the latter by the sagitta times `sqrt(s)`, so scalar
    normalization has squared norm at least `64N/C^4`. Full Gaussian
    normalization recovers the original source up to a quarter-turn.
    The actual norm-85 three-row arc has endpoint content 17 and full
    content 1. The checker passes 304 frames and 2,912 physical rows;
    Root and Luna independently audited the proof. See the
    [chord-normal content audit](primitive_chord_normal_reciprocal_content_audit.md).

308. **All-anchor cycles share one label space and an exact small global divisor.**
    Raw deficits `c_ij=N-Re(conjugate(z_i)z_j)` have common parameter
    `Z=2N`. Every even-cardinality Eulerian edge set gives integer
    square products of both its deficits and their complements. The
    augmented edge labels are `v_i+v_j+w`, so their rank is at most
    `m`, with equality on an explicit primitive circle construction.
    The Eulerian character structure was known in the earlier graph
    note; this is its exact raw-deficit and common-parameter dictionary.
    For a Gaussian-primitive tuple with at least three rows, the gcd
    of ALL complements is exactly 1 or 2, determined by coordinate
    parity. In general it is multiplied by the norm of the full
    Gaussian gcd. Thus a common integer affine normalization of the
    complete raw-root set reduces its diameter by at most two in the
    primitive case, independently of individual anchor contents.
    For large cohorts at `C<=sqrt(2)`, the retained diameter is at
    least `(1/2)N^(1/2-epsilon)`. The mixed-cut Runge remainder can
    also remain a unit when all local points lie on one shared circle,
    not just separate norm equations. An actual four-cycle on norm 65
    has distinct roots `2,40,9,5` and cleared remainder `4 mod 5`.
    These results do not improve the general endpoint count. See the
    [joint-anchor normalization and local-compatibility proof](all_anchor_deficit_cycle_squareclasses.md).

309. **Connected sparse cycle models retain the normalization loss on binary tuples.**
    Assume the full tuple is Gaussian-primitive and every individual
    point has coprime integer coordinates. Equivalently, each source
    prime uses only its two extreme allocation values. For any
    connected spanning edge graph, no odd source prime divides the
    common complement gcd. At a prime outside `2N`, complement
    divisibility is exactly the signed congruence `z_j=-z_i`, and
    its valuation is twice the coordinate valuation of that sum.
    Including the exact two-adic calculation, the graph gcd is
    `K^2` or `2K^2`. An odd cycle forces `K=1`. For a bipartite
    graph, `K` divides every primitive pair residue within either
    part; if the larger part has `q` vertices, the obtuse Gram
    budget at `C<=sqrt(2)` gives `K<=N^(1/(4(q-1)))`.
    For an even cycle in geometric order, this leaves normalized
    root diameter at least `(1/4)N^(1/2-epsilon-1/(m-2))` once
    the large-cohort threshold of item 303 holds. All pair deficits
    are distinct in this range: equal chords would violate the
    previously proved multiplicative-rectangle separation theorem.
    Outside this short-arc range, repeated-factor cancellation can
    change the graph and its gcd. A literal norm-65 six-cycle has
    roots `5,9,5,13,9,117` and gcd 1; removing even multiplicities
    leaves `13,117` and gcd 13. Its endpoint constant is about
    7.093, so it does not contradict the small-constant statement.
    This extends a normalization obstruction, not the general
    counting bound. See the [sparse graph extension](all_anchor_deficit_cycle_squareclasses.md).

310. **Linear cut support can have long characters and still admit a short phase certificate.**
    In the five-copy Walsh model with one distinct physical entry flipped
    per row and at most two assignments per old label, grouping cuts gives
    `2M-1` classes. Its saturated zero-mean character lattice is exactly
    `{c^t S/2: c integral, sum c=0}`, with minimum at least `M/2`.
    At the archived nearby-prime weights, every nonzero composite has
    logarithmic norm above `3W_0/10`. This defeats a generic sublinear
    character deduction or a `W_0/4` height target, but leaves the sharper
    `W/2` target for a denominator-two row certificate available.
    Four explicit rows give such a certificate for the canonical assignment
    at `M>=32` and the relabelled assignment at `M>=16`. The exact
    Gaussian axis/diagonal gap implies
    `C_source>exp(3ell/4)/(sqrt(2)e)`, strengthened by the fourth root
    of any common Gaussian norm. Since `ell=4log M+O(1)` in the archived
    construction, its actual normalized arc constant grows at least as
    `M^3`. This supplies the missing phase exclusion for that canonical
    norm countermodel without disputing its norm-only conclusions. See the
    [saturation and four-row phase proof](linear_support_character_height_obstruction.md).

311. **Larger aligned cosets improve the repeated-Walsh growth exponent.**
    Let `M=2^t`, with `b>=5` physical copies of each nonzero Walsh label.
    An affine coset of size `h` on which every assigned label has the same
    nonzero restriction gives an integral signed row certificate with
    physical coefficient sum `bM/2-h`. For distinct split prime logs in
    `[ell,ell+1/r)`, `r=b(M-1)`, exact endpoint phase forces
    `(h-b/2)ell+D/2<1+2log(hC)-log8`, with `D` the original common
    Gaussian log norm. Canonical and relabelled assignments have such
    cosets with `h>=sqrt(M)/2`. At large `M` the copy count exceeds `h`,
    and the factorial cost of the resulting distinct primes gives
    `M=O_C((log R/loglog R)^(2/3))`. This is a growth theorem for these
    assignments and nearby prime weights, not a general profile extraction.
    See the [higher-coset proof](linear_support_character_height_obstruction.md).

312. **Near-affine assignments have growing certificates with a quantified exception budget.**
    For `a(x)=Lx+b` on `F_2^t`, `rank L>=t-1` and `t>=6`, an elementary
    binary quadratic argument constructs a subspace of dimension
    `d=floor(t/3)` on which `u dot Lv` vanishes for every pair.
    At least `2^(t-d-1)` disjoint cosets have constant nonzero label
    restriction; changing fewer rows leaves one intact. This includes
    repairing the possible zero labels, subject to distinct physical
    flip capacity. The aligned-coset height certificate then forces
    `b_copy>2^d>=M^(1/3)/2` at large `M` for fixed `C` and nearby
    prime logs. Distinct prime factors give
    `M=O_C((log R/loglog R)^(3/4))`, including arbitrary source units
    and common content. No assumption `ell` is comparable to `log M`
    is needed. Nonlinear assignments and arbitrary endpoint tuples
    remain outside this theorem. See the
    [affine assignment and exception proof](walsh_affine_assignment_plane_certificate.md).
    Item 317 subsequently improves the exponent to `2/3` using a larger
    universal isotropic direction, with its stated exception budget.

313. **Symplectic averaging removes the prime-size hypothesis from a two-thirds radius bound.**
    For `M=2^(2d)`, let the row assignment be `a_x=Jx` for nonzero
    `x`, where `J` is nonsingular alternating. The row-zero assignment
    is arbitrary and all physical flipped columns are distinct. With
    arbitrary distinct split primes, let `W_0` be their total log norm,
    `D=log Norm(g)` the common content, and `F` the sum of logs of the
    `M-1` nonzero-row flipped primes. Lagrangian cosets give exact
    certificates whose row and label marginals are both
    `sqrt(M)/(M-1)`. Averaging their actual Gaussian heights and using
    the elementary phase grid gives
    `sqrt(M)F<=W_0/2+(M-1)(log(MC^2/8)-D/2)`.
    Since `F>=log(M!)`, the original radius necessarily satisfies
    `log R^2>=2sqrt(M)log(M!)-2(M-1)log(MC^2/8)+MD`.
    Thus `M=O_C((log R/loglog R)^(2/3))`, uniformly in copy count,
    prime sizes, prime orientations and row units. The optional mass
    condition `F>=eta W_0/b` also forces
    `b>=2eta sqrt(M)-8K_C`; it is not needed for radius growth.
