    Only the certificates are averaged: no symmetry of actual prime
    values or angles is assumed. The assignment hypothesis remains
    essential. See the
    [weighted symplectic phase theorem](walsh_symplectic_weighted_phase_growth.md).

314. **Complementary parity certificates remove arbitrary prime weights for ordinary and canonical assignments.**
    In even binary dimension, write `W_0=O+A+Q` for odd labels,
    even labels other than zero and the all-ones vector, and the
    all-ones label. Averaged even Lagrangian cosets give a height bound
    involving `A`, while the disjoint odd-row pairs `x,x+w` give an
    opposing bound involving `O`. Combining them eliminates the
    uncontrolled parity imbalance and gives
    `W>=sqrt(M)F_e+2F_o+(M/2)(Q+D)+(M A_2+(M-4)A_h)/2`,
    where `A_s=log8-2log(sC)`. The distinct flipped primes in `F_e`
    force `W=Omega_C(M^(3/2)log M)`. In odd dimension the even-parity
    hyperplane itself has a nondegenerate alternating form, and
    symplectic averaging applies there. Restricting canonical flips
    to even-index rows gives the ordinary assignment in one lower
    dimension. Constant restricted columns cancel in all certificates
    because their zero-row coefficient is zero; their full weight
    remains charged to the original radius. Consequently all these
    assignments have exponent `2/3` without a prime-size or relative
    mass hypothesis. See the
    [ordinary-dot and canonical weighted proof](walsh_ordinary_dot_weighted_phase_growth.md).

315. **Symmetric affine assignments tolerate exceptional rows with explicit growth loss.**
    Suppose outside at most `K` rows the assigned labels equal `Lx+v`,
    where `L` is symmetric of rank at least `t-k`. A codimension
    `q=ceil(log_2(K+1))` affine coset avoids every exception. Restriction
    loses at most `2q` rank; a complement to the restricted radical is
    nondegenerate symmetric. Translating its coordinates removes the
    affine term. Its form is alternating or has an orthonormal basis,
    so items 313--314 apply to at least `M/(2^k 4^q)` actual rows.
    Each restricted nonzero label retains exactly the same number of
    distinct physical columns; zero-label columns cancel from all
    certificates, including a possible flip at the unused zero row.
    This gives, with `W=log R^2`,
    `M<=A_C 2^k(K+1)^2 [1+(W/log(2+W))^(2/3)]`.
    Fixed `k,K` retain exponent `2/3` with arbitrary distinct prime
    sizes. More generally fixed `k` and `K<=M^delta` give exponent
    `2/[3(1-2delta)]`, improving one when `delta<1/6`.
    The symmetric affine approximation is a hypothesis, not a
    deduction from endpoint geometry. See the
    [physical restriction and radius proof](walsh_symmetric_affine_restriction_growth.md).

316. **A finite nonlinear control identifies the remaining certificate gap.**
    An explicit balanced assignment on 32 rows uses every nonzero label
    once and one label twice, but has no aligned affine plane. For a
    general coset of size `h` and nonzero character restriction, if `k`
    assigned labels match, the exact physical coefficient sum is
    `bM/2+h-2k`. Exhaustive enumeration for the example gives maximum
    matches `2,3,4,3,2` at coset sizes `2,4,8,16,32`. At five or more
    copies every such height exceeds `W_0/2` for the specified nearby
    actual prime weights. Balanced nonplanar four-row signs have old
    coefficient sum `3bM/4`, so they do not remedy this finite example.
    This is an obstruction to these particular certificates, not an
    endpoint construction or an asymptotic counterexample. An independent
    enumeration checks all 1,240 affine planes. See the
    [nonlinear coset audit](walsh_nonlinear_coset_height_obstruction.md).
    A separate exact positive-rational-weight sign model also shows that
    strict obtuseness alone need not force a relative flipped-weight
    lower bound; it makes no claim about actual prime logarithms. See its
    [literal physical-column check](check_weighted_symplectic_flip_countermodel.py).

317. **Every binary bilinear form has an isotropic subspace of nearly half the dimension.**
    For any bilinear form on `F_2^t`, without symmetry or nonsingularity,
    there is a subspace of dimension `max(0,floor((t-2)/2))` on which
    the form vanishes in both arguments. For nondegenerate alternating
    polar form, write `B(x,y)=A(Tx,y)` with `T+T*=I`. An elementary
    parity count finds a nonzero vector whose first odd quadratic
    moments vanish; adjoint identities then kill the intervening even
    moments. Its powers under `T` either give the desired subspace or
    a smaller invariant isotropic space through which one quotients
    and applies induction. Isotropic vectors in the polar radical
    handle the degenerate cases; an anisotropic one-dimensional
    radical splits off directly. This proof does not invoke a
    symmetric-form theorem for a nonsymmetric form.
    For rank-at-least-`t-1` affine assignments it supplies aligned
    cosets of size `h=2^floor((t-2)/2)>=sqrt(M)/(2sqrt(2))`.
    Fewer than `M/(2h)` edited labels leave one intact. With actual
    nearby distinct primes, the earlier height certificate forces
    `b_copy>h`, hence exponent `2/3` for these near-affine profiles.
    This improves item 312's growth exponent without a symmetry
    hypothesis on its assignment matrix. The general endpoint goal
    remains open. See the
    [binary bilinear proof and affine consequence](walsh_arbitrary_binary_bilinear_isotropic_bound.md).

318. **Three complementary certificate families remove the prime-weight restriction for general affine assignments.**
    Suppose at most `K` rows differ from an affine label map `Lx+a_*`
    of corank at most `k`, with all actual physical flips distinct.
    Take the universal isotropic direction and remove its intersection
    with `ker L^T`; its size is at least
    `sqrt(M)/(2sqrt(2)2^k)` unless the elementary prime-count baseline
    already suffices. Translating a zero fibre of the restricted affine
    map gives `V subset H`, with `|V|=h`, `|H|=M/h=nh`.
    Three families use nonzero-character `V`-cosets outside `H`,
    differences of two `V`-cosets inside `H`, and differences of two
    whole `H`-cosets. Their Fourier supports partition the nonzero
    labels. Mixing with weights `(h-1)/h`, `(n-1)/(hn)` and
    `(h-1)/M` gives total weight `1-1/M` and exactly `W_0/2` as
    the unflipped height. Actual pair phases independently bound every
    label mass by `2W_0/(M-4)+(M-2)kappa_+/(M-4)`, where
    `kappa_+=max(0,4log C-log4)`. This controls the adverse flip
    contributions without any assumed prime-weight balance.
    With `q=1+hK/M`, the resulting inequality is
    `hF_out<=q(8W_0+L_C Mlog M)`. Distinct flipped primes outside
    `H`, together with the baseline for small `h/q`, prove
    `log R^2>=c_C M^2 log M/(2^k sqrt(M)+K)`.
    The bound permits singular and nonsymmetric affine maps, arbitrary
    prime sizes, offsets, exceptions, units and common content.
    At fixed corank, `K=O(sqrt(M))` gives exponent `2/3`, and
    `K=O(M^delta)`, `1/2<delta<1`, gives exponent `1/(2-delta)`.
    These remain profile theorems. See the
    [three-family weighted phase proof](walsh_three_family_weighted_affine_growth.md).

319. **Prime-copy capacity gives a rank-free growth improvement for near-affine profiles.**
    If the actual corank is `k` and `x=2^k`, the affine image has
    `M/x` labels. Its `M-K` unedited rows need distinct physical
    flip slots, so `b>=x(1-K/M)`. For `K<=M/2`, the factorial
    cost of those primes gives `W_0>=xMlog M/8`. Combining this
    with item 318 and splitting at `x=M^(1/4)` eliminates the
    unknown corank. For `K>M/2`, the ordinary prime-count baseline
    gives the same coarse conclusion:
    `log R^2>=c_C M^2 log M/(M^(3/4)+K)`.
    Thus affine assignments of any rank, and their modifications on
    at most `O(M^(3/4))` rows, have growth exponent `4/5` with
    arbitrary distinct prime sizes. For `K=O(M^delta)` with
    `3/4<delta<1`, the exponent is `1/(2-delta)`, still below one.
    The approximation by an affine label map is essential; this is
    not an improvement to the general endpoint count. See the
    [capacity corollary](walsh_three_family_weighted_affine_growth.md).

320. **Every nonlinear nonzero binary vector field has a growing aligned flat.**
    For any `a:F_2^t -> F_2^t minus {0}`, with `M=2^t`, the
    [rank extraction theorem](walsh_arbitrary_nonlinear_aligned_flat_extraction.md)
    produces a common nonzero restriction on disjoint cosets of a
    subspace of size `h>=t/[16(log_2(t+2))^2]`, for `t>=4096`.
    Their union contains at least `M^(3/4)` rows. No affinity,
    degree, balance, or injectivity is assumed. The start uses
    `Q_xy=a(x) dot (x+y)` and the binary rank bound
    `rank(1+Q+Q^T)<=2t+3` to find many mutual-one edges.
    At support size h, a symmetric compatibility matrix has diagonal
    one and rank at most `(t+2)^(2h)`. Subtracting its diagonal
    and selecting one common direction gives the density recurrence
    `rho' >= rho^2/[2(t+2)^(2h)]` when the family is large enough.
    Linear-complement representatives ensure that the extended
    restriction is identical on every retained coset and stays nonzero.

    For actual near-equal logs `u<=log p_j<u+1/r`, the aligned
    phase certificate forces `b>h` for sufficiently large M at fixed C.
    Distinct primes then imply
    `log R^2>=c_C M(log M)^2/(loglog M)^2`, equivalently
    `M=O_C(1+log R (logloglog R)^2/(loglog R)^2)`.
    Units and full common content are retained. This is a growth
    improvement for all nonlinear repeated-Walsh assignments, but
    still requires the near-equal prime logs. Root, Luna, and a fresh
    Astra instance independently audited the extraction and arithmetic.
    The [finite nonlinear audit](walsh_nonlinear_m32_m64_coset_audit.md)
    distinguishes small-size obstructions from the asymptotic theorem;
    its exact finite statistics do not assert any general incidence
    balance or linear-program feasibility.

321. **All below-half-height Walsh characters are classified, without bounding row coefficients.**
    The [Fourier-gap proof](walsh_all_character_half_height_classification.md)
    shows that a nonzero `{0,1,-1}` function has normalized Fourier
    absolute sum one exactly when it is a signed character on an
    affine subspace; otherwise that sum is at least `3/2`.
    A two-coordinate Fourier marginal proves the gap directly: failure
    of support closure gives a cell of signed mass `-1/4`, while
    failure of sign multiplicativity gives one of mass `-1/2`.
    In a b-copy Walsh model with `b>=4` and one distinct-column
    flip per row, every zero-sum integer certificate with a coefficient
    of magnitude at least two, or with a noncoset support/sign pattern,
    has physical absolute coefficient sum at least `bM/2`.
    Thus a certificate below `r/2=b(M-1)/2` must be a coset character,
    and its matching count k must satisfy `2k-h>b/2`.

    For the archived nonlinear `M=32,b=5` map, exhaustive coset
    minima are `78,78,80,90,108` at sizes `2,4,8,16,32`.
    The full saturated rational-row character lattice consequently has
    minimum exactly `78>155/2`. Each label retains an unflipped
    physical column, so integrality forces twice every rational row
    coefficient to be integral. With actual near-equal distinct prime
    logs, every nonzero character has Gaussian height strictly above
    `W_0/2`, by a gap greater than `(u-1)/2`. This strengthens the
    finite obstruction from selected supports to all characters, without
    asserting an endpoint realization or a common-content conclusion.
    Root, Sol, Luna, and a fresh Astra instance audited the proof.

322. **The exact pair-slack identity isolates the weighted extraction problem.**
    Put `q_a=W_a-4F_a/M`, `u_d=kappa-qhat(d)>=0`, and
    `Psi=sum_(d in V minus {0})(-1)^(ell(d)+1)u_d`.
    For any nonzero coset character, let Fp be its selected flip weight,
    Fmatch its matching flip weight, and Fcell the total flip weight
    in the corresponding restriction fibre. The
    [slack identity](walsh_pair_slack_fixed_family_obstruction.md)
    proves exactly
    `V_Beta=W_0/2-kappa/2+Psi/2+2hFcell/M-2Ftot/M+Fp-2Fmatch`.
    The actual phase lower bound therefore requires
    `Psi>=2(2Fmatch-Fp)+(4/M)(Ftot-hFcell)-4log(h/2)`.
    Arc constants and common content cancel outside u.

    A single family selected independently of the weights cannot close
    the gap. Choose `w in V` with `ell(w)=1`, use nine copies,
    and put heavier prime logs on `a dot w=1`. With the heavy/light
    ratio tending to two, every certificate in that prescribed family
    has height above `W_0/2`, while every individual pair Gram is
    strictly negative by an amount growing with the prime scale.
    Two narrow clusters of actual distinct split primes realize this
    with `W_0=O(Mlog M)`. This is not an endpoint construction;
    other subspaces, weight-dependent selections, and simultaneous
    phase constraints remain available. Exact rational and actual-prime
    fixtures check the identity and all pair Grams.
    A restriction lemma preserves a route to adaptive choices: if no
    label is assigned more than b times, every subspace H of size N
    has a translate with at most b rows whose labels restrict to zero.
    Patching these rows, extracting, and discarding affected cosets
    leaves at least `N^(3/4)-bh` genuinely aligned rows when positive.
    This works for H chosen using the weights, retains the original
    radius, and does not itself control the signed sum Psi.
    Item 333 later obtains the needed adaptive control under a
    hypothesized bounded growth ratio and removes the extra weight
    hypothesis for a slower unconditional growth improvement.

323. **Complete fair cuts obstruct a universal partition-certificate mixture.**
    For `M=2k>=6`, average a nonzero balanced `{0,1,-1}`
    row certificate of support m over all balanced cut columns.
    Its mean absolute half-coefficient `A_M(m)` is nondecreasing
    with m by conditional Jensen, and
    `A_M(2)=k/(2k-1)`,
    `A_M(4)=k(3k-5)/[(2k-1)(2k-3)]`.
    A nonnegative mixture whose baseline coefficient is at most
    `1/2` on every cut, of total mass L and support-at-least-four
    mass alpha, must satisfy
    `L<=(M-1)/M-[(k-2)/(2k-3)]alpha`.
    Near-unit phase mass therefore allows only `O(1/M)` weight
    on longer certificates. The universal pair mixture gains exactly
    `2/M^2` per flipped physical column, insufficient to recover its
    `W_0/(2M)` missing phase mass when `Ftot<=W_0`.
    This is a [pointwise mixture obstruction](complete_fair_partition_mixture_barrier.md),
    not a counterexample to endpoint realizability or to other kinds
    of certificates. Sol proved it; Root and Luna audited it independently.

324. **Minimal weighted-obtuse sign profiles have additional exact structural restrictions.**
    If M sign rows in `M-1` positive-weight coordinates have all
    off-diagonal Gram entries negative, they have full column rank
    and one positive integral kernel mass. Every column bisects that
    same mass, and any two row-pair difference supports must intersect.
    Pure-integer enumeration excludes all five- and six-row minimal
    patterns with arbitrary positive coordinate weights. Separately,
    replacing just one nonconstant column of a Hadamard core can
    preserve strict weighted obtuseness only by using that column
    or its negative; summing cross-part Gram entries proves this
    regardless of the retained weights. A graph-count argument also
    excludes the seven-row kernel mass `(2,1,1,1,1,1,1)`.
    See the [structural note](minimal_weighted_obtuse_hadamard_core_rigidity.md).
    General minimal-rank Hadamard classification remains unproved.
    These finite restrictions do not improve the general growth bound.

A separate [six-row binary certificate audit](m6_five_column_weighted_obtuseness.md)
treats the prescribed central dependence `(1,1,1,1,2,2)`. Luna found exact
nonnegative certificates excluding all 21 five-column subsets of its seven
balanced cut classes. Root verified the certificates, explicitly normalized
the weak feasibility problem, and added nonzero weak witnesses for the nine
boundary cases. The full seven-column system has a strict unit-weight
witness. This finite result is not a classification of maximal binary codes
or a parity theorem for odd row counts.

The independently checked [primitive-chord transform](endpoint_primitive_chord_transform.md)
also gives `M<=2+C^3 sqrt(R)/(4g)` on a minor arc, where `g` is
the coordinate gcd of its extreme chord. Primitive extreme chords
are possible at the endpoint scale, so this is only a conditional
uniform estimate for large `g`, not an improvement to the general
growth rate. The [CM pencil normalization](cm_pencil_infinity_normalization.md)
and [real-order audit](polynomial_real_order_audit.md) likewise add
exact reductions and checks, without a new endpoint bound.

A fresh direct-coordinate audit also found that the existing four-point
Pell family has the fixed primitive affine relation
`15z_0+z_1-12z_2-4z_3=0`, with anchored triangle determinants
`(-32,96,8)`. Thus a blanket radius-power lower bound for the smallest
affine relation is false even as the normalized arc constant tends to
zero. This does not address multiple relations on a growing full-cut
profile; see [the exact affine-kernel audit](four_point_bonus_counterexample.md).

325. **Full-support phases give a positive residual measure for arbitrary weights.**
    In the repeated Walsh model put `q_a=W_a-4F_a/M`,
    `A_M=log 8-2log(MC)` and
    `l=(W0+D-2F+2A_M)/M`. Every full-support character implies
    `r_a=q_a-l>=0`, with exact total
    `sum r_a=W0/M+(2-6/M)F-(1-1/M)(D+2A_M)`.
    For a row subspace of size h, nonzero restriction ell, and any
    row coset, the exact residual phase condition is
    `(h/2)Rcell+(2h/M)Fcell+Fp-2Fmatch>=F+2log(M/h)`.
    Averaging over every row coset gives
    `Rcell>=2F(1/h-1/M)+(4/h)log(M/h)` for every nonzero label fiber.
    These simultaneous restrictions are stronger than pair-Gram
    nonnegativity and exclude the nominal balanced heavy-halfspace
    version of the earlier fixed-family shield. They do not exclude
    every variant of that construction by the same character.
    See [the exact residual identities](walsh_full_support_residual_mass.md).

326. **Actual phases force average class-weight regularity without a weight hypothesis.**
    For `M>=16`, arbitrary assignments, distinct prime weights, and
    common content in the repeated Walsh model, all coset phases imply
    `sum_(a!=0)|W_a-W0/(M-1)|
    <=40F/log M+2W0/M+8log M+8log^+ C=O_C(W0/log M)`.
    An elementary density lemma finds a K-point affine flat in any
    subset of density at least `2(K/M)^(1/K)`. Apply it to the negative
    level sets of `mu_a=r_a-2F/M`: the averaged phase inequality bounds
    every affine-flat sum of mu below by `-2F/M`. Integrating the
    resulting exponentially decaying level-set bounds controls all
    negative residual mass. Centering at the actual class mean gives
    the stated total-variation bound, with the common content retaining
    its favorable sign. Its common-content corollary is redundant:
    the earlier pair-slack average already gives the stronger
    `D<=4log C-log 4+W0/(M-1)`.
    Root proved the class-weight result and a fresh Astra
    independently audited every constant and the density recurrence.
    See [the regularity theorem](walsh_phase_class_mass_regularity.md).
    Average regularity alone does not control the signed slack of the
    aligned flat needed for a growth improvement.

327. **A sparse approximate-slack condition extends nonlinear growth to arbitrary prime weights.**
    Fix `0<delta<=1`. Suppose actual nonnegative pair slack `u_d`
    differs from some `c>=0` by at most `(log M)/8` outside a set
    of at most `M^(1-delta)` nonzero directions. A random subspace of
    dimension `s=floor(delta log_2 M/2)` can avoid that exceptional set.
    Some coset has at most `b+1` low-weight or zero-restriction rows;
    patching these rows, applying item 320, and discarding contaminated
    flats yields an actual aligned flat with flip mass at least
    `(h/2)log M`, where `h>=s/(16(log_2(s+2))^2)`.
    The constant part of its signed slack contributes exactly c,
    since the character signs sum to one. The resulting phase bound is
    `W0>=(1/32)Mh log M` for sufficiently large M depending on C,delta.
    Thus the improved count of item 320 holds under this explicit
    additional slack hypothesis, without requiring nearly equal primes.
    See [the conditional proof](walsh_sparse_approximate_slack_growth.md).
    No argument yet forces the hypothesis for arbitrary actual weights.

328. **A non-Walsh Hadamard example obstructs every saturated primitive character at fixed order.**
    The normalized Paley matrix of order twelve has a balanced four-row
    transform norm `4/3`, so the Walsh `3/2` gap does not generalize.
    Nevertheless, take five copies of each nonconstant column and one
    distinct physical flip per row, assigning any label at most twice.
    Every nonzero zero-sum integer c has physical coefficient norm
    `B(c)>=28>55/2`, and this covers the full saturated character lattice.
    The proof exhausts the 36,894 sign-normalized ternary vectors,
    identifies all 187 norm-one cases, and handles arbitrary larger
    amplitudes by Hadamard inversion. Actual sufficiently nearby split
    prime logarithms give strict negative pair Grams and a positive
    primitive half-height gap for every such character.
    See [the theorem](paley_twelve_full_character_height_obstruction.md)
    and [Sol's independent audit](paley_twelve_full_character_independent_audit.md).
    The order-twenty support-four and support-six diagnostic has raw
    minima 24 and 28; it is not a full classification. Neither result
    asserts an actual endpoint configuration or an obstruction at
    unbounded Paley orders.

329. **Fixed reflection choices cannot provide a new nonconformal projective map.**
    Composing whole-tuple anchor swaps and chord-bisector reflections
    gives only `q -> kappa q` or `q -> kappa/q`, preserving the
    primitive least radius and angular span. If a single projective map
    agrees pointwise with one of two fixed conformal maps on at least
    five inputs, it equals one of them: three inputs choose the same
    branch and determine the projective map. A fixed family of K
    conformal maps has the analogous threshold `2K+1`. An exact
    four-point counterexample checks the limitation of the five-input
    argument. See [the reflection rigidity note](chord_reflection_projective_no_go.md).
    This does not treat a family of axes growing with the tuple.

330. **Actual-point double inversion supplies a concrete map but can lose the endpoint scale.**
    With an actual source point a and `N=R^2`, inversion about a with
    scale `tN`, followed by inversion about `-a` with scale `(4-t)N`,
    maps the circle back to itself. After reanchoring and reflection,
    it is exactly `X -> X/k`, where `k=(4-t)/t`.
    At `t=3`, both scales are integers and the small angle compresses
    by three, but the four-point Pell fixture changes its least squared
    radius from `358853785` to `2085984659911668125` and its normalized
    span from about `1.912` to `175.944`. Two larger exact fixtures
    likewise show substantial height growth. See
    [the inversion and all-edge calculation](actual_point_double_inversion_height_test.md).
    This tests a candidate construction; it does not establish a
    nonconformal endpoint image for every tuple.

331. **Simultaneous finite coset-weight optima have exact rational certificates.**
    With unit flip weights and class weights at least five, impose
    `h sum_(a|V=ell)W_a-W>=4k_max-2h` for every subspace and nonzero
    restriction. The archived nonlinear 32-row map has exact minimum
    `W=155` across all 2,077 constraints. A seeded 64-row map has exact
    minimum `W=496` across all 23,562 constraints, compared with 504
    for the best uniform weights. Its optimum is
    `W_a=63/8+(chi_4(a)+chi_29(a))/16`; a 58-constraint rational dual
    proves optimality. The [note and portable checker](walsh_simultaneous_coset_weight_lp.md)
    record both primal and dual certificates, checked independently
    by Root. This is a finite half-height diagnostic, not an actual
    endpoint configuration or an asymptotic growth improvement.

332. **A nonlinear three-bit product has polynomial-size aligned flats and a new family growth bound.**
    The permutation `f=(0,1,3,6,7,4,5,2)` satisfies
    `(f(u)+f(u+w)) dot w=1` for every nonzero three-bit direction w.
    Apply f independently to `2m` blocks and replace its sole zero
    label at the origin by a duplicate nonzero label. The resulting
    `M=2^(6m)` assignment has capacity two. Pairing the blocks and
    choosing an independent nonzero direction in each block gives a
    row subspace of size `h=2^m=M^(1/6)` on whose every nonzero-
    restriction coset the assignment is aligned. Each restriction has
    exactly `M/h^2` such cosets, unaffected by the origin repair.
    The actual near-equal-prime phase bound forces `b>h` eventually,
    hence `log R^2>=c_C M^(7/6)log M` and
    `M=O_C((log R/loglog R)^(6/7))` in this family.
    Every nonzero derivative of f has four values, each twice, so f
    agrees with any affine map on at most four of its eight inputs.
    Slicing one block shows the product differs from every global
    affine map on at least `M/2-1` rows after repair. Thus the result
    is not covered by the previous sublinear-exception affine theorems.
    See [the nonlinear foliation proof](walsh_nonlinear_triple_gadget_foliation.md).
    This family theorem does not place general circle configurations
    in a Walsh profile or establish a radius-independent bound.

333. **Four-row phases and finite-color Ramsey remove every extra prime-weight hypothesis.**
    Averaging the exact four-row inequalities over all row cosets gives
    `u_d<=u_e+u_(d+e)+4F/M+4log 2` for distinct nonzero d,e.
    Averaging over e then yields the pointwise bound
    `u_d<=6W0/M+2a_C+4log 2`, where
    `a_C=max(0,4log C-log 4)`. Under a hypothetical
    `W0<=K Mlog M`, only a fixed number of slack intervals of width
    `(log M)/8` are needed. The finite vector-space Ramsey theorem
    supplies an arbitrarily large fixed-dimensional linear subspace
    whose nonzero directions lie in one interval. Copy capacity and
    the prime-count bound allow a row coset with at most `b+1` bad
    rows; patching, nonlinear extraction, and discarding contaminated
    flats leave an actual aligned certificate with large flip mass.
    Choosing its support h larger than `16(K+1)` contradicts the
    exact phase inequality, which would force `(7/8)h<=10K+1+o(1)`.
    Consequently `W0/(Mlog M)->infinity` for every actual repeated-
    Walsh assignment, with arbitrary distinct prime sizes, row units,
    common content, and copy count. Equivalently, this family has
    `M=o_C(log R/loglog R)`. Quantitative vector-space Ramsey with
    `s=K^2` gives the stronger explicit family estimate
    `W0>=c Mlog M(log_2^* M)^(1/3)` and hence
    `M=O_C(log R/[loglog R(log_2^* R)^(1/3)])`, above enormous
    fixed-C thresholds. The pointwise slack bound also gives, by
    Parseval, the stronger class regularity
    `sum|W_a-W0/(M-1)|=O_C(W0/sqrt M)`.
    Astra found the main argument; Root, Sol,
    and a separate Luna instance audited its algebra, quantifiers,
    ambient-radius normalization and restriction step. See
    [the arbitrary-weight Ramsey proof](walsh_arbitrary_weight_ramsey_growth.md).
    The general circle problem still lacks an extraction into this
    structured model, so its best general bound is unchanged.

334. **The four-row extension beyond Walsh symmetry has a genuine quartic defect.**
    For arbitrary weighted sign rows put
    `T=sum_j w_j s_1j s_2j s_3j s_4j`. The exact balanced four-row
    character identity and its nonunit phase bound give
    `u12+u34<=u13+u14+u23+u24+(W-T)+8log 2`.
    A Walsh parallelogram removes the unflipped quartic defect.
    In contrast, normalized Paley matrices of order `M=q+1`, for
    primes `q=3 mod 4`, have absolute nonconstant-column quartic
    sum at most `3sqrt(q)+4` for every quadruple, by the squarefree
    cubic/quartic character-sum bound. With fixed b copies, one
    distinct physical flip per row, and actual nearby prime logs,
    every quadruple therefore has `W-T=(1-o(1))W`.
    Row deletion cannot produce a small-defect quadruple. These
    actual-prime profiles have `W=O(Mlog M)` and satisfy every pair
    and balanced four-row necessary phase-height inequality for large q,
    but no short-arc localization is asserted. They themselves have
    `u_max=O(W/M)`, so this obstructs the low-defect extraction route,
    not a possible general maximum-slack theorem or the endpoint goal.
    See [the identity, proof and scope](general_four_row_quartic_slack_obstruction.md).
    Root independently checked the Boolean identity, constants,
    prime-cluster perturbations, and cited character-sum theorem.

335. **A tighter Ramsey parameter choice improves the arbitrary-weight family growth rate.**
    In item 333 choose `m=ceil(log_2 K)` and `s=2^14 K m^2`,
    instead of `s=K^2`. For integer `K>=2^24`, the existing
    aligned-flat theorem still gives `h>=32K`, while the Ramsey
    threshold has iterated logarithm at most `2^20 K^2 m^2`.
    Taking `K=floor(sqrt(T)/[2^12 log_2 T])`, where
    `T=log_2^* M`, preserves all varying-parameter cutoffs and
    gives the contradiction in the original exact phase inequality.
    Hence `W0>=c Mlog M sqrt(T)/log_2 T` and, writing
    `T_R=log_2^* R`,
    `M=O_C(log R log_2 T_R/[loglog R sqrt(T_R)])`.
    This sharpens the growth saving in the same arbitrary-weight
    repeated-Walsh model; it does not widen the family hypothesis.
    Root derived the refinement and Sol independently checked all
    parameter inequalities and the radius inversion. The companion
    checker adds 1,112 exact integer parameter fixtures. See the
    [quantitative appendix](walsh_arbitrary_weight_ramsey_growth.md).

336. **Paley fourth moments exclude cheap characters through growing square-root support.**
    For a zero-sum ternary character c supported on h rows of the
    order-`M=q+1` Paley matrix, put `L(c)=sum|H^T c|/M`.
    Orthogonality and the uniform quartic character-sum bound give
    `L(c)>=sqrt(h)/sqrt(3-2/h+h^2(3sqrt(q)+5)/(q+1))`.
    Consequently, for every fixed `0<epsilon<1/3`, L is uniformly
    above one throughout `4<=h<=(1/3-epsilon)sqrt(q)` at large q.
    The explicit range `q>=4099`, `h<=sqrt(q)/16` gives
    `L(c)>=sqrt(8/7)`. In the repeated-column one-flip model with
    `b>=5` and label capacity two, all such saturated characters,
    row-pair characters, and every character of amplitude at least
    two exceed primitive half-height. Norm-one ternary characters
    correspond to rank-one rectangles of area M, hence have
    `h|M` and `M/h` active labels. Capacity also excludes these
    when `h>=2sqrt(M)`. Higher-support characters of norm slightly
    above one remain uncontrolled. This is an unbounded obstruction
    to short character extraction, not an endpoint construction or
    an improved general point count. See the
    [moment proof and exact scope](paley_sqrt_support_fourth_moment_gap.md).

337. **A one-sided block-phase cone has a uniform endpoint count, and angular collapse alone gives no extraction.**
    For arbitrary moving sign profiles with a literal common row unit,
    orient every nonconstant nonunit Gaussian block at an actual
    anchor. If all block phases are nonnegative and every row's
    separating-phase sum is less than `pi/2`, then
    `Delta>=2(|d|/R)^(1/r)`, with r the number of such blocks.
    Integrality of each block's nonzero imaginary coordinate proves
    this inequality. At `Delta<=C/sqrt R`, r>=3 is impossible
    for `C<=2`, and otherwise forces `R<=(C/2)^6`; r<=2 gives
    at most four distinct points. The resulting count is uniform
    in R for this explicit cone. Independent row units, cancellation,
    and phase winding are not removed by the proof.
    Conversely, every finite sign profile admits exact Gaussian-
    primitive realizations with `Delta->0` and any prescribed positive
    rational limiting block weights: use `(a_j T+i)^(d_j)` with
    distinct even a_j and T divisible by all square differences.
    Their block norms are pairwise coprime. Applied to growing Paley
    profiles, this yields actual simultaneous angular collapse and
    strict pair obtuseness while every quartic defect remains of
    order W. Their endpoint constants diverge. Thus unscaled angular
    compactness cannot supply the missing general reduction. See
    [the uniform cone theorem and realization lemma](one_sided_block_phase_cone.md).

338. **Adaptive diagonal maps have an exact radius formula, and source-anchor choice really changes it.**
    For half-angle rows `(X_i,L)` and the primitive map `diag(a,d)`,
    each transformed pair has raw dot and determinant
    `D_ij=a^2 X_i X_j+d^2 L^2` and
    `E_ij=adL(X_j-X_i)`. Its reduced Gaussian denominator norm is
    `(D_ij^2+E_ij^2)/(gcd(D_ij,E_ij)^2 epsilon_ij)`, with the
    exact parity factor `epsilon_ij` equal to one or two. The target
    squared radius is the ordinary lcm of every such edge norm.
    This gives a raw radius lower bound uniform in positive
    `rho=a/d`: for each positive pair,
    `N'>=2X_i X_j/(X_i-X_j)^2`. It does not bound the normalized
    endpoint scale, because increasing rho also compresses angles.
    Reanchoring the source before applying a fixed nonconformal map
    changes the target: at `L=1`, source cotangents `(2,3)` and
    `diag(2,1)` give `N'=629`, whereas reanchoring at the first
    finite point gives `N'=3349`. Root caught and corrected the
    initial confusion with reanchoring an already mapped target.
    The corrected formula keeps source-anchor minimization available;
    it does not establish existence of a successful map for general
    source tuples. See
    [the exact formula and order-of-operations audit](adaptive_diagonal_radius_distortion.md).

339. **Different source-anchor targets obey a parameter-independent product content bound.**
    Normalize distinct source phases by `q_0=1`, and let N be their
    least squared radius. For fixed coprime positive a,d put
    `U=a+d`, `V=a-d`, and
    `Q_ij=(Uq_i+Vq_j)/(Vq_i+Uq_j)`. These are the images after
    reanchoring at j and applying the same diagonal map; the exact
    symmetry is `Q_ji=Q_ij^(-1)`. Let `n_ij` be the two-point
    squared radius of `{1,Q_ij}`, and N_j that of the full jth target.
    Then `A=product_(i<j)n_ij^2/product_j N_j` is a positive integer.
    If B is the product of the source primitive pair residues, the
    full part of A supported outside `2N` divides `B^(m-2)`.
    At a split prime, the target radius exponent is the range of
    signed valuations at its anchor. The surplus over this range
    is bounded by same-sign pair minima; subtracting the two
    numerators or denominators bounds each minimum by the source
    pair residue. This remains valid at primes dividing ad, without
    a determinant or parameter factor. Outside `2NB`, therefore,
    `product_j N_j=product_(i<j)n_ij^2` prime by prime.
    The correction is sharp already for `H=(1,4+i,9+i)` and
    `diag(1,2)`, where `N=697`, `B=A=5`. This couples genuinely
    different target circles, unlike coordinate changes of one fixed
    physical map. It gives no sufficiently small individual N_j or
    bounded-endpoint target. Root and Sol independently audited the
    valuation proof, including parity, relative normalization and
    all parameter-prime cases. The checker passes 532 exact cases
    with 94 nontrivial corrections outside the source radius. See
    [the product identity and its precise scope](adaptive_diagonal_anchor_radius_product.md).

340. **The anchor-product content bound now includes every source prime.**
    In item 339, take `m>=2`, coprime positive `a!=d`, and put
    `G=gcd(N,|(a+d)(a-d)|)`. The complete integer quotient obeys
    `A | B^(m-2) G^((m-1)(m-2))`. At a split prime with
    `h=v_p((a+d)(a-d))>0`, transformed source valuations are signed
    clipped source differences, with outward excess only at the two
    boundary levels. Same-sign excess minima are charged to source
    pair residues, including negative source levels. The exact
    baseline loss is
    `E_h=2sum_(i<j)min(|s_i-s_j|,h)`
    `-sum_j[min(s_j-s_min,h)+min(s_max-s_j,h)]`, bounded by
    `(m-1)(m-2)min(h,v_p(N))`. When h=0, equal-level cancellation
    spikes remain and are residue-charged; they are not set to zero.
    For `diag(2,1)`, `diag(3,1)`, and
    `diag(2^k+1,2^k-1)`, k>=1, one has G=1 for every least primitive
    source norm, so the full quotient divides `B^(m-2)`.
    Source overlap is necessary: `H=(1,2+i,3+i)`, `diag(3,2)` gives
    `N=25`, B=1, edge norms `(5,85,445)`, full target norms
    `(425,445,7565)`, and A=25. Root and a separate Luna audit checked
    the proof. The accompanying checker passes 966 full divisibilities
    and 4,830 local audits, including 324 outward spikes. No individual
    small target or improved point count follows yet. See
    [the full source-prime theorem](adaptive_diagonal_source_prime_content.md).

341. **Endpoint-map existence has a complete small-parameter reconstruction criterion.**
    For a primitive m-point source of squared radius N, m>=8, and
    source and target endpoint constants at most two, every full
    nonconformal rational map has a representative at an actual source
    anchor z_j recovered from `E|N`, a nonzero Gaussian integer Z, and
    one positive integer a. All three have size `N^O(1/m)`, with
    explicit constants. Put `W=Z conjugate(z_j)/E=r+is`; require W
    integral, `b=s/(2a)` integral, and `d^2=a^2-b^2-r` a positive
    integer square, then apply `((a,b),(0,d))`. The exact all-pair
    least target radius and actual angular width finish the test.
    Necessity uses reciprocal clipped conductor `Q=N/E` and the
    projection divisibility `Q | Wgram z_j`; inversion and the
    triangular adjugate cover either radius ordering. The raw search
    count has N-exponent `137/(4m)+O(m^-2)`, and is at most
    `m 2^113 N^(70/m)` for m>=256. A necessary scalar prefilter
    requires `NS=Fminus Fplus`, where S is a sum of two squares of
    size `N^(27/m+O(m^-2))`, and the positive factor gap has size
    `N^(21/(2m)+O(m^-2))`, with explicit m-dependent constants.
    Root and a fresh Sol independently audited the reverse identity,
    anchor normalization, radius ordering and exponents. The checker
    verifies 1,872 forward and inverse recoveries each, full target
    radii and 9,993 rational exponent fixtures. These tests support
    the algebra; no candidate is guaranteed to pass. See
    [the reconstruction criterion](endpoint_map_small_parameter_reconstruction.md).

342. **Norms admitting large nonconformal endpoint maps form a sparse arithmetic set.**
    Uniformly for every integer M>=128, the number of least source
    squared radii N<=X admitting a full nonconformal endpoint map on
    any m>=M points, with both constants at most two, is
    `O_epsilon(X^(beta_M+epsilon))`, where
    `beta_M=1/4+8/M+23/(M-4)`; the implied constant is independent
    of M. In particular `beta_128=247/496<1/2`. The selected
    triangular representative satisfies
    `N | E(b^2+(a+d)^2)(b^2+(a-d)^2)`, with
    `E<=2^8 N^(8/m)`, `a,d<=2^15 N^(7/(m-4))`, and
    `|b|<=2^17 N^(1/4+9/(m-4))`. Counting these quartic values
    and their divisors proves the result. For fixed exact m, the
    sharper exponent is `1/4+61/(4m)+O(m^-2)`.
    The explicit primitive source norms `N_n=4n^2+1` come from
    `2n-i,2n+i`; all but `O_eta(Y^(247/248+eta))` indices n<=Y
    fail an explicit arithmetic sieve for maps retaining at least
    128 points. These exhibited sources have only two points.
    No large endpoint source on an excluded norm is claimed, and
    the sparse permitted set could still contain every hypothetical
    counterexample to uniformity. Root and Sol independently audited
    the proof, including analytic constants for all m>=128 and the
    uniform divisor bound. The checker passes 1,980 actual map cases
    and 9,873 exponent fixtures. See
    [the source-norm sparsity theorem](endpoint_map_source_norm_sparsity.md).

343. **Actual cancellation families test the limits of pair-support extraction.**
    The support-packing consequence of the existing exact pair chord
    inequality is not a new arithmetic theorem. Two explicit
    primitive families instead audit proposed extraction steps.
    A four-point Pell recast has one negative anchored block phase,
    one common row unit, complete two-block exchange graph K4,
    packing mass two, and unbounded radius on `29 sqrt(R)` arcs.
    The six-block five-point affine-shape family has two negative
    anchored phases after a literal common-unit rewrite. Its ten
    pair supports have sizes three through five, and its columns
    are distinct modulo complement, so synchronized merging creates
    no two-block exchange. Its full pair-support packing optimum
    is exactly two: weights one-half on pairs 01,02,14,24 load all
    six blocks once. An unreduced unimodular integral monomial
    change of blocks preserves the literal radius product only
    if it is a signed permutation. Rational changes with gcd
    correction remain outside this argument. The five-point arc
    constant tends to `2sqrt(5)`, so this is not an obstruction
    to extraction restricted to C<=2. Root independently checked
    the Pell tuple and the support certificate; Luna audited the
    analytic Pell bound. A separate Luna calculation also confirmed
    that equal first and third subset moments in this fixed
    six-coefficient profile force all five rows to coincide, in
    agreement with the existing signed-shape obstruction. See
    [the phase-exchange extraction audit](opposite_phase_exchange_graph.md).

344. **The tangent normalization retains an exact congruence but loses multiplicity in real limits.**
    At an actual endpoint `z_0=g(p,q)` with primitive (p,q), put
    `A=p^2+q^2`, `rho=g sqrt(A)`, and for an integer displacement
    delta set `x=p delta_x+q delta_y`, `y=p delta_y-q delta_x`,
    d=-x. Then `y^2=d(2gA-d)`, `|delta|^2=2gd`, and
    `d+By=0 mod A` for an explicit B with `B^2=-1 mod A`.
    In physical coordinates `n=x/sqrt(A)` and
    `s=y/sqrt(A rho)`, the equation is exactly
    `s^2=-2n-n^2/rho`, and the displacement-lattice covolume is
    `rho^(-1/2)`. Thus these lattices have no compact full-rank
    lattice limit at this scale. Four distinct points in the
    existing primitive Pell family all converge to (0,0) after
    this normalization. Counting distinct real limit points
    therefore loses multiplicity. This does not rule out a
    compactification retaining arithmetic and multiplicity data,
    or prove failure of every compactness approach. Root tightened
    that scope and checked the exact coordinate identities.
    A fresh Sol then proved a rational-direction height floor on
    the same four-point family. Its physical directions approach
    `arctan((sqrt(5)-1)/2)` with error `O(N^(-1/3))`.
    The nonzero integer form `b^2+ab-a^2` implies
    `dist_mod_pi(arg(a+ib),arg(z_j))>=c/(a^2+b^2)-O(N^(-1/3))`.
    Thus angular approximation within `K N^(-1/4)` requires
    Gaussian direction height at least `c_K N^(1/8)` for large
    indices. These four-point arcs have normalized length tending
    to zero. A stronger extraction for many points must therefore
    use their growing cardinality. Root independently checked the
    limiting direction and the quadratic integer-form proof. See
    [the endpoint coordinate model](anisotropic_endpoint_lattice_compactness_obstruction.md).

345. **The eight-point target has an exact source-deletion gcd formulation.**
    For primitive equal-norm Gaussian points, put
    `H_i=gcd_G(z_k:k!=i)` and
    `L_ij=gcd_G(z_k:k not in {i,j})/(H_i H_j)`.
    The latter quotients are Gaussian integers. If
    `A=product Norm(H_i)` and `F=product Norm(L_ij)`, then
    `log A=V_1` and `log F=V_2`, including every repeated prime layer.
    Thus the still-open intrinsic inequality is exactly
    `A^8 F^3 <= exp(B) N`. The singleton blocks and, separately,
    the pair blocks are pairwise Gaussian-coprime. Nonincident
    singleton/pair blocks are coprime; incident overlap is allowed.
    The pair blocks supported by one rational prime form at most
    two disjoint edges. These facts give a factorization-free way
    to state the missing estimate, not a proof of it. Direct triangle
    products still lie in the existing determinant cone. Root and
    Astra independently checked the identities on actual primitive
    tuples; the expanded global-content checker passes 1,200 circle
    tuples and 512 additional repeated-prime eight-point fixtures.
    See [the source-gcd formulation](finite_local_test_attack.md).

346. **Odd moments and parity exclude the low-degree rational-linear bonus failures.**
    In a literal single-use family `H_j(T)=a_j+iT`, equal signed
    moments of orders `1,3,...,2s-1` force two rows at Hamming
    distance at most `2s` to coincide after their leading units
    align. Newton's identities pair the changed coefficients with
    their negatives, so their actual Gaussian row ratio cancels.
    This collision lemma permits repeated coefficients and independent
    row units. Distinct rows therefore have distance at least
    `2s+1`; appending parity raises that to `2s+2`.
    For the primitive endpoint application, assume fixed nonzero
    rational coefficients with pairwise distinct absolute values and
    active columns. Fixed resultants bound every cross-block overlap
    and the common Gaussian content, giving primitive radius
    `R(T)~T^m` up to family-dependent constant factors. Consequently
    `s=floor((m+1)/4)` and the original eight-row defect satisfies
    `D<=16m-56s-40`. Exact column defects `0,1,4,9` give a strict
    leading bonus margin in every active degree through 21. The only
    apparent positive degree-18 profiles are excluded by the padded
    row-incidence identity, and its zero-excess profile is excluded
    by parity. Root, Luna, Astra and Sol independently checked the
    relevant algebra. All specialization constants depend on the
    fixed template; no uniform statement over moving coefficients
    or arbitrary Gaussian clusters follows. See
    [the rational-linear moment and incidence arguments](odd_moment_separation.md).

347. **Two deleted Hadamard columns admit no distinct cubic-moment lift.**
    Select any eight rows of any order-twelve Hadamard matrix, with
    arbitrary row and column signs, and delete any two columns.
    The resulting matrix `S` admits no nonzero real vector with ten
    pairwise distinct absolute values satisfying both
    `S a=alpha 1` and `S(a^3)=beta 1`. Restoring two zero coordinates
    and using the four omitted rows gives either four parallel pairs
    or four triples. Pair differences have only three possible
    nonzero magnitudes. The exceptional zero-pair case contradicts
    Bessel's inequality, `224>192`; the triple cases force repeated
    absolute values or incompatible quadratic invariants. This
    excludes fixed active ten-factor endpoint realizations of the
    stated family. Its sign codes already satisfy the strict bonus
    margin, so it does not improve the general eight-point estimate.
    Root independently audited the proof and reran the exact checker:
    495 restrictions, 126,720 row signings and 8,363,520 deletions
    pass, along with the cubic and triple-gap identities. See
    [the cubic-moment variant](critical_pell_moment_codes.md).

348. **Even column counts give an integer moment obstruction in every degree.**
    Let `T` be any eight-row sign matrix with `T T^t=L I`, `4|L`,
    and an even number of plus signs in every column. After deleting
    any two columns, a balanced column remains: the full defect is
    `2L`, so at least `L/2` columns were balanced. Use that retained
    column as a zero-sum row vector `lambda`. The coefficients
    `c=lambda^t S/4` are integral, their own retained coordinate is
    two, and Parseval gives `sum c_j^2<=L/2`. Hence
    `0<sum |c_j|<=L/2-2`. Expanding these integer multiplicities
    in Newton's identities excludes distinct nonzero absolute
    coefficients satisfying the first `s=L/4-1` odd signed moments.
    Endpoint geometry forces exactly that many moments in the fixed
    active rational-linear model of degree `L-2`. No Hadamard
    completion or balanced deleted column is required. A separate
    parity-padded extension allows Gram defect `K<=4` with explicit
    parity and nonvanishing hypotheses. Root, Astra and two separate
    Luna instances audited the retained-column proof. Root and Luna
    independently reran the complete Paley24 checker: 735,471 row
    subsets, 759 positive profiles and 11,385 deleted codes. All the
    latter admit an even shorter eight-term certificate. This is an
    infinite family obstruction; arbitrary endpoint configurations
    have not been placed in this family. See
    [the integer certificate and energy proof](critical_pell_moment_codes.md).

349. **Balanced characters prove the actual even-layer weight inequality.**
    For eight distinct common-unit endpoint points with `C<=2`, suppose
    every nonconstant split-prime threshold layer has even cardinality.
    Let `P` and `B` be the total pair-cut and balanced-cut log-norm weights,
    and let `D` be the log norm of their complete common Gaussian factor.
    Then `B>=5P+35D-140log C`, proving the requested intrinsic inequality
    in this actual subprofile. Arbitrary prime powers, unequal weights
    and nested layers are permitted. For every balanced row character
    `lambda`, the quarter coefficients `lambda^t S/4` are integral and
    give a conjugate-primitive Gaussian product whose squared phase ratio
    equals the source character. Affine allocation rigidity proves it is
    a nonunit. Its integer perpendicular coordinate yields a half-height
    lower bound. Summing all 35 characters gives exact coefficients
    15 on pair cuts and 18 on balanced cuts, hence the inequality.
    With arbitrary units, `C<=sqrt(2)` and even total unit parity, replace
    `C` by `sqrt(2)C`. Odd layers and odd total unit parity remain outside
    this theorem. Root, Astra and Luna independently audited the proof.
    The checker covers all 126 even columns, 11,385 Paley codes, literal
    Gaussian identities and 840 nested-layer identities with 156
    nontrivial content cancellations. See
    [the actual balanced-character theorem](even_column_balanced_character_height.md).
    A related [paired-factor capacity argument](tensor_pair_axis_capacity.md)
    bounds the literal tensor base factor by `C^2/8` for arbitrary units
    and every fixed `C`, under explicit conjugation-injectivity hypotheses.
    It credits the previously known small-constant exclusions and records
    a scalar integer-character averaging barrier; it gives no general
    growth improvement.

350. **An odd-column code evades the complete short Newton certificate lattice.**
    In the normalized `H12 tensor H2` matrix, select rows
    `(0,1,2,4,6,9,19,23)` and delete columns zero and one. Its retained
    profile is `(2,3,2,15)`, with positive intrinsic excess three,
    minimum Hamming distance eleven and zero padded Gram defect.
    The full rational certificate lattice
    `{S^t mu in Z^22: mu in Q^8, sum mu=0}` has minimum nonzero
    `l1` norm eleven. Seven independent coordinates reconstruct the
    entire lattice vector with denominator six; exhaustive enumeration
    of all 433,905 integral pivot vectors of mass at most ten finds
    none, while a row-difference certificate attains eleven. This
    exhausts all rational row coefficients, not just bounded numerators.
    The complete normalized tensor-row scan finds 1,320 odd-column
    positive row subsets, all with full profile `(1,2,3,2,16)`.
    The lattice-minimum assertion concerns the specified representative
    deletion. This is a finite sign-code obstruction to a proof method,
    not an odd-moment solution or an endpoint counterexample. See
    [the exact lattice boundary example](tensor24_odd_column_certificate_gap.md).
    A separate Sol audit proves that odd-moment feasibility requires at
    least five sign changes for every nonzero real row-space character,
    after ordering by squared coefficients. Exact enumeration of all
    10,155 support-minimal characters exhibits an ordering and signing
    satisfying that necessary condition simultaneously. Conformal
    decomposition extends the check to every real character. Thus
    sign variation alone also leaves this code possible; coefficient
    magnitudes or further polynomial identities are still needed. See
    [the simultaneous variation audit](tensor24_odd_column_variation.md).
    Item 354 subsequently excludes its full nonlinear moment system,
    and the complete odd-positive tensor family, by a stronger root-order
    identity. The certificate and variation limitations remain valid.

351. **The common quadratic twist does not provide Gaussian quarter roots.**
    For balanced row characters, the primitive half-character product
    `A_lambda` satisfies `Norm(A_lambda)=t h_lambda^2`, where `t` is
    determined by the aggregate allocation parity at each split prime.
    Hence `A_lambda/(h_lambda sqrt(t))` lies in the common field
    `Q(i,sqrt(t))`. But the Gaussian squareclasses of `A_lambda` can
    have rank 21: the exact full 127-cut profile has that rank, strict
    pair separation, full affine rank and positive intrinsic excess 21.
    Its quarter-root compositum therefore has degree `2^21` over `Q(i)`.
    This degree still depends only on eight rows; it obstructs a single
    quadratic quarter-root field, not every bounded-degree-field method.
    Even in one fixed quadratic extension, `A=(2+i)(x+iy)^2` with
    `(x+2y)^2-5y^2=1` has imaginary part one, so its square root has
    perpendicular distance to an axis tending to zero. A simultaneous
    source-character argument must use more than common-field membership
    and integrality. These fixtures do not satisfy an asserted endpoint
    realization. Root independently audited the squareclass-rank proof
    and Pell identities. See
    [the exact common-twist obstruction](odd_layer_character_quadratic_twist_obstruction.md).
    An additional Sol audit keeps the rational content in every monomial
    relation among the 35 half-characters. The primitive factor is exactly
    the ordinary row character indexed by their integer linear combination;
    a zero combination leaves only a positive rational integer. A nested
    four-subset exchange has content ratio `p^6`, illustrating why that
    content cannot be dropped. On the full 127-cut profile, every nonzero
    integer row character has formal height at least `64h`, while the
    scalar lower bound asks for `63.5h`. Thus collecting all multiplicative
    relations and applying scalar axis gaps still leaves this formal
    profile possible. Additive identities are not covered by this
    obstruction. See [the exact character-relation reduction](balanced_half_character_torus_relations.md).

352. **Aggregate allocation parity permits some odd threshold layers.**
    The quarter-character exponents are integral whenever the total
    allocation across the eight rows is even at every split prime.
    Individual singleton and triple layers may then occur. With their
    weights denoted by `S` and `T`, the same actual common-unit argument
    gives `B+10T>=5P+35D+2K-140log C` for `C<=2`, where `K>=0`
    is the exact loss in the layer triangle inequality before primitive
    reduction. For arbitrary units, retain the even total unit-parity
    hypothesis, `C<=sqrt(2)`, and replace `C` by `sqrt(2)C`.
    Aggregate parity is invariant under common scaling and prime
    orientation; it cannot be enforced by renormalization. The singleton
    term cancels, and `K` can vanish with positive singleton weight,
    so this does not settle the full intrinsic target. Root and a fresh
    Astra independently derived the extension and its cancellation term.
    Root rejected a stronger proposed ratio argument: fixing the first
    character sign breaks the purported cut-size symmetry. Correcting
    all anchored and complementary pairs recovers exactly ten copies
    of each of the 28 ordinary row pairs, hence only the existing bound.
    The corrected checker tests all 254 nonconstant columns and 840
    literal mixed nested identities with 306 odd layers. See
    [the aggregate-parity certificate and ratio audit](aggregate_parity_balanced_character_height.md).

353. **Critical odd moments determine the absolute root sign order.**
    If `2s+1` nonzero real numbers have distinct absolute values and their
    first `s` odd power sums vanish, their signs in increasing absolute
    order must be `++--++--...` or its global negation. Newton's identities
    write the root polynomial as `F(t)+r` with `F` odd. Rolle's theorem
    and reflection make every intermediate fiber `F(t)+u r`, `|u|<=1`,
    real-rooted with simple roots; following its roots from the odd fiber
    gives the asserted order. With `2s+2` roots there are only two patterns,
    `+--++--...` or `++` followed by that pattern, again up to negation.
    The latter follows by counting positive critical points of
    `Q(x)/sqrt(x)` in `P(t)=Q(t^2)+r t`. Root proved both statements;
    Astra independently audited both and Luna audited the critical case.
    Exact rational isolation checks both families, including a degree-12
    example of the second successor pattern. These are nonlinear moment
    theorems, not a reduction of arbitrary endpoint arcs to fixed templates.
    See [the root-order proof](critical_odd_moment_root_order.md).

354. **All 21,120 odd-positive tensor deletions fail the nonlinear moments.**
    The fixed degree-22 code from item 350 has sixteen distance-eleven
    row-pair certificates. Item 353 requires each to use the same ordered
    coefficient magnitudes and signs with pattern `++--++--++-` up to
    negation. An exhaustive prefix search has 3,029 states and no full
    assignment. A separate ternary-state implementation reproduces it;
    ten certificates already suffice, with 177,754 states and no depth-21
    state. Sol then enumerated all 735,471 eight-row subsets of the
    normalized Paley-12 tensor Sylvester-2 matrix. The 1,320 odd-positive
    subsets have sixteen balanced columns each. Their 21,120 deletions
    reduce to 9,056 cut multisets and four classes under row permutations,
    column permutations and column signs. Each class fails the eleven-root
    test. Root audited the equivalence reduction and reran the exact C++
    enumeration; no distance-twelve condition or numerical magnitude solve
    is required. This excludes this entire normalized finite family under
    nonzero, distinct-absolute real coefficients. It does not classify all
    degree-22 sign matrices or imply a general lattice-circle count. See
    [the fixed-code proof](tensor24_odd_column_critical_order_obstruction.md),
    [the independent core audit](tensor24_odd_column_critical_order_core.md),
    and [the family exclusion](tensor24_odd_column_family_critical_order.md).

355. **Fixed additive character polynomials retain a generic height margin.**
    In the common-source-unit setting, the exact normalized half-character
    clearing rule extends to every fixed homogeneous additive polynomial.
    After torus cancellations and a real or imaginary projection, let `E`
    be its reciprocal row-exponent support. At each source prime put
    `m_p=max_(L in E)|2L dot a(p)|` and
    `kappa_p=d sum_i a_i(p) mod2`. Multiplication by
    `sqrt(product p^kappa_p) product p^((m_p-kappa_p)/2)` clears every
    supported term literally, including nested odd layers. Applying the
    previously proved support-multiplicity theorem shows that a nonzero
    polynomial of diagonal order `k` costs at least `32kh` on the full
    127-cut equal-weight profile, versus the endpoint requirement
    `127kh/4`. Four disjoint pair differences attain this coefficient.
    This concerns allocation-based termwise clearing; extra divisibility
    of an evaluated sum and height-dependent coefficients remain outside
    the argument. Separately, all 630 four-term parallelograms among the
    anchored 35 characters factor into pair and balanced four-row sine
    directions, with summed factor heights `128h` or `160h`, both above
    `W=127h`. This last audit is a factorwise scalar test, not a computation
    of every additive numerator's content. Root checked the arithmetic
    normalization, the imported support theorem and both exact checkers.
    See [the general fixed-polynomial obstruction](additive_balanced_character_generic_content.md)
    and [the four-term factor audit](additive_balanced_parallelogram_audit.md).

356. **One polynomial coefficient couples all pairwise root orientations.**
    For any eight orthogonal sign rows of length `4s+4`, delete a constant
    and a balanced column, and suppose the retained coefficients satisfy
    the first `s` odd-moment equations. The row polynomials
    `P_i(t)=product_j(t-S_ij a_j)` share their first `2s` leading
    coefficients. Their coefficients `kappa_i` at degree `2s+1` are
    pairwise distinct: every difference is exactly a nonzero constant
    times the shared-root polynomial, with an extra factor `t` for
    within-group pairs. Their ordering fixes the initial sign orientation
    of every critical or successor pattern. Final row sign sums divide
    the rows into at most three coefficient blocks, so there are only
    seven possible nonconstant first signed columns after that order is
    fixed. Furthermore, at every prefix the signs of all `P_i(t)-P_j(t)`
    must define a transitive value ordering. The sign is computed exactly
    from the parity of unprocessed common positive roots, which is
    determined by prefix row counts and pair distances up to a harmless
    global reversal. These are degree-independent necessary conditions;
    they do not alone prove a uniform exclusion. The exact pair fixtures
    test the polynomial identities, all ten parity/block cases, and all
    28,672 prefixes of signed length-six row pairs. See
    [the common spectral-order theorem](critical_moment_spectral_orientation.md).

357. **Every partial orthogonal eight-row template of length sixteen is excluded.**
    Let `T` be any orthogonal `8-by-16` sign matrix, and delete one constant
    and one balanced column. Its retained `8-by-14` matrix has no nonzero,
    distinct-absolute real coefficients whose first, third and fifth power
    sums are constant across rows. The root-order and common coefficient
    lemmas reduce every possible matrix to five choices for the sizes of
    the final height classes. An exact search tries every signed column,
    including a retained constant column and arbitrary repetitions, with
    all 28 pair distances tracked exactly. The five cases exhaust
    59,684; 87,000; 77,636; 87,000; and 59,684 dead states. None attains
    the sixteen required distances seven and twelve required distances
    eight after fourteen columns. Memoization depends only on the prefix
    length and exact pair counts because all pair types and orientations
    are already fixed. Root audited the complete coverage, coefficient
    orientation and search logic and reran the uncapped C++ checker.
    No Hadamard completion or classification is used. This is a general
    theorem at this finite template degree, not an arbitrary-degree
    exclusion or the radius-independent endpoint theorem. See
    [the partial-orthogonal exclusion](partial_orthogonal16_critical_pattern_obstruction.md).

358. **The new root orders bound three arbitrary-node moment fibers.**
    For any fixed distinct positive nodes, sign vectors with the same first
    `s` odd moments differ in at least `2s+1` places. At supports `2s+1`
    and `2s+2`, item 353 restricts their signs further. The exact graph of
    these pairwise necessary conditions has maximum clique sizes five for
    `(m,s)=(6,1)`, seven for `(10,2)`, and three for `(8,2)`. The graph
    leaves larger supports unrestricted, so each actual moment fiber is
    certainly a clique. An uncapped exhaustive search with a greedy-color
    upper bound proves the finite maxima. In particular eight arbitrary
    sign rows on ten distinct positive nodes cannot share first and third
    moments, with no orthogonality assumption. Root audited the graph and
    the complete branch-and-bound argument and reran the checker; a
    separately implemented graph with the additional variation condition
    gives the same maxima. Extremal abstract cliques are not asserted to
    have realizing node values, and no uniform-in-dimension fiber bound is
    claimed. See [the finite moment-fiber bounds](moment_fiber_compatibility_graph.md).

359. **Bounded row heights and one permutation give a degree-independent graph.**
    In the partial-orthogonal setup, let `r_i=u_i-u_0` be relative prefix
    positive-root counts and normalize the polynomial values by
    `(-1)^(p_0-u_0)`. Their signs are `(-1)^(delta_i-r_i)` and their
    strict value order is a permutation. These data recover all pair
    positions modulo four from the shared-root parity identity. The
    successor-B first occurrence is detected by its zero relative height;
    after it is touched that height never returns to zero. A signed column
    selects a contiguous interval touching or spanning the zero gap in
    the value order. Reverse that interval, and reverse the whole order
    when row zero is selected. Empty and full selections are constant
    self-loops. There are at most 1,215 height vectors and `8!` permutations
    for each of ten parity/group-size cases, independently of degree.
    An actual solution must give a path from the prescribed initial state
    to `(r=delta, order=kappa)` with length `4s+2`, every cross distance
    `2s+1`, and every within-group distance `2s+2`. These exact quantities
    are edge weights; the bounded state does not recover them. Even a path
    with those weights would still require actual real magnitudes.
    Root and Sol independently audited the compression. Astra's completed
    implementation audit checks all 256 column masks on 45,890 states
    through depth five and 413,010 transitions; Root separately reran all
    ten cases through depth two. No all-degree path exclusion is claimed.
    See [the finite weighted-graph reduction](critical_moment_compressed_automaton.md).

360. **The compressed graph has at most 326,496 valid states per case.**
    For each of the 1,215 possible height vectors, every pair admits zero,
    one or two value comparisons under the exact phase and height rules.
    A unique comparison imposes a predecessor relation; sign compatibility
    orders all negative values before positive values. Thus compatible
    permutations are exactly linear extensions, counted by an integer
    recurrence on the 256 subsets of eight rows. Exhausting the height
    vectors gives 322,560 states for `q=0,4`, 325,584 for `q=1,3`, and
    326,496 for `q=2`, for either parity. This is a complete valid-state
    census, with no graph traversal or realizability assumption. Root's
    checker also compares 97,200 sampled height/permutation tests with the
    original validator. The smaller bound makes a full graph computation
    practical but does not itself exclude any weighted path. See
    [the exact compressed-state count](critical_moment_state_census.md).

361. **Aggregate parity gives a six-row gap against a uniform cut profile.**
    For even `k` rows in one source-unit class and `C<=2`, primewise even
    total allocation permits Gaussian quarter-characters. Averaging their
    exact heights over balanced signs gives
    `sum_r(c_(k,r)-1/2)W_r >= D/2+K_k/L_k-2log(kC/8)`, where
    `c_(k,r)=(1/2)E|r-2A|`, `A` is hypergeometric, and `K_k>=0`
    is the exact nested-layer cancellation. For six rows the coefficients
    are `1/2,2/5,3/5`; uniform weights on all 31 intrinsic cuts give
    left side `-W'/62`. Relative error at most `1/20` gives
    `D/2+3W'/248<=2log(3C/4)`, bounding the total weight
    `W=D+W'` by `(496/3)log^+(3C/4)`.
    No fixed-size parity selection follows from the extraction results:
    private odd prime coordinates preserve full affine rank and prevent
    every six-row parity sum from vanishing, even after dominant even
    columns make the intrinsic cut profile arbitrarily uniform. The
    construction works with actual distinct split-prime logarithms and
    literal equal-norm Gaussian points, but has no endpoint angle control.
    Odd parity does not supply the Gaussian quarter-root needed here.
    Root and Luna audited the constants, twist distinction and countermodel;
    the exact coefficient and parity checker passes. See
    [the higher-row parity formula and its limit](higher_row_aggregate_parity_uniform_limit.md).

362. **Actual endpoint pairs need not have real-rooted spectral differences.**
    For `y+x sqrt(75)=(1351+156 sqrt(75))^k`, take the three Gaussian
    factors `x+i(y-8x)`, `5x+iy`, and `x+i(y+8x)`. Their rational norms
    are pairwise coprime, all factors grow, and their logarithmic norm
    proportions tend to `1/3`. Their product is
    `-x(200x^2+7)-iy`. Its negative and conjugate give primitive points
    on one circle with arc constant at most `(27/20)/sqrt(x)`, tending
    to zero. Nevertheless the two monic slope polynomials have difference
    roots `+/- i sqrt(1+1/(11x^2))`; their first odd moments remain
    separated. Small evaluation at `i` therefore does not itself imply
    the common leading moments or real-rooted differences required by
    the template argument. This is a two-row refinement of one cut;
    canonical grouping combines the three factors. It neither rules out
    a transfer using canonical groups nor supplies a near-uniform
    eight-row fixture. The direct logarithmic-derivative kernel also
    has an exact centered form `L S diag(x_c^2 y_c^2/N_c^2) S^t L^t`
    when `L1=0`. Its positivity is automatic before imposing endpoint
    closeness; the Pell derivative gap tends to `11sqrt(3)/10` even
    though normalized point separation is of order `R^(-2/3)`.
    Root independently checked the identities and norm-coprimality
    proof and reran all 32 exact Pell fixtures and their centered
    eight-row kernel identities. See
    [the actual-circle spectral counterfixture](actual_endpoint_spectral_nonreal_difference.md).

363. **Exact weighted paths exist in infinitely many compressed degrees.**
    The full reachable even-`s`, `q=2` graph closes at 322,564 states
    and 2,903,076 labeled edges. Four SCCs are transient singletons and
    one closed SCC has 322,560 states. The terminal is reached in eleven
    steps, with cross distances five, eight within distances six, and
    four within distances two. Each cut-size map permutes the closed
    component, and each specific mask of size `k` appears on exactly
    `322560/binom(8,k)` edges. Active edge weights
    `[0,10,28,56,70,56,28,10,0]` therefore give a strictly positive
    integer circulation of length 83,220,480 and every pair distance
    41,610,240. Twenty-nine replayable active closed walks have label
    rank 29 modulo a prime, hence full rational rank.
    More strongly, an explicit integer combination of those walks
    corrects the eleven-step path to signed-flow labels for `s=2`:
    length ten, cross distance five, and every within distance six.
    The cycle correction's least edge coefficient is `-6`; adding one
    positive circulation makes every active giant-component edge strictly
    positive. Adding `K` copies, for any integer `K>=1`, gives connected
    integer flows with source-to-terminal divergence and the exact target labels for
    `s=2+20805120K`. Directed Euler trails give actual paths with these
    labels and no constant columns. Thus the compressed ordering
    constraints cannot prove an all-degree path exclusion. This does
    not construct real coefficients satisfying the odd moments or
    lattice-point endpoint configurations. Root compiled and reran the
    complete graph and independently replayed all recorded walks and
    the integer correction. See
    [the closed graph, circulation and weighted paths](critical_moment_compressed_graph_even_q2.md).

364. **The full centered row space gives a magnitude-sensitive positivity condition.**
    For the punctured orthogonal template with `s>=2`, write `x_j=a_j^2`
    and absorb the signs of `a_j` into the columns of `V`. With four-row
    group sums `h_Aj,h_Bj`, the centered row-space projector has diagonal
    `q_j=[8-(h_Aj^2+h_Bj^2)/4]/[4(s+1)]`
    `+(h_Aj-h_Bj)^2/[32(s-1)]`. If `H_kl=sum_j x_j^(k+l+1)` and
    `v(x)=(1,x,...,x^(s-1))^t`, all common-row odd moments imply
    `x_j v(x_j)^t H^(-1)v(x_j)<=1-q_j`.
    This optimizes over every real combination of the seven centered
    row directions. For a nonconstant last column it implies
    `(|a_n|/|a_(n-1)|)^(4s-2)<=(1-q_n)(4s+1)/q_n`.
    The full projector condition `K+Q<=I` is equivalent to the moment
    equations for fixed signs and magnitudes; diagonal and coupled
    Vandermonde determinant inequalities are necessary relaxations.
    The nonconstant-column value satisfies
    `q_j>1/(2s+1)>1/(2s+2)`, strictly improving either applicable
    single-pair Bessel bound. This comparison does not claim dominance
    over every nonlinear pairwise moment identity. A fresh Astra derived
    the formulas; Root and Luna independently audited them. This is a
    constraint on real magnitudes omitted by the compressed graph,
    not an all-template exclusion or a transfer to arbitrary circles.
    The exact Fraction checker passes the rank-seven projector formulas,
    364 Vandermonde minors and all 23 nonconstant group-sum types. Its
    arbitrary-node fixture is explicitly not a moment solution.
    See [the multirow Christoffel condition](critical_moment_multirow_christoffel.md).

365. **The Christoffel scalar and determinant relaxations admit explicit magnitudes.**
    For `s>=100`, these relaxations are feasible if and only if the
    centered row space has no nonzero vector supported on at most `s`
    columns. Sufficiency uses
    `x_j=1-cos((2j-1)pi/(2(4s+2)))/20`: discrete Chebyshev orthogonality
    gives `K_jj<21/38<3/5`, while `q_j<=2/(s-1)` already proves all
    scalar inequalities for every template when `s>=5`.
    For the integer row-difference matrix `B`,
    `det(BB^t)=8(4s+4)^6(4s-4)=D_s` and
    `det(I_J-Q_J)=det(B_(Jc)B_(Jc)^t)/D_s`.
    Under the support condition, the numerator is a positive integer.
    Since `(3/5)^s D_s<1` for `s>=100`, all `s`-subset determinant
    inequalities follow. A sparse supported row combination conversely
    forces a zero right side against a positive Vandermonde determinant.
    For item 363's word family, exact mask counts and a Rademacher
    fourth-moment bound give `||Q_J||<39/40`, so the support condition
    holds. Thus the explicit magnitudes pass both relaxations on that
    family. This preserves the graph's discrete tests, not necessarily
    actual polynomial-value orders or the original odd moments. Root
    and Astra supplied separate parts of the proof. Exact checks include
    144 zero and 220 positive complementary Gram minors and an all-degree
    polynomial certificate for the mask bound. See
    [the exact relaxation characterization](critical_moment_christoffel_relaxation_limit.md).

366. **The two-character common-twist determinant factors exactly.**
    For distinct six-row balanced characters `lambda,mu` modulo sign,
    write `Norm(A_lambda)=t h_lambda^2`, `Norm(A_mu)=t h_mu^2`,
    `g=gcd(h_lambda,h_mu)`, and `B_+=A_((lambda+mu)/2)`,
    `B_-=A_((lambda-mu)/2)`. Literal primewise content gives
    `B_+B_-=(h_mu/g)A_lambda` and
    `B_+bar(B_-)=(h_lambda/g)A_mu`, even with nested allocations.
    Hence the signed real-coordinate determinant is exactly
    `h_mu Re(A_lambda)-h_lambda Re(A_mu)=-2g Im(B_+)Im(B_-)`.
    Its natural height is `sqrt(t)lcm(h_lambda,h_mu)=|B_+||B_-|`.
    On an actual common-unit arc with `C<=2`, affine rigidity and the
    two ordinary character bounds give this height at least `2R/C^2`.
    This is precisely the average of their usual logarithmic bounds;
    the new-looking Pell determinant gives no larger radius exponent.
    The equal-weight 31-cut profile retains a `9w/2` leading margin.
    The absolute-real-part branch is treated separately and is not
    silently identified with the signed determinant. Root and Luna
    audited Sol's proof; all 1,800 literal nested-allocation identities
    and all 45 profile pairs pass. See
    [the exact pair determinant factorization](six_row_common_twist_determinant_factorization.md).

367. **Every displayed odd common-twist trigonometric determinant is a scalar product.**
    For `m=2d+1` balanced source characters of common exponent parity
    `kappa_p`, form integer rows from
    `h_i^d` and `h_i^(d-r)Re(A_i^r),h_i^(d-r)Im(A_i^r)`, `1<=r<=d`.
    With `B_ij=A_((lambda_i-lambda_j)/2)`, their determinant satisfies
    `|D_d|=2^(2d^2)F_d product_(i<j)|Im(B_ij)|`.
    The local exponent of `F_d` is
    `[sum_(i<j:c_i c_j>0) min(|c_i|,|c_j|)-kappa_p d^2]/2`.
    It is a nonnegative integer: for odd parity the number of same-sign
    pairs is `d^2+(u-d)(u-d-1)`, and for even parity each minimum is even.
    The exact trigonometric Vandermonde identity supplies the determinant
    factor, including the signed triple formula `D_1=-4F_1 product Im(B)`.
    Its phase-height inequality is exactly the product of ordinary
    scalar character bounds after removing `F_d`. This covers the
    displayed family with value-dependent coefficients involving the
    `h_i`; it does not exclude other additive identities or additional
    arithmetic of the evaluated scalar factors. Root and Astra derived
    the extension; Luna independently audited it. Exact checks cover
    855 one-prime triples, 100 several-prime triples, 1,440 six-source
    character triples, 80 general determinant fixtures, and every
    independent unit choice on three prime generators at `d=1,2`. See
    [the odd trigonometric determinant factorization](common_twist_triple_determinant_factorization.md).

368. **Two cubic angle contractions fail on an explicit four-point endpoint family.**
    For odd `d`, the map `u -> u^d` has exact least target radius
    `|lcm_G bar[(a_i^d+i b_i^d)/(1+i)^epsilon_i]|`, with the parity
    units retained in the actual phases. Polynomial divisibility implies
    `R_d>=R` for every primitive source tuple. More sharply, the actual
    four points `(n+sigma i)(n+1+tau i)/(1+i)`, with `n` a positive
    multiple of ten, have `R asymp n^2` and endpoint constant below four.
    Their cubic images have least radius `R_3 asymp n^10=R^(5+o(1))`
    and angular width `asymp n^-3`, so the new endpoint constant grows
