    has integer distance at least five: a shorter signed list would
    force opposite equal-magnitude terms, which aggregate cancellation
    has removed. Threshold embedding and parity again force `K5` at
    total width nine.

    A repeated coefficient has nested threshold supports. The unique
    minority-edge columns permit at most two, necessarily a two-set
    inside a three-set. They give opposite nonzero weights on disjoint
    edges, with only the parity edge zero. Two complete affine
    parametrizations and integer polynomial certificates exclude this:
    the four cubic equations generate `3200 u` in one symmetry case
    and `9600` in the other. The first forces another zero edge and
    the second is impossible. No numerical feasibility assumption
    or unverified elimination result is used.

    For fixed rational signed-factor families, grouping equal absolute
    coefficients, removing zero factors and cancelling common polynomial
    orientations leaves this exact aggregate width. Polynomial Bezout
    bounds the remaining specialized Gaussian gcd. Effective widths
    seven through nine therefore cannot support five persistent endpoint
    rows, even with repeated factors. Raw factor count cannot replace
    effective width, and moving coefficients remain outside this moment
    consequence. Root supplied the reduction, Astra the certificates,
    and Sol and Luna independently audited the algebra and boundary
    cases. Both permanent checkers pass. See the
    [extended moment theorem](five_row_nine_factor_moment_exclusion.md)
    and [repeated-edge lemma](repeated_k5_zero_edge_exclusion.md).

422. **Repeated six-factor moments have only two admissible coefficient rays.**
    At `C<=1/2`, aggregate count rows in the signed-factor model
    must be affinely independent: every split-prime valuation is an
    affine function of those counts, including shared factors, and
    the existing allocation-rigidity theorem applies after full gcd
    removal. Equal first moments therefore require at least five
    distinct positive coefficient groups for five rows. With six
    factors and any repetition, exactly one of the five groups is
    doubled.

    Enumerating all 3,360 five-cliques of integer distance at least
    three in `{0,1,2} x {0,1}^4` and evaluating exact cofactor normals
    leaves 96 positive, distinct-coefficient cases. Up to permutation
    of the singleton groups, their rays are `(1,2,3,4,5)` and
    `(2,1,3,4,5)`, forty-eight times each. Each has two complementary
    fibers of exactly five rows. Their literal signed-product tuples
    are the six-factor representative at `(u,v)=(2,-5)` and `(1,2)`,
    up to conjugation, row permutation and common coefficient scale.
    The existing content estimate applies even at these repeated
    magnitudes and gives normalized span at least
    `2/sqrt(5 sqrt(2))>1/2`. Thus the exact equal-first-moment six-factor
    exclusion also permits repeated magnitudes and moving rational
    parameters.

    For fixed rational factor constructions this closes effective
    width six. Width at most two has at most four aggregate vectors;
    widths three through five force equal first moments and are
    excluded by distance-three counting, using parity at width five.
    Widths seven through nine are excluded by item 421. Consequently
    five fixed distinct rows of effective width at most nine cannot
    persist on target arcs as `T` tends to infinity. This conclusion
    has a coefficient-dependent threshold and no reduction from
    arbitrary circle configurations.

    Astra supplied the classification and permanent exact checker;
    Sol independently enumerated the graph with rational row reduction
    and audited the valuation transfer. Root identified the signed
    parameters for the first ray, checked the combined conclusion and
    replayed the checker. See the
    [repeated six-factor classification](sixfactor_repeated_magnitude_classification.md).

423. **Arithmetic alignment restores endpoint scale on the four-point Pell family.**
    Let `x=4UV=a-b`, `T=x^2+1=ab`, with the established Pell source
    of squared radius `5abc`. The endpoint-swapping matrix
    `[[x,tau],[1,-x]]` preserves its exact angular span. At `tau=x^2`,
    two mandatory coprime Gaussian denominators force image width
    at least `sqrt(10)V`, while the source width tends to zero.
    At `tau=x^2+2`, exact interior contents reduce the representatives
    to `B_0=x+i`, `B_1=(17a-b)+i`, and `B_2=(a+2b)+i`.
    Removing the single ramified factor from `B_2` leaves a factor
    coprime to `B_1`, and their product covers `B_0`. The least target
    squared radius is exactly
    `ab(288a-31b)(7a+3b)/2`. Its normalized width is below fifteen
    and tends to `14.732989546...`, despite the increasing radius.

    More generally, for fixed positive integers `p,q`, the matrix
    `[[qx,pT-qx^2],[q,-qx]]` preserves that same span, including
    `p<q`. Its two interior factors are `F_1=qB_0+8pa` and
    `F_2=2qB_0+3pb`. Since `B_0|F_1 F_2`, their conjugate product
    clears all four phases and gives image width below
    `16 max(p,q)`, uniformly in the Pell index. The map is
    nonconformal when `p!=q`. The failing parameter corresponds to
    a rational alignment whose numerator and denominator grow.

    This preserves exponent one half on the stated family; neither
    `N'<=N` nor an image constant at most two is required by items
    300--302. It supplies no general map-existence theorem or
    unconditional growth improvement. Root derived the formulas;
    Astra independently reconstructed the bad primitive targets,
    Sol audited both parameters, and Luna independently proved and
    checked the rational extension. The checker compares exact
    full-tuple Gaussian normalization with ordinary all-edge lcms
    at four Pell indices and tests thirty-two rational alignments.
    See the [endpoint-swap proof](endpoint_swap_arithmetic_sensitivity.md).

424. **The general endpoint swap has exact contents and a compulsory overlap cost.**
    For primitive positive endpoint `(x,y)`, write
    `M_D=[[xy,D-x^2],[y^2,-xy]]`, `D>0`. It exchanges the endpoints
    and preserves the half-angle interval, even with a negative
    upper-right entry. For primitive `(u,v)`, put `d=yu-xv`,
    `c=gcd(d,v)=gcd(y,v)`, `d'=d/c`, `v'=v/c`, and `h=gcd(d',D)`.
    The exact ordinary image content is
    `ch gcd(x(d'/h)+(D/h)v',y)`, including endpoint rows, signs
    and primes shared with `y`.

    In integer cotangent coordinates with endpoint `A`, set
    `g=gcd(A,L)`, `g_i=gcd(X_i,L)`, `T=(A^2+L^2)/g^2`.
    Then `d_i'=(X_i-A)/gcd(g,g_i)`, and the exact additional
    clearing factor `E=lcm_i[d_i'/gcd(d_i',T)]` satisfies `E|g^2`.
    The least multiple of `T` clearing every transverse determinant
    is `TE`; this assertion concerns ordinary row content only.

    For `y=1`, even `x`, and `D=kT` with `gcd(k,T)=1`, write the
    `r` primitive interior rows as `H_i=d_i+v_i(x+i)` with positive
    coprime `d_i,v_i`. Let `Q_i,Q_i'` be the reduced Gaussian source
    and target denominators after removing their gcds with `x+i`.
    Those gcds have the same exact norms `gcd(d_i,T)`, with no
    assumption `d_i|T`. The complete radii satisfy
    `N=T Norm(lcm_G Q_i)` and `N'=T Norm(lcm_G Q_i')`.
    If `Omega=product Norm(Q_i)/Norm(lcm_G Q_i)`, then
    `N'<=(2k^2)^r Omega N`, improved to `k^(2r) Omega N` for odd `k`.

    The product step is insufficient from five points onward:
    `Norm(Q_i)>=(x+sqrt(T))v_i` implies
    `Delta^4 Omega N>=2^r x^(r-2)` for `Delta=2 arctan(1/x)`.
    For `r>=3` this upper-bound certificate diverges regardless
    of the source's small normalized width. The actual target can
    still benefit from sharing. More precisely, putting
    `w_i=(k/gcd(d_i,k))v_i`, its exact overlap `Omega'_k` must obey
    `Omega'_k(C'_k)^4>=2^r x^(r-2)product_i w_i`.
    These formulas retain all powers, opposite Gaussian orientations,
    ordinary contents and the ramified prime. They identify a necessary
    target cancellation; they do not prove its existence or impossibility.

    Astra derived the content and overlap formulas, root removed an
    unnecessary divisibility hypothesis, and Sol audited the complete
    radius identities. Another Astra instance and root independently
    derived the product limitation and necessary target bound. The
    permanent checker passes 668,160 signed contents, 2,182 cotangent
    cliques and 199 full source/target configurations, including powers
    above the anchor exponent. See the
    [content and overlap proof](endpoint_swap_content_and_overlap.md).

425. **At most twelve fixed integer alignments can all preserve endpoint scale.**
    Continue the even-`x`, `y=1` setup of item 424 with distinct
    interior rows `H_i=d_i+v_i B`, `B=x+i`, `T=x^2+1`. Put
    `F_i=gcd_G(B,d_i)` and
    `L_i(X)=(d_i+X v_i B)/F_i`. These Gaussian linear polynomials
    have coprime coefficients, and their nonzero pair resultants are
    `R_ij=B(d_i v_j-d_j v_i)/(F_i F_j)`.

    For a fixed finite parameter set `S`, with every `k` coprime to
    `T` and `K=max S`, a primewise interpolation argument gives
    `product_(k in S) gcd_G(L_i(k),L_j(k)) | R_ij (K-1)!`.
    Choose a parameter of maximal gcd valuation: the remaining
    valuations are charged to the integer parameter differences.
    This retains arbitrary prime powers and the ramified prime.
    Target excess denominators divide these polynomial values, so
    their exact overlaps satisfy the ordinary integer divisibility
    `product_(k in S) Omega_k | [(K-1)!]^(r(r-1)) product Norm(R_ij)`.

    The common half-angle interval gives
    `Norm(R_ij)<=4 Norm(Q_i)Norm(Q_j)` and hence
    `product Omega_k <= [2(K-1)!]^(r(r-1)) (N/T)^(r(r-1))`.
    Bounded source width makes `N/T=O(x^2)`. Bounded image width
    at each fixed parameter, by item 424, forces
    `Omega_k>=c_k x^(r-2)`. Thus for fixed `r>=3` and `x` tending
    to infinity, simultaneous boundedness requires
    `|S|(r-2)<=2r(r-1)`.

    Root strengthened this to the absolute bound twelve by retaining
    the two endpoints and any three interior points in each source.
    Their Gaussian denominator lcms divide those of the full source
    and each full target. Their exact spans remain unchanged, so
    the five-point case applies with uniform constants even when
    the selected labels and total source cardinality vary. The
    bound includes the conformal parameter one. Powers of two give
    parameter sets automatically coprime to the odd number `T`.

    This controls simultaneous boundedness along a family; it is not
    a bound on successful parameters at one isolated finite source.
    It excludes the Pell family's all-parameter property from the
    five-point setting, without excluding one fixed nonconformal
    map or an adaptive parameter. Astra supplied the resultant
    proof and checker; root and Sol independently audited it and
    the subset strengthening. The permanent checker passes 804
    configurations with shared prime powers and nonconsecutive
    parameter sets. See the
    [simultaneous alignment theorem](endpoint_swap_simultaneous_alignment_capacity.md).

426. **Triangle contents determine the intrinsic cotangent denominators exactly.**
    For a primitive equal-norm tuple, write `s_ij` for the positive
    reduced denominator of its rational half-angle cotangent, with
    denominator one at an antipodal edge. Its minimal clearing
    scale is `L_0=lcm s_ij`, independently of the presentation or
    actual anchor. If `a_T=|D_ijk|/2` and
    `A_T=Norm(gcd_G(z_i,z_j,z_k))`, then
    `a_T=eta_T A_T s_ij s_ik s_jk` exactly, where `eta_T=2` when
    the three points have the same coordinate-parity class and is
    one otherwise. The proof uses the actual pair least norms,
    whose triple product is `(N/A_T)^2`, and the chord-product
    identity, retaining the ramified correction.

    Put `S=product_(i<j) s_ij` and
    `b_m=binom(floor(m/2),3)+binom(ceil(m/2),3)`. Then
    `product_T a_T=(product_T eta_T A_T) S^(m-2)` and
    `(2N)^b_m S^(m-2) | product_T a_T`. Source threshold cuts
    supply the `N` factor; the two actual parity classes supply
    the factor of two. This charges shared conductor and residue
    primes simultaneously. It also implies the weaker intrinsic
    chain `L_0^(m-2) | product_T lcm(s_ij,s_ik,s_jk) | product_T a_T`.

    The exponent `m-2` in the latter chain is primewise sharp on
    actual primitive circles: at any inert prime `p>m`, phases
    with half-angle rows `(H,t)` for `t=0,p^h,1,...,m-2` and
    `p` not dividing `H` give denominator valuation `h` on exactly
    one edge. Exactly its `m-2` incident triangles have valuation
    `h`. These fixtures can have small angular width but have no
    asserted bounded endpoint constant.

    On a target arc, the triangle bound gives
    `S<=2^(-b_m/(m-2))(C^3/16)^(m(m-1)/6)N^(floor(m/2)/4)`.
    The exact edge-cofactor dictionary
    `|(z_i-z_j)/gcd_G(z_i,z_j)|^2=4s_ij^2/epsilon_ij`
    identifies this with existing collective residue accounting,
    rather than an additional saving. It does not prove the
    exponent-four cotangent height target or improve the general
    bound. Astra supplied the initial intrinsic divisibility;
    root derived the exact triangle identity and sharpness family;
    Luna independently audited the contents, parity and constants.
    The permanent checker passes 31 actual-circle fixtures and
    84 fully normalized sharpness fixtures, including antipodes.
    Root also verified the exact formula on 6,064 literal triples.
    See the [intrinsic-scale proof](intrinsic_cotangent_scale_triangle_divisibility.md).

427. **Fixed linear triangle sums cannot improve cubic order universally.**
    Every fixed real linear combination of the determinants `D_ijk`
    reduces by affine area identities to `sum mu_ij D_0ij`. On
    an open ordered angular shape simplex, its cubic leading term
    is proportional to `sum mu_ij a_i a_j(a_j-a_i)`. The monomial
    `a_i a_j^2` occurs in exactly one summand, so universal cubic
    cancellation forces all `mu_ij=0`. The original expression is
    then identically zero on every planar configuration. This rules
    out a nonzero fixed linear certificate gaining two angular
    powers solely from the circle order.

    The quantifier over all shapes is essential. On rational
    half-angle rows `(0,e,2e,3e)`, the nonzero fixed combination
    `D_012-D_123` equals
    `72N e^5/[(1+e^2)(1+4e^2)(1+9e^2)]`. Thus cancellation on a
    special shape locus remains possible, even with bounded integer
    coefficients. Primitive rational-circle realizations validate
    both statements at small angular widths; no bounded endpoint
    constant is asserted for those families.

    The same audit identifies an anchored triangle Pluecker triple
    with its chord Ptolemy triple after full primitive normalization.
    Their three terms have one common positive real factor, and
    the unique proportional coprime integer triples coincide.
    This supplies no extra conductor beyond the existing positive
    pentagon calculation. Astra proved the restricted statement;
    root audited its scope and exact exceptional-shape formula.
    The checker passes 1,722 symbolic checks and 15 actual-circle
    fixtures. See the [linear triangle audit](fixed_triangle_linear_cancellation_audit.md).

428. **The rational endpoint pencil has an exact relative-parameter height bound.**
    With endpoint half-angle rows `1,x+i`, integer `x>0`, the fixing
    matrices `G_(p/q)=[[q,x(p-q)],[0,p]]` form the positive rational
    multiplicative group projectively. Composition with the conformal
    endpoint reflection turns the existing swap pencil into this
    fixing pencil. For two parameters with reduced relative ratio
    `mu/lambda=P/Q`, their full primitive squared radii satisfy
    `x(P+Q)<=2sqrt(N_lambda N_mu)`. One anchor-to-interior edge
    divides each full all-edge lcm. Its exact ordinary target content
    is `gcd(P,d)gcd(Q,v)`, and the possible ramified factor is at
    most two; these facts give the bound without a product estimate.

    For a coprime rational endpoint `x=a/b`, retaining the possible
    coordinate content at primes dividing `b` gives
    `a(P+Q)<=2b^2 sqrt(N_lambda N_mu)`. Thus bounded squared radius
    gives a finite parameter search, but at endpoint scale the
    integer-endpoint bound still permits parameter height of order
    `x^3`. It neither bounds the full orbit uniformly nor proves
    that a nonconformal admissible image exists.

    A finite exact example also prevents an automatic descent claim.
    The five half-angle rows `1,1+i,2+i,3+i,7+i` have full primitive
    squared radius `125`. Any pencil image with squared radius at
    most `125` has `p+q<=15`; all 71 coprime positive choices show
    identity is the only such parameter. Parameter three instead
    has squared radius `425`, so a larger fixed image constant is
    not excluded. Pair-selected four-row reciprocity is recorded as
    the known secant-symmetry dictionary, with no extension to the
    other rows. Sol supplied the proof and checker; root and Luna
    audited the contents, and root independently checked 63 further
    radius cases.
    The permanent checker passes 60 relative-height comparisons,
    12 subset equalities, exact matrix products and the 71-candidate
    example. See the [composition and height note](endpoint_swap_composition_orbit_height.md).

429. **Fixed alignments and all pair-selected choices can fail on an endpoint family.**
    Fix the extreme endpoints of the primitive five-point cubic
    family, whose normalized source width tends to `2sqrt(5)` and
    is below five. Write the endpoint half-angle row as `B=P+iQ`
    and interior rows as `H_h=u_h+i v_h`, with
    `d_h=Q u_h-P v_h>0`. The map selected by interior pair `i,j`,
    after conformal adjustment, has all-row representatives
    `F_h=d_i d_j v_h+v_i v_j d_h B`. It swaps the two selected
    interior rows and the endpoints, but retains every unselected
    row in its full denominator lcm.

    On the actual family with parameter `t` a positive multiple
    of `600`, the source Gaussian polynomial denominator lcm has
    degree six. Each selected four-row subset already has this
    polynomial lcm. The fifth-row residual factors have degrees
    four, three and three for the three possible pairs; the full
    target lcms therefore have degrees ten, nine and nine.
    Explicit polynomial gcds certify every cancellation. The
    complete equal-norm polynomial tuples have Gaussian gcd one,
    so a cleared Bezout identity bounds all specialization content
    by a fixed integer. These are consequently the degrees of the
    true primitive radii, not just unreduced representatives.

    Thus `N'_12=Theta(t^20)` and
    `N'_13,N'_23=Theta(t^18)`, while the preserved endpoint span
    is asymptotic to `120/t^3`. The three normalized image widths
    grow as `Theta(t^2),Theta(t^(3/2)),Theta(t^(3/2))`.
    Even adaptive choice among these three pairs cannot keep a
    bounded target constant. This does not exclude other parameters,
    other endpoint choices, larger source cardinalities or a
    theorem restricted to sufficiently small source constants.
    Astra supplied the explicit calculation, proof and checker;
    root and Luna independently audited the full-lcm and Bezout
    arguments. The exact polynomial checks and twelve specialized
    target comparisons pass. See the
    [actual pair-selection obstruction](endpoint_pair_selected_five_point_obstruction.md).

    There is also a complete fixed-parameter obstruction on this
    same source family. For every fixed positive rational alignment
    `lambda!=1`, retain only endpoint row `B` and interior row three.
    Its raw fixing image is `C_3=d_3+lambda v_3 B`, where
    `d_3=20(t^2+4)(t^2+9)(t^2+36)` and
    `v_3=40(t^2+18)`. The difference from its conjugate is
    `120i lambda t v_3`. At `t=0`, the real value is
    `25920(1-lambda)`, and at `t^2=-18` it is `45360`.
    Thus `C_3` is conjugate-coprime. Its gcd with
    `B=(t+i)(t+2i)(t+3i)(t-6i)` has degree three, so the
    three-row denominator lcm has degree seven. Its true primitive
    squared radius is `Theta_lambda(t^14)`, forcing the full image
    width to be at least `c_lambda sqrt(t)`. The constants depend
    on the fixed alignment, so this does not control an arbitrary
    source-dependent parameter. The separate three-pair argument
    covers exactly those three moving parameter choices.

430. **Adaptive endpoint alignments have a necessary polynomial height cost.**
    On the cubic five-point family from item 429, let `t` be a positive
    multiple of `600`, `B=P+iQ`, `P=t^4+25t^2-36`, and `Q=60t`.
    For coprime positive `p,q` with `p!=q`, write `H=p+q` and retain
    the entire image under endpoint-fixing alignment `p/q`. Its third
    interior row is `C=qd+pvB`, where
    `d=20(t^2+4)(t^2+9)(t^2+36)` and `v=40(t^2+18)`.
    With `K0=2821754880000`, the true full primitive squared radius
    obeys, uniformly over all these varying parameters,
    `N'>=t^14 H^2/[62208 K0^2 p^2 q^3(p-q)^2]`
    and consequently `N'>=t^14/[62208 K0^2 H^3(p-q)^2]`.

    Factor `B=US`, with `U=(t+2i)(t+3i)(t-6i)` and `S=t+i`.
    The actual target factors as `C=U(20q bar(U)+pvS)`.
    Its ordinary coordinate content is at most
    `K0 p q |p-q|`. The raw Gaussian overlap has norm at most
    `9600q t^6`: the remaining gcd divides `1200q`, and the
    primitive Gaussian integer `S` uses just one orientation over
    each split prime. The exact reduced Gaussian denominator lcm
    of the subset `1,B,C` then gives the stated lower bound. Every
    subset radius divides the full target radius; no product of
    unreduced row norms substitutes for the lcm.

    Since the preserved endpoint angle is at least `30/t^3`, any
    fixed bound `C'` on the normalized target width forces
    `H^3(p-q)^2>=c_(C') t^2`, hence `H>=c_(C') t^(2/5)`.
    If `|p-q|` remains bounded, this strengthens to
    `H>=c_(C',|p-q|) t^(2/3)`. In terms of the source squared
    radius `N~t^12/720^2`, these are powers `N^(1/30)` and
    `N^(1/18)`. The identity parameter is excluded, as required
    by its growing ordinary content. These are necessary costs
    on one family, not a general point-count improvement or a
    proof that all adaptive choices fail. Root and Sol derived
    the bounds; Luna independently audited the contents, dyadic
    factor and Gaussian orientation estimate. The checker passes
    21 five-row cases with fixed and varying parameters, comparing
    independent Gaussian-lcm and all-edge primitive radii. See the
    [adaptive alignment height proof](endpoint_adaptive_alignment_height_floor.md).
    A further all-row audit retains exact ordinary parameter contents
    and proves `gcd_G(C_i,C_j)|W_ij gcd_G(B,q)`. The endpoint does
    not automatically recover the latter overlap in the full lcm:
    at `t=600,p/q=170/169`, the same orientation above `13` occurs
    with exponent one in the endpoint and both normalized first
    interior rows. Their lcm still has exponent one. The checker
    includes this exact prime-power fixture. No stronger all-row
    bound was accepted from the proposed overlap gain.

431. **The full invariant restriction image has an exact cyclic index.**
    For `m=2q` and every active depth `1<=k<=floor(m/6)` in the
    all-cut hierarchy, fix a cut with `q-k` inside rows. The
    restriction of the integral lattice `V_Z` in `K_k` is onto
    the full integral squarefree translation-invariant matching
    lattice `W_Z` of degree `2k` in `q+k` variables. Each matching
    basis vector lifts to `2k` disjoint triangle bracket products
    and `q-3k` doubled crossing brackets. Having exactly `q-k`
    connected components ensures all larger collapse restrictions
    vanish, while the chosen restriction is the specified basis
    vector with integral coefficient one.

    Exchanging an inside vertex of one triangle with an outside
    vertex of another gives a monomial `Z` in the chosen restriction
    kernel. At any actual configuration of distinct rational
    directions, all its brackets are nonzero, so numerical
    evaluation satisfies `f(Z)!=0`. Thus the full numerical-zero
    lattice `Lambda=ker f` has full rational restriction image:
    a basis lift `Q` is corrected by `f(Z)Q-f(Q)Z`. This is an
    individual-cut statement, not independent simultaneous control
    of every cut.

    More generally, for any integral surjection `T:V_Z->I` and
    evaluation nonzero on `ker T`, define
    `f(V_Z)=b Z` and `f(ker T)=a Z`, with positive `b|a`.
    Evaluation modulo `a` induces the exact cyclic quotient
    `I/T(ker f) ~= Z/(a/b)Z`. In the hierarchy `I=W_Z`.
    The gcd of all maximal restriction minors is therefore exactly
    `a/b`, and the Smith invariant factors are `1,...,1,a/b`.
    All gcds range over the full indicated integral lattices.
    This identifies the full-lattice content; it does not bound
    the coefficient heights required to obtain full restriction
    rank. Stronger collective or covolume arguments remain open.
    Astra supplied the proof and checker; root and Luna independently
    audited the integral lifts and exact sequence. The checker passes
    44 matching lifts and nonvanishing kernel witnesses, plus 336
    primitive and nonprimitive evaluation-image index cases.

    Cyclicity alone also fails to supply a root-of-index bound on
    spanning coefficient height in an actual invariant system.
    Take six binary directions `(s,1),(0,1),(1,1),(2,1),(3,1),(4,1)`,
    with `s>=5` and `s=5 mod 6`, and the cut on the first two rows.
    In an explicit integral basis of `K_1` the restriction is
    `[I_2 0]`, its full numerical-zero image is
    `{(x,y):x+4y=0 mod s}`, and its cyclic index is `s`.
    Any two independent image vectors include one of sup norm at
    least `s/5`, whereas explicit zero relations span the image
    with coefficient sup norm at most `7s`. The full relation
    lattice covolume has order `s^2`. The checker derives the
    saturated basis by unimodular operations, verifies the exact
    polynomial evaluations, and checks twenty specializations.
    These are actual circle directions but their angular span
    stays positive; this is not a bounded-endpoint family or an
    obstruction to a collective argument using other cuts. See the
    [full restriction image and index theorem](full_invariant_restriction_image_and_index.md).

432. **The whole distance matrix has an exact primitive Smith form.**
    For any `m>=3` distinct integer points on a circle of squared
    radius `N`, put `E_ij=|z_i-z_j|^2/2`, let `d` be the gcd of
    its off-diagonal entries, and let `g` be the gcd of all signed
    triangle determinants. The three nonzero Smith factors are
    exactly `d,d,N g^2/d^2`. Every two-minor is divisible by `d^2`
    and the principal two-minors are `-E_ij^2`, so their gcd is
    precisely `d^2`. The factorization
    `E=Y diag(N,-1,-1) Y^t`, where `Y_i=(1,x_i,y_i)`, makes
    every three-minor equal to `N D_I D_J`; their gcd is `N g^2`.
    These statements retain all evaluated content, row units,
    common Gaussian factors and prime-power exponents.

    If the complete tuple is Gaussian-primitive, then `gcd(d,N)=1`:
    an extreme-allocation pair at each conductor prime has its
    half-squared distance a unit there. Hence `d^3|g^2`.
    More precisely `d=kappa h^2`, where `kappa=1` if both
    coordinate-parity types occur and `kappa=2` if all points
    have the same type. At odd primes outside `N`, conjugation
    and the equal-norm equation make every distance valuation
    even. Opposite parity types give an odd half-squared distance;
    within one type its two-adic valuation is odd. All triangle
    determinants are even, so `g=2 kappa h^3 a` with integer
    `a>=1`. Therefore the primitive distance matrix `E/d` has
    nonzero Smith factors `1,1,(4/kappa)N a^2`.

    In the common-unit model, `h` is exactly the gcd of the
    primitive chord residues, and the triangle formula is
    `|D_ijk|=4 Norm(gcd_G(z_i,z_j,z_k)) t_ij t_ik t_jk`.
    The endpoint assumption gives only
    `h^3 a<=C^3 N^(1/4)/(16 kappa)`, the existing triangle
    exponent. The complete Smith form consequently identifies
    the conductor and evaluated triangle content but supplies no
    new estimate for singleton and pair source contents `A,F`.
    Root and Astra derived the matrix and parity identities;
    Sol independently audited both. See the
    [primitive distance Smith theorem](primitive_distance_smith_form.md).

433. **Eight-row relation cofactors satisfy a nonlinear congruence.**
    At a three-inside, five-outside cut, the integral matching basis
    `A,B,C,D,E` of `W_(5,2)` satisfies
    `Phi=BCE-AD(A+B+C+D+E)=0`. Let `R` be the four-by-five restriction
    matrix of four numerical-zero relations, and let `c` be its raw
    signed maximal-minor vector. For the actual matching evaluation
    vector `v`, write `G_v=gcd_G(v)` and suppose the exact conductor
    congruence is `H | kappa Rv`. Then
    `H/gcd_G(H,kappa G_v) | Phi(c)`. Normalize `v` first and use the
    cofactor-adjugate identities at a unit coordinate at each prime.
    This proof retains every prime power without assuming rank modulo
    that prime or inverting a cofactor.

    Since `H` is conjugate-primitive, its remaining norm divides the
    ordinary integer `Phi(c)`. Complement reflection gives a second
    coprime divisor of the same integer. Their product has logarithm
    at least `2(1-eta)w-272 sigma-4 log T`. If the four row coefficient
    sums are at most `L`, Hadamard gives `|Phi(c)|<=6L^12`. Consequently
    `12 log L+log 6<2(1-eta)w-272 sigma-4 log T` forces `Phi(c)=0`.
    When `R` has rational rank four, its kernel is therefore a rational
    point on the Segre cubic. Lower rank makes the cofactor statement
    vacuous; singular or boundary points are allowed.

    Removing the cofactor content `q=gcd(c)` costs the factor
    `gcd(M,q^3)` from a norm modulus `M`. The exact fixture
    `R=5[I_4 | (1,2,3,4)^t]`, `v=(1,1,3,1,3)`, `H=2+i` has
    `q=5^4` but primitive-cofactor cubic value `42`, so that content
    cannot be silently discarded. The checker verifies the universal
    cubic, integral basis, 76 modular fixtures with nonzero cubic
    values, and this content-loss example. Astra derived the result;
    root independently audited the proof and height losses. The
    existence of four relations at this height and a contradiction
    from compatibility across cuts remain unproved. See the
    [Segre cofactor congruence](eight_row_segre_cofactor_congruence.md).

434. **A Chow form forces common basepoints for the supplied short relations.**
    For `m=2q>=8`, let `n=q+1`, `t=n(n-3)/2`. The matching quadrics
    define a birational map from the blowup of `P^(n-2)` at its `n`
    frame points to an integral image `X_n subset P^(t-1)`, of degree
    `delta=2^(n-2)-n`. The unequal-pair matching criterion identifies
    the basepoints; their linear terms show that one blowup resolves
    them. Ratios of matching coordinates recover the generic labelled
    configuration up to translation and scale. These facts give the
    stated degree from `(2H-sum E_i)^(n-2)`.

    The Chow form has degree `delta` in each of its `n-1` hyperplane
    rows. Fixed integral incidence identities, localized at each
    matching coordinate, imply that the normalized conductor modulus
    divides a fixed integer times every Chow value of actual numerical
    relations. Gaussian coordinate gcd normalization permits a unit
    coordinate at each prime power; the fixed integer absorbs all
    chart denominators. Complement reflection supplies a coprime
    second divisor of the same ordinary integer. Its product has
    logarithm at least `2(1-eta)w-2m(2m+1)sigma-4log T`.

    If relations of coefficient height at most `exp(h)` have no
    common point on `X_n` at a cut, at most `t` of them span the image.
    Integer combinations with coefficients in `{0,...,delta}` give
    `n-1` rows with nonzero Chow value. Its logarithmic height is at
    most `delta(n-1)h+O_m(1)`. Therefore
    `delta(n-1)h+2m(2m+1)sigma+4log T+O_m(1)<2(1-eta)w`
    forces a common point at every first-smaller cut.

    This criterion applies to relations actually supplied by the
    existing successive-minima estimate. With invariant dimension `r`,
    primitive evaluation exponent `A_m`, and `L=floor((r-1)/2)`, one
    obtains `L` independent relations with coefficient exponent at most
    `A_m/(r-L)+o(1)`. At the fixed value `m=400`, exact arithmetic proves
    `40 delta(n-1) A_m<r-L`. The balanced threshold places them in
    `K_1`, and the full-profile errors `eta=o(1)`, `sigma,log T=o(w)`
    make the Chow criterion applicable. These common points can lie
    on the boundary or exceptional images, or arise from identically
    zero restrictions. No membership in `K_2` follows.

    Sol supplied the complete proof and finite checker; root and
    Astra independently checked the matching geometry and root audited
    the incidence, content and height arguments. The checker verifies
    small matching spaces, complete finite-field base loci, coordinate
    recovery examples and the exact `m=400` integer inequality. It does
    not compute the general Chow form or its incidence certificate.
    See the [Chow basepoint criterion](first_smaller_cut_chow_basepoint.md).

435. **Compatible boundary points occur in a large actual relation space.**
    Fix any distinct rational directions, even `m>=16`, and a quartet
    `A`. There is a nonzero integer numerical-zero quartet polynomial
    `Q_A`, for example the difference of two squared matchings weighted
    by their actual squared values. Set
    `U=(Lambda intersect K_2(m))+Q_A K_1(A^c)`. It consists of actual
    numerical zeros in `K_1`. Its dimension is at least
    `r-s-binom(m,m/2-1)t-1`, greater than `r/2` at `m=24,30,400`.
    Its polynomial gcd is one: the deeper numerical kernel contains
    products of numerical zeros on two disjoint quartets with the
    corresponding complementary `K_2` spaces, whose graph gcds are one.

    At a first-smaller cut only two-inside, two-outside quartet splits
    can have nonzero image. That image is exactly a scalar multiple of
    `W_(n-2,2)` on the outside complement variables. Collapsing all those
    variables while leaving the two quartet variables nonzero supplies
    a common boundary point `p_ij`. No point from distinct outside
    directions annihilates a nonzero image. All chosen points are
    simultaneous limits of the single global degeneration
    `z_i=a_i` on `A`, `z_j=t b_j` on its complement as `t->0`.
    Thus actual numerical vanishing, large dimension, polynomial gcd
    one and this form of cross-cut compatibility do not force an
    interior point. No coefficient-height bound for this space is
    asserted, and it need not be the entire short relation space.

    Astra proved the construction; Sol and root independently audited
    it. The checker passes all 11440 cuts at sixteen rows, 432 nonzero
    sample restrictions, all three projective limit orders, an exact
    image-rank check and graph gcd certificates. Item 436 supplies
    the additional arithmetic height information for its nonzero
    extension.

    There is also a separate coherent interior-point existence model
    at `m=10`, where `K_2=0`. Fix any actual rational directions `P`
    and any globally distinct rational configuration `b`. Requiring
    every first-smaller restriction to vanish at the outside image of
    `b` imposes at most 210 scalar equations on `K_1`, of dimension
    477. Adding numerical vanishing at `P` leaves a space of dimension
    at least 266 with these coherent interior common points. Each
    fixed quartet space `E_A` of item 436 has dimension only ten.
    Thus this space is not contained in any one `E_A` or their finite
    union. This is a linear dimension existence theorem, without an
    explicit short basis or a full-profile height assertion. It shows
    that even removing boundary points cannot replace the missing
    quantitative arithmetic reduction. See the
    [coherent boundary and interior models](coherent_boundary_basepoints_of_numeric_relations.md).

436. **Quartet-supported boundary extensions admit an integral height descent.**
    Fix even `m>=10`, a quartet `A`, and its complement `B`. Let
    `Lambda_A` contain all rational quartet numerical zeros, and put
    `E_A=K_2(m)+span_Q(Lambda_A K_1(B))`. Any integer `W in E_A`
    outside `K_2(m)` obeys
    `log C_W>=2^(m-3)(1-eta)w-4 sum_(i in A)log|K_i|`, hence at least
    `2^(m-3)(1-eta)w-16 sigma`. This allows arbitrary cancellation
    between product summands and the full deeper kernel.

    The balanced evaluation map on quartet invariants has determinant
    one in the integral basis `X^2,XZ,Z^2`, where
    `X=Delta_12 Delta_34`, `Z=Delta_14 Delta_23`. Fixing a complement
    inside set and one outside monomial, and varying the three quartet
    pair splits, extracts an integral triple from the coefficients of
    `W`. It lies in the rational balanced image of `Lambda_A`, so the
    unimodular inverse reconstructs an integer quartet numerical zero.
    Some such triple is nonzero if `W` is outside `K_2`, and each entry
    is bounded by `C_W`.

    Aggregate all `2^(m-4)` Gaussian blocks with a fixed intersection
    pair in `A`. The exact balanced scalar congruence holds for their
    product before correction losses are charged. The complementary
    pair has the same scalar and a coprime norm modulus. Their product
    gives the displayed exponent, losing only the four quartet
    corrections once each. No basis-height estimate for the original
    product decomposition is used.

    Root proved this descent; Sol and Astra independently audited it.
    The checker verifies every first-smaller cut at `m=10,12`, mixed
    products of two independent quartet numerical zeros, a numerical
    deeper-kernel term, and separate Gaussian prime-power aggregation
    fixtures with shared correction primes. Thus the extension in
    item 435 cannot supply a nonzero restriction at the short height
    of item 434. Arbitrary short relations need not lie in any one
    `E_A`, and the theorem does not apply automatically to sums over
    all quartets. Short vectors inside `K_2` remain uncontrolled.
    See the [quartet coefficient-height descent](quartet_boundary_height_descent.md).

437. **Every active cut kernel has an exact evaluation-content exponent.**
    For `m=2q`, `0<=k<=floor(m/6)`, and a cut of size `s`, put
    `g_k(s)=max(0,2s-m,k+s-q)`. Every monomial of an invariant in
    `K_k` has at least that total first-coordinate degree inside
    the cut. The torus gives total first-coordinate degree `m`.
    Vanishing whenever any `q-k+1` first coordinates are zero forces
    each surviving monomial's support to meet every such subset.
    Its inside support has size at least `s-q+k`; total degree also
    gives the bound `2s-m`. Distinct surviving monomials cannot
    cancel after that coordinate specialization.

    In the primitive central system, the shear `(X,Y)->(X+iY,Y)`
    preserves invariant values. The monomial order therefore gives
    the exact divisor `D_k=product_S n_S^g_k(|S|)` of every integer
    value on `K_k`. A graph consisting of `2k` disjoint triangles
    and doubled pairs on the remaining vertices lies in `K_k` and,
    after relabelling, attains `g_k(s)` for every cut size. At `k=0`
    use only doubled pairs. Their edge multiplicities are at most
    two. If `G_k` is the full evaluation gcd and
    `B=product_(i<j)b_ij` the residual bracket product, primewise
    comparison gives `D_k | G_k | D_k B^2`.

    The primitive evaluation height and numerical-zero lattice
    covolume on `K_k` consequently have logarithm `A_k w+o(w)` in
    the fixed full-profile limit, where
    `A_k=A_0-sum_s binom(m,s)max(0,k-|s-q|)` and
    `A_0=m2^(m-2)-q binom(m,q)`. Fixed-profile error terms are retained
    in the note. This proves a height formula for the restricted
    evaluation functional, not membership of short relations in
    deeper kernels. Root supplied the coefficient-support proof;
    Luna independently audited it, proved the graph attainment
    formula, and wrote the exact checker. Astra independently audited
    the gcd and height arguments. Tests include exhaustive small
    monomial supports, graph cut minima through forty rows, binomial
    identities and two actual equal-norm local prime fixtures. See the
    [higher-kernel evaluation heights](higher_kernel_evaluation_heights.md).

438. **The kernel hierarchy has an exact Specht filtration.**
    For `m=2q`, the degree-two-each invariant space is the
    multiplicity-free sum of permutation modules
    `Specht(2a,2b,2c)`, where `a>=b>=c>=0` and `a+b+c=q`.
    The precise kernel is
    `K_k=direct_sum_(a>=b>=c>=k) Specht(2a,2b,2c)`.
    The ambient decomposition is the classical spin-one `SO_3`
    description; the new filtration assertion follows from its
    exact maximum number of collapsed null rows.

    For the first three Gram principal minors, a highest-weight
    polynomial is `Delta_1^(a-b)Delta_2^(b-c)Delta_3^c`.
    Shifting each vector by `t_i u` for one isotropic vector `u`
    gives respective highest total parameter degrees `1,2,2`,
    with nonzero leading terms. The product therefore has degree
    `a+b=q-c`. All `GL_m` mixes preserve this upper bound.
    Complete polarization, realized as a multilinear weight
    projection after an invertible mix of disjoint clone groups,
    preserves a nonzero top coefficient. It yields a constituent
    vector nonzero with exactly `q-c` collapsed rows. The remaining
    rows can be taken on the null cone because it spans the
    three-dimensional spin-one space and the polynomial is
    multilinear in those slots. More collapsed rows always give
    zero. Multiplicity one then identifies each kernel exactly.

    The hook formula determines `r_k=dim K_k` and the exact layer
    `D_k=r_k-r_(k+1)` by summing the constituents with `c=k`.
    Together with item 437, successive minima guarantee an outside
    relation at coefficient exponent at most `A_k/D_k` when the
    next kernel is nonzero. At the terminal layer the correct
    denominator is `r_k-1`, not `D_k=r_k`. This supplies no short
    quotient lift and does not upgrade the proper-image criteria.
    Root derived the Gram-minor argument; Sol and Astra independently
    audited its polarization and null-cone steps. The checker passes
    forty highest-weight examples and exact dimensions, heights and
    minima-index checks through twenty rows. See the
    [Specht filtration theorem](kernel_specht_filtration.md).

439. **Coherent cut evaluations satisfy joint differential identities.**
    For `m=2q`, depth `k`, `s=q-k` and `p=q-3k`, package the
    depth-`k` restrictions evaluated at one distinct configuration
    `b` as the squarefree polynomial
    `E_(Q,b)(x)=sum_(|S|=s) F_(S,Q)(b_outside) x_S`.
    Every `Q in K_k` satisfies
    `(a D_1+c D_b)^(p+1) E=0` for all scalars `a,c`, where
    `D_1=sum partial_i` and `D_b=sum b_i partial_i`.
    The top Gram determinant is unchanged by translating the
    parameter column along the first two spin-coordinate columns;
    the remaining leading factors have total degree `p`. This
    argument survives row mixing and multilinear projection.

    An explicit elementary-symmetric matrix gives the joint linear
    constraints and bounds the coherent evaluation rank by
    `binom(m,s)-binom(m,2k-1)`. At terminal depth `m=6k`,
    `E_(Q,b)(b^2)=Q(b)`: numerical evaluation at that same point
    is already a linear combination of the coherent cut evaluations.
    The all-depth probability identity
    `A_k/2^m=m/4-E max(k,|Bin(m,1/2)-m/2|)` proves
    `A_k>binom(m,s)` at every active depth. Consequently the
    aggregate minima count alone fits inside large actual numerical
    zero spaces with coherent interior points. This comparison
    does not give them short integral bases.

    At the terminal depth, factor each homogeneous restriction as
    `e_S=(product_outside P_j) r_S`. The quotient is an integral
    degree-one-each invariant on the outside rows. The resulting
    integer array obeys, for every `(2k-1)`-set `U`,
    `sum_(i outside U)(X_i,Y_i) r_(U+i)=0`.
    These are circuits of the half-angle numerators, whose norms
    vary, rather than circuits of the original equal-radius points.
    Their universal common divisor has the exact core order
    `max(0,|T minus U|-2k-1)` at block `T`, with extra universal
    content bounded by the pair-residue product. The note retains
    the corresponding primitive-height upper bound and distinguishes
    it from the height of a specific numerical zero. Root, Astra
    and Sol audited the identities; Luna independently checked
    the integral reconstruction and normalization. See the
    [coherent cut identities](coherent_cut_evaluation_differentials.md).

440. **Short restrictions cannot vanish accidentally at the actual configuration.**
    At any active depth, put `s=q-k` and fix a cut `S` of size `s`.
    Dividing its homogeneous restriction by the product of outside
    `P_j` leaves an integral multilinear polynomial
    `r_S=sum_(|J|=2k)c_J Y_J P_(outside minus J)` with coefficient
    sum at most `C_Q`. If its actual Gaussian value is zero,
    reduce modulo the product of all core blocks whose intersection
    with the outside labels is `J`. Exactly `2^s` blocks occur.
    Only the displayed monomial with index `J` survives; conjugate
    primitivity makes its inside `Y_j` factors units. Taking norms
    after cancelling the outside correction factors gives
    `log C_Q >= 2^s(1-eta)w-2 sum_outside log|K_j|`
    whenever the polynomial restriction is nonzero. When `m=6k`,
    the complementary coefficient equality doubles the
    leading term to `2^(s+1)(1-eta)w` with the same total correction
    loss.

    Thus, below these thresholds, vanishing of the actual coherent
    array puts `Q` in `K_(k+1)`; at terminal depth it forces `Q=0`.
    The statement permits arbitrary cancellations and does not
    assume a short graph decomposition. It excludes the coherent
    kernel at the actual configuration from the relevant short
    relations. The common-point argument still supplies an
    unspecified point, however, and does not identify it with the
    actual one or force the actual array to vanish. Root derived
    the all-depth extension; Astra and Sol independently audited
    the grouped conductors and the Gaussian-to-integer step. See
    [the actual-configuration height theorem](coherent_cut_evaluation_differentials.md)
    and its [arithmetic checker](check_actual_cut_nonvanishing.py).

441. **The six-row coherent kernel and selected-minor content are exact.**
    In the gradient basis `G=grad Phi` of `K_1(6)`, let `R` be
    the fifteen-row matrix of normalized coherent cut evaluations.
    With `M=(A,B,C,D,E)` the matching vector at the actual six
    directions, all fifteen polynomial identities `R M=0` hold.
    The four rows indexed by cuts `12,45,23,34` have signed
    cofactor vector `F M`, where
    `F=Delta_12 Delta_56 Delta_36 Delta_16 Delta_45`.
    All factors are nonzero on distinct directions. Thus `R` has
    rank four there, without a generic-position qualification, and
    its primitive integer kernel is generated by `M/gcd(M)`.

    Divide each of those four rows by its compulsory core content.
    The resulting five cofactors have common factor
    `q_tree=F gcd(M)/(D_12 D_45 D_23 D_34)`. Its compulsory
    part is the product of fourteen explicitly listed core norm
    blocks; the remaining factor divides the squared pair-residue
    product. Consequently the four normalized row heights give
    an exterior estimate `32w`, their selected cofactor content
    removes `14w`, and the primitive kernel height is exactly
    `18w+o(w)`. This remains above the exclusion threshold `8w`.
    Selected-row content is distinguished from the gcd of all
    maximal minors of the overdetermined matrix. The result
    sharpens this intermediate lattice calculation but does not
    improve the circle-point growth bound.

    Root identified the matching-vector kernel and the sparse
    four-row certificate. Astra verified the full symbolic matrix
    and every core order; Luna independently checked the integral
    basis, a polynomial one-parameter family and all its minors
    on eight distinct-row fixtures. See the
    [six-row kernel and content theorem](six_row_coherent_kernel_and_content.md)
    and the [independent matrix checker](check_terminal_six_cut_matrix.py).

442. **Localized six-row relations generate the generic twelve-row coherent kernel.**
    For each six-set `I`, the polar relation
    `Q_I=sum_j M_j(actual I) G_j(variable I)` has zero coherent
    array by item 441. Multiplying it by any of the five terminal
    gradient invariants on the complementary six-set gives an
    element of the coherent kernel in `K_2(12)`. The resulting
    4,620 generators span that kernel at the distinct rational
    configuration `b_i=i`, and on a nonempty Zariski-open set.

    Exact modular certificates at the same configuration give
    image rank 121 and generator rank 341, whose sum equals the
    known source dimension 462. These are characteristic-zero
    lower bounds; the symbolic inclusion of the generators in
    the kernel makes both bounds exact. A separate rank-462
    certificate verifies the source basis, and the joint lowering
    matrix has nullity 121 there. No constancy on all distinct
    configurations is inferred from these certificates.

    Varying one row gives a pencil `E_0+t E_1` whose stacked rank
    is exactly 176. The differential identities give its upper
    bound from the eleven-row joint-harmonic dimensions 55 and
    66; the modular certificate gives the matching lower bound.
    Thus the constant kernel has dimension 286. Local generators
    have degree at most one in the moving row, so 55 further
    linear vectors complete its field kernel. Their wedge with
    a constant basis has degree exactly 55 and no common
    polynomial factor: a vanishing specialization would produce
    another constant kernel vector, contradicting independence.
    This determines the generic kernel Pluecker degree in each
    row parameter. It does not bound its arithmetic coefficient
    height or the height of arbitrary sums of local generators.

    The same note distinguishes full-matrix and selected-row
    content at six rows. For each core cut a permuted four-row
    tree has a unit normalized maximal minor in the pure-core
    limit, so the gcd of all maximal minors has no compulsory
    factor from that core. This is compatible with item 441's
    fourteen-block content for one fixed tree. Root proposed
    the localized module and one-row pencil; Sol supplied the
    certificates and the elementary primitive-wedge proof.
    See the [generic coherent-kernel theorem](generic_terminal_coherent_syzygies.md).

443. **The full terminal coherent image and its rank are known at every distinct configuration.**
    Homogenizing a squarefree polynomial killed by `D_1,D_b`
    identifies it with one multigraded component of a Cox--Nagata
    invariant ring. The Castravet--Tevelev generator theorem, in
    the precise nonzero-Pluecker-coordinate form of Sturmfels--Xu
    Theorem 7.1, expresses that component by products of odd-set
    determinants on disjoint label blocks. This applies whenever
    the `b_i` are distinct; the generic Sagbi hypothesis is not
    substituted for the generator theorem's actual hypothesis.

    An explicit signed determinant identity replaces a block of
    size `2s+1` and a singleton by a triple and a block of size
    `2s-1`. Its only division is by a nonzero difference `b_j-b_a`.
    A Vandermonde coefficient calculation, or a divided-difference
    column operation, proves the identity for all sizes. At
    `m>=3d`, every oversized block has a singleton available, so
    iteration expresses the entire squarefree degree-`d` joint
    kernel as products of `d` disjoint triple circuits, with any
    remaining labels unused. At `m=6k,d=2k`, these are exactly
    coherent images of the terminal triangle invariants.

    Surjectivity at every distinct point also proves constant
    rank. The coherent matrix rank can only fall from its generic
    maximum, while the differential-kernel dimension can only
    rise from its generic minimum. Their equality everywhere
    forces both to be constant. A caterpillar Sagbi degeneration
    computes that dimension by words whose positions partition
    into odd alternating chains. Equivalently, the prefix walk
    stays between zero and `2k` and ends at `2k`. Reflection at
    the two boundaries yields the exact formula
    `rho_k=binom(6k,2k)-2binom(6k,2k-1)+binom(6k,2k-2)`.
    Thus the twelve-row kernel has dimension 341 at every
    distinct configuration, not only on the generic set of
    item 442. The latter's particular local generators still
    need a separate all-point spanning proof.

    Root identified the Cox--Nagata connection and supplied the
    rank-constancy and word-count arguments. Astra proved the
    determinant balancing identity and grading correspondence;
    Sol independently audited the identity and primary-source
    hypotheses; Luna independently audited rank constancy and
    the reflection count. The checker verifies coefficient
    identities, recursive balancing and the finite walk counts.
    Clearing the explicit difference denominators can have large
    arithmetic cost, so this geometric surjectivity does not
    supply a short integral inverse or a new growth bound. See
    [odd-block balancing and the full coherent image](coherent_nagata_balancing.md).

444. **The terminal kernel determinant line has an exact degree at every depth.**
    Put `d=2k`, `m=3d`, and let `h(n,e)` be the squarefree joint
    differential-kernel dimension. Moving one binary direction gives
    a matrix pencil. Odd-block balancing on the other `3d-1` labels
    supplies both `f` and `t f` for every degree-`d` joint invariant,
    proving stacked rank `rho+delta`, where
    `delta=h(3d-1,d)=binom(3d,d)(d-1)/(3(2d+1))`.
    The image determinant line has degree `beta=rho-delta`.
    Factoring every maximal minor into its primitive source and image
    exterior factors then forces source degree `delta`, with no
    remaining univariate polynomial scalar factor. This proves that
    the polynomial-kernel minimal indices are zero or one at every
    distinct fixed configuration. It does not identify the specialized
    integer gcd with a polynomial gcd.

    The global source-kernel Pluecker coordinates are simultaneous
    `SL_2` invariants of binary degree `delta` in each row. Their
    mandatory majority content gives logarithmic covolume at most
    `delta*A_0(6k)w/2+o(w)`. This bound misses the actual-cut exclusion
    threshold for every `k`; the twelve-row first-minimum exponent is
    `16860/31`, compared with the needed `32`. Root proposed retaining
    the image factor; Astra supplied the all-size pencil argument and
    height comparison, independently audited by Sol. See
    [the determinant-line degree and height theorem](terminal_kernel_determinant_line_height.md).

445. **Localized six-row relations span along an entire projective pencil.**
    For the twelve-row family `(t,1,...,11)`, the local relations whose
    six-set avoids the moving row have exact rank 286, equal to the
    constant polynomial kernel. The full local family has generic
    rank 341. A degree-one propagation lemma makes these 341
    directions independent at every finite parameter where the
    coherent rank is 121, and their leading coefficients handle
    infinity. Thus localized generation holds on this entire
    projective family outside the eleven collisions, over any
    characteristic-zero extension. The required constant-family rank
    is not proved for every fixed eleven-tuple. Sol supplied the
    lemma and exact modular certificate; root reran the checker.
    See [projective-pencil propagation](local_six_syzygy_pencil_propagation.md).

446. **Ordering, integer circuits and reconstruction do not imply positivity.**
    At ordered slopes `b_i=i` for six rows, the coherent polynomial
    `9 L_012 L_345-L_013 L_245` is nonzero with mixed signs, is killed
    by both lowering operators, and evaluates to zero at `x_i=b_i^2`.
    It comes from the actual terminal invariant
    `9 T_012 T_345-T_013 T_245`. Rows `(N,i)` preserve this zero while
    making the slopes arbitrarily clustered. Their half-angle norms
    vary, and equal-radius normalization does not preserve the same
    integer circuit coefficients. This exact countermodel supplied
    by Luna lacks the extracted full core profile; it rules out the
    proposed sign-only shortcut, not the arithmetic short-height
    theorem. See [the ordered-circuit countermodel](terminal_ordered_circuit_sign_countermodel.md).

447. **The terminal coherent kernel is a critical-level conformal-block space.**
    For a multilinear ternary invariant `Q` on `m=3d` rows, the
    highest-root operator `D_z=sum_i z_i a_i partial_(c_i)` satisfies
    `D_z^d Q=(-1)^d d! (product_i a_i) Q((1,z_i,b_i/a_i)_i)`.
    Total coordinate degree, a global coordinate swap and squarefree
    homogenization prove the identity without a distinctness
    assumption. Consequently the coherent kernel equals the
    highest-root annihilator pointwise. The primary genus-zero
    conformal-block quotient criterion identifies it with the dual
    coinvariant bundle for `SL_3`, all fundamental labels, and level
    `d-1`. The dual convention is recorded explicitly.

    Root recognized the matching fusion dimensions; Sol and Astra
    independently derived the operator identity and checked primary
    sources. A finite checker audits the sign and indexing at
    `d=1,2,4`. The identity opens access to collision factorization
    and connection residues, but does not by itself supply a height
    floor or improve the general growth estimate. See
    [the exact conformal-block identification](terminal_coherent_conformal_block_identity.md).

448. **Fusion residues determine additional universal kernel content.**
    Let `W` be the primitive polynomial Pluecker tuple of the
    terminal coherent kernel. On the distinct affine locus the
    induced determinant connection has the exact scalar form
    `nabla W=-tau_2 (sum_(i<j) dlog(z_i-z_j)) W`, where `tau_r`
    is the trace of the conformal-block quotient residue at an
    `r`-label collision. Primitive coordinates have zero generic
    pair-diagonal order; stable-curve global generation identifies
    their nonzero limit with the actual embedded determinant frame.
    These facts determine the pair residues. Subtracting those
    logarithmic terms leaves a regular polynomial one-form, which
    dilation invariance forces to vanish.

    Comparing the same connection along a generic coalition gives
    the exact numerator order
    `nu_r=tau_r-binom(r,2)tau_2`. This comparison is made for
    `r<=m/2`, within the published collision chart; binary invariant
    symmetry gives the complementary orders. Thus no conclusion
    about numerator content is inferred from a divisor-class
    identity alone. Vanishing of all lower coefficients is a
    polynomial identity, so `product_T n_T^nu_(|T|)` divides every
    actual integer coordinate, including nongeneric residue tuples
    and retained nested prime layers.

    The extra order beyond majority content at twelve rows is 15
    on each balanced six-cut. It lowers the kernel covolume upper
    coefficient from 185,460 to 171,600 and the first-minimum
    exponent from `16860/31` to `15600/31`, still above 32.
    Exact fundamental-fusion recurrences give the full collision
    table and verify insufficiency of this refined estimate through
    `k=15`; no all-depth insufficiency theorem is claimed here.
    Root supplied the residue-to-numerator comparison, Astra wrote
    the proof and arithmetic transfer, Sol independently audited the
    bundle extension and dual sign, and Luna checked fusion data.
    The general circle-point growth bound remains unchanged. See
    [fusion residues and universal core content](terminal_kernel_fusion_content.md).

449. **The annihilator and determinant calculation extend to higher rank.**
    For multilinear `SL_n` invariants on `m=nd` rows, substitution
    of the binary Veronese curve preserves every raw coefficient:
    a row's coordinate index is its unique binary exponent. The
    generalized coherent polynomial `Q(1,z,x_2,...,x_(n-1))`
    has kernel equal to the level-`d-1` highest-root annihilator.
    The same connection argument gives its determinant row degree
    and coalition orders from type-A fusion Casimirs, and hence a
    covolume upper coefficient `B(n,d)`.

    Root proposed varying the rank; Sol supplied the general
    operator identity and an exact 77-case computation for
    `2<=n<=8`, `2<=d<=12`. Comparing `B/h` with the stronger
    arithmetic threshold of item 450 gives no strict contradiction.
    Equality occurs only at `(2,2)` and `(3,2)` in that grid;
    the nearest strict miss is `(4,2)`, with 116 versus 110.
    The calculation retains half-integer complementary-cut formulas
    when `m` is odd and calibrates the affine connection convention
    at the four-row boundary case. These are finite comparisons,
    not an all-parameter inequality. See
    [higher-rank coherent kernels and fusion heights](higher_rank_terminal_fusion_grid.md).

450. **Weyl symmetry strengthens the coefficient-height obstruction.**
    For a nonzero integer vector in the generalized coherent kernel,
    fix one nonzero source coefficient. Its coordinate assignment
    partitions the labels into `n` blocks of size `d`. Every
    ordered pair of coordinate families gives a numerically zero
    degree-one binary residual containing that same coefficient,
    up to sign. Isolating its monomial at all projected core factors
    gives a divisor whenever a core cut contains a whole coordinate
    block and misses another. Assigning each such cut to one
    witness pair counts its norm only once and controls cancellation
    against row corrections before multiplying divisors.

    The union count is
    `U(n,d)=2^(nd)-2(2^d-1)^n+(2^d-2)^n`, and the resulting floor is
    `log C_Q >= U(n,d)(1-eta)w-2(n-1)sum_i log|K_i|`.
    It holds under the extracted pairwise prime-disjoint oriented
    core hypotheses. The Veronese monomial bijection preserves
    coefficient norm exactly; no coefficient conversion is lost.
    At rank three the leading coefficient is `6(2^d-1)`, raising
    the six-row threshold from 8 to 18 and the twelve-row threshold
    from 32 to 90. A numerical zero at the original Veronese tuple
    alone does not meet the coherent-kernel hypothesis.

    Root supplied the same-coefficient union and exact correction
    accounting; Luna wrote the proof and combinatorial checks,
    independently audited by Sol. The new floor still does not
    beat the available determinant bound in item 449. See
    [the Weyl-union coefficient floor](higher_rank_weyl_union_floor.md).

451. **Transpose symmetry proves exact identities and two all-size comparisons.**
    Fundamental fusion paths ending in the rectangle `d^n` are
    standard tableaux. The level-`d-1` condition says precisely
    that the bottom-left corner appears before the top-right
    corner. Transposition exchanges this condition with its
    complement, giving the exact rank identity
    `h(n,d)+h(d,n)=dim Specht(d^n)`.

    The Casimirs of complementary transposed prefix shapes have a
    fixed sum. Combining this with the trace of the partial Casimir
    on the full invariant space makes the unnormalized Casimir
    deficits invariant under transposition. Pair subtraction then
    proves that every coalition order, the determinant row degree,
    and `B(n,d)` are unchanged by exchanging `n,d`. This is a
    tableau and trace proof, not an extrapolation from the grid.

    The boundary families have the explicit common numerator
    `B(n,2)=B(2,n)=n*4^(n-1)-n*binom(2n,n)/2`.
    Elementary central-binomial estimates prove `B/h>=U` for
    every pair with `min(n,d)=2`, with equality exactly at
    `(2,2)` and `(3,2)`. The all-interior comparison remains open.
    Root supplied the corner-order observation and the pairwise
    transpose cancellation; Astra proved the trace identities and
    all-size boundary estimates. An independent tableau checker
    verifies the formulas and finite boundary data. See
    [transpose symmetry and the boundary comparisons](terminal_fusion_transpose_and_boundary_comparison.md).

452. **Tensor products justify repeated divisibility at one core prime.**
    For a fixed nonzero source coefficient, let `f_T,e_T` count its
    coordinate blocks wholly inside and wholly outside a core cut.
    Choosing `min(f_T,e_T)` disjoint full/empty coordinate pairs
    makes their partial actual evaluations vanish independently.
    Over the Gaussian DVR, each evaluation kernel splits in its
    free balanced monomial module. The intersection of the partial
    kernels is their tensor product, so coefficient extraction adds
    the individual conductor valuations. This avoids multiplying
    repeated divisibility assertions about the same scalar.

    Summing over prime-disjoint cores gives
    `log C_Q >= sum_T min(f_T,e_T)log n_T-2 sum_i log|K_i|`.
    Each correction valuation is charged at most once at its prime.
    The resulting fair-profile coefficient is
    `M(n,d)=sum_(f,e) n!/(f!e!(n-f-e)!)(2^d-2)^(n-f-e)min(f,e)`.
    It equals the earlier union count for `n<=3` and exceeds it
    by six when `n=4`. For every `n`,
    `M(n,2)=n*4^(n-1)-n*binom(2n,n)/2=B(n,2)`.
    Thus the entire level-one family reaches equality, with no
    strict exponent improvement. Astra proved the module statement
    and row-correction accounting; root and Sol independently
    audited them. Exact checks include 672 primitive one-core
    Gaussian fixtures. See
    [the tensor multiplicity floor](higher_rank_tensor_multiplicity_floor.md).

453. **The local coefficient multiplicity is sharp in every rank and degree.**
    Root constructed the explicit level-one kernel
    `L(v)=det[P_i v_i | Y_i v_i]` on `2n` rows. Each color-pair
    coefficient is a signed product of its within-pair brackets.
    The weighted second highest-root derivative vanishes because
    its top substitution repeats two determinant columns. At a
    generic coalition of `s` selected labels, the common coefficient
    order is exactly `max(0,s-n)`.

    To target an arbitrary source coefficient at degree `d`, choose
    two labels per color, crossing the cut for every partial color.
    This gives `s=n+f_T-e_T`; the selected coefficient has order
    `f_T`, hence primitive local order `min(f_T,e_T)`. Multiplying
    by `d-2` disjoint rainbow determinants restores all remaining
    rows and the weight `det^d`. Leibniz proves the degree-`d`
    annihilator condition. This is a genuine formal-DVR kernel
    section, not just a valuation pattern.

    Astra, Sol and Luna independently audited the construction.
    Its checker expands the determinant and the annihilator,
    verifies product fixtures, and checks 219,299 occupancy cases.
    No stronger individual-coordinate valuation floor is universal
    at a generic coalition. Additional special residue relations or
    simultaneous conditions at different primes remain possible;
    the construction does not glue a global integer section or
    furnish an endpoint circle configuration. See
    [generic local coefficient sharpness](local_tensor_coefficient_floor_sharpness.md).

454. **The stronger multiplicity floor still gives no finite-grid gain.**
    Luna independently counted full, empty and partial color blocks.
    With `q=2^d`, the multiplicity coefficient is
    `q^n E min(F,E)`, where each block is full or empty with
    probability `1/q` each. Its fixed-`q` asymptotic is
    `q^n(n/q-sqrt(n/(pi*q))+o(sqrt(n)))`.

    Exact comparisons on `2<=n<=8`, `2<=d<=12` give `B/h>=M`;
    equality occurs throughout `d=2`, and every `d>=3` comparison
    is strict. Additional samples for `d=3,...,6` through `n=12`
    are also strict. These are finite checks and do not prove the
    all-interior inequality. At twelve rows, the floor remains
    `90w`, below the determinant average `15600w/31`. See
    [the occupancy count and comparisons](occupancy_candidate_floor.md).

455. **Local fusion data do not select a short global integer vector.**
    Sol proved that the coherent kernel over a Gaussian DVR is
    saturated in the fixed source module, so all intrinsic Smith
    exponents of that inclusion are zero. A positive coalition
    order instead compares a global polynomial determinant section
    with a nonzero local frame. Full rank after normalizing output
    rows therefore does not imply a zero global coalition order.

    The index-`D` lattices `x=0 mod D` and `x+Ny=0 mod D`, with
    `D=N^2+1`, have the same determinant and local Smith data at
    every prime but first minima `1` and `sqrt(D)`. This isolates
    the missing position of the local subspaces in one global
    coefficient lattice. A separate twelve-row finite-field
    calculation gives localized-six presentation slopes consisting
    of 311 zeros and 30 ones at one six-label collision; those
    presentation slopes must not be identified with the global
    numerator order 15. One sufficient unresolved route is a
    globally controlled positive-rank sublattice with covolume
    exponent below 90 per rank. Root and Astra audited the scope
    and the lattice example. See
    [the local-to-global slope gap](nonarchimedean_fusion_slope_scope.md).

456. **Localized determinants generate the entire kernel at every distinct configuration.**
    For `m=nd`, the coherent kernel is spanned by the `2n`-row
    determinants `det[V | diag(z)V]_I` times complementary invariants
    of weight `det^(d-2)`. An incidence argument proves the maximal-minor
    ideal has expected height, is irreducible, and is generically
    reduced. Eagon--Northcott gives Cohen--Macaulayness, hence primeness;
    row grading and invariant projection then give the asserted span.
    This closes the earlier all-point generation gap at twelve rows,
    rather than extending a generic finite rank test by assumption.

    If the largest repeated direction has multiplicity `r`, the same
    incidence calculation gives exact ideal height
    `max(0,min(m-2n+1,m-r-n+1))`. Thus expected height persists whenever
    `r<=n`, although primeness need not. Root, Astra and Sol independently
    audited the generation proof. The checker verifies nonvacuous
    incidence witnesses, determinant identities and smaller generation
    matrices. See [the determinantal generation theorem](distinct_configuration_determinantal_kernel_generation.md).

457. **A global resolution independently computes kernel rank and degree.**
    Write `e=d-2` and
    `a_j=sum_(a+b=j,e>=a>=b>=0)(a-b+1)f^(e^(n-2),e-b,e-a)`.
    The row-multilinear invariant part of Eagon--Northcott gives terms
    `F_j=direct-sum_(|S|=2n+j) O(-1_S)^(a_j)`. Their alternating ranks
    equal the coherent-kernel rank; their alternating row degrees
    equal the primitive Pluecker degree. Extension across configurations
    of maximum multiplicity at most `n` leaves a codimension-at-least-two
    complement and excludes a hidden common divisor of the Pluecker tuple.

    At `(n,d)=(3,4)`, the term ranks are
    `(4620,7920,4455,880,66)`, giving rank `341` and row degree `55`.
    The checker agrees with the fusion calculation in all 77 earlier
    parameter cases. Root replaced initially vacuous Laplace fixtures
    by fixed-seed generic matrices and checked 90 nonzero identities.
    This is an algebraic resolution, not a height estimate for integral
    lifts. See [the coherent-kernel resolution](coherent_kernel_eagon_northcott_resolution.md).

458. **A single local support has an exact leading lattice height.**
    Under the full Boolean profile, the content of a local `2n`-row
    determinant is its cut divisor up to a factor of logarithmic size
    `o(w)`. Matching coefficients attain each separate cut minimum,
    giving primitive height `B(n,2)2^(m-2n)w+o(w)`. Tensoring with the
    fixed complementary invariant lattice preserves saturation and
    multiplies its Gram matrix by the squared local-vector norm.

    At twelve rows, each six-row support therefore supplies a rank-five
    lattice of per-rank height `1152w+o(w)`. The larger-support family
    `K_S tensor invariants(S^c)` has the upper estimate
    `2^(m-nd0)B(n,d0)/h(n,d0)` per rank; the cases `d0=2,3,4` give
    `1152`, about `795.43`, and about `503.23`, all above `90`.
    Root corrected the distinction between exact content and its
    residual factor, and between this family and a different product
    of coherent kernels. See [the support-family diagnostic](local_generator_support_family_diagnostic.md).

459. **Full Boolean circuits retain small coefficients but require oriented completion.**
    Actual small-imaginary rows give simultaneous three-row and
    four-row circuits with pairwise coprime private norm factors of
    positive block height and integer coefficients of height `o(w)`.
    The split-norm family
    `U=(a-3)^2+16`, `V=(a+3)^2+16`, `W=a^2+25`
    satisfies `U+V=2W` with bounded coefficients and has a rank-two
    determinant lift of the expected row size. A common Gaussian
    block can also be inserted by an integer shear.

    For the displayed pair Gaussian factors, with only whole-factor
    conjugation allowed, exact polynomial CRT forces that shear to
    have size at least a constant times `a^5`, rather than `a^4`.
    This costs half a block in row height for that restricted family.
    Independently orienting primes within composite norms is not
    covered. The checker verifies twelve arithmetic fixtures and
    all eight exact CRT leading coefficients. See
    [the small-imaginary circuits and completion gap](full_boolean_small_imaginary_circuits.md).

460. **Linked determinants control integral generation at a simple coalition.**
    For `z_i=s a_i` inside a coalition and `z_j=b_j` outside, the
    ideal of normalized local determinants equals the sum of the
    maximal-minor ideals of
    `[V_T,s a V_T; V_O,b V_O]` and `[V_T,a V_T; s V_O,b V_O]`.
    Three kernel-line incidence charts bound every allowed special
    fiber by the expected dimension. Murray--Osserman's linked
    determinantal theorem then gives Cohen--Macaulayness and excludes
    vertical components, proving saturation of the polynomial ideal.

    Invariant projection costs only the fixed rectangular hook product;
    at twelve rows, `144 K_R` lies in the normalized-generator span.
    This includes arbitrary coalition depth `s=pi^e`, with no factor
    growing in `e`. The unit residual-difference hypotheses are explicit.
    Root and Sol independently audited the geometric proof; the checker
    verifies 945 minor identities and the invariant lattice's unit
    minor. A direct projection calculation has denominator `72`,
    consistent with the safe bound `144`. See
    [the linked saturation theorem](linked_determinantal_coalition_saturation.md).

461. **Residual factors control local and global integral generation.**
    For fixed `n,d`, the normalized generator matrix has rank `h(n,d)`
    wherever
    `D_T=product(a_i-a_k) product(b_j-b_l) product b_j`
    is nonzero. At `s=0`, item 460 proves this; at `s!=0`, every
    direction has multiplicity at most two, so item 457 proves it
    even across cross-group coincidences. Nullstellensatz gives an
    integral identity expressing `A D_T^H` in the ideal of all
    maximal minors, for fixed constants `A,H`.

    After any characteristic-zero DVR specialization, Smith normal
    form therefore bounds `length(K_R/N_R)` by `v(A)+H v(D_T)`.
    This removes the unit-residual assumption without introducing a
    term proportional to the coalition depth. The constants are
    existential and computable, with no numerical exponent claimed.
    Root and a second Sol instance independently audited the proof.
    It uses the gcd of all maximal minors, not a chosen large minor.
    See [the residual-discriminant index bound](residual_discriminant_local_index_bound.md).

    Root then joined these estimates over rational primes. If
    `Delta_ij=t_ij product_(T containing i,j)n_T` with disjoint
    core-prime supports, put `B=product|t_ij|` and
    `Gamma=product gcd(X_i,Y_i)`. The complete primitive local family
    satisfies `[K_Z:N_prim] | A B^H Gamma^(H m(m-1))`.
    A unit projective chart after row primitivization bounds every
    local residual discriminant; division by actual column content
    ensures that the primitive columns contain the local normalized
    span. No additional comparison index is needed. Since
    `Gamma<=product|Y_i|`, the extracted profile gives logarithmic
    index `o(w)`. This controls integral joining of supports but does
    not supply the required short vector. See
    [the global primitive-generator index theorem](global_primitive_local_generator_index.md).

462. **Even exact redundant generation does not imply a short vector from these numerical data.**
    In the correct ambient dimension `462`, embed the saturated
    rank-`341` lattice
    `K_q=ker(1,q,...,q^341) subset Z^342` by zero extension.
    It has covolume `q^341 Theta(1)` and first minimum between `q`
    and `sqrt(q^2+1)`. A unimodular change of its consecutive basis,
    followed by extra primitive columns, gives `4620` primitive
    generators all of height `exp(1152w+o(w))`, while its covolume
    exponent is `171600` and its first-minimum exponent is
    `171600/341>90`.

    A selected maximal minor can have exponent `341*1152` while
    the gcd of all maximal minors is one. The same numerical ranks
    as item 457 can even be realized by a split exact integer
    resolution. Every nonzero singular value of the full generator
    matrix has the displayed column-height scale as well. Thus those
    ranks, saturation, generator heights, a large selected minor and
    good real conditioning do not force the desired relation.
    Root caught the contrary inference before accepting a uniformity
    claim; Luna supplied and root refined this exact countermodel.
    It is an abstract lattice example, not a circle configuration.
    See [the redundant-generator height obstruction](redundant_local_generators_height_obstruction.md).

463. **A three-row discriminant reduction has genuine finite oriented-factor examples.**
    For constant imaginary coordinates and `X_i=r+g a_i`, the common
    root condition gives `f(t)=g t^2+2rt+s` with `gs-r^2=1`.
    Pair-private divisibility yields integer Lagrange quotients
    `(q_1,q_2,q_3)=(u,-v,w)`. With consecutive gaps `A,B` and
    `C=A+B`, coefficient comparison gives
    `g=u-v+w`, `2r'=wB-uA-gC`, and `(r')^2+1=guAC`.
    The alternate Vieta root need not be integral. Centering the
    common root also does not force `s` to have the size of `g`;
    an explicit family has `s=2` and unbounded `g`.
