    Sol and a fresh Luna instance found two exact finite fixtures.
    The smaller-node fixture has `g=109`, `r=-33`, nodes
    `(134,291,304)`, gaps `(157,13,170)`, and quotients
    `(73,-4513,4549)`. After removing the bounded ramified factor
    two, all seven core norms are pairwise coprime and split-supported.
    Direct Gaussian divisibility certifies the pair and triple gcd
    orientations, not just their rational norms. These examples
    show finite consistency, not a balanced infinite family or a
    counterexample to uniformity. The exact checker also verifies
    nonintegrality of a Vieta mutation and the centered-root family.
    See [the three-row interpolation scope](three_row_discriminant_interpolation_scope.md).

464. **Collective determinant coefficients have a valid arithmetic floor and an all-size cap.**
    Root proposed retaining all coefficient-rank constraints by taking
    full kernel-wedge coordinates. For a nonzero scalar coordinate
    `F_S` of the primitive polynomial wedge `W`, put
    `r_(S,T)=ord_T F_S-nu_T(W)`. After the common coalition power is
    removed, the universal tuple remains primitive over a polynomial
    UFD. Every generator wedge is its polynomial multiple. The ideal
    of all projected minors, together with item 461, therefore gives
    the actual divisibility
    `product n_T^r_(S,T) | A B_res^H Gamma^(Hm(m-1)+2E) w_S`,
    where `E=m delta/2` and `w_S` is a primitive integer basis-wedge
    coordinate. This transfer allows nongeneric actual residues.

    Independently, the coefficient-support grid lemma gives
    `sum_T ord_T F<=delta m 2^(m-3)` for every nonzero binary invariant
    of row degree `delta`. Bracket products attain equality. It follows
    that `sum_T r_(S,T)<=B(n,d)` for every nonzero determinant
    coordinate, including constant linear combinations. Thus generic
    exterior-coordinate divisibility cannot strictly exceed the
    existing fusion covolume exponent. Root, Astra and Sol audited
    the cap and its conventions for full coalitions. See
    [the sharp invariant order cap](invariant_full_boolean_coalition_order_cap.md)
    and [the arithmetic exterior-floor barrier](exterior_coefficient_coalition_floor_barrier.md).

    At `(n,d)=(2,3)`, an exact polynomial enumeration covers all
    `binom(20,4)=4845` raw-coordinate projections. There are 1725
    identically zero coordinates, 240 with summed extra order 8,
    and 2880 with summed extra order 18. The minimum is exactly
    four times the scalar coefficient floor, giving no collective
    improvement even in this first case. The checker verifies an
    explicit two-matching witness and the three displayed fusion
    budgets. Special arithmetic excess beyond generic orders remains
    outside this barrier and is not controlled here.

465. **The actual anchors are conjugate-primitive, and an exact finite fixture meets this condition.**
    The central truncation reduction supplies
    `gcd_Z[i](X_i+iY_i,X_i-iY_i)=1`. Thus ordinary row content is
    exactly one, coordinates have opposite parity, and the global
    generator-index theorem simplifies to `[K_Z:N_prim] | A B^H`.
    This removes a correction term without improving the existing
    subpower index conclusion or the point-count growth rate.

    The finite fixtures in item 463 have ramification above two in
    some rows; their scope has been clarified. Luna supplied an exact
    stronger fixture with `Y_i=1` and even real coordinates
    `(1469178,31686,153548)`. Its common, pair and private core norms
    are `109`, `(157,13,85)`, and `(1483897,4513,195749)`, with
    pairwise disjoint split-prime supports and actual compatible
    Gaussian orientations. Every row is conjugate-primitive, and
    the pair residuals are `(84,-86,142)` in the `12,23,13` order.
    The checker verifies exact products, prime factorizations,
    Gaussian divisions and norm gcds. This is a finite configuration,
    not an asymptotically balanced family. Its prime common and pair
    blocks prevent this particular fixture from being refined into
    all fifteen nonempty four-row blocks. See
    [the conjugate-primitive fixture](finite_full_support_conjugate_primitive_configuration.md).

466. **Actual norms give a full barycentric system, but its isolated four-row circuit has balanced models.**
    Put `k_i=Norm(K_i)`, `tau_i=product_(j!=i)t_ij` and
    `A_i=n_i product_(T not containing i,|T|>=3)n_T^(|T|-2)`.
    Exact interpolation of `x^2+1`, with `x_i=X_i/Y_i`, gives
    `sum_i(k_i/tau_i)A_i X_i^j Y_i^(m-4-j)=0` for
    `0<=j<=m-4`. The norm-block height in each `A_i` is
    `((m-5)2^(m-2)+m+2)w+o(w)`. These identities allow nonconstant
    subpower imaginary coordinates. Keeping the remaining three
    interpolation coefficients also retains the positive quadratic
    of discriminant `-4`, with every overlapping denominator charged.

    At four rows, the lower circuit is
    `sum_i(k_i/tau_i)n_i n_[4]\{i}=0`. Astra constructed an
    unbounded balanced model of this isolated equation using eight
    distinct quadratic Gaussian norms on an explicit arithmetic
    progression. Their rational-prime supports are pairwise disjoint,
    their Gaussian factors and corrections are conjugate-primitive,
    and the coefficients are the actual coupled products of six
    bounded edge residuals. The construction does not realize those
    residuals as a rank-two determinant array, the complete metric
    equations, or tiny imaginary row coordinates.

    At five rows, combining two moments gives a Gaussian relation.
    Its term has exact rational content `n_i n_[5]\{i}`, of height
    `2w+o(w)`. Removing it leaves complementary cut factors and
    preserves the original angular differences by a common rotation.
    Reanchoring restores numerator height `8w+o(w)`, so the written
    reduction in support size is not a height descent. See
    [the many-row norm system and its scope](many_row_norm_barycentric_system.md).

467. **Conjugation and real ordering do not by themselves force a short kernel vector.**
    The local determinant `det[(P_iV_i|Y_iV_i)]` is unchanged
    under `P_i -> bar(P_i)=P_i-2iY_i`, and equals the determinant
    written with `X_i` in place of `P_i`. Its integer coefficient
    matrix gains no independent rows by adjoining its conjugate.
    Taking a Gaussian norm doubles both the divisibility order and
    the upper logarithmic height.

    Sol proved that, for every fixed invariant size and every `B`,
    strictly ordered positive even `X_i` with `Y_i=1` can have
    coherent-kernel first minimum greater than `B`. Row multilinearity
    makes every nonzero invariant survive as a nonzero coefficient
    polynomial after this substitution. A finite collection of such
    polynomials is avoided on the ordered even integer lattice.
    Common even shears preserve the kernel and make the directions
    arbitrarily close to the real axis. This does not preserve the
    balanced norm-factor profile or the normalized circle radius.
    The actual normalized Hermitian equations remain a coupled
    near-square system. See
    [the conjugation and ordered-row audit](ordered_gaussian_kernel_metric_audit.md).

468. **Compatible integral norm and bracket data have an exact Gaussian realization criterion.**
    For a nonzero rational rank-two bracket array and positive norms,
    three rows determine a rational symmetric binary form `Q`.
    There are `m-3` remaining linear norm compatibilities. One
    cleared triple-area equation makes `det Q=1`; together with
    positivity of the first norm, this gives Euclidean realization.
    All the other triple-area equations then follow. They are not
    additional independent constraints beyond the full norm system.

    If the norms and brackets are integral and one norm is a Gaussian
    norm, there is a simultaneous Gaussian-integer realization.
    The rational dot products are integral because their squares
    equal `N_iN_j-Delta_ij^2`. The rank-one Gaussian Gram identities
    then supply a common divisor of norm `N_1`; division constructs
    all the rows. Sol and Astra independently found the argument,
    and Luna audited the split, inert and ramified valuations.
    Exact conjugate-primitivity is not automatic: the data
    `N_1=N_2=25`, `S_12=15`, `Delta_12=20` admit no realization
    with both rows conjugate-primitive.

    After all Boolean factors are canceled, the first triple equation
    is `4UV-(W-U-V)^2=4(t_12 t_23 t_31)^2`, where, at three rows,
    `U=t_23^2 k_1 n_1 n_23`, and cyclically for `V,W`.
    Its Gaussian lift is a triangle with the three displayed side
    norms and determinant `t_12 t_23 t_31`. Thus its small additive
    correction is an exact area identity, not by itself a strict
    height inequality. See
    [the norm-metric realization criterion](boolean_norm_metric_realization_criterion.md).

469. **All fixed-metric integral rotations are classified by one common Gaussian norm.**
    For any Gaussian rows, write `P_i=H Q_i` with the `Q_i`
    Gaussian-coprime. Root proved
    `d=Norm(H)=gcd_Z({Norm(P_i)},{Delta_ij})`. The Gaussian Gram
    entries generate the ideal `(d)` by Bezout; the square identity
    for their real parts proves the reverse rational divisibility.
    Every integral realization of the same oriented Gram matrix is
    exactly `P_i'=H'Q_i` with `Norm(H')=d`. Under the full Boolean
    profile, `n_[m] | d` and `d/n_[m] | product_i k_i`, so
    `log d=w+o(w)` and there are only `exp(o(w))` rotations for
    this one fixed Gram matrix.

    If both realizations have positive real coordinates and
    `|Im(P_i)|<=B`, they coincide whenever one row satisfies
    `N_i>4dB^2`. Astra strengthened root's initial determinant
    estimate by using the diameter `2B` of the appropriate circle
    cap. This threshold holds in the desired full profile, so at
    most one rotation has the tiny imaginary coordinates. It does
    not exclude that rotation or count the possible Gram matrices.
    Luna's exact checker covers 14,400 small tuples and all 3,580
    resulting fixed Gram classes, as well as the primitive fixture
    and the explicit primitive-realization obstruction. See
    [the common rotation classification](gaussian_common_rotation_classification.md).

470. **Primitive Gaussian completion costs only residual height.**
    Start with an integral realization of the full Boolean norm and
    determinant data, with all row norms odd and all core primes
    split. Put `K=product_i k_i` and `B=product_(i<j)|t_ij|`.
    Astra proved that one common rational norm-one rotation, followed
    by division by ordinary row contents `g_i`, produces
    conjugate-primitive Gaussian rows and coherent oriented factors
    `H'_T` with `n'_T=Norm(H'_T) | n_T`. The precise bounds are
    `product_i g_i | KB` and
    `L=sum_T log(n_T/n'_T)<=2log B+log K`.
    The new correcting norm is at most `k_i exp(L)`, and each new
    determinant residual is at most `|t_ij| exp(L)`.

    At a proper core prime of depth `e`, the norm and determinant
    equations force the incident Gaussian gcd to have norm depth
    at least `e`. Crossing residual valuations bound its rational
    content. After row primitivization, one common orientation
    survives to depth at least `max(0,e-2R_p)`, where `R_p` is
    the sum of crossing residual valuations. At the full core,
    rotating its common Gaussian factor to one orientation leaves
    depth at least `max(0,e-sum_i v_p(k_i))`. Disjoint core support
    allows each loss to be charged once.

    Root and Sol independently audited the argument. The exact
    checker verifies 40,061 admissible valuation patterns, while
    the proof covers arbitrary depths. Thus balanced compatible
    metric data admit a conjugate-primitive oriented profile with
    the same leading block heights. Angular differences survive;
    small imaginary coordinates relative to the integer real axis
    need not. This reduction isolates a remaining common-rotation
    condition and supplies no strict exponent gain. See
    [the primitive completion theorem](boolean_metric_primitive_completion.md).

471. **The full-profile reduction has the required quantifiers, including sharper pair residuals.**
    Root and Astra independently retained the actual Gaussian pair
    gcd in the central extraction. For primitive anchor numerators
    `P_i`, its norm satisfies
    `log Norm(gcd_G(P_i,P_j))=(d_0i+d_0j-d_ij)/2`.
    The retained pair core loses at most `2s` of this threshold
    mass. Consequently
    `log|t_ij|<=log(C_0/2)+zeta W/4+2s`, avoiding the extra
    factor `2^m` in the generic block-error estimate.

    With `k=m+1`, `w=W/2^m`, and original cardinality `M`, the
    individual block, correction, imaginary-value and pair-residual
    errors are `O(k2^m/sqrt(M))`. Aggregate correction and residual
    logarithms are subpower if `k^3 2^m/sqrt(M)->0`. Both allow
    every fixed `m` and the full fixed `c<1/2` logarithmic growing
    range. The strict small-arc gap gives
    `w>=4(M-1)log(sqrt(2)/C_0)/2^m`, so `w` really tends to
    infinity, even for arbitrarily slow unbounded original counts.
    One fixed-dimensional positive residual exponent gap would
    suffice for uniformity, without uncontrolled growing-dimensional
    constants. Items 472 and 474 show that dimensions two and three
    cannot give that gap. The exact checker covers 138,180 allocation
    tuples and 772,964 pairs. See
    [the full-profile quantifier audit](endpoint_full_profile_quantifiers.md).

472. **Small imaginary coordinates force a cost in lifting a short lattice basis.**
    Write `P_i=H Q_i`, where the `Q_i` have Gaussian gcd one,
    and put `d=Norm(H)` and
    `h=[Z^2:span_Z Q_i]=gcd|Delta_ij|/d`.
    Astra proved `gcd(h,product Norm(Q_i))=1` and
    `h | gcd|t_ij|`. A prime of the index puts all primitive
    quotient rows on one nonisotropic projective line; the full
    prime incidence then gives the residual divisibility.

    If a basis of this lattice has vector lengths at most `L` and
    is expressed through the rows with coefficient sums at most
    `C`, then `C>=h sqrt(d)/(2LB)`, where `B=max|Im(P_i)|`.
    Thus every basis of subpower geometric height costs at least
    `exp(w/2-o(w))` in row coefficients. The saturated small-value
    lattice has covolume `sqrt(sum Delta_ij^2)/(dh)`; it may have
    one tiny vector and a long second minimum. Transference alone
    does not exclude that shape.

    An explicit full balanced two-row family uses
    `H=a+i`, `Q_1=2a+1-2i`, `Q_2=4a+1-4i`, with
    `a` a positive multiple of 2210. All three block norms have
    disjoint split-prime supports, `K_i=1`, `Y_i=1`, `t_12=-2`,
    and `h=2`. Its short-basis coefficients attain the half-block
    scale. The checker covers forty family members and 7,012
    primitive index cases, alongside the finite three-row fixture.
    See [the row-lattice transference audit](small_imaginary_row_lattice_transference.md).

473. **Reanchoring has one exact least circle and an algebraic correction cocycle.**
    For actual conjugate-primitive anchor rows, every transition is
    `h_ab=bar(P_a)P_b/g_ab`, where
    `g_ab=Norm gcd_G(P_a,P_b)=gcd_Z(S_ab,Delta_ab)`.
    If `z_a` are the original equal-norm points with common Gaussian
    gcd `G`, the denominator lcm at anchor `a` is associated to
    `z_a/G`. Its norm is exactly `R^2/Norm(G)`, independently
    of the anchor.

    Under the actual all-pair core divisibilities, let
    `B=product_(T!=empty)H_T` and `E=lcm_G(bar(K_i))`.
    The common least squared radius is exactly
    `product_(T!=empty)n_T * Norm(E)`.
    The core point at anchor `a` has correcting factor
    `E_a=E K_a/bar(K_a)`, and its transition cocycles are forced
    by the original lift. In central truncation, `Norm(E)|D^2`,
    where `D` is the common modulus of the original corrections;
    `Norm(G)=n_empty D^2/Norm(E)`. This charges the empty block
    and all corrections without multiplying anchor radii. The
    identities expose no second independent tiny-rotation condition.
    Sol supplied the proof and 6,573 primewise allocation checks;
    root audited the all-pair divisibility hypothesis. See
    [the all-anchor radius and rotation identities](all_anchor_rotation_radius_cocycle.md).

474. **The complete three-row small-imaginary profile has an unbounded balanced family.**
    A fresh root search for Gaussian linear factors with constant
    imaginary row products found the seven factors
    `t-i`, `t-6-5i`, `t-6+3i`, `t-6+4i`, `t-4+3i`,
    `t-3+2i`, and `t-7-6i`, assigned respectively to
    the common, three pair, and three private blocks. The three
    incident four-factor products have imaginary parts
    `(240,180,420)` and polynomial determinant residuals
    `(-60,180,240)`.

    Normalize each factor by its value at zero and restrict
    `t` to positive multiples of `8088851149545216141000`.
    Astra's exact resultant certificate shows that all seven
    normalized Gaussian factors are integral, conjugate-primitive,
    odd, and pairwise disjoint in rational-prime support for the
    entire progression. The correcting factors are
    `(7+16i,47+90i,5+14i)`, the row imaginary coordinates are
    `(16,90,14)`, and the actual determinant residuals are
    `(-122,18,208)`. These are fixed constants. Every block norm
    has logarithm `w+O(1)` for `w=2log t`, and every row has
    logarithmic modulus `2w+O(1)`.

    Sol independently checked the polynomial identities and supplied
    the exact least circle: with `E=912-211i`, its squared radius
    is `product_T Norm(H_T(t))/4500`. Four explicit Gaussian
    points on it have radius asymptotic to `t^7/(30sqrt(5))`
    and arc length asymptotic to `(28/sqrt(5))t^3`.
    Thus the arc is `Theta(R^(3/7))=o(sqrt(R))`, with four
    fixed points and Gaussian gcd one.

    This is a full simultaneous asymptotic profile, including all
    norm, orientation and determinant equations; it supersedes
    finite examples as evidence of three-row feasibility. It rules
    out a universal three-row residual-height exclusion, while
    leaving the special `Y_i=1` problem and the four-row system
    open. It does not supply unbounded point counts. See
    [the balanced Gaussian family](balanced_three_row_gaussian_polynomial_family.md)
    and [its least-circle audit](three_row_balanced_family_least_circle.md).

475. **Quadratic composition cannot extend the displayed three-row polynomial family.**
    To split both factors with roots `6-3i` and `6-4i` after a
    rational quadratic substitution, completing the square would
    require `(6-d-3i)/A` and `(6-d-4i)/A` to be squares in
    `Q(i)`, for rational `A!=0,d`. Their norms force both
    `z^2+9` and `z^2+16` to be rational squares, with `z=6-d`.

    Astra proved the required fixed elliptic curve
    `y^2=x(x+9)(x+16)` has exactly eight rational points.
    Its two-isogenous curve is `y^2=x(x-1)(x-49)`.
    The first descent image is exactly `{1,-1,3,-3}`; complete
    modulo-16 obstructions eliminate the other classes. The second
    image is trivial, using a modulo-49 obstruction and the real
    sign. The standard two-isogeny formula gives rank zero.
    Good reductions at 5 and 11 each have eight points, and the
    eight displayed rational points exhaust the group. Root checked
    the descent against the cited primary mathematical source and
    independently counted both reductions.

    The only nonnegative finite x-coordinates are 0 and 12, so
    `x=z^2` forces `z=0`. The two Gaussian squares would then
    have ratio `3/4`, which is not a square in `Q(i)`. Thus
    no rational quadratic, including nonmonic and negative-leading
    ones, gives this simultaneous splitting. This excludes only
    the prescribed polynomial-composition extension, not arbitrary
    four-row families or other factorizations at integer parameters.
    The checker certifies the full finite residue obstructions and
    the torsion/reduction calculations. See
    [the quadratic-extension obstruction](quadratic_extension_gaussian_square_obstruction.md).

476. **The three-row polynomial configuration belongs to a rational family.**
    Root and Luna derived the vertical-line surface
    `p+q+r=1, pqr=X^2`. Its seven Gaussian-rational roots are
    `i`, the three `X+i(s-1)`, and the three
    `X(1+1/s)+is`, with `s=p,q,r`. The row opposite `s`
    has the common root, the other two pair roots, and its private
    root; its imaginary part is the fixed constant
    `Y(s)=X(s^2-1)(X^2+s^2)/s^2`.

    If `X!=0`, the three parameters are distinct, and none is
    `0,1,-1`, all fourteen roots including conjugates are distinct.
    The three `Y(s)` are nonzero and distinct. Every pair determinant
    is the difference of the corresponding imaginary constants times
    its two shared norm quadratics. The hyperboloid
    `s^2-x^2-y^2=1` gives a rational two-parameter subfamily through
    `(p,q,r,X)=(s^2,-x^2,-y^2,sxy)`. An exact Fraction checker
    verifies all coefficient and determinant identities for an
    explicit member different from item 474.

    The note also records the unique quartic-root completion formula
    and the exact common-quadratic square criterion. A search of
    18,480 point/quadratic pairs found no simultaneous splitting;
    that finite failure is not an exclusion theorem. See
    [the rational triangle family](quartic_root_completion_and_quadratic_split_criterion.md).

477. **Every full rational polynomial profile specializes to a full primitive integer family.**
    For monic degree-`e` blocks `H_T` coprime to one another and
    all their conjugates, suppose the incident products have nonzero
    constant imaginary parts. Root proved that a rational base point
    `t_0=2^(-L)` makes each primitive row value have odd norm.
    Normalize every block by its value there. Integer Bezout
    certificates leave only finitely many possible bad primes, and
    a single progression makes every normalized block congruent to
    one at every such prime. This supplies integral blocks with
    odd, pairwise coprime norms, avoiding all correction norms.

    The row corrections and imaginary parts are fixed. The exact
    pair residual is already `Im(bar(K_i)K_j)`, by degree saturation
    and evaluation at the base point. All block logarithms are
    `w+O(1)`, and all correction heights are `O(1)`. A common
    Gaussian multiple of the conjugate corrections constructs
    `m+1` integer points with
    `R=Theta(h^(e(2^m-1)))` and arc length
    `O(R^((2^(m-1)-1)/(2^m-1)))=o(sqrt(R))`.

    The quantifiers matter: polynomial profiles in arbitrarily large
    `m` would disprove uniformity, even with constants depending on
    each family, because its parameter may then grow. Only `m=2,3`
    are currently constructed here. The converse from integer
    profiles to polynomial families is unproved, so a polynomial
    exclusion alone would not establish the original theorem.
    The checker verifies whole-progression certificates in three
    block degrees and eighteen actual integer/circle realizations.
    See [the specialization theorem](boolean_polynomial_integer_specialization.md).

478. **Pairwise Vieta integrality has an exact correction-sensitive criterion.**
    In the actual positive unimodular norm form, take two primitive
    binary row vectors and their Gaussian realizations. Write their
    primitive Gaussian quotient as `u+iv` after removing the actual
    Gaussian pair-gcd norm `D`. Astra proved that the alternate
    determinant-one form through the same two norm values is
    integral exactly when `D|u` and `|v|` is one or two. The proof
    uses the content of the entire difference matrix; inspecting
    only its leading coefficient would miss essential denominators.

    Here `D=G_proper e`, with `e|Norm(K_i)Norm(K_j)` and
    `t_ij=e v`; correction primes are retained. For four balanced
    rows `log D=3w+o(w)`. The family in item 474 has primitive
    pair residues `(-2,18,16)`. Its only potentially integral pair
    also fails `D|u` for every progression value, by an explicit
    polynomial remainder. Thus it has no integral pair alternate.

    In the positive end-anchor chamber such an alternate increases
    the leading coefficient. Integral changes of binary coordinates
    preserving subpower imaginary coordinates can only shear and
    change signs, leaving that coefficient unchanged. A rational
    change avoiding this restriction requires a denominator of
    size `exp(3w-o(w))`. These are limitations of the specified
    descent, not a four-row exclusion. Root audited the formulas;
    the exact checker covers 2,165 positive forms. See
    [the Vieta descent barrier](four_row_integral_vieta_descent_barrier.md).

479. **The isolated four-row pair cross ratio has an exact positive coprime model.**
    In a full four-row polynomial profile, the normalized real rows
    satisfy `f_i-f_j=lambda_ij product_(T contains i,j)n_T`.
    Every difference has constant real sign, and its leading
    coefficient is the difference of the corresponding row leading
    coefficients. The four-point identity cancels every triple and
    full block, leaving an equation in six pair blocks.

    Sol found the exact solution
    `11(t^2+1)(t^2+9)-16(t^2+36)(t^2+49)`
    `+5(t^2+25)(t^2+225)=0`. Its six factors are distinct Gaussian
    linear norms and positive on the real line. The coefficient
    ratios arise from four ordered rational leading coefficients.
    This rules out an obstruction based only on that six-block
    equation and positivity. It does not supply the other nine
    blocks, the triple additive equations, or the constant-imaginary
    row products. The exact checker passes. See
    [the cross-ratio scope](four_row_polynomial_pair_cross_ratio_limit.md).

480. **The polynomial map is nondegenerate, but elementary phase and hyperplane counts do not exclude it.**
    The full and co-singleton blocks force `1,F_1,...,F_m` to
    be linearly independent: evaluating a putative relation on the
    full block and its conjugate kills its constant term and the
    sum of its coefficients; a co-singleton then kills each
    remaining coefficient individually.

    Every phase map `(F_i+i)/(F_i-i)` and every reduced pair ratio
    has degree `d=2^(m-1)e` and contact exactly `d` with one at
    infinity. Their total ramification is `2d-2`, with `d-1`
    already at infinity. For squarefree blocks the finite zeros
    and poles are unramified, leaving an unassigned budget of
    `d-1`. Pair root-power sums are differences of the original
    row moment equations and add no linear rank.

    Luna and root independently computed every rank in the target
    arrangement `z_0=0, z_i+/-i z_0=0`. Its exact subgeneral
    parameter is `2m-1`, so the direct Cartan--Nochka hypothesis
    fails for `m>2`; its leading coefficient is zero at `m=2`.
    Root checked the quoted threshold in the primary source.
    For `m>=3`, no subarrangement with `m+2` members is in
    general position either. This invalidates the proposed ordinary
    general-position count, not every possible refined geometric
    argument. Sol assembled and audited the phase cancellations.
    See [the map geometry](boolean_polynomial_map_geometry.md).

481. **The full four-row real polynomial system has a rigorously certified nondegenerate solution.**
    A fresh direct search fixed the full root at `i` and treated
    the other fourteen Gaussian roots as 28 real variables. The
    28 equations are `Im(sum_(T contains j) z_T^k)=0`, for
    four rows and `1<=k<=7`. Newton's identities make these
    precisely the reality conditions for all nonconstant
    coefficients of the four monic degree-eight row products.

    Astra found and refined a nondegenerate candidate, then stored
    a rational center and approximate inverse in a reproducible
    certificate. Exact Fraction arithmetic verifies, with
    `rho=10^(-30)`,
    `||A F(x_0)||_infinity<10^(-60)`,
    `||I-A J(x_0)||_infinity<10^(-59)`, and `||A||<2700`.
    Root supplied the elementary bound
    `||J(x)-J(x_0)||<=37632 rho` on the certified cube.
    Thus `x-AF(x)` maps it into itself and contracts by less
    than `1.014*10^(-22)`. Its unique fixed point is a genuine
    solution. The Jacobian stays invertible, making this an
    isolated algebraic solution of the rational polynomial system.

    All thirty roots and conjugates stay separated by more than
    `0.02` in the maximum norm, and every imaginary root
    coordinate has absolute value greater than `0.2`. The four
    row imaginary constants stay positive and above `0.003`,
    with pairwise gaps above `0.002`. Hence all fifteen linear
    norm blocks are disjoint and every pair determinant has its
    required nonzero constant residual. This is the full real
    polynomial profile, not an isolated six-block relation.

    Root and Sol independently ran and audited the exact checker,
    including the variable ordering, Jacobian and continuity bounds.
    This rules out a four-row exclusion using only these real
    polynomial conditions. It does not prove the roots are in
    `Q(i)`, so it does not give integer circle points via item 477
    or contradict the uniform goal. Clearing denominators or taking
    field norms does not automatically preserve constant imaginary
    parts. See [the certified real solution](four_row_real_polynomial_profile_certificate.md).

482. **One small imaginary coordinate determines the four-row angular test.**
    For a fixed integral oriented Gram matrix, the exact identity
    `Y_j=(S_1j Y_1+Delta_1j X_1)/N_1` propagates a subpower
    first imaginary coordinate to every row of the full balanced
    four-row profile. All integral realizations are parametrized by
    `G|gcd_G(N_1,Z_12,Z_13,Z_14)`, `Norm(G)=N_1`, with
    `P_1=bar(G)` and `P_j=Z_1j/G`.

    In the positive-real endpoint chamber, put `a=floor(sqrt(N_1))`.
    If `Y_1^2<2a-1`, necessarily `X_1=a`. Thus a subpower solution
    requires `N_1-a^2=b^2` with subpower `b`, and only the two
    divisors `a+/-ib` remain. For each choice, three explicit Gaussian
    divisibilities decide integrality of all other rows. Primitive
    realizations automatically recover the prescribed block orientations.
    Sol derived the reduction and root audited its signs, valuations
    and metric hypotheses. No uniform failure of these tests is proved.
    See [the divisor reduction](four_row_one_coordinate_divisor_reduction.md).

483. **The full degree-one four-row system has a five-star affine-pencil reduction.**
    Reindexing its fifteen factors by the five vertices and ten edges
    of `K_5` produces monic quintics `Q_a` satisfying
    `Im(bar(Q_a)Q_b)=(Y_b-Y_a)n_ab`. These are quadratic minors.
    Unimodular polynomial row reduction therefore ends with row degrees
    summing to two, so the five quintics always have a constant real
    relation. Exact rational intervals on the existing contraction cube
    prove that the certified solution has span exactly four, a unique
    relation with all coefficients nonzero, and balanced reduced degrees
    `(1,1)`. It consequently has a common frame `Q_a=h A_a+g B_a`,
    with `deg(h,g)=(4,3)` and `Im(bar(h)g)=1`.

    After normalization, `A_a=t+alpha_a`, `B_a=Y_a t+beta_a`.
    Writing `d_a=beta_a-Y_a alpha_a`, rational Gaussian contacts force
    `(delta(alpha_b-alpha_a)+d_a+d_b)^2-4d_a d_b`
    to be a negative rational square. All `d_a` share a sign and one
    class modulo Gaussian norms, including denominator valuations.
    The certified solution has all `d_a>0` and strictly decreasing
    `alpha_a` in increasing `Y_a` order. Its associated pairwise norm
    matrix has a rigorously negative principal minor, preventing an
    unjustified positive-semidefinite Gram interpretation.

    Astra and Sol independently derived and audited the identities;
    root checked the proof and both exact interval programs. The star
    representation makes the `S_5` reanchoring action explicit. Rational
    contacts, the common frame and distinct private factors remain
    essential; the isolated discriminant conditions also admit a
    degenerate example with all ten norm factors equal. No rationality
    conclusion or improvement in the radius dependence follows.
    See [the star-pencil theorem](four_row_star_pencil_reduction.md).

484. **Eight contacts uniquely reconstruct the missing polynomial frame over its input field.**
    Fix a real rational affine pencil and ten distinct oriented contacts
    in `Q(i)` satisfying its ten quadratic norm identities. A coprime
    frame with `deg h=4`, `deg g<=3` is determined up to scale by
    any eight contacts: the cross-product of two possible frames has
    degree at most seven and eight distinct zeros. Nonzero constant
    `Im(bar(h)g)` implies the required coprimality. Normalizing `h_4=1`
    therefore gives an invertible eight-by-eight linear system over
    `Q(i)`, so even a frame initially known only over an extension field
    descends to `Q(i)`.

    Existence still requires the two remaining complex contact residuals,
    the seven nonconstant coefficients of `Im(bar(h)g)` to vanish,
    its constant to be nonzero, and the root-separation conditions.
    The private roots are then explicit Gaussian-rational coefficients.
    A separate seven-by-seven Sylvester system parametrizes every monic
    determinant-one frame in this degree chart by a coprime real
    quartic/cubic pair `p,r`. With `p` monic integral and `r` integral,
    the complementary coefficients are integral exactly when
    `Res(p,r)=+/-1`; rational denominators may absorb a nonunit resultant.

    Astra proved the reconstruction and resultant statements; Luna and
    root independently audited the hypotheses, scaling and converse.
    The checker tests all 45 eight-contact subsets of a scalar fixture
    and separately rejects omitted compatibility tests. Those fixtures
    are not a rational full profile. The theorem removes an additional
    field-extension concern once rational input is supplied, but finding
    that input remains open. See [the reconstruction theorem](five_star_contact_frame_reconstruction.md).

485. **The integer five-star lift preserves the exact residuals but has only the generic relation bound.**
    Placing each correcting factor `K_a` in its corresponding star
    gives actual Gaussian integers `Q_0,...,Q_4` of logarithmic modulus
    `(5/2)w+o(w)`, with `D_0a=Y_a n_0a` and `D_ab=t_ab n_ab`.
    These ten edge norms are pairwise coprime. Their minor content
    divides `t_e t_f` for any two distinct edges and is consequently
    subpower. The saturated rank-three relation lattice has covolume
    `exp(w+o(w))`, yielding one relation of coefficient height at most
    `exp(w/3+o(w))`. Every three-supported primitive relation instead
    has height `exp(w+o(w))`; thus that short relation must use at least
    four stars. There is no lower bound here for four- or five-supported
    relations.

    The ten complementary three-term edge congruences are exact, but
    the earlier localized coefficient-minor rule contributes only at
    maximal relation order, where it reproduces the known covolume.
    No polynomial degree reduction follows from five numerical values.
    Sol established these statements and checked the integral kernel
    basis and complementary minors exactly; root audited the argument.
    The same checker independently verifies item 482's nearest-square
    threshold and both congruence signs on an existing three-row fixture.
    These tests do not construct a full four-row small-residue family.
    See [the integer star lift](four_row_integer_five_star_lift.md).

486. **A moment invariant excludes quadratic lifting of the known families, including every reanchoring.**
    Suppose a full degree-one `(m+1)`-row profile extends a common real
    quadratic pullback of an `m`-row profile. The new row contains one
    preimage of every old root `z_T`, together with one private root `r`.
    With `w=q(r)`, its real Newton sums force
    `Im(sum_T z_T^k+w^k)=0` for `1<=k<=2^(m-1)-1`.
    For `m>=3`, writing `A,B,C` for the first three imaginary moments
    of the old root union, elimination of `w` gives the necessary
    identity `E=4AC-3B^2+4A^4=0`.

    Exact rational bounds on the certified four-row solution instead
    give `E>42`; the stored center has `E=42.48732299...` and error
    less than `9240*10^(-30)`. Thus no real quadratic, branch choices,
    or private root can extend that profile in this way. Root further
    proved that reanchoring preserves each relevant union moment:
    it conjugates precisely an incident row's roots, whose imaginary
    power sums are already zero. Real affine changes multiply `E`
    by a nonzero fourth power, and conjugation leaves it unchanged.
    The exclusion therefore covers the whole reanchoring orbit.

    The entire vertical three-row family in item 476 has `A=0`,
    `B=4X`, and `E=-48X^2!=0`. The same theorem excludes all its
    common real-quadratic extensions to four rows. This condition
    requires the additional row; it is distinct from item 475's
    rational splitting obstruction for a particular seed.

    Astra established the general moment test and exact certificate;
    root and Luna audited the argument, and root added the reanchoring
    invariance and family-wide corollary. General degree-two block
    restrictions need not share a common quadratic composition, so
    neither result excludes arbitrary larger profiles or proves the
    uniform endpoint bound. See [the moment obstruction](quadratic_lift_five_row_moment_obstruction.md).

487. **The integer star congruences require depth trimming, not whole-prime deletion.**
    The original proof of item 485's localized minor conclusion incorrectly
    removed every core prime dividing a correction factor. A small
    correction may contain one copy of a prime whose core exponent is
    arbitrarily large, so that deletion need not have subpower cost.
    The repaired proof retains all stars and all prime powers. At a split
    prime, write `b_c=v_pi(Q_c)`, `b_min=min_c b_c`, and
    `d_pi(J)=max(0,min_(c notin J)b_c-b_min)`. For `r` integer relation
    rows and an `r`-element column set `J`, their coefficient minor is
    divisible by `p^d_pi(J)`. The two Gaussian orientations combine by
    taking the maximum exponent, not the sum.

    Since every star core has support of size at most two, for `r<=2`
    the forced exponent is bounded by the correction valuations. Summed
    over primes it therefore has logarithmic size `o(w)`. At `r=3`,
    the leading complementary edge depth is exactly the one already
    present in the saturated-kernel minors. The earlier covolume result
    survives, but its former whole-prime proof does not. The expanded
    exact checker covers 180 relation-lattice fixtures, both orientations,
    high prime powers, and nonprimitive stars. See the repaired
    [integer star argument](four_row_integer_five_star_lift.md).

488. **Four small nearest-square defects force one integral oriented realization.**
    Let four rank-two Gaussian integer columns have Gram matrix `S`,
    `a_i=floor(sqrt(S_ii))`, and `B=S-aa^t`. Put
    `E=max(1,max|B_ij|)`, divide the columns by their common Gaussian gcd,
    and let `L` be the least modulus of the four co-singleton gcds.
    If `6E^3<L`, the integer cofactor argument excludes ranks three and
    two for `B`. Rank one then gives a rational unit rotation; its second
    coordinates have integer squares and are therefore integers.
    Thus simultaneously `S_ij=a_i a_j+b_i b_j` and
    `Delta_ij=a_i b_j-a_j b_i`, with `b_i^2=S_ii-a_i^2`.

    For balanced four-row core data with positive pair dot products,
    subpower nearest-square defects give `E=exp(o(w))`, whereas
    `L>=exp(w/2-o(w))`. Consequently the three divisibility tests in
    item 482 hold automatically once all four defects are small.
    Dividing the new rows by their ordinary contents and trimming only
    the affected prime-power depths recovers primitive balanced data.
    This is a conditional sufficiency theorem: extracted near-axis
    profiles already have these defects, and their exclusion is unproved.

    A three-column Pell family has fixed nonsquare defects `13,21,37`
    and a fixed nonsingular Gram defect, but its primitive integer
    relation grows with the Pell parameter. It shows that this general
    rigidity argument needs four columns; it is not a full Boolean
    profile. Sol and root established the theorem and primitive repair;
    Luna independently audited them. The exact checker includes a
    genuine `6E^3<L` fixture, prime-power trimming, and twelve Pell
    instances. See [the Gram rigidity theorem](four_row_nearest_square_gram_rigidity.md).

489. **The extraction gives an explicit target for improving growth.**
    With `W=log(R^2)`, `w=W/2^m`, and fixed dimension `m>=4`, a robust
    hypothetical logarithmic residual-height lower bound `H>=f_m(w)`
    combines with `H<=4(m+1)W/sqrt(M)` to give
    `M<=max(Q_m,[4(m+1)W/f_m(W/2^m)]^2)`. The threshold `Q_m`
    explicitly retains profile width and height onset. Aggregate heights
    incur `(m+1)^3` instead of `(m+1)`.

    A lower bound larger than `sqrt(w log w)` by an unbounded factor
    would improve the current growth order. The concrete target
    `sqrt(w log w loglog w)` would give
    `O(log R/(loglog R logloglog R))`; `w/log w` would give
    `O((loglog R)^2)`. A positive fixed multiple of `w` would give
    uniformity. None of these arithmetic lower bounds is proved.
    The full dimension-dependent envelope retains all `2^m` and onset
    losses. An explicit diagonal comparison shows that sublinear gaps
    for every fixed dimension alone still do not force uniformity.
    Astra proved the inversion, and root and a separate Astra instance
    audited it. See [the conditional quantifier audit](residual_height_gap_growth_quantifiers.md).

490. **A fixed Gaussian root gives a parity and field-minimality obstruction to norm descent.**
    Let `P=X+iY` over a real number field `K` of degree `d`, with
    nonzero constant `Y`, and suppose `P(r)=0` for `r in Q(i)`.
    If `Norm_(K(i)/Q(i))(P)=A+iC` has constant imaginary part, then
    evaluation at `r` gives `2iC=-(-2i)^d Norm(Y)`. Thus `d` must
    be odd and `C=(-4)^((d-1)/2)Norm(Y)!=0`. Neither total reality
    nor Galois normality is assumed. Every normalized full profile
    has the common root `i`, but the certified profile's field degree
    is not known here.

    If a row is defined over a proper real subfield, its norm from
    the larger field is a proper power. A nonconstant polynomial's
    proper power cannot have a nonzero constant imaginary part:
    factor `B^e-bar(B)^e` over the roots of unity. Thus every row
    would have to generate the chosen coefficient field.
    More generally, for a monic row of degree `n>1` and a proper
    field enlargement of relative degree `e`, the imaginary degree
    becomes `(e-1)nf+h>=nd/2>d/2`, where `f` is the smaller field
    degree and `h` its nonzero imaginary norm degree. Under bounded
    content this also exceeds the endpoint threshold, even if the
    smaller imaginary norm is nonconstant.

    Root constructed an exact odd-degree example over `Q(cuberoot(2))`
    with common root `i` and imaginary norm `-64`. Its monic quartic
    reduces modulo five to `t(t-2)(t^2+4t+2)` at a degree-one prime;
    the final quadratic is irreducible. It therefore does not split
    over that Gaussian coefficient field, and enlarging the field
    destroys its constant-imaginary norm. It is a scope test, not
    a full profile. Astra and Luna independently audited the example
    and the parity proof. See [the fixed-root norm theorem](fixed_gaussian_root_norm_descent_parity.md).

491. **Primitive content of rational norm descent is controlled at every prime-power depth.**
    For descended block forms `B_T`, use the five actual circle
    polynomials `Z_0=product B_T` and
    `Z_i=product_(T not containing i)B_T product_(T containing i)bar(B_T)`.
    The common gcd of the four row products is a different object:
    it always includes the full block. Factor the thirty oriented
    forms by their `Q(i)` root orbits, with exponents `e_jO` in
    `Z_j`, and put `D=product Phi_O^(min_j e_jO)`.
    Homogeneous resultant identities give a fixed nonzero Gaussian
    integer `C` such that `D(a,b)|G(a,b)|C D(a,b)` for every primitive
    rational parameter pair with nonzero point values.

    Distinct oriented orbits give bounded `G`. At a collision,
    retaining the dominant orbit depth at each prime loses only
    bounded logarithmic mass, even at fixed resultant primes with
    arbitrarily large valuations. A nonbinary anchored valuation
    vector requires a positive proportion of correction height;
    a binary vector supplies only one cut. Consequently orbit
    collisions cannot preserve all fifteen distinct balanced,
    prime-disjoint cores with subpower corrections. This conclusion
    does not exclude a different smaller profile after cancellation.

    For integer `t` tending to infinity, let `q_i` be the degree of
    the nonzero imaginary row norm and `g=deg D`. Exact chord
    factorization gives primitive chord divided by square-root
    radius of order `t^(q_i-(d+g)/2)`. Thus `q_i>d/2` fails the
    endpoint scale under bounded content. Sol proved the content
    and exponent formulas; root and Astra audited them. The checker
    passes 408 primitive parameter fixtures, including collisions
    and all five actual circle points. General algebraic-unit
    paths are not evaluations of these same one-variable forms.
    See [the content and chord theorem](real_algebraic_norm_descent_content.md).

492. **A full quadratic-field profile cannot meet the bounded-content norm-descent threshold.**
    Suppose the original full profile has monic rows of degree
    `n>2` over `Q(sqrt(D))`, all containing the normalized root `i`.
    If every row norm has imaginary degree at most one, coefficient
    comparison and evaluation at `i` force
    `P_i=A_i+s_i sqrt(D)(t-i)`, with rational monic `A_i` divisible
    by `t^2+1` and nonzero pairwise distinct rational `s_i`.
    The pair bracket then makes the entire shared norm product
    `S_ij=(s_i A_j-s_j A_i)/(s_i-s_j)` rational of degree `n`.

    For one original row, however, its Gaussian norm `N_i` and its
    quadratic conjugate have gcd exactly `t^2+1`. Every rational
    divisor of `N_i` must divide this gcd. This contradicts the
    degree of `S_ij`. Hence at least one imaginary row norm has
    degree at least two. Under the distinct-orbit hypothesis of
    item 491, quadratic descent therefore has a primitive chord
    divided by square-root radius growing at least linearly in `t`.

    The single-row threshold really is degree one: the displayed
    form has imaginary norm `2D s_i^2 t`. The obstruction uses the
    pair structure and does not follow from item 490's parity result
    alone. Root found the argument; Astra and Luna independently
    checked the signs, field assumptions and gcd multiplicities.
    Orbit collisions and more general field degrees retain their
    stated limitations. See section 3 of
    [the norm-descent note](fixed_gaussian_root_norm_descent_parity.md).

493. **Every real cubic field has a monic quartic satisfying the individual norm condition.**
    For `q=e_2`, choose a trace-zero element `Y_0` with `q(Y_0)!=0`.
    Then `x=1/Y_0` is isotropic with nonzero trace. The element
    `w=3x/Tr(x)-1` has trace zero and `q(w)=-3`; choose a nonzero
    orthogonal trace-zero `v` with `q(v)=-3 delta`, `delta!=0`.
    Thus `q(a+bw+cv)=3(a^2-b^2-delta c^2)`.

    Root constructed rational quartics `a,b,c` with
    `a^2+1=b^2+delta c^2`, `a(i)=-i`, and `b(i)=c(i)=0`, using a
    rational point on `v_0^2+delta u^2=1`. Hence `U=a+bw+cv`
    satisfies `q(U)=-3`. Dividing `U+i` by its leading coefficient
    gives a monic quartic `P=X+iY` with fixed root `i` and
    `Im Norm(P)=-4 Norm(Y)!=0`. Its nonzero trace-zero `Y` generates
    the original cubic field, so the construction does not evade
    item 490 by using an unnecessarily large coefficient field.

    The construction works in both totally real and non-totally-real
    fields. It does not establish linear splitting over `K(i)` or
    compatibility between different rows. Luna independently audited
    the trace-form basis and quartic identity; Astra wrote the proof
    and exact checker. Sixteen signed rational-form fixtures pass.
    See [the cubic norm construction](cubic_norm_descent_root_incidence.md).

494. **Split cubic rows impose a degree bound on their common rational factor.**
    Normalize a row by `p=U+i`, where `q(U)=-3`, and let `G` be
    the monic gcd of its three coefficient conjugates. The identity
    `e_2(p)=2i Tr(p)` puts `G^2` into `Tr(U)+3i` and
    `bar(G)^2` into `Tr(U)-3i`. For simple input roots, differentiation
    gives `G bar(G)|(Tr U)'`, so `2deg G<=deg U-1`.
    In degree eight, `deg G<=3`. The fixed root `i` uses one degree,
    preventing a complete nonbase cubic orbit from lying in one row.
    The same identity shows that two conjugate zero values force the
    third, so no row contains two members of a nonbase cubic orbit.

    If `K(i)/Q(i)` is non-Galois, distinct elements of that cubic
    extension already have distinct `Q(i)`-orbits. The thirty
    distinct oriented input roots then satisfy item 491's bounded
    content condition automatically. In the cyclic case, orbit
    collisions between distinct input labels require disjoint cuts;
    this also holds for opposite orientations. Such collisions can
    still have bounded content and are not all excluded.

    Each degree-eight row has at most three Gaussian rational roots.
    Counting their incidences, including the full root `i`, bounds
    their total number among the fifteen input labels by seven.
    Astra proved the orbit statements and root audited them. The
    exact finite incidence count passes. These are necessary
    restrictions, not a full cubic-field exclusion. See
    [the root-incidence theorem](cubic_norm_descent_root_incidence.md).

495. **The explicit cyclic cubic quartic family never splits over its coefficient field.**
    Set `K=Q(alpha)`, `alpha^3-3alpha+1=0`, and use the trace-form
    basis `w=2-alpha^2`, `v=alpha^2+2alpha-2`, `delta=3` in item 493.
    For every nonzero rational parameter `r`, its monic quartic
    `P_r` has a residual cubic `F_r=P_r/(t-i)` that does not split
    completely over `K(i)`.

    At 17, the embeddings with `alpha=7,13` and `i=4` eliminate
    all sixteen unit parameter residues. At the first embedding,
    the only exceptions are `r=2,3,16`; the second gives each an
    irreducible quadratic factor. For nonunit parameters, integral
    expansions at zero and infinity give
    `Disc(F_r)/r^2 = c_0+O(r)`, `c_0=7 mod 17`, and
    `Disc(F_r)*r^2 = c_inf+O(1/r)`, `c_inf=3 mod 17`.
    The two leading residues are nonsquares. These are congruences
    for the exact 17-adic coefficients, not assertions that the
    coefficients are literally the integers seven and three.
    Thus arbitrary parameter valuations and unit parts are covered.

    A nonconstant composition `P_r(f(t))` cannot split either:
    splitting would place every root of `P_r` in `K(i)` by applying
    `f` to a root of the composite. This includes quadratic real
    compositions fixing `i`, which otherwise preserve the constant
    imaginary norm and produce rows of degree eight.

    Sol proved the obstruction; root, Astra and Luna independently
    audited the local cases. The exact checker also computes the
    field determinant norms in two cubic fields. It does not prove
    a general cubic-field or full-profile obstruction. See
    [the cyclic nonsplitting proof](cubic_norm_descent_mod17_nonsplitting.md).

496. **The cyclic quartic classification has two parameters and a genuine local boundary.**
    In the field and basis of item 495, every polynomial of degree at
    most four satisfying `q(U)=-3` and `U(i)=-i` has degree exactly
    four. Write `U=a+bw+cv` and `s=t^2+1`. The fixed root and the
    quadratic identity force `a=-(t^3+3t)/2+ks^2`, `b=sB`, `c=sC`,
    and `B^2+3C^2=(ks-t/2)^2+1-2kt`. The case `k=0` would force a
    rational determinant with square `1/12`, so it is impossible.

    Normalize the leading pair by the rational rotation
    `w'=p w+q_0 v`, `v'=-3q_0 w+p v`, `p^2+3q_0^2=1`.
    Coefficient comparison then gives exactly item 493's family,
    parameterized by `r in Q\{0}`. Thus the full solution set has
    both `r` and the independent rational basis rotation. An arbitrary
    rotation preserves the trace form, not necessarily field
    multiplication or splitting. Root derived the coefficient
    reduction and Luna independently proved the classification; see
    [the complete parameterization](cubic_quartic_complete_parameterization.md).

    Anisotropy of `x^2+3y^2` modulo 17 makes every rational rotation
    integral at 17. Sol's exact finite certificate excludes splitting
    for all eighteen rotation residues whenever `v_17(r)=0`.
    Three rotations have two vanishing leading coefficients; these
    are handled by primitive quadratic reductions at the bad places,
    using both embeddings of `i`. Discarding those places would
    leave four unchecked parameter residues.

    The nonunit boundary really behaves differently. For the fixed
    rational rotation `p=-13/14`, `q_0=-3/14`, every rational
    nonzero parameter with `v_17(r)>=3` gives a residual cubic splitting
    completely at all six embeddings into `Q_17`. Its discriminant
    is a nonzero square at each place, and the reduction retains a
    simple root near `i`; together these force cubic splitting.
    Root found this family and Astra proved uniform control of the
    entire power-series remainder. This is local splitting only,
    not splitting over `K(i)`; see
    [the local boundary proof](cubic_rotated_mod17_local_escape.md).

    A separate rational fixture has six simple split reductions at
    197, which lies in the same residue class modulo 36 as 17.
    Thus the finite residue obstruction cannot simply be asserted
    at every split prime in that class. The global splitting question
    for the two-parameter family and the arbitrary-profile height
    gap remain open.

497. **Rational offsets in Pisot norm descent require corrections of positive power height.**
    Let `K` be a real number field of degree `d>1`, and suppose
    `P=X+iY`, with `X in K[t]`, nonzero constant `Y in K`, a fixed
    root in `Q(i)`, and polynomial norm `A+iC` with constant `C`.
    Item 490's parity formula implies that `d` is odd. If `X(c)/Y`
    were rational at any rational `c`, writing that value `a/b`
    in lowest terms would give
    `(a+ib)^d-(a-ib)^d=(2ib)^d`. At `1+i`, opposite parity gives
    unequal valuations `s` and `ds`; both odd gives `d+1` and `2d`.
    Thus every such normalized value is irrational.

    Suppose also that `P` is monic and `epsilon` is a Pisot unit in
    `K`, positive at the distinguished real embedding. On
    `t_n=c+epsilon^n`, put `T_n=epsilon^n` and
    `rho=max_(sigma!=id)|sigma(epsilon)|<1`. The norm of the
    evaluated element, rather than evaluation of the polynomial norm,
    has phase converging at rate `O(T_n^-delta)` to
    `eta=B/bar(B)`, where `B=Norm(P(c))/P(c)` and
    `delta=min(1,-log(rho)/log(epsilon))`. The rational-value result
    proves `eta not in Q(i)`; its relative degree `D` is at most `d`.

    More generally, any rational unit-circle sequence with an
    irrational algebraic phase limit of degree `D` and that rate
    requires a rational correcting rotation of Gaussian height
    `H>=c_0 T_n^[delta/(D(2D+1))]` to become a ratio of two Gaussian
    integer points on an origin-centered radius-`R_n` circle in an
    arc of length `C sqrt(R_n)`. The proof combines a polynomial
    numerator bound, `H(eta_n)<=H R_n`, and the chord bound.
    Both radius inequalities use the actual radius after common
    content removal, so arbitrarily large cancellation is retained.

    In `K=Q(cuberoot(2))`, the unit `epsilon=1+alpha+alpha^2`
    gives `delta=1/2` and `D=3`, hence `H>=c_0 epsilon^(n/42)`.
    The explicit quartic of item 490 satisfies the hypotheses.
    Root proved the valuation and height statements; Astra and Sol
    independently audited them. See
    [the rational-phase proof](norm_descent_rational_phase_gap.md)
    and its [exact checker](check_norm_descent_rational_phase_gap.py).
    Algebraic offsets, several growing embeddings and arbitrary
    extracted integer profiles are outside this result; no general
    growth improvement follows.

498. **Algebraic offsets can escape the irrational phase obstruction.**
    For a fixed algebraic offset `xi in K`, the same Pisot asymptotic
    has rational limiting phase if and only if `U(xi)` is rational.
    In the field `alpha^3=1/2`, put
    `g=(4t^4-2t^3+10t^2-7t+6)/5` and
    `h=(34t^4-12t^3+20t^2-37t-14)/100`, then set
    `b=2(g^2+1)`, `a=g+b h`, `c=1+4g h+2b h^2`, and
    `U=a+b alpha+c alpha^2`. The identity `a^2+1=bc/2`
    gives `e_2(U)=-3`, and `U(i)=-i`.
    With `Y=15625/(4624 alpha^2)`, the polynomial `P=Y(U+i)`
    is monic of degree 16 and has imaginary norm `-4 Norm(Y)`.

    At `xi=alpha`, however, `U(alpha)=26/5`. The Pisot unit
    `epsilon=1+2alpha+2alpha^2` is the pure-cubic unit of item 497
    in a different field basis. On `t_n=alpha+epsilon^n`, the
    limiting phase is `((26+5i)/(26-5i))^2 in Q(i)`, so a fixed
    rational rotation can align the limit. This does not establish
    the rate required by the primitive radius, splitting into the
    coefficient field, or a full Boolean configuration. It prevents
    extending item 497 to arbitrary algebraic offsets by the same
    irrational-limit argument. See section 5 of
    [the rational-phase note](norm_descent_rational_phase_gap.md).
    Astra constructed the example; root checked all its polynomial,
    field and norm identities exactly, and a second Astra agent
    independently audited the construction and its scope.

499. **Fixed cubic Pisot norm paths cannot reach the endpoint with small corrections.**
    In a fixed cubic field of signature `(1,1)`, retain the monic row,
    fixed Gaussian root, constant imaginary polynomial norm and Pisot
    unit hypotheses of item 497, but allow every fixed offset `xi in K`.
    For any `0<kappa<1/6`, all sufficiently large indices require
    `H(u)>T_n^kappa` for a rational rotation `u` to produce an actual
    endpoint pair. The primitive phase height is `T_n^(h+o(1))`.
    Corvaja--Zannier's full-place gcd estimate proves that common
    Gaussian content is subexponential; multiplicative independence of
    two unit conjugates removes every exceptional translated subtorus
    after finitely many indices.

    An irrational limiting phase has relative degree three and is
    excluded by the height and chord inequalities. A rational limit
    has contact order `ell<h`; a second Subspace Theorem estimate
    controls cancellation between the contracting conjugates at every
    sufficiently large index. Fixed alignment then has normalized
    chord at least `T_n^((h-ell)/2+o(1))`. In item 498, exact
    differentiation gives `ell=1`, so this grows as `T_n^(15/2+o(1))`
    at the least possible radius. Root proved the theorem and Astra
    independently audited the source, exceptional sets, content and
    contact steps. See [the proof](cubic_pisot_norm_path_endpoint_obstruction.md)
    and the extended [exact checker](check_norm_descent_rational_phase_gap.py).
    There is no uniformity over varying fields, polynomials, units,
    offsets or multiplicative groups; no general count bound follows.

500. **The Gaussian-moat rectangle method extends to composite blocks.**
    The user supplied the `openai/math` repository. Its Gaussian-moat
    paper combines determinant divisibility, random conjugation,
    Boolean-cube expansion and a shared-displacement information budget.
    At source revision `adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a`,
    Sol and root extended the rectangle lemma to pairwise rational-prime-
    disjoint, conjugate-primitive Gaussian blocks of comparable log norms.
    If `P` is their product norm and an origin-centered rectangle has
    half-length product at most `P^(1-d)`, the fraction of signed
    products admitting a nonzero lattice multiple there is at most
    `C_kappa exp(-c_kappa d^3 r)`, for sufficiently large `d^3 r`.
    The weighted fixed-line and common-divisor estimates retain all
    prime powers. Exact tests independently check the least integer
    multiplier and averaged Gaussian-content bound.

    This is a probability bound over all sign choices. Actual endpoint
    chords supply particular signs, and their triple-common divisor
    weight does not exceed the worst-case determinant ceiling by a
    guaranteed positive proportion. The finite prime-avoidance sieve
    is constant on each fixed norm fiber. Moreover a nonzero displacement
    between points of a short circle arc identifies its ordered pair.
    For a shared displacement package `D` and `p_0=Pr(D=0)`, the
    near-maximal residue-entropy and small data-cost hypotheses of the
    source force `epsilon+kappa>=1-p_0`. This prevents a literal transfer
    of its inexpensive full displacement data. Squared chord lengths
    save at most one bit under the existing multiplicative Sidon theorem.
    Primitive residuals can lose all starting information, but an exact
    three-point family shows that they also lose the residue update map.
    The remaining candidate count is bounded by a divisor fiber
    `nu_N(t)<=tau(N)`, which still depends on the radius. See
    [the composite-block theorem and transfer audit](gaussian_moat_composite_block_transfer.md)
    and its [exact checker](check_gaussian_moat_composite_block_transfer.py).
    The source argument was inspected in prose, not compiled in Lean.
    No stronger general point-count growth is claimed.

501. **Nearby block conjugations have a deterministic witness-height cost.**
    Let two signed products of prime-disjoint conjugate-primitive blocks
    have the same norm `P`, and let `q` be the product norm of the blocks
    whose orientations differ. If both signed lattices have nonzero
    witnesses in an origin-centered rectangle of half-lengths
    `R_1>=W_1>=1`, put `A=R_1 W_1`. Then necessarily
    `q<=2R_1^2/P` or `q>=P/(2A)`. Below the second threshold,
    determinant divisibility makes the witnesses collinear. Their exact
    least integer multipliers and common Gaussian content then force
    the larger witness to have modulus at least `sqrt(Pq)`.
    If one actual witness is conjugate-primitive, the other collinear
    witness is at least `q` times as long.

    An extracted row has `r=2^(m-1)` incident blocks with log norm
    `w+o(w)` and fits a rectangle with `R_1=exp(rw/2+o(w))` and
    `W_1=exp(o(w))`. For fixed `m>=3`, every change of
    `1<=h<r/2` block orientations is excluded at this same height.
    Directly multiplying a different original row to fill this support
    costs at least `exp(rw/4-o(w))` in multiplier modulus, including
    all overlaps with correction factors. Half-support changes and
    general multirow cancellation remain open. See
    [the proof](signed_block_flip_witness_height.md) and its
    [exact checker](check_signed_block_flip_witness_height.py).
    Sol proved the lemma; root and Astra independently checked it.

502. **Ordinary divisor fibers can underestimate the squared radius by an unbounded factor.**
    For even `r>=2` and integer `s>=1`, put `D=r^2+1`,
    `a=2rDs`, `h_+=(a+r)+i`, `h_-=(a-r)+i`, and
    `q_+=Norm(h_+)`, `q_-=Norm(h_-)`. The two Gaussian numerators
    are conjugate-primitive and mutually coprime, whereas
    `gcd_Z(q_+,q_-)=D`. Their ordinary norm lcm is
    `N_ord=q_+q_-/D`, but their Gaussian lcm has norm
    `q_+q_-=D N_ord`. Both `q_+` and `q_-` exceed `sqrt(N_ord)`.
    Thus both count in the residual-one divisor fiber at `C=2`,
    yet they cannot fit an anchored Gaussian circle at that radius.

    The actual primitive three-point realization has normalized arc
    length tending to two as `s` tends to infinity for fixed `r`.
    Using the ordinary lcm would instead predict a limit
    `2D^(-1/4)`, arbitrarily small as `r` grows. This is a precise
    failure of sufficiency for the divisor-only data, not a counterexample
    to a uniform upper bound for those fibers or for circle arcs.
    See the final section of [the transfer note](gaussian_moat_composite_block_transfer.md).
    Root derived the family; Luna independently checked the proof for
    all parameters. The checker in item 501 includes 120 exact fixtures.

503. **Fixed-multiplier flip costs have a primitive half-flip boundary.**
    For conjugate-primitive `U=X+iY=FA`, with `F=a+ib` and `q=N(F)>1`,
    the raw flip obeys
    `|Im(bar(F)A)|>=2sqrt(q-1)|X|/q-|Y|`.
    Every proper flip of a balanced row therefore has positive-power
    imaginary height if its correction multiplier is kept fixed.
    This stronger raw-product assertion cannot be extended to arbitrary
    bounded Gaussian multipliers. For `u^2-5b^2=-1`, take
    `F=(u+2b)+ib`, `A=b+i(2b-u)`. Then
    `FA=2ub+i` and `(2+i)bar(F)A=(10b^2-1)+2i`.
    The blocks are conjugate-primitive with disjoint norm supports and
    comparable norms; both thin witnesses are conjugate-primitive too.
    This is a two-block boundary example, not a full many-row profile.

    Singleton orientation divisibility excludes subpower-coefficient
    relations among at most three distinct full signed products.
    The first remaining four-term circuit has all changing blocks split
    two against two, and reduces to
    `c0 ABC+c1 A bar(B) bar(C)+c2 bar(A) B bar(C)+c3 bar(A) bar(B) C=0`.
    The Pell family realizes such a circuit with one group a unit and
    fixed coefficients, so a universal coefficient gap for that entire
    class is false. Three large groups and full-row compatibility remain
    additional requirements. See the appended sections
    of [the witness note](signed_block_flip_witness_height.md).
    Astra supplied the raw-flip and relation arguments; Sol found the
    initial Pell cancellation; root strengthened it to primitive
    witnesses, and Astra and Sol independently audited the formulas.

504. **Phase updates lose the source sieve's informative zero test.**
    For fixed squared norm `N` and split `p` not dividing `N`, every
    point and every transition ratio is a unit modulo either Gaussian
    prime over `p`. Every multiplicative transition word therefore
    preserves every nonzero candidate starting residue. Its passing
    set is always the same `p-1` residues. On actual circle paths the
    passing event is certain, so it adds no information even when the
    transition word itself reveals the anchor. If `p|N`, the source's
    requirement of nonzero residues at both factors rejects the entire
    norm fiber. This is a failure of this particular transferred test,
    not an impossibility theorem for other information methods.

    An exact oriented-area update pays the full destination entropy
    under independent sampling. A cheap cyclic-index update can be
    independent of the anchor but lacks the source's additive residue
    law. Finally a rational norm-one rotation sending every point of a
    primitive cluster to Gaussian integers must be a Gaussian unit;
    conjugation adds at most one further bit of symmetry. See
    [the state-update audit](gaussian_moat_torus_state_update_obstruction.md).
    No radius-uniform point-count consequence follows.

505. **One bounded circuit can have three large groups; two independent circuits pay height.**
    For `t=1 mod15`, set `A=t+i(t+5)`, `B=t+1+i(t+4)`,
    `C=t+2+i(t+3)`, and form the four even-parity signed products
    `T0=ABC,T1=A bar(B)bar(C),T2=bar(A)B bar(C),T3=bar(A)bar(B)C`.
    Their primitive, pairwise-coprime norms are all `2t^2+O(t)`,
    and `-T0-6T1+8T2-3T3=0` identically. Thus a single bounded
    signed circuit has no height gap even with all three groups large.
    Its four equal-radius points have arc length of order `rho^(2/3)`,
    not endpoint scale, and do not contradict the goal.

    For any such disjoint blocks, two independent Gaussian coefficient
    relations `c,d` obey `2H(c)H(d)>=min(|A|,|B|,|C|)`.
    Each coefficient minor is divisible by the corresponding oriented
    block. For integer coefficients this strengthens to the minimum
    norm. The family above has the independent relation
    `(0,-bar(A),2bar(B),-bar(C))`, with height of order `t`,
    showing the Gaussian order is sharp. The cheap identities from
    actual rows have different supports; multiplying them by one
    common Gaussian monomial to fill those supports already costs a
    positive height exponent. See [the proof and family](four_term_signed_circuit_height.md)
    and [the exact checker](check_four_term_signed_circuit_height.py).
    Sol found the family, root proved the sharper minor bound, and
    Astra and Luna independently audited the identities and scope.

506. **Conjugation leaves only half-distance corrected sign witnesses.**
    In a rectangle about the real axis, conjugating a signed witness
    preserves its height. The interval in item 501 therefore applies
    to both the flip norm `q` and its complement `P/q`.
    On `r` fixed balanced blocks with endpoint modulus and subpower
    imaginary height, every pair of admissible signs has Hamming
    distance `0,r/2,r` for all sufficiently large block sizes.
    Choosing one sign from each antipodal pair gives mutually
    orthogonal vectors in `R^r`, hence at most `2r` admissible signs;
    for odd `r`, at most two. The Pell family attains the arithmetic
    bound for `r=2` using its two witnesses and their conjugates.

    Four even-parity patterns with three changing groups of positive
    asymptotic norm mass must have a fourth common group of the same
    mass. Item 507 excludes that remaining thin-witness pattern by
    arithmetic. The actual original rows and their thin pair products
    have different supports, so the sign-code count does not count
    the original circle cluster. See the new section of
    [the witness note](signed_block_flip_witness_height.md) and
    [the conjugation checker](check_signed_witness_conjugation_code.py).
    Root derived the extension; Astra, Sol and Luna independently
    checked the conjugation and orthogonality steps.

507. **Four thin signed witnesses satisfy an unconditional height gap.**
    Let `A,B,C` be nonunit conjugate-primitive Gaussian integers,
    `D` a possibly unit conjugate-primitive factor, and suppose all
    four norms are pairwise coprime. Form the signed products
    `B0=DABC,B1=DA bar(B)bar(C),B2=D bar(A)B bar(C),B3=D bar(A)bar(B)C`.
    For arbitrary nonzero Gaussian corrections, put `Uj=Kj Bj`,
    `M=max|Kj|` and `Y=max|Im Uj|`. Then

    ```text
    min(N(A),N(B),N(C)) <= 8 M^2 max(1,Y)^4.
    ```

    Opposite-edge determinants have the repeated divisors
    `N(D)N(A),N(D)N(B),N(D)N(C)`. Their four three-row identities
    have rank exactly two on the primitive norm vector
    `(N(A),N(B),N(C))` when coordinates and determinants are nonzero.
    The integer cross product, retaining its different column heights,
    gives `N(D)<=8M^2Y^4`. If the smallest changing norm exceeds
    `M^2`, all needed nonvanishing conditions persist when suitable
    pairs of witnesses are conjugated. Any group can then become
    common, giving the same bound on every group. In the complementary
    case the stated minimum bound is immediate.

    For balanced log norms `w+o(w)`, subpower corrections force
    `Y>=exp(w/4-o(w))`; a common height bound is at least
    `exp(w/6-o(w))`. This is a positive exponent for a compatible
    arithmetic pattern, not just a restriction on an isolated relation.
    The full Boolean profile has different opposite-edge divisors,
    and no sufficiently cheap common-support construction is known.
    See [the full proof](four_signed_witness_matching_norm_gap.md)
    and [the exact checker](check_four_signed_witness_matching_norm_gap.py).
    Astra found the rank-two argument; Sol sharpened the column bounds;
    root used conjugation to remove the balance assumption. All three
    independently checked the final bound, and Luna wrote the checker.

508. **A four-witness parity gap extends the matching-norm argument.**
    Group four signed words into the eight possible relative patterns:
    four even groups with norms `e_0,...,e_3` and four odd groups
    with norms `o_0,...,o_3`. Allow arbitrary Gaussian corrections,
    including overlap with the prime-disjoint cores. The four
    determinant triangle identities have rank two on the primitive
    vector `(e_1,e_2,e_3)`, giving
    `max(e_1,e_2,e_3)<=2Y^2T^2 max(o_j)^2`, when all imaginary
    coordinates and determinant residuals are nonzero. An explicit
    correction-height cutoff guarantees that nonvanishing.

    For four pairwise orthogonal thin signs on a fixed balanced
    support, every even pattern occurs `alpha` times and every odd
    pattern `beta` times. The inequality and its conjugate give
    `alpha<=2beta` and `beta<=2alpha`: normalized fourth correlation
    is at most `1/3`. At support sizes eight and sixteen this forces
    zero fourth correlation and `1+binom(k,2)<=r`. It does not give
    a uniform count: the independent coordinate characters on
    `F_2^m` have unbounded cardinality, satisfy every quartet test,
    and have no closed XOR circuit of any size. These are abstract
    signs, not Gaussian witnesses. See [the parity proof](four_signed_witness_parity_gap.md)
    and [the checker](check_four_signed_witness_parity_gap.py).
    Sol derived the extension; Astra, Luna and root checked its
    divisor, rank, conjugation and scope claims.

509. **Only original rows and pair quotients fit the multiplicative height budget.**
    For `r=2^(m-1)` and any integer vector `epsilon`, set
    `F(epsilon)=sum_(T subset [m])|sum_(i in T)epsilon_i|`.
    Then `F>=r max|epsilon_i|`, and `F<=r` holds exactly for zero,
    signed coordinate vectors, and directed differences `e_i-e_j`.
    Every other integer vector has `F>=3r/2`. The latter follows
    from conditioning on three signed Bernoulli coordinates, after
    excluding entries of magnitude at least two.

    Primewise orientation imbalance transfers this exact inequality
    to full-profile Gaussian words, retaining the loss
    `sum|epsilon_i| log Norm(K_i)` from overlapping corrections.
    Ordinary rational norm divisions do not change the imbalance.
    An output at the original row height first forces bounded
    exponent vectors and then the stated classification. Zero net
    exponent can leave a large real factor but cannot supply a
    growing signed core with a subpower correction. Thus ordinary
    multiplicative cancellation cannot create a new common support
    at this height. Additive cancellation and large Gaussian
    divisions are outside the theorem. See [the proof](full_profile_monomial_height_classification.md).
    Root proved the classification and norm budget; Luna and Sol
    independently audited varying exponents and correction overlap.

510. **Actual pair quotients give triangle frames and an additive norm gcd.**
    For the full four-row profile, let
    `V_i=K_i H_i bar(H_(I\{i}))` and
    `L_i^ell=V_i H_iell bar(H_jk)`, where `{i,j,k,ell}=I`.
    Then `bar(L_i^ell)L_j^ell=bar(P_i)P_j/G_ij`, with determinant
    `t_ij`. Each three-column frame has norm scale `exp(4w)` and
    subpower pair determinants. Its linear relation clears back
    to the existing five-star relation.

    The loop `4->3->2->4` is a shear with coefficient
    `-Pf(t)/(t_13 t_14)` in its actual frame basis. Two-loop and
    commutator traces, and every fixed closed-word trace, are rational
    functions of the six residuals alone, with explicit numerator
    and denominator bounds. An exact split-prime fixture disproves
    automatic preservation of a second isotropic line. Ambient
    matrix size therefore does not establish a residual height gap.

    Set `a_i=Norm(K_i)n_i n_(I\{i})` and
    `(b_1,b_2,b_3)=(n_12n_34,n_13n_24,n_14n_23)`.
    For `Z_ij=x_ij+i t_ij`, the three integers
    `(t_ik x_ij-t_ij x_ik)/t_jk` at vertex `i` are exactly
    `a_i b_1,a_i b_2,a_i b_3`; their gcd is `a_i`, including
    correction-prime overlaps. The associated six norm equations
    and directed triangle cycles retain necessary arithmetic data,
    but do not realize the fifteen oriented blocks or force the
    original small imaginary coordinates. A separate primitive Pell
    family realizes the exceptional directed three-cycle with bounded
    imaginary parts. See [the complete identities and limitations](endpoint_triangle_frame_holonomy.md)
    and [the exact checker](check_endpoint_triangle_frame_holonomy.py).
    Astra derived the frames, holonomy and directed-cycle analysis;
    Sol proved the additive gcd; all three model agents and root
    supplied independent algebraic and exact checks.

511. **Eight primitive points realize the translated four-group pattern.**
    Put `lambda=9+4sqrt(5)`, `F=1+2i`, and
    `H_r=x_r+F y_r`, where `x_r+y_r sqrt(5)=lambda^r`.
    For `n=1 mod60`, take the four blocks with indices
    `n-2,n,n+2,n+4`. Their norms and `Norm(F)` are pairwise
    coprime. Use all eight sign words having either one or three
    unbarred factors, multiplying the former by `F` and the latter
    by `bar(F)`. All eight points are individually conjugate-primitive,
    distinct, of equal norm, and have global Gaussian gcd one.

    Their leading phases cancel, and the exact Pell expansion puts
    them in an arc of length at most
    `8*5^(1/4)*lambda^6 sqrt(R)`. A quartet that keeps one block
    unbarred has the Hadamard pattern after reorienting the other
    three blocks; the remaining points reverse its common factor.
    This refutes a proposed translated-pattern exclusion even with
    a primitive global extension. It is only a fixed eight-point
    family for a fixed, large arc constant. Its absolute imaginary
    coordinates are not subpower in the block height, so the
    origin-based four-witness gap is unaffected. See [the family](primitive_eight_point_translated_pell_family.md)
    and [the checker](check_primitive_eight_point_translated_pell_family.py).
    The family attains the existing fixed shifted-Pell bound of eight.
    Astra proved disjointness and the geometry; root selected the
    full primitive odd parity class; Luna independently audited both.

512. **Every fixed quadratic norm-one Pell template has at most eight rows.**
    The fixed-template theorem now allows
    `J_r=f_(2r+1)+i f_(2r)`, with growth unit
    `lambda_0=(3+sqrt(5))/2`, rather than only its suborbit
    `J_(3r)=H_r`. Fixed shifted norm gcds and the ramified content
    remain bounded, so primitive normalization preserves the growth
    exponent. The smaller unit permits a potential third-order
    phase resonance, which the old large-root estimate did not exclude.

    In that case the active width is `K<=12`, while a nonzero
    difference polynomial is divisible by `f=X^2-7X+1`.
    Writing it as `fQ` gives `||fQ||_1>=5||Q||_1`. Among quotients
    of norm at most two, every nonmonomial multiple costs at least
    fourteen. The only remaining difference is `+/-X^a f`, whose
