    coefficient sum is odd. Equal-norm Gaussian prefactors require
    that sum to be even. Thus the resonance is impossible,
    `K<=4`, and the count is at most eight, including two-row
    templates and arbitrary fixed multiplicities. The equality and
    conductor conclusions persist.

    The argument extends to every fixed norm-one algebraic unit
    `lambda>1` in a real quadratic field. For nonsquare
    `D=Norm(F)`, take `J_r=c(x_r+F y_r)` with a fixed integer
    clearing factor and `x_r+y_r sqrt(D)=lambda^r`. The norm
    recurrence has a fixed positive Wronskian; it bounds all
    distinct shifted norm gcds and retains bounded within-block
    conjugate content. Thus global primitive normalization costs
    only a bounded factor. The phase ratio `F/sqrt(D)` imposes
    the same parity. Unit trace at least four excludes every
    higher-order cancellation directly; trace three is precisely
    the finer-unit case above. The count eight is independent of
    the field, unit and fixed template, under the stated endpoint
    hypothesis along an unbounded sequence. See [Sections 7--8 of the template theorem](pell_product_endpoint_obstruction.md)
    and [its focused checker](check_finer_pell_parity_obstruction.py).
    Root identified the finer-unit exception and parity closure;
    Sol supplied the complete normalization and proof; Astra audited
    the saved argument independently. This is a restricted uniform
    count, with no improvement to the general dependence on `R`.

513. **Norm-minus-one Pell templates also have a uniform count.**
    For the same fixed templates built from a real-quadratic
    algebraic unit of norm minus one, the norm recurrence and its
    positive Wronskian still bound all shifted overlaps. The phase
    parameter is now `q=-lambda^(-2)`, with
    `lambda>=(1+sqrt(5))/2`. If a row difference first appears at
    odd phase order `nu`, its coefficient norm and active width
    satisfy `||P||_1<=K<=4nu`. The conjugate-root estimate excludes
    `nu>=7`.

    For `nu=5`, the difference polynomial is divisible by both
    `X^2+A X+1` and `X^2+(A^3-3A)X+1`, where
    `A=trace(lambda)^2+2>=3`. Reverse-triangle convolution bounds
    exclude coefficient norm at most twenty. In the only smallest
    case `A=3`, the quotient would have to be a signed monomial,
    but the product has coefficient norm one hundred. Thus
    `nu<=3`, `K<=12`, and there are at most
    `prod_s(E_s+1)<=2^12=4096` rows. No sharp count is asserted.

    A four-row full-Fibonacci example with widths `(1,3,4,3,1)`
    attains `K=12`: all four exponent sums equal six, their
    polynomials agree at `q=-phi^(-2)`, and their third phase
    terms differ. Its primitive radius is of order `phi^(12n)`
    and its angular width of order `phi^(-6n)`, so it is an
    actual endpoint family. Individual coordinate contents need
    not be bounded, while the global Gaussian gcd is bounded.
    This explains why the norm-one width bound cannot simply
    be carried over. See [Section 9 and the explicit rows](pell_product_endpoint_obstruction.md).
    Root identified the sign change and the rough uniform bound;
    Sol proved the stronger elementary order bound; Luna found
    the exact four-row example; Astra independently audited the
    completed argument. All units, shifts, multiplicities and
    prefactors remain fixed as the parameter grows. These results
    do not address arbitrary Boolean profiles or growing templates.

514. **Actual coordinates recover the co-singleton norm and fix the candidate sign.**
    In the primitive full four-row profile, put
    `Z_ij=bar(P_i)P_j/G_ij=x_ij+i t_ij`,
    `h_i=Norm(K_i)n_{ {i} }`, `e_i=n_(I\{i})`, and
    `A_i=h_i e_i`. The earlier additive gcd recovers `A_i` from
    three pair-quotient combinations. Actual coordinates satisfy
    `gcd(A_i,X_i t_ij+Y_i x_ij)=h_i`, recovering `e_i` exactly.
    The proof factors the second argument as `h_i c_ij Y_j`;
    the co-singleton norm is coprime to both `c_ij` and `Y_j`.
    No coprimality between the correction norm and `e_i` is needed.

    If both primitive nearest-square signs `Y_i=+b,-b` pass this
    gcd test, their sum forces the full singleton norm to divide
    `t_ij`. Thus `0<|t_ij|<n_{ {i} }` permits at most one sign.
    Passing the test does not establish the remaining Gaussian
    divisibilities or a positive residual-height gap. See
    [the coordinate test](four_row_one_coordinate_divisor_reduction.md#5-an-exact-private-norm-gcd-and-a-unique-candidate-sign)
    and [its expanded checker](check_four_row_integer_five_star_lift.py),
    including 144 gcd recoveries and 144 sign exclusions with
    overlapping correction/core valuation depths.

515. **Resonant Fibonacci factors have an exact primitive-height reduction.**
    For odd `d`, let `G_d=F_((d+1)/2)+i F_((d-1)/2)`.
    Its norm is `F_d`, and its oriented Gaussian gcd with `G_e`
    is associated to `G_gcd(d,e)`. In each proportional class
    of affine indices `d_s=m_s d_0`, the factorization into
    homogeneous cyclotomic layers is integral. Distinct fixed
    layers, their opposite orientations, and distinct affine
    classes have bounded gcd loss, with valuation depth retained.
    If `W_(c,e)` is the range of row exponents at a layer, the
    true primitive radius obeys
    `log R=(log(phi)/2)sum_c d_c sum_e totient(e)W_(c,e)+O(1)`.
    This removes growing overlaps before comparing endpoint exponents.

    In one proportional class, Gaussian prefactor parity gives
    monic reciprocal integer polynomials `A_i` of even degree
    `L=sum_e totient(e)W_e`, with fixed `A_i(z)A_i(-z)` and
    `ord_0(A_i-A_j)>=ceil(L/4)`. Möbius inversion proves the
    converse: every finite admissible layer family lifts to an
    exact Gaussian template after common-factor removal and fixed
    equal-norm prefactors. Its endpoint constant may depend on
    the template. This reduction neither bounds that constant
    across changing templates nor covers arbitrary circle rows.
    See [the reduction and converse](resonant_fibonacci_cyclotomic_reduction.md)
    and [the exact checker](check_resonant_fibonacci_cyclotomic_reduction.py).

516. **One-class cyclotomic fibers have new restricted uniform counts.**
    If every active nonbase layer index is an odd prime power,
    the fiber in item 515 has at most four rows, independently
    of its degree, rates, or multiplicities. Low jets force the
    prime-power chains below the first contact `h` to move together;
    each remaining higher layer costs at least `2h` in a total
    degree budget at most `4h`. The resulting integer boxes have
    at most four parity-compatible rows, including all small cases.
    Four is attained already at degree four.

    More generally, projection to layer coordinates `e>=h` is
    injective: a largest nonzero lower coordinate would contradict
    the vanished Möbius-transform coordinate there. If every active
    index has at most `r` distinct prime divisors, write
    `c_r=product_(j<=r)(1-1/p_j)` for the first `r` odd primes.
    Each retained unit of width costs at least `c_r h`, giving
    at most `2^floor(4/c_r)` rows: 128 for `r=2`, 256 for `r=3`.
    Without this restriction, an elementary totient estimate gives
    only `exp(O(sqrt(log L)))`, still depending on polynomial degree.

    The [complete finite checker](check_resonant_cyclotomic_fibres.py)
    covers every profile of degree at most 40: 20,886 profiles,
    1,506,841 orientations, and 1,437,928 profile/signature pairs.
    Its largest fiber is four. All 70,528 pairs satisfy the exact
    degree-distance inequality after polynomial gcd cancellation.
    An explicit common nonzero first coefficient verifies that
    the center may drift even when all pair separations have high
    order. These finite checks are not a theorem at unbounded degree.
    See [the uniform restricted proofs](resonant_fibonacci_cyclotomic_reduction.md#7-a-sharp-four-row-bound-for-odd-prime-power-layers).
    The general circle bound remains unchanged.

517. **The three coordinate gcd tests are dependent at residual scale.**
    In the full four-row profile, fix `i`, put `A=A_i`, and use arbitrary
    candidate integers `X,Y`. For `L_j=X t_ij+Y x_ij`, set
    `d_j=gcd(A,L_j)` and `d=gcd(A,(L_j)_j)`. The triangle identities
    imply `d_j/d` divides `|t_ij|`. The outputs therefore cannot supply
    three independent exponential divisibility gains. A depth-safe
    modular root reduction retains modulus
    `A/gcd(A,gcd(x_ij,t_ij)^2)>=A/|t_ij|^2`; correction overlaps do not
    authorize discarding an entire prime power.
    See [the proof](four_row_one_coordinate_divisor_reduction.md#6-the-three-gcd-outputs-differ-only-at-residual-scale).
    The checker passes 720 arbitrary-candidate gcd comparisons and
    144 modular-root checks in addition to the earlier actual-row tests.

518. **Cyclotomic fiber size is controlled by low-jet nullity.**
    Write `rho` for the rational nullity of the matrix
    `M[d,e]=mu(e/d)1_(d|e)`, odd `d<h`. Canceling a pair's common
    factors gives weighted degree-distance at least `2h`. If `L<=4h`,
    the weighted affine box embedding has pairwise nonpositive inner
    products and affine dimension at most `rho`. A normalized Gram
    trace-square argument gives at most `2rho+1` polynomials in the
    whole fiber, or `rho+1` when `L<4h`.

    For actual growing fixed templates, phase alignment forces the
    fixed prefactor ratios to depend linearly on the even base-layer
    differences. Exact prime allocations are therefore affine in
    the layer counts, including overlaps and the true common gcd.
    On a `C<=sqrt(2)` arc, geometric affine rigidity gives at most
    `rho+1` points. Positive effective degree is an explicit hypothesis:
    stationary templates with arbitrary fixed prefactors are excluded.
    See [the complete affine-rank proof](cyclotomic_affine_rank_reduction.md).

519. **The proposed universal nullity bound of three is false.**
    Let `h=4199` and take the union of divisors of
    `(4199,4275,4335,4845)`. Its charged support cost
    `2*1_(1 in E)+sum_(e>1)phi(e)=16792` is below `4h=16796`,
    but the truncated Möbius matrix has exact nullity four.
    There is an infinite odd-parameter family and a separate
    squarefree example. The exhaustive maximum of three through
    odd `h=31` remains valid only in that finite range.
    See [the counterexample proof](cyclotomic_nullity_four_counterexample.md)
    and [the exact checker](check_cyclotomic_weighted_nullity.py).

520. **Five actual primitive points fit arcs of length o(sqrt(R)).**
    For odd `k>=19`, with `k=0` or `1 mod 3`, use four orders
    `n=((k-2)(k+2)(k+4),k^2(k+4),k(k+2)^2,k(k+2)(k+4))`.
    If `v_j(e)=1_(e|n_j)`, the rows `v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4,v_1+v_2+v_3`
    have even base differences and minimum contact `h=n_1`.
    Their exact width degree is `L=4k^3+15k^2-k-20`, with
    `4h-L=k^2-15k-44>0`. At `k=19`, `h=8211` and `L=32812`.

    Explicit products of the four Gaussian Fibonacci factors, with
    prefactors `1+2i` for the singleton rows and `1-2i` for the triple
    row, realize the family after the complete common gcd is removed.
    Its normalized arc length tends to zero. This refutes a universal
    four-row count in the one-class model and gives `M(C)>=5` for
    every fixed `C>0`, but supplies no unbounded-count family.
    See [the proof and explicit rows](cyclotomic_five_row_subendpoint_family.md),
    [the exact circle checker](check_cyclotomic_five_row_subendpoint.py),
    and [the finite odd-mask search](check_cyclotomic_odd_subset_search.py).
    At the tested rates no six of the eight odd masks meet the degree
    budget; that finite statement does not exclude other constructions.

521. **A uniform count is proved for the unrestricted one-class model.**
    For every finite set of odd active indices, arbitrary prime powers
    included, charged support cost at most `4h` implies `rho<=1125`.
    A prime-power compression replaces a level by the intersection of
    all preceding support slices and fills missing lower slices. An
    explicit linear map on the old kernel, together with an independent
    copy of its lost kernel inside the new one, proves nullity cannot
    decrease. The geometric totient sum pays for every added column,
    including the special base charge. Repetition produces a divisor
    downset without increasing cost.

    Its nullity counts orders at least `h` in a roots-of-unity union
    of size at most `4h`. The graph joining orders with gcd at least
    `2h/15` has degree at most 224. Six independent vertices would
    already have union size greater than `4h`; hence there are at most
    1125 high orders. Item 518 then gives **at most 2251 polynomials
    in every one-class endpoint fiber**, or 1126 with strict contact
    slack. No degree, multiplicity or prime-support restriction remains
    within that model, and the constants are deliberately not optimized.
    See [the full proof](cyclotomic_uniform_rank.md) and
    [the rational-rank checker](check_cyclotomic_prime_power_compression.py).
    Its 34,188 exact comparisons supplement the independently audited
    proof. This still does not cover nonproportional affine classes or
    arbitrary circle configurations.

522. **Mixed classes retain reciprocity but require integer width control.**
    With `xi=phi^(-n)` and class parameters `(A_c,B_c)`, the factor
    arguments are `gamma_c xi^(A_c)`, where `gamma_c` is an algebraic
    unit. The automorphism fixing `i` and sending `sqrt(5)` to
    `-sqrt(5)` sends `gamma_c` to its inverse. Total base parity gives
    a common leading coefficient, so the canceled pair remains
    reciprocal under that automorphism and its degree is at least
    twice the contact slope. The affine/obtuse count therefore still
    applies using the full coupled rational kernel.

    That kernel cannot have a uniform dimension bound based only on
    minimum support cost: `N=8K` slope-two, width-one classes with
    consecutive odd intercepts have at most `2K` rational low-frequency
    equations, leaving dimension at least `6K`. Nevertheless their
    width-one integer box contains no nonzero first-harmonic cancellation,
    by geometric-series dominance at `|phi^(-2)|<1/2`. This is a formal
    rank countermodel, not an actual large fiber. The next mixed-class
    argument must use coefficient widths, rather than classwise Möbius
    vanishing or rational nullity alone. See
    [the exact mixed-class scope](mixed_affine_cyclotomic_rank_scope.md).

523. **Common-slope mixed classes have a uniform count.**
    For `d_c(n)=An+B_c`, with fixed positive even A and distinct odd
    intercepts, allow arbitrary odd layers and widths. Put
    `D=sum_(c,e) phi(e)W_(c,e)` and let h be the minimum odd harmonic
    contact. Endpoint compatibility gives `D<=4h`. For an actual pair,
    the coupled coefficient is `P_k(q^k)`, where `q=-phi^(-2)` and
    `P_k` is an integer Laurent polynomial of coefficient mass at most D.
    The conjugate root has modulus `phi^(2k)`, so for logarithmically
    large k the only possible cancellation is `P_k=0`, class by class.

    When `D>=2^32`, three Bertrand primes in suitable disjoint dyadic
    intervals recover every remaining small harmonic: the congruence
    `c_e(dp)=c_e(d) mod p` forces their product to divide a class moment
    of magnitude at most D, while that product exceeds D. All classwise
    low moments therefore vanish for actual bounded integer differences.
    Ordinary-cost compression and colored roots of unity bound the
    direct-sum classwise kernel by 1125. Global total-base parity and
    sigma-reciprocity give at most 2251 rows. For smaller D, the full
    coordinate dimension and the same obtuse-set bound give `2D+1`.
    Thus `2^33+1=8589934593` is a deliberately crude absolute count.
    The original rational coupled kernel is not asserted to be bounded.
    See [the complete proof](common_slope_cyclotomic_uniform_count.md)
    and [exact arithmetic checks](check_mixed_affine_prime_amplification.py).

524. **The count extends to frequency-separated slope families.**
    Distinct slopes with distinct 2-adic valuations have disjoint odd
    harmonic frequency sets; their odd parts may be arbitrary. Write
    `L=sum A_c phi(e)W_(c,e)` and let tau be minimum pair frequency.
    For each slope with `L/A>=2^32`, item 523's upper-budget version
    decouples all class moments below tau, using `ceil(L/A)` and the
    least odd h with `Ah>=tau`. After compression, give the root groups
    of that class A labeled copies. Their total size is at most
    `L<=4tau`; the same graph argument bounds the combined low-group
    nullity by 1125. All remaining active coordinates have slope
    greater than `L/2^32`, so there are fewer than `2^32` of them.
    The global affine dimension is therefore at most `1125+2^32`,
    yielding at most `8589936843` rows, independently of the number
    and sizes of the slopes, intercepts, layers and multiplicities.
    See [the frequency-separated theorem](frequency_separated_affine_uniform_count.md).
    Distinct slopes with the same 2-adic valuation can interfere; that
    case is not covered by this argument alone. Item 526 handles
    additional overlapping families. Both theorems here concern fixed growing
    templates, with potentially template-dependent entry thresholds.
    Neither establishes a bound for arbitrary centered-circle arcs.

525. **Prime-power compression works for arbitrary selected Möbius rows.**
    For any set R of odd row indices and finite odd column support E,
    the same compression produces a divisor downset F with no larger
    ordinary totient cost or charged base cost, and
    `dim ker M_(R,E)<=dim ker M_(R,F)=|F\R|`. No interval or
    downward-closure hypothesis on R is required. The slice map
    preserves every row block except one, which it sets to zero; its
    lost kernel embeds disjointly into the new selected-row kernel.
    After compression, rows outside F vanish and any selected rows
    inside F are independent in the full triangular matrix.

    The extension permits independent colors and fixed positive cost
    weights. It does not preserve the values on omitted rows, so it
    does not by itself transport equations coupling different colors.
    See [the exact extension, Section 5](cyclotomic_uniform_rank.md).
    An exact rational check of all 4096 support/row subset pairs in
    `{1,3,5,9,15,45}` passes 10496 compression comparisons and the
    final identity `nullity=|F\R|`.

526. **Integral packet projections handle overlapping slope frequencies.**
    Let the distinct affine slopes in each fixed 2-adic valuation
    bucket form a divisibility chain. There may be arbitrarily many
    buckets, slopes, intercepts, odd layers and multiplicities.
    The absolute count `8589936843` still holds for the stated fixed
    growing Fibonacci templates. It also holds when a bucket has at
    most two arbitrary slopes, even if they are incomparable, and
    the two kinds of buckets may be combined.

    Four Bertrand intervals extend item 523's integer separation to
    low harmonics avoiding one chosen odd prime p. For a smallest
    slope A, choose p dividing the next slope ratio. Only the A-group
    contributes at its off-p frequencies. Once those class moments
    vanish, the difference between its level-zero and level-one
    p-slices has every low moment zero. Equalize the entire two slices
    using the one of smaller aggregate width cost, then use
    `Psi_s(z)Psi_(ps)(z)=Psi_s(z^p)` to rescale `(A,B)` to `(pA,pB)`.
    The choice is global within a class, not coordinatewise. This
    integral operation preserves each original color's low physical
    phase coefficients and does not increase the integer width cost.

    Promote eligible groups until all surviving slopes exceed
    `L/2^32`; fewer than `2^32` coordinates then remain. The kernel
    of the composed map lies in the original direct sum of classwise
    low-jet kernels, whose weighted colored compression bounds its
    dimension by 1125. There is no loss proportional to chain length.
    Only the original rows need total base parity and actual Gaussian
    realization; the final count uses their original obtuse embedding.
    For two arbitrary slopes, promote the smaller using a prime where
    its valuation is lower; the fixed least common multiple proves
    termination. See [the complete packet theorem](divisibility_chain_affine_uniform_count.md).
    The remaining same-bucket slopes `6,10,14` illustrate why this
    promotion rule does not cover every incomparable set. This is an
    obstruction to the operation, not a large-row counterexample.

527. **Actual residuals have an exact imaginary-content gcd.**
    For conjugate-primitive actual rows `P_i=X_i+iY_i`, with nonzero
    imaginary coordinates and `Delta_ij=G_ij t_ij`, one has
    `gcd(|Y_i|,|t_ij|)=gcd(|Y_i|,|Y_j|)=gcd(|Y_j|,|t_ij|)`.
    This retains all correction/core overlap depths: coordinate
    primitivity implies `gcd(Y_i,N_i)=1`, while `G_ij|N_i,N_j`.
    At a prime where the two Y-valuations differ, the residual's
    valuation is their minimum; additional depth is possible only
    when the Y-valuations agree.

    The common content `g=gcd_i|Y_i|` divides every residual and is
    coprime to every shared norm. Virtual coordinates `X_i+iY_i/g`
    preserve the corresponding determinant identities after dividing
    residuals by g, but their norms become
    `N_i-(g^2-1)(Y_i/g)^2`. They need not retain Gaussian core
    divisibility. An exact two-row example and full-profile fixtures
    certify this failure, so content normalization is a filter rather
    than a residual-height gap. See
    [the proof and normalization limit, Section 7](four_row_one_coordinate_divisor_reduction.md)
    and [the expanded exact checker](check_four_row_integer_five_star_lift.py).
    The new checks comprise 72 pair identities, including 44 nontrivial
    contents, four common-content fixtures, and four virtual norm
    failures.

528. **At most three original affine classes per bucket admit a uniform count.**
    At a physical frequency t, the phase constants of two contributing
    nonproportional classes have ratio `+/-phi^(m-m')`, where
    `m=B_c t/A_c` and `m'` are distinct odd integers. The ratio is
    irrational, so a two-term integer moment equation separates
    individually, with no coefficient-height threshold.

    In a bucket with at most three original classes, select its
    numerically smallest slope A and a larger slope B. An odd prime
    with `v_p(A)<v_p(B)` excludes at least one color at every off-p
    frequency `Ak`, leaving at most two. This gives the individual
    off-p zero moments needed by item 526's cost-preserving packet
    map. Current slopes remain divisors of their original least
    common multiple and each processed color increases its slope,
    so finitely many promotions leave one common slope. The previous
    arithmetic cutoff then leaves fewer than `2^32` output coordinates.
    The composed kernel again lies in the original classwise low-jet
    kernels and has dimension at most 1125. Original total parity and
    obtuse geometry give the same bound `8589936843`.

    These buckets can be combined with the divisibility-chain or
    two-slope buckets of item 526. Original class labels and ratios
    must be retained throughout; intermediate images need not have
    the original parity or Gaussian realization. In particular,
    `6,10,14` is covered with one original class at each slope, but
    not with arbitrarily many classes at those three slopes. See
    [the proof](three_class_affine_uniform_count.md) and
    [the exact promotion checker](check_three_class_affine_promotion.py).

529. **A one-shot multiprime projection has bounded cost, but refinement can grow.**
    Suppose an individual class's low moments vanish at harmonics
    coprime to a product of distinct odd primes. Higher prime-depth
    coordinates are already exact single-prime packets. On the
    remaining Boolean prefix cube, the full alternating difference
    has every low moment zero. Remove it, then split recursively
    into integral single-prime packets. A geometric series bounds
    each original coordinate's total charge by less than three times
    its original totient weight. Thus a fixed linear family map
    preserves all low jets with total width cost at most `3D`.

    Cost preservation is false even in the two-prime cube. For
    `b=(1,0,0,-1)`, every p/q-packet gauge costs at least
    `pq-|p-q|`, compared with the original `1+(p-1)(q-1)`.
    At p=5,q=7 this is `25 -> 33`; scaling by two gives an even-base
    fixture `50 -> 66`. For squarefree odd P, the pair
    `b_P=1,b_1=-mu(P)` has cost `phi(P)+1`, while its unique complete
    base-packet refinement costs `sigma(P)-1`. Their ratio is
    unbounded over odd primorials. This does not refute stopping
    before complete refinement, and these are not endpoint families.
    Individual-class separation with arbitrarily many excluded
    primes also remains to be proved. See
    [the projection and cost obstructions](multiprime_packet_cost_obstruction.md)
    and [the exact checker](check_multiprime_packet_cost.py).

530. **Positive Hankel minors retain core divisibility but leave a budget gap.**
    For actual primitive rows `P_i=x_i+i y_i`, choose a positive common
    multiple L of all nonzero `|y_i|,|t_ij|` and put
    `X_i=L x_i/y_i`, `C_i=X_i^2+L^2`. Coordinate primitivity makes
    the denominators units at every incident core prime, so
    `n_T|C_i` for i in T and `n_T|(X_i-X_j)` for i,j in T,
    with full prime-power depth and correction overlaps retained.
    The positive Gram matrix `H_r[a,b]=sum_i X_i^(a+b)/C_i` gives
    an integer `D_r=(product_i C_i)det H_r`, equal by Cauchy--Binet
    to the sum over r-subsets S of squared Vandermonde factors on S
    times the C_i outside S.

    A summand has guaranteed n_T-exponent
    `f_T(S)=|T|-|T intersection S|+|T intersection S|(|T intersection S|-1)`.
    The simultaneous divisor exponent is the sum over T of these
    separate minima. It is strictly smaller than
    `a_m(r)=(m-r)2^(m-1)+r(r-1)2^(m-2)` for every r<m: no proper
    S attains the minimum for every singleton block. In the balanced
    actual profile, subpower y,t and correction norms give
    `log D_r=a_m(r)w+o(w)`. For m=4 the guaranteed exponents are
    `17,18,25,48`, versus sizes `24,24,32,48`. Equality at r=m is
    the ordinary squared Vandermonde. This audits the guaranteed
    divisors only; extra arithmetic divisibility is not excluded.
    See [the full-profile Hankel audit](positive_hankel_full_profile_budget.md)
    and [its exact checker](check_positive_hankel_full_profile_budget.py).
    No positive residual-height gap or general count improvement follows.

531. **A direct four-witness bridge requires four disjoint source edges.**
    Anchor rows and standard primitive pair quotients are Gaussian words
    indexed by edges between the original points. If two source edges
    share a vertex, their orientations have one fixed relative sign on
    every cut separating both. A common-support Hadamard quartet has
    both relative signs among its three changing columns. Consequently
    one changing group G satisfies
    `Norm(G) | Norm(K_r)Norm(K_s)`, where K_r,K_s are the source
    corrections. The argument retains every oriented prime-power depth,
    correction/core overlaps, and splitting of composite core factors.

    Three growing changing groups with subpower corrections therefore
    require a matching of four disjoint edges, hence at least eight
    original points. Four explicit cuts on eight vertices supply the
    desired incidence columns, but their Gaussian divisors need not
    have small imaginary parts. The criterion does not cover additive
    constructions or large uncharged multipliers.

    Separately, thin Gaussian division V=DU with nonreal D satisfies
    `|U|^2<=|Im V||U|+|V||Im U|`. Subpower imaginary parts and numerator
    modulus at most `exp(alpha w+o(w))` force output modulus at most
    `exp(alpha w/2+o(w))`. The threshold is sharp for the primitive,
    coprime-norm factors `(a+2+i)(a-i)=(a+1)^2-2i`, a positive even.
    Root and Sol independently audited the proofs. See
    [the direct-divisor matching criterion](thin_edge_divisor_matching_criterion.md).
    Neither statement supplies the missing full-profile height gap.

532. **Exact nested extraction improves aggregate residual height to order W/M.**
    First retain one common Gaussian-unit class and remove its full gcd.
    Write M for its cardinality, W for its log squared radius, k=m+1,
    and w=W/2^m. Nonnegative pair excesses `delta_ij=d_ij-W/2`
    have total at most WM/4. Combining their first-moment bound with
    the Bessel Fourier-energy bound selects one k-tuple satisfying
    `sum_tuple delta<=k(k-1)W/[2(M-1)]` and relative pattern error
    `eta<=2(2^k-1)/sqrt(M-k+1)` simultaneously.

    Retain every threshold layer, using its orientation relative to
    the selected anchor. Then `P_i=product_(T containing i)H_T`
    exactly, with no correcting factors, and
    `Norm(gcd_G(P_i:i in S))=product_(T containing S)Norm(H_T)`
    for every nonempty row subset S. Each H_T and P_i is
    conjugate-primitive. At a given prime, the supported T form two
    nested chains on disjoint lower- and upper-row sets; different
    blocks can share rational primes. Their log norms remain within
    eta w of w. Empty-layer mass removes the selected tuple's own
    common gcd in norm, without changing the pre-selection scale W.

    The actual primitive edge imaginary residues give
    `H_sum=sum_i log|Y_i|+sum_(i<j)log|t_ij|`
    `<=k(k-1)W/[4(M-1)]`. This sum is independent of the anchor.
    A hypothetical lower bound `H_sum>=f(w)` on one fixed positive
    balanced neighborhood of this nested class would therefore give
    `M<=max(Q,1+k(k-1)W/[4f(W/2^m)])`, with all fixed thresholds
    explicit. In particular `f(w)/log w -> infinity` would improve
    general growth, `f(w)=c w/log w` would give O(loglog R), and
    `f(w)=c w` would prove uniformity. No such lower bound is proved.

    The positive Hankel guaranteed divisor extends primewise to
    overlapping blocks and can gain valuation when a prime spans
    several layers. Squarefree layers still have the previous slack,
    so this gives no universal height gap. Coprime-block signed-witness
    and random-conjugation theorems cannot be imported unchanged.
    Sol wrote the extraction; root and Astra independently audited it.
    Root derived the conditional growth comparison, reviewed by Sol
    and Luna. See [the exact nested extraction and quantifiers](exact_nested_profile_residual_extraction.md)
    and [its exact checker](check_exact_nested_profile_residual_extraction.py).

533. **A Kummer-cover argument bounds the full Boolean polynomial model.**
    Suppose every nonempty Boolean block H_T is a complex polynomial
    of the same positive degree d, and the blocks and their conjugates
    are pairwise coprime. Repeated roots within one block are allowed.
    If each row `P_i=K_i product_(T containing i)H_T=X_i+i c_i`
    has a nonzero constant imaginary part, then there are at most
    35 nonanchor rows, independently of d and the coefficients.

    Normalize `f_i=X_i/c_i`. Each pair difference is a nonzero constant
    times the product of the shared norm blocks. Removing the full
    common norm block gives sections of a ruled surface, of
    self-intersection `e=(2^(m-1)-2)d`, with precisely prescribed
    subset collisions. Adjoin square roots of all section ratios.
    The resulting degree `q=2^(m-1)` Kummer cover has a smooth
    resolution: a contact of order a produces a chain with alternating
    nonzero and zero inertia labels. The construction preserves all
    repeated-root depths.

    For m>=36 its normalized Chern deficit is at most
    `16-4m+d[(36-m)2^(m-1)-16m-36]<0`, whereas its normalized
    canonical square is at least
    `32-8m+d[(3m-20)2^(m-1)+4m+20]>0`.
    Positive canonical intersection with a nef ruling fiber and
    Riemann--Roch prove general type. Bogomolov--Miyaoka--Yau then
    contradicts the negative deficit. The squarefree calculation is
    included separately, with an exact, slightly stronger deficit.

    An intrinsic section-arrangement extension over a base curve of
    genus g gives, for m>=36,
    `d[(m-36)2^(m-1)+16m+36]<=4(m-4)(g-1)`.
    Thus the prescribed pattern is also impossible over genus one;
    for higher genus it forces an explicit genus cost. This assumes
    all pair collision divisors are specified at every point of the
    base in one common line bundle.

    This rules out arbitrarily large balanced polynomial constructions
    of this form, including ones over Q(i). It does not cover variable
    imaginary polynomials, overlapping blocks, or arbitrary integer
    configurations. In particular it supplies no new general bound
    in R. Root proposed the section-arrangement route and derived the
    cover budget; Sol wrote the proof, Astra audited it independently,
    and Luna supplied the exact checker. See
    [the Kummer-cover theorem](boolean_section_kummer_uniform_bound.md)
    and [its checker](check_boolean_section_kummer_uniform_bound.py).

## Remaining mathematical task

It suffices to prove the bound for one fixed positive arc constant, for
example `C = 1/2`: dividing a longer arc into `ceil(2C)` pieces then gives
the bound for arbitrary `C`.

The extraction results now reduce any failure of uniformity to nearly
uniform cut profiles, regardless of how slowly the point count grows.
Central truncation further reduces these profiles to independent Gaussian
blocks with small integral corrections and simultaneous primitive residue
equations. The reconstruction theorem supplies a converse with every
integrality cost controlled, so excluding the stated abstract families
would settle the original objective. Squareclass and higher-power phase
separation are additional necessary restrictions, but tiny corrections
can satisfy all such power-class tests. Congruences beyond half of the
row conductor recover the actual equations; their simultaneous small
solutions remain the unresolved arithmetic requirement. The existing
defect inequalities, generic polynomial divisibility, fixed-prime-support
theorems, and the direct all-points GCD application do not supply a
contradiction.

The latest symmetry reduction makes this requirement constructive:
in each fixed admissible frozen-block window, the relevant primitive
numerators must be the uniquely prescribed continued-fraction
candidates. A failure of any candidate test excludes that completion.
What remains unproved is a uniform obstruction to the simultaneous
success of those tests with the full remaining cut profile. The
number of possible frozen collections has not been bounded.

The subsequent symmetry analysis restricts possible descent arguments.
Even an arbitrarily large projective matrix must preserve the logarithmic
primitive radius to relative error `O(1/M)` if both its input and output
are `M`-point endpoint clusters. A non-pure rational map of fixed degree
and negligible coefficient height instead inflates the endpoint constant
once sufficiently many rows are retained. These statements neither
construct a smaller configuration nor compare different projective
orbits. They are not a substitute for the simultaneous arithmetic
obstruction still needed above.

The original intrinsic sufficient lemma is: find fixed `B >= 0` and a
height threshold such that every separately normalized primitive
eight-point cluster at arc constant `1/2` satisfies

```text
D + W_4 <= 2 W + B.
```

Here `D` is the weighted squared cut imbalance, `W_4` is the weight of
four-versus-four layers, and `W` is the conductor weight after dividing
out that eight-point cluster's own common Gaussian factor. This is
**not proved**. The capped test with values
`(2,9,4,1,1,1,4,9,2)` lifts the statement correctly to inherited layers
and has binomial mean `277/128 > 2`. It would give the even-cluster bound

```text
M <= 2048 + 64 B / (21 log 2),
```

with an additional explicit bound for radii below the assumed threshold.
The common-unit case suffices, with at most a factor four lost when
selecting that unit class. See
[the normalization, constants, and determinant-cone obstruction](finite_local_test_attack.md).
Item 372 supplies weaker alternatives. Either
`D+(1/2)W_4<=2W+B` or `5V_1+2V_2<=V_3+V_4+B` would suffice, with
the same intrinsic normalization and an appropriate fixed height
threshold. The second is the literal source-gcd inequality
`A^6 F^3<=exp(B)N`. These alternatives remain unproved for arbitrary
endpoint tuples; their larger conditional count constants are irrelevant
to the goal of removing radius dependence. See
[the sufficient-test calculation](weaker_intrinsic_finite_tests.md).
Appendix D of the multipoint note retains the alternative, stronger
inherited-layer target with any fixed positive coefficient `delta`.

and proving such growth in `2 log T` alone would suffice, but is a stronger

mixed-layer distributions, whose defect approaches `2 W`.

conjugations remain exact radius-preserving symmetries and are explicitly
excluded from item 225. A continuation should keep that existence gap
separate from further improvements to map-parameter estimates.

Items 226--233 now restrict an admissible map to an exact critical
triangular form, lift all its points to a common near-square circle, and
identify the common content and complete anchor covariance. Reanchoring
does not generate independent lifted circles, and the remaining normalized
strip can still have size N^O(1/m). The available near-square theorem
therefore does not improve the general growth rate. Product minimization
fails as a standalone construction on an actual four-point endpoint set;
local perturbations are discrete; and arbitrarily large full-circle
configurations can have no nonconformal radius descent at all. A proposed
existence theorem must exploit the short-arc condition as well as a
many-point property absent from the Pell examples. The direct common-axis
route also retains a proved power cost on those four-point examples.
These results have been independently audited and checked in exact
arithmetic, but no new general point-count growth rate has been proved.
The best audited prose estimate remains
`(1+epsilon) log R/log log R`; the R-independent goal is unproved and active.

Items 234--239 give complete local isolation of the Pell examples and then
of every four-point cluster at a bounded R^(1/3) scale, with explicit
endpoint separation. The general conic-pencil theorem retains all shape
dependence; its distance-product formulation is an application of the
classical five-point determinant. Equally spaced real configurations show
that all of these geometric product inequalities can hold with growing
cardinality. No argument yet forces a large actual endpoint cluster to
contain a bounded-shape or bounded-pairing-gcd quadruple. Thus these local
results do not improve the general growth rate. The audited prose estimate
remains `(1+epsilon) log R/log log R`, and the uniform goal remains active
and unproved.

The common-circle conjugation identity synchronizes the two Gaussian
orientations in the global quartet gcd. It still does not select one
quartet small at all primes: actual fair profiles can make every individual
quartet content grow while removing every source prime from the common gcd.
The precise endpoint angular condition is absent from these obstruction
families and remains essential to the next extraction argument.

Items 240--244 now bound the global quartet gcd by R^O(1/m), factor it
exactly through deletion contents, and retain all denominators in its
integral Plucker realization. Actual circle families show why this common
gcd cannot be replaced by a bounded-size witnessing subset without using
endpoint geometry. Individual pair rotations and reflections have only
O_C(1) integral source points, so a bounded collection of those operations
cannot carry a growing fraction of a cluster into a descent.

Imposing the actual phases gives a further fixed-profile exclusion:
five rationally isolable nonunit block phases force bounded radius by
Roth's theorem, including arbitrary row units. General profiles can lack
such isolable coordinates. Their interacting, undetermined phases remain
outside that argument. None of these results improves the general count
`(1+epsilon) log R/log log R`. The uniform endpoint theorem remains
unproved and the goal remains active.

Items 245--246 extend fixed-target arithmetic to interacting block phases
and account exactly for shared-prime cancellation. Primitive rank-one
patterns with at least nine nonunit blocks are now excluded, and the
normalized eleven-core pattern has the effective arc lower bound
`L>=(1/2)R^(7/11)`. Complete balanced cuts still fail the scalar Roth
packing threshold, even after optimizing over every integral coefficient
vector. A general cluster need not contain one of the excluded whole
patterns. The best general estimate therefore remains
`(1+epsilon) log R/log log R`; the uniform goal is unproved and active.

Items 247--250 handle multiple moving phase groups and unequal kernel
weights. The interleaved core family has a constant uniform in its number

kernel weight; and two power classes reduce to a primitive one-parameter

exponents within their stated families. The direct monomial-vector Subspace
test still lacks the necessary height margin, and complete balanced cuts
survive the natural row restriction and exact column regrouping operations.
No argument yet brings an arbitrary large endpoint cluster into an excluded
family. The best general bound remains `(1+epsilon) log R/log log R`, and
the uniform goal remains unproved and active.

the conditional count `M<=r+1` in their number of varying split primes.
